review_text:
Stumbling upon a chance dinner at newly opened restaurant Estela was a little like falling into the arms of Don Draper. The unmarked doorway and dark, chic surroundings were mysterious and intriguing, much like the tall, dark and handsome stranger himself. 

Engaging with Estela through its food further perpetuated the mystery, as the flavors revealed little about its culinary origins. Blood sausage croquettes pointed to Spanish, yet Virginia ham was undeniably American. And there were times when I even tasted some Asian flavors. My takeaway was that Estela has no definitive roots and has instead embraced the culinary influences of the multiple cultures it has come into contact with. This absence of a definitive past shouldn't matter, because, like Don's work, the food speaks for itself.

The food is served tapas style to encourage sharing of many dishes, with sizes increasing further down the menu. We decided to order several small plates, including the raw scallops with citrus and bronze fennel, the trout with fava, yuzu, and horseradish, and the egg with gigante beans and cured tuna, as well as a larger dish of the pork with carrots, Marcona almonds, and dandelion greens.

This was one of those rare dinner moments where every single dish that came out was truly well-executed. There were no hit-or-miss inconsistencies here. The ingredients used in each dish were minimal but to the point. I did notice that there was a common thread of utilizing citrus flavors to bring some lightness to the food.

For instance, the raw scallops were reminiscent of the sashimi yuzu appetizers that are staples at Japanese restaurants, yet the fennel and red pepper accents threw you for a loop so that the dish couldn't completely claim Asian origins.

The trout similarly had that Asian quality with its yuzu seasoning, but the fresh and seasonal fava beans and peas seemed very American farmers' market to me. I thought the wispy ribbons of horseradish were a pretty brilliant and unique way of imparting some spice to a dish.  

The egg with gigante beans and cured tuna was my favorite out of the small plates. I loved the warm and savory broth, and the combination of eggs, chunky beans and tuna was a highly satisfying and hearty one. 

I normally don't seek out pork at a restaurant, because I find that it usually ends up occupying two extreme ends of the spectrum--dry, tasteless pork chop loins or extremely fatty, heavy belly pieces. The pork at Estela occupies a happy medium between the two. The meat was lovely and tender and rimmed with just a touch of fattiness to provide rich, juicy flavor. 

Desserts can be an afterthought at many places, but that wasn't the case here. I thought the chocolate sherbet thoughtfully showcased its main ingredient in all sorts of lovely ways. The icy sherbet scoop and the crunchiness of the hazelnuts and coffee beans were extremely fun to eat.

Estela currently enjoys a somewhat anonymous existence in its unmarked address on E. Houston, but this won't last for long. It'll be in your best interest to drop by for a walk-in during its low-key phase before favorable word-of-mouth makes it impossible to score a table. I'm hoping to sneak in another order of the pork as well as the ricotta dumplings and anchovies on my next visit, hopefully before the onslaught of diners crowd me out because they want a piece of Estela's globetrotting cuisine for themselves.

I know how much it costs to order 90% of the menu here.
At once.
A lot.
And oddly, I don't feel that morning-after-I-just bruised my credit card sadness that I have experienced in the past. 
Oh sure, my baggy dress is tighter and my wallet... well lighter.
But I would go back (Truth be told, I already have plans to).

So without further adieu:
A gracious elegant/organic/slightly industrial redo of the Nolita House space with Former Isa mega-talent Ignacio Mattos in the chef toque has landed on Houston. When I walked in, it was packed. I was seated on an oddly comfortable window seat, teeny tiny glass of white wine at my side waiting for my friends. As they trickled in we grabbed a super tiny table in a tinier corner and eye balled the menu.

Pickle plate. Yes please. Beef tartar. Yes. Cured tuna with gigante beans and egg. Olli's Ham plate. Lettuce with Tahini. Burrata with lovage. Trout with Fava and horseradish. Raw scallops with bronze fennel. Calamari with romesco. Pork with Carrots.

Yes, yes and yes. (okay Meg Ryan... I'll shut up).
I have two words for you: AMAZE BALLS.

The best beef tartar of all time. Sunchokes? Pickled Elderberry? Really.
The pork was perfectly cooked. The Lettuce (with tahini and sunflower seeds)... as my friend said, "Even their sunflower seeds are REALLY good", could make me a salad eater. I could have eaten 10 plates of Olli's ham which was magic pork surrounded by melt in your mouth lardo. The calamari was unadulterated brilliance. The service, attentive. My only sadness was that white wines came in a super tiny glass... I like a larger glass. But really? If that's is my only criticism, as my mother would say, "Stop your whining." 

I can't say enough about this place. And so I will stop. (But hope to be a regular there). Just save me a seat, okay?

I really REALLY wanted to love this place. I've heard and read raving reviews so my foodie gf and I had to check it out. We went on a Friday night around 8pm which was crowded but not over the top. 

We had some cocktails at the bar area which was lovely then seated for a dinner service. I had the de la lousiana, which was like a manhattan for all you whiskey drinkers out there. We enjoyed the drinks then had 3 appetizers and a main course to share.

Raw scallops- one big scallop sliced into 4 thin slices. Mind you, I LOVE raw scallops. I often order it from other restaurants so I've had high expectations. When the plate arrived, there were thin slices of raw scallops with tangerines and dill on top. Honestly it wasn't worth the money and I didn't see any wow factor in this dish. The sweet tangerines with raw scallops didn't compliment each other and I didn't think it was anything special. I would've enjoyed it more if it was with something more acidy.

Burrata cheese - A big chunk of burrata cheese with sliced radishes on top. Again, no wow factor here. It was just mediocre.

Beef tartare - Probably the best dish we've had through the evening (Yes, it was yummy but wasn't the best beef tartare I've ever had before). The crispy sun chokes added a lot of texture which I appreciated but again, wasn't the best tartare I've had in NYC.

Ricotta dumplings - A huge disappointment. Don't except actual dumplings. It was more like a bite sized cut up ricotta cheese smothered in butter, fava beans and edamame. For $22, I would've expected more.

Overall, great cocktails but disappointed in the food section. Would I come back again? Maybe, maybe not. I hope to come back to try other things!

Salami ***
great from dipalo's

peas and fava beans ***** 
with creme fraiche, horseradish, peashoot sauce.  best dish of the night.
 
raw scallop ****
with grapefruit and bronze fennel and red pepper accents.  almost a cervice like - great summer dish

razor clams ****
with toasted garlic slices and chilli flakes, lemon juice.  too much lemon juice but still a great dish

Steak **
Too much going on.  Wagyu beef was great, but there was peppercorn, barley, eggplant, anchovy, greens.  too many tastes going on.

Dessert **
lacking in choice. only pana cotta and sorbet.  yogurt sorbet was good.

I wanted to like it here, but was disappointed. The bar, which is quite lovely is so big, compared to the size of the front of the restaurant. I felt very closed in, while waiting up front for our table.  

The waitstaff was nice, but the bartender seemed indifferent to us.

The food was mixed, some dishes were good, but some were just ok.  Overall I found it fair, but I think I should downgrade that to disappointing, based on the fact that dinner was expensive.   You could definitely get a better meal for less in a lot of other restaurants.

We ordered a number of dishes off the menu, here are the ones I remember...olives were good, burrata- yummy, raw scallop-disappointing...i tasted the citrus but not the scallop...  kohlrabi bland...baked cod-- fair...ricotta dumplings nice...calimari--good.

It has only been opened a short time, so maybe I would go back again to give it another chance, but not really sure at this point. :  (

Amazing new place! Tried many dishes and everything was excellent.  The ricotta dumplings were phenomenal, the zucchini and hazelnut salad was delicious and the tomato and melon salad had the best honeydew I've ever tasted.  Panna cotta was perfect too.

I liked this place - we had been there before it was Estela and I like what they did to the space. 

Blood sausage croquettes were very good, as was the mixed greens salad. I found the calamari a la plancha a little chewy but overall good.

The quail was the "BIG" surprise. It apparently comes with the head and one claw attached...perhaps a little too farm to table for me. I wish we had been warned as I would not have ordered it. (See photo)

The panna cotta was delicious. 

Overall a fun place but I probably wouldn't go out of my way to eat there. Maybe for a drink and quick snack if I'm in the area.

Food was great; the insane sound level ruined the experience. Too bad!
I would recommend trying to find a time either earlier in the evening or possibly lunch (if they serve it).

I went back to Estella to see if I would get the same amazing service and food. It was even better. Every dish is so different in a way that you want it all. The squid with ink was tender and so tasteful . All the main dishes are a symphony of flavors exploding in your mouth. No joke!! They have 3 desserts that you lose by picking any one of them.  Love this place, man

Stellar food. Light and simple but fresh and perfectly executed. I had the kohlrabi -- wonderful combination of that delicious vegetable and fragrant hazelnuts. The cod was similarly excellent, extremely simple but marvelously springy and tender. Very few additional flavors, making it suitable for true cod lovers.

Complimentary bread was superb. As were the desserts, which reflecting the style of the place were not overly decadent but rather light and sophisticated. The panna cotta, with a lovely shock of salt, was the standout here. 

Service -- Nori (?), I believe -- was wonderful. All in all a fantastic experience.

Pros:
- Some excellent dishes
- Nicely decorated space
- Friendly wait staff

Cons:
- A lot of the plates aren't shareable
- Horrible acoustics, loud and hard to hear each other
- Some of the dishes were bland

I really wanted to like Estela - it sounded like a great place and a lot of the dishes on the menu were interesting. i went here on a Monday night with 5 friends and we were told by the waiter that for our group size we should order 7 or 8 of the medium plates and 3 entrees to share. We took his adivce and found a few standouts (burrata, calamari, mussels and beef tartare) and some dishes that were definite passes [spigarello (very bitter), quail (bland, no figs in sight and impossible to share), riccotta dumplings (nothing special) and egg with beans (how do you share a poached egg between 6 people?)]. I will mention that the portions are SMALL. After that many dishes we all agreed we would need to pick up a slice on the way home to actually feel full.

Overall, the food was pretty good but the few bland dishes, the unshareable plates (which is odd for a restaurant that is designed for people to share), the small portions and the horrible acoustics lead to my rating. This would be a terrible place for a first date because you would not really be able to hear  each other and, unless you know the person well, it is uncomfortable sharing some of these dishes since your used forks get everywhere in there and you need to use your hands.

Mad for the atmosphere and the amazing small plates. a resident of UES, don't always get downtown to try the newest hotspots but read about Estela in the all the press --  new yorker, etc. --  and decided to make the trek, and well worth it! i''l be BAAAACKKKKK!!!

It is dark and nicely decorated but people next table were way too loud......

Came here after long day at work, by myself. Around 9pm on a Thur, this place was packed. Snagged the last table in the corner. Lucky me! Promptly, I was handed a menu with wine list at the back. All small plates with four bigger plates options. Great! Ordered a glass of German reisling, grilled calamari and mussels a la pancha. Just sat and chilled. While i was sipping my wine, I could not help but drawing attention to the middle age female bankers sitting at the table next to me. They just talked way too loud. I was really annoyed. Literally, I was forced to listen to all their whining....Please, I don't need live Bloomberg TV while I am trying to relax. Quiet!. In between all those money talk, my food arrived. The mussels escabeche on toast were four cute little pieces creatures - juicy and tender mussels lied on top of a creamy sauce and crisp toast. Perfect snack to go with my reisling. The grilled calamari with caramelized onion and romesco. Oh the calamari was perfectly charred and not chewy at all. The romesco was blended in cashews and it serve sort of palate cleaner in between my bites of calamari. it was so good. 

All in all, I like my dinner here - service was decent, food was good and light, nice wine selection also. The only complaint is the noise level. I may think twice before I come here next time when I just want some peacefulness and relax with a glass of good wine.

The food was alright but definitely expensive for what you are given. My girlfriend and I had dinner here last night and we tried to share 4 dishes plus the pickles to start which actually aren't pickles they are "pickled" carrots and string beans. We asked the waiter what the pickles were like and he said he hadn't tried them recently so didn't know, some clarity on this would have been nice when we ordered. The waiters kept trying to clear our food before we were even finished with it and once actually did take away both of our plates while we were chewing and didn't realize in time they were taking everything off the table. 
Ok so on to the food, we ordered the beef tartare with sun choke which left a lot to be desired, it was very bland. We ordered the burrata thinking it would be a nice plump ball and instead it was all mashed up like ricotta cheese and was very sloppy. The oil soaked toasted baguette underneath it was gross and soggy. The quail with fig for $20 was only half the tiny quail and enormously overpriced. We each had 1 mouthful of this dish and the plate was done. The ricotta dumplings with mushrooms were our favorite but again you get like 5 small dumplings for $22 which is just a rip off. Their wine glasses are also very small so go for a bottle because their idea of a glass of wine is what you would consider to be a "half glass" at any normal restaurant. Probably why the wine by the glass prices aren't that bad.
I didn't have a particularly bad experience but it was just boring with not that great of an ambiance. I'd prefer to spend my money elsewhere.

If you can find this place you will enjoy the dining experience. On the 2nd floor of a nondescript apt. bldg in a seedy looking part of Houston this is 't the place to bring mom and dad. Small and a little cramped, the service is lacking but the food was terrific. The menu is divided into small plates and not-so-small plates with a few "larger" entrees so order several and enjoy. . The ricotta gnocchi were extremely light and flavorful and the salad was flavorful. The sea bass was moist and delicious while the lamb was also delicious. So for an out of the way dining experience definitely give it a try.

Walk up a small flight of stairs, open the door, and you are welcomed into a cozy restaurant in the middle of Nolita. 
This place is not huge, so reservations are recommended. The menu is small, but every dish is delicious. The dishes are listed according to size, those on top are the smallest, those at the bottom are the largest.

We started off with some burrata with salsa verde and charred bread. This was DELICIOUS. It was like burrata cooked in some kind of cheesey sauce on top of bread. We also tried the calamari a la plancha- I wish there was more calamari though. We had the cod with cabbage as well, the cod was delicious. 

I would have given it 4 stars but since the dishes were so small, I'm taking away one star. All the dishes are meant to be shared but its kinda hard to share when all you can get is... one bite of food.

I had been wanting to try Estela for a while and then after I read the review in the Times I decided that I must go! I couldn't get a reservation last minute of course so I decided to just go early and sit at the bar. I walked in on a Wednesday night at around 6 and I was the first person there, score! The restaurant is up a few stairs and you almost feel like you're walking into someones apartment building. Once inside the decor is very cool, my only complaint being that the bar stools are TRES uncomfortable! Not only are they too short for the height of the bar but there really is nowhere to rest your feet so they kinda just dangle there as your butt bones get sore from the hard wood on top. While I was waiting for my friend I ordered the Tompkins Square cocktail: Rye, kirschwasser, Maurin Quina, Benedictine, and allspice dram. This was the equivalent of a very bitter Manhattan, meh. By 7:30 the place was jammed and LOUD. We decided to order a few things off the menu and were really having a hard time deciding as everything sounded good. For wine we ordered the 2010 Fronton de Oro Tintilla from the Canary Islands and for $60, feel free to skip it. It was very light and did open up a bit but wasn't worth the price in my estimation. For food we ordered the kholrabi with hazelnuts, mint, and fossa cheese and if you only order one dish, make this be it. This was fabulous and all the flavors together were perfect. I had never heard of fossa cheese and it reminded me a bit of grated parmesan. Next up the burrata with salsa verde and charred bread. The burrata was creamy goodness but the salsa verde lacked much flavor. For our third and final dish we ordered the egg with gigante beans, cured tuna, and harissa. I could definitely smell the dish coming which was a bit off putting but once we dug in there was no reason for concern. The harissa was SPICY! This dish definitely had some kick which I love but was a bit too much for my friend. The amount of food we ordered was just right for us. I thought the place was great, a solid 4 stars and worth a drop-in.

I enjoyed my meal at Estela; while none of the flavor combinations were particularly new, the dishes I had were for the most part delicious. 

The beef tartare with crispy sunchoke was a solid dish; the sunchoke added great texture, and the beef was clearly very good quality.  I did find the dish to be a bit salty the more I ate it.  I especially enjoyed the burrata served on pieces of charred bread; the cheese was light and dressed in a great-tasting olive oil.  The mussels escabeche was less memorable; while the mussels were good, the accompanying sauce was highly seasoned, and it didn't help that the small pieces of bread soaked up much of the sauce.  The quail with concord grapes was also a good dish but finicky to eat.  I had never had grapes paired with quail, and the combination worked well.

The ricotta dumplings were served underneath thinly shaved white mushrooms and pecorino cheese.  This dish was rich but had good flavor nonetheless.  The steak was odd to me; on the outside, some pieces seemed overcooked but, inside, they were rare and very chewy.  The accompanying eggplant was very salty and difficult to eat, and I found the char on the leeks left an unpleasant bitter aftertaste.

For dessert, we had the concord grape sorbet, which was served with creme fraiche, dried blueberries, and a granola mixture.  It tasted like a delicious breakfast, and I enjoyed the textural contrast from the granola.  The sorbet, though, did have a very concentrated flavor that was a bit reminiscent of Welch's grape juice.  The honey panna cotta was, unfortunately, too sweet; while the honey was obviously very good quality, it overpowered the lightness of the panna cotta.

Service was friendly but a little bit awkward at times, particularly when the server started to switch out our utensils and plates while we were still finishing up a previous course.  The dining room is friendly and warm.

Was excited to try it. We grabbed two seats at the bar. The bartender and bar back were AWFUL. Whether waiting for a table or eating at the bar, the bar is often the first impression of a place.

The butch bar lady never smiled once, rolled here eyes when I finally requested a drink menu, after waiting in vain for an offer of one which never came. The bar back walked away while we were asking him a question...and these two morons giggled and talked about us, because we asked for less cane syrup in the "daisy" cocktail.

Apps were inventive and nice, but I won't detail, as the bar staff was so bad we thought we were on a prank TV show. They must be kidding and we will not be back, and I highly reccommend people do not try this place. 

This bar experience, coupled with all the reviews that mention the quick plate clearing...indicative of a place that is sloppily aggressive about turning tables, makes this place "all hype".

Despite all the restaurant choices in NYC, the culinary landscape can get boring at times, and new spots are still the most exciting remedy...but this place is a miss.

We were shocked at the treatment that we received from the maitre d', Quinn. First of all, upon our arrival 15 minutes prior to the reservation, there were four empty 2-tops. After waiting 30 minutes at the bar, the same tables were still open and we were told we had to wait for a table near the bar to be cleared. The table we were seated at was incredibly uncomfortable and very small.  

While sitting at the table, a group of very loud and obnoxious women stood right behind us making it nearly impossible to talk. My boyfriend stood up and kindly ask the maitre d' if we could move to one of the (still) open tables in the back. Quinn responded, "it's a crowded downtown restaurant, deal with it." We were shocked, not only was she incredibly rude, but for two people who eat at "downtown restaurants" 5 to 6 times a week, it was just plain dumb. 

The food, however, was good. But not good enough to deal with their horrible service.

Great vibe.  OK food.

Definitely order the beef tartare.  This was the standout dish of the night.  Skip the calamari.  Everything else is sort of, well, forgotten.  My husband had the steak, which the chef recommends medium rare.  It was not the best steak I've had.  I think I had the cod.  It was unremarkable. 

What was remarkable were the desserts.  The panna cotta was fantastic. 

Given I was here less than 1 week ago, the fact that I can't remember much beyond the tartare does not bode well for Estela.  Glad we checked it out, but def a once and done sort of place.

My new favorite tapas bar in my neighborhood. I highly recommend you to go. My favorite dishes are Raw Scallop with daikon radish & Beef tartare with sunckoke. Grilled squid is  wonderful too. Two dishes I don't recommend you to order ( Lamb chop & Chocolate mousse from dessert. )
Cute place, good vibe, tiny portions.  Food is very good but you will leave hungry unless you want to spend a fortune ordering everything on the menu.

The food was good here, a lot of different flavors you wouldn't think to mix together- my issue was there was not enough of it. There were two of us and we let her know we were pretty hungry, we ordered:  Whipped cod and matzo, Burrata with salsa verde and charred bread , Raw scallops, Beef tartare and sunchoke and the Ricotta dumplings.

The standout dishes for me were the beef tartare and the burrata. They took the dish with the burrata away when there was some left so that made us unhappy. Our dumplings came and there were literally like five of them. I mean really they knew we were sharing we couldn't get 6? So we ordered the chocolate dessert, also tiny but very good and some cheese. We left there slightly hungry and tipsy from the great Rosemary Society cocktails. 

Would I come here again? Maybe if I could get the beef tartare and the Rosemary Society at the bar. For dinner probably not unless I was really not hungry.
Creative dishes. Handsome decor.  Prices less than insane. They mailed me my credit card after I left it there. That's pretty groovy.

Everything was wonderful here, except for our waitress who was a little cold and not attentive at all.  But whatever, I'll leave that one alone for now - she might've been having a bad day.

Ambience:  perfectly lively place, fully packed, great for a date or small group.  

Food:  amazing.... mouthwatering... beautiful... fresh!  
-  Burrata - incredible.
-  Mussels escabeche - not the hugest fan, but my bf enjoyed very much.
-  Ricotta dumplings - delish!
-  Steak - AMAZING.  a must-order for sure.

Came in on a Friday without reservations but managed to get a table for 4. Server was a bit pushy when we only ordered 5 tapas and 2 mains telling us it wouldn't be enough even after we added to the order. Sure enough, it was plenty. Besides that the food was EXCELLENT!

Located above the street just in case you run into any problems locating it.

This place just did not do it for me. Some of the small plates were good, such as the egg salad and the razor clams, but other dishes were just terrible, such as the monkfish. (While I like me some fish that is just this side of dead, monkfish is not a fish designed to be served barely cooked, but this one was. It even had a smell to it as it came out.) The cheese course was OK, though not spectacular.

The food might qualify the place for three stars, but service was spotty at best. (We got attitude from the waitress several times, and when the cheese course came, it took several people to figure out which of the five cheeses was which. Incidentally, we had to flag someone down just to attempt to get that information.) It's loud in there, and the staff seems to think it's the customers' fault, too. (We were quiet, but they didn't make any effort to work with us on the communication front.)

It was OK.  Small plate (aka, large profit margin) place, meant to share, so it's recommended you order 3 per person, although there are a few entrees.  I got what they were trying to do, lots of mis-matched flavors, creative cookery, but I wasn't overwhelmed. It felt like I'd had it before.  I like yuzu, but not in everything. The steak tartare was more like a beef tataki. More yuzu flavor than beef. There was lots of beef, I just couldn't really taste the rawness of it. Lots of yuzu.   Good scene, bar was full.  I did enjoy the pot de crème very much.  Like I said, it was good, not blown-away or awesome.  Just good.
The ricotta dumplings are to die for.  And the salsa verde with burrata is a brilliant combo.

This was a spectacular experience. The chef is a young man from Paraguay who has worked in several renowned places including El Buli. The menu offers a variety of tapas, small plates, and a few entrees. It is however so much more than this! You get a wide variety of tastes very quickly and the tastes are rich and unexpectedly succulent, including the beef tartare which didn't hit you in the head with rawness but was tasty and succulent at the same time. The mussels on small bruschetta was ethereally delicious and even enticed the vegetarians to try them. The ricotta and honey ( with a touch of vinegar) was so perfect a taste that I must learn how to do it at home! You may have trouble finding the locale as the restaurant is above an Irish Bar ( owned by one of the Estela owners) but worth the search.

Love at first bite.
It's really not hard to capture exactly what it is Estela has to offer as really, it covers just about every base in my dining book with flying colors. 
Tucked above Houston Street's bustling sidewalk is this intimate, romantic but-not-too-much-so spot with a stellar central bar and wooden tables--both small and large-abound. The unfussy interior lets the food (and wine) shine in thier own right which is a refreshing balance not often found in the area. 

After heading to the *spectacular 6 top in the back (i hate that I just gave that secret away but it's pretty much perfect for anything from a girls dinner, birthday, meet-the-paretns type of deal, etc) it was immediately clear that pretty much anyone in the mood for a few near-perfect small plates and spot on glass and bottle offerings would be more than impressed.

Clean, bright flavor pairings and sleek, unfussy plating technique were the name of the game and, like the aforementioned relatively unadorned interior, let each and every component sing its own song, which in essence equates to a kickass party in your mouth, one bite after another.

Snack on: 
-The pickles (no, not the jarred kind), this was a perfectly acidic, flavorful small serving of pickled carrots atop a cooling craime fraiche.
-Salted cod and potato croquettes with a lick your plate clean borani sauce--these were light and airy unlike many I've tried before.

While you wait for the standout small plates of:
-Burrata--un-fricking believably good. For someone who never passes up on a plate of this ooey-gooey goodness, this plating, atop salsa verde and charred bread was divine.
-Beef tartare--Served alongside lightly toasted bread, this remained delicate and not at all gamey
-Both the endive and celery salads--I would honestly come back just for these guys. The former's richly nutty mix of walnuts, anchovy and ubriaco roso gave this dish enough heft to satiate yet not too much to keep us from wanting more. The latter salad was uber-refreshing and hit that perfect light meets louder components of celery, nuts, cheese...mmm
-Calamari a la plancha--always delicious and this time was no exception--perfectly charred without being rubbery and the greens gave it a nice hint of freshness.
-While the slightly heartier portion of spiced lamb rib, with cilantro and honey, were delicious, it was a bit greasy whereas the steak was absolutely melt in your mouth, perfectly cooked and was really a star come its taleggio and anchovy power-packed wallop.
-Finally, do not, i repeat DO NOT skip the ricotta dumplings. They are out of this world. Not gnocci, more like gnudi, these delightful balls from heaven absoltuely melted and were not nearly as rich as they sound on paper.

**Skip the sea-faring folks as our orders of raw scallops and cod were defintiely the misses of the night. The citrus element of the scallop dish was mildly unappealing and the cod was almost too salty to take...that being said, they were mere blips in an otherwise phenomenal, return-worthy meal.

Oh, and that pot au creme?....Nom nom. Drool. drool.

Bring a date, your mom, your sister, your green hat, even your buddies (there was a rousing bar scene goin on even at 11p on a Sunday) and get yourself to this gem. Now.

I hate trekking down to the LES and Nolita during really cold weather but Estela was totally worth it.  I loved the meal we had here.  I thought the dishes were really interesting and delicious and the ambiance was nice. The ricotta dumplings were so wonderfully rich and cheesy and had this amazing broth underneath.  Yum.  The mussels escabeche were also really delicious and inventive.  The dishes couldn't have been more dissimilar, but I loved the flavors in both.  We also had the burrata (not the creamiest burrata I have ever tasted, but damn good), the beef tartare (the crispy sunchokes were a nice flavor and textural touch).  We also ordered the Virginia ham (which was just as good as you would expect) and the lemon curd dessert with milk ice cream, green tea meringue and cake.  I know the dessert sounds odd, but it was fantastic.  All of the flavors and textures worked together beautifully.  The only dish I didn't love was the calamari a la plancha.  The flavor was ok but the calamari were overcooked and tough.

 Note that the restaurant is a little hard to find - you have to go in the front door of what appears to be an apartment building and the door to the restaurant is within the entryway to the building.  We were a little confused.

i'm a fan.  with its cramped quarters and seemingly limited staff, i thought the service was going to be horrendous, but it was surprisingly not!  the staff is warm and friendly, and helps one another out rather than say "let me get your server" (at least this was the case when i went).  get the STEAK.  it may sound boring, but it's delicious, and you won't want to share.  i was underwhelmed by the ricotta dumplings-- they were a little too mushy for my taste.  the cocktails weren't too sweet, which is usually an issue for me, so that was another star in my book.  FYI - the place is right next to/above Botanica Bar, in case you have trouble finding it.

Recipe for a perfect night at dinner for two before a show at the Public Theater:  Burrata, Ricotta Dumplings, and Steak.  Add a couple glasses of wine and you're good to go.  You won't be disappointed.  Great service too!

This place is awesome. Really cute decor (although very small and crowded) and excellent service. 

We loved basically everything we ate. Our favorite was the scallops, but we also enjoyed the burrata, the razor clams, the turnip, the calamari, and the beef ribeye (although for the price that was a bit of a small serving). 

The only small negative was that we waited almost 30 minutes for our reservation, but they threw in a comped dessert so we didn't really mind. And the dessert was awesome - the lemon curd was so tasty.

Was excited to come here a couple days ago but was unimpressed. We were disappointed right away when we had an 8PM reservation that wasn't honored until 8:30PM. The place is pretty small so there wasn't a place for us to wait either. It is what it is, only in NYC right? 

The food here was mediocre. Though there were items we liked, there were some items that stood out for how bad they were. First, a few highlights - We really enjoyed the mussels, ricotta dumplings, and desserts. These were great - flavor, presentation, etc. all on point. Unfortunately what stood out for us were the disappointments, namely the razor clams, which were not cleaned properly and came with a mouthful of sand, and the calamari that lacked flavor and wasn't any good.

The night ended on a positive note with 3 desserts that were all great. Ending on a high note probably saved this from a 2 star review.

The atmosphere is great; perfect for a first date or dinner with friends... just nice and cozy.  Drinks are WONDERFUL and the food is even better (Definitely a place for foodies).  have been here a couple of times and its always AMAZING :)

While some of the dishes were good, I was hoping for a little more wow factor based on the positive reviews they have received.  The ambiance and decor fits the neighborhood and I was expecting more of the young, hip, trendy crowd to fill the place.  But there was a surprisingly good mix of older guests among the hipsters.  

We were able to get a table for 2 but told they needed the table back at 9:30 which gave us 1-1/2 hours which was fine with us.  But our food came out very slowly between dishes.  Our last dish took a very long time and our waitress never checked on us.  One of our small plates was brought to the table next to us, because they told their waiter they didn't order it and we told their waiter that we ordered it.  Our waitress never came to say anything then either.

Some of the dishes were quite good, while others fell flat.  Just a couple of dishes that I remember having.  Egg salad and salt-cured tuna (mojama) on matzo was nothing special.  The tuna wasn't as flavorful as I was hoping it to be.  The beef ribeye was very good except it is very small for the price and a main dish.  This was the last dish that took the longest to come out, so we were disappointed that it was a small portion.

This was one of the best meals I've had in a long time, and that says a lot, as I think I eat some very good meals. The atmosphere is trendy, yet warm and cozy with dim lighting.  Perfect for date night or enjoying a meal with a friend. We lucked out with the one larger table in the back of the restaurant in a little nook, making it slightly separate from the rest of the noise of the restaurant. 

The concept is fresh, creative, farm to table style food done in tapas style. Our group of 5 ordered to share so that we could try a little of everything. Our order included bison tartare, burrata with salsa verde, mussels escabeche on toast, cured salmon on matzoh, scallop crudo, turnip and apple salad, ricotta dumplings, cod with blue foot mushrooms, and the pork with beets, butter beans, and onions. I can't say a negative thing about any of the dishes, but I will say that the mussels escabeche on toast is my idea of heaven. I could eat that dish every day of my life, it was that good. Burrata, dumplings, and biston tartare were also great. For me, the flavors in every dish were spot on and everything was delicious. I'm a big fan of broths, emulsions, sauces - anything that adds extra flavor, dimension, and depth to a dish - and Estela creatively executed this in every dish. Service was attentive. Great cocktail and wine list. Will be back, hopefully soon.

3 star rating for the quality of the food; 1 star for the service. 

Decided to take my friend here for her birthday after seeing that this one of the 4 nominated best new restaurants in NYC. The food was good overall, but the service was pretty awful. 

First, we walked in and the host looked up our reservation and decided to ponder for a while where to seat us when the restaurant was completely empty at around 6pm on a Monday. 

Next, our waiter was pretty useless in helping us choose how much to order and seemed like he wanted nothing to do with us. Later, he poured water that splashed all over my hand and didn't even bother to apologize. 

When it was time to leave, we walked by the staff upon exiting and they didn't even have the decency to say thanks for coming? Have a good night. See you next time. 

Guess it's only appropriate to say --

Have a nice night, see you never again. I'll go spend $150 on dinner for 2 at some other new "trendy" restaurant. Really unimpressed and annoyed that I didn't pick a better restaurant for my friend's birthday! Save your money and go elsewhere!

I was here this past weekend for a private event and I although the plates are very small, they were unusually accommodating to my party who had many dietary restrictions. One was vegan, one vegetarian one cant eat nuts.  They made something off menu for each one.  Pretty amazing right?

The atmosphere was warm cozy, not too dimly lit.  Decor was also very well appointed.  I love the idea of fresh, local ingredients in a world where restaurants are mostly chained to their bottom lines.  Keep in mind the place is small so this isn't a place where you can go and LINGER but if you want to have a bottle of wine and some great food - this is the place.

The stuff we liked: the burrata, beef and sunchoke tartare, and razor clams were very good. Lamb was a little over-seasoned but the meat itself was great. Quail with butter beans and quince was ok. No real Wow factor overall. 

Stuff we didn't like: Unless 2 of you are prepared to spend upwards of $250 for dinner (including wine) and not leave hungry, I'd recommend eating something before you go to Estela. The plates are fine, but small and pricey. But even one of the "large" dishes was in my book a tapas plate- 2 slices of pork shoulder for $28 might satisfy one of the neighborhood models, but c'mon. 

The place: sceney and a little loud. And even with a reservation, we were plopped into a tiny table in the bar area that would probably be used for walk-ins or cocktails only. Our server was friendly and helpful.

Last night was the second time we tried to stop in to eat dinner based on great reviews. There were waits both times, but last night we stuck it out, and were eventually placed at the table closest to kitchen, where there is a point of order screen for the servers, bascially on top of us. It was not a good table. Oh, well. We were a walk-in. 

The atmosphere was fair, at best. It just seemed very busy. Waiters are running around, the room is narrow, my elbows were hit countless times, and since it's not on the ground level, the floor would shake every time someone would walk by. Ok, enough with me being nit-picky. I will say that our waitress was very friendly, and effecient.  

Onto the food: Every dish we ordered seemed to be loaded up with salt and had a vinigery/acidic aftertaste. The lamb in particular was so over seasoned, I couldn't take it down without water. We couldn't even finish the Burrata with salsa, or the apple celery fossa. 

The only items we enjoyed were the scallops, and half-enjoyed the muscles. Again, the muscles were served with bread dipped in a havily acidic... something? 

The dishes were small, they are overpriced, and because we didn't finish two of our dishes, we left hungry. We were very dissapointed with this restaurant. Hopefully they start laying off the salt.

I came in last night with a group of 4 for an early 5:30 reservation. Immediately loved the atmosphere! Great bar space and plenty of heat. Awesome service. We were seated when the party had fully arrived and had no problem transferring our bar tab to the table. I've heard a lot of good things about their drink specials, but I'm a whiskey girl and stick with Bullet bourbon, neat. Yumm.

We were encouraged to order several plates, as most dishes are a small, tapas-like portion. Good call. We chose the oysters, burrata, beef tartare, ricotta dumplings (x2) and beef with potatoes. 
Everything was delicious (!!!) except for the oysters. Unfortunately they overwhelmingly tasted of rock salt- to the point that I found them unenjoyable, and I typically love oysters. That was the only dish that wasn't absolutely enjoyable though. My favorite was the tartare and dumplings. 

After dinner, we went back to the bar for night caps and dessert. I'm not much for sweets, so I ordered a coffee (French press only, nice!) and a neat bourbon, which I added to my coffee with the bartender's sincere approval. 

All around great service- friendly staff, quick orders, and a low punk mix playing in the background (I remember humming to the Misfits), which was rad. 4 stars because again, the oysters.. Just weird.. Anyways, to each their own!

Walked in here last night around 7 without a reservation and was seated immediately. (big plus!). The food was delicious and the ambiance was very casual, which was perfect for a Sunday night. 

We had the oysters, octopus, lamb ribs, burrata cheese, and ricotta dumplings. My favorites were the oysters and the burrata with the lamb as a close second. The oysters were very refreshing with just a hint of a citrus-y flavor and a nice pop from the roe. The burrata was creamy and salty, perfectly complimented by the salsa verde it was swimming in. The lamb ribs were nicely spiced with just a hint of sweetness from the honey. The octopus and dumplings weren't bad, but the other dishes were far better. I felt that the dumplings especially were a bit disappointing as they were lacking the flavor that the other dishes excelled in. 

Overall, I was very impressed and will definitely go back to try the rest of the menu!

It was OK - for the 'small' plates & the prices. It was just OK, I think overpriced too. I was seated at the end of a table of 4. there were 5 in our party & although we made reservations it was as if we were squeezed in while the rest of the restaurant was empty at 6pm. Sadly my chair was right beside the register so as it got busier, EVERY time a staff member needed to place an order, print out a check or indeed chatter with not much to do it was by my constantly kicked  / shoved or leaned on chair. Really annoying, this disrupted my dinner. Not a great experience.

It's not hard to see why Estela was one of the hottest openings of 2013. Not particularly restricted to any genre of cuisine or style of cooking, dining here really makes for one exciting and refreshing experience. 

The set-up of this rather obscure second floor restaurant is unabashedly downtown NYC - with a small bar in the front and tightly spaced wooden tables filling the rest of the narrow space. Service is attentive without being overbearing or stuffy in the least bit, really adding to the fun and casual vibe. 

The menu is short and very thoughtfully curated, with lighter items at the top moving down to slightly heartier dishes. Everything is meant to be shared, as small plates if you will, so it's probably best to come here with a party of 2-4. Having read and heard many high praises about Estela, the bf and I started with their highly acclaimed beef tartare with sunchoke and mussels escabeche on toast. We rounded out our savory order with the endive, walnuts, anchovy and ubriaco rosso, lamb ribs with charmoula and honey, and ricotta dumplings with mushroom and pecorino sardo. While every dish was tasty and well-executed in their own way, standouts for me were the mussels escabeche and beef tartare. The mussels were briny and plump, singing with a myriad of bright flavors and acidity that represented Spanish flavors in the most simple way. The tartare was everything it's hyped up to be, just straight up glorious with the different textures and a heavy hand of seasoning - completely unlike your average steakhouse tartare in every way. The lamb ribs were also perfectly cooked, fall off the bone tender livened up with the African charmoula seasoning. The endive "salad" added some much needed relief to the other protein heavy dishes and the rich ricotta dumplings, which just embodies umami. They're quite like the ricotta gnudi at Spotted Pig, perhaps even more ethereal as the thin skins burst open to creamy, almost burrata-like insides. 

We rounded out the savories with a finale of parsnip ice cream with caramel and a few glasses of different white wines. The parsnip ice cream was perfect in texture, and very pronounced vegetal flavor. Combined with the barely sweetened, ganache-like caramel - the dessert was very reminiscent of roasted parsnip in the best way possible. So simple, yet so mind-bending.

My boyfriend took me here for my birthday this past Saturday. The food was absolutely delicious! Wow! I honestly think this is my favourite resto in NYC right now. Located right in the Lower East Side. Very casual yet the best dining experience ever! Service is fantastic. Nothing bad to say.

I've been twice now and everything was beyond! Once for a casual dinner and drinks at the bar and the second time for brunch with a big group of us. Both times the food and service were excellent. The staff is so friendly and accommodating, props to Emma (I think that was her name) for my off the cuff request for a Michelada and she made it work and it was actually really good! My favorite dish and I think the group of us agrees is the Mussels escabeche. But you can't go wrong. Will definitely return!

As I work my way through the millions of places to eat in New York, the BF choose Estela, an up and coming restaurant that would appeal to our ever changing taste buds.  

You will walk by this place at least once without realizing.  Look for a black door with a one page menu and at the top you'll see the words Estela - yep - you found it.  Walk up a few stairs and into a cozy place on the right with dim lighting and happy patrons.  Tables are packed pretty close together and this seems to be a NY dining theme.  If the food is good I have no problem making polite conversation with my neighbors.  

Jennifer's way to dine: cocktails, appetizers, wine, more appetizers, more wine, entrees, more wine, dessert, and then after dinner drinks.  Don't ask questions, just do it!

We were feeling adventurous and truly wanted half the menu and we had to hold ourselves back a little.  Everything we had was truly divine.

The Scallop Crudu appears to be a signature dish at Estela and was a wonderful way to start out culinary adventure.  All the citrus flavors complimented the delicate scallops and thinly sliced radish.  

Salted Cod on matzo is not the preparation most will associate with Salted Cod.  Usually it's a croquette or a spread of some kind.  This was a Salted Cod mixture with shiitake piled on top of a matzo cracker.  We both savored each bite as we enjoyed the texture and overall taste of the Salted Cod.  

The BF had never tried Beef Tartare before and I had only tried it a few times previously.  We decided to indulge in our adventurous side and try the Beef Tartare with sunchoke.  This was the stand out of the evening by far.  The presentation was outstanding and as we took delicate bites of the perfectly cubed beef mixed with sunchoke I watched the BF's eyes light up as he realized how beautiful Tartare could be.  This is best preparation I've seen of Tartare in my travels thus far.  The sunchoke added a crunchy texture element to each bite and was similar in size to the beef so you could not tell the difference until the flavors exploded in your mouth.  It's a must have at Estela!

We had read some excellent reviews of the Burrata with Salsa Verde and could not pass up the opportunity to try it.  The portion size of Burrata was ginormous and could easily be shared among three or four if everyone was getting an entree as well.  The Burrata was smooth and creamy and mixed surprisingly well with the bright green Salsa Verde.  The charred bread was an excellent vessel for spreading the Burrata and Salsa Verde mixture.  I will admit to asking for second serving of bread to help with cleaning the bowl.

For our entree we shared the beef and were pleased with the medium rare preparation.  Our server steered us in the right direction with this choice and we were happy to devour every last morsel on the plate.  The accompaniments with the beef and not coming back to me at the moment, all I remember is blissful happiness.

At this point we were full and could not possibly indulge in dessert.  Even though dessert was not an option we did enjoy some coffee and port to finish out our evening.

Our service from hostess, to server, to bus boy was outstanding.  The atmosphere is romantic and dimly lit for intimate conversations.  I would gladly return to Estela to try their seasonal menu and have some Beef Tartare again!

Dined on 4/7/14.

So I work in the neighborhood for almost a decade and I know the block Estela is on very intimately, but even so we had to walk into Botanica Bar (right below Estela) to find this place.  Hint: gray door with number 47 on it (to the left of Botanica Bar, you are welcome for the free advertising ha), yes regular building door that other folks that live in the building use, and after a few steps and bearing right, you are where you want to be: in a very cozy, first floor restaurant that greets you with "I am impressed you guys are on time for your 530pm reservation", it made me chuckle, I wanted an early dinner and I got it, it also allows you to see how the restaurant operates as it's "waking up".  Lovely decor, excellent service, and many many workers, I felt like there must be a queen bee somewhere in the kitchen. It was endearing, the restaurant works like a well oiled machine even when around 630 it gets busy on a Monday night when its pouring, good sign, I say.

 So with that moving onto the food: (two people were quite full from the following, and I will agree while the plates are good size they are  slightly overpriced, that's being generous, but the old quality over quantity definitely applies here)

Beef tartare with sunchoke - While this was only my third beef tartare in life, as I only started eating raw meat and fish a few years back and generally stick to fish and ceviche and so on, I was like YES!  This could be my favorite dish, well of course until the next came, I wonder what I would choose if I had to, like in a competition, but this may be it folks!  The crunch in the dish, elevates to another level.   

Quail with broccoli di Cicco and lardo - This is wonderful, very simple and the broth is outstanding, the meat cooked to perfection and the greens, well they are marvelous!  Maybe I wished there was more of it as its only half a quail, get your own I say, don't share :).

Burrata with salsa verde and toast - This has quickly become a thing I order first, as  am well enamored with burratas, and this one doesn't disappoint by any means!  The perfect touch : the toast on the bottom.  definitely great item to share but in my humble opinion no more than by 3 folks.  But maybe I am just not willing to share.

Octopus with potatoes and pimentón - At first my buds created an illusion, I started tasting lobster, which isn't a bad thing at all in my world, as for the actual octopus - grilled to perfection and the fact it's sliced into small pieces makes it that much more enjoyable.  They hit it out of the ballpark with this one! So proud to use an American reference here.

Lamb ribs with charmoula and honey - this dish for me was a time machine that transported me back to my trip to China in November, where I tasted the best lamb I have probably ever had, why do I reference this?  Because THIS lamb reminded me of the best lamb I had 4 months ago or so in China.  Right amount of fat, perfectly cooked and seasoned, yes more please!

Mussels escabeche on toast - possibly, no undoubtedly my least favorite dish from the evening.. You weren't sure if to bite it all at once (my friend did and it was too much) and or try to separate in which case everything started falling apart, this not being the worst of it anyway, too much green, the muscles aren't fully cooked (and while you are told that prior to ordering) it's still not something I can get used to I guess.  I think this dish could be great as are the others, just needs some fine tuning. 

Panna cotta - very smooth and enjoyable, however I was so full at this point my friend had to finish it!

So the only question remains, whom do I coerce to come with me next?

Estela has been on my bucket list for months & was excited to finally check it out last night. I really wanted to like this restaurant more but I wasn't impressed like I had hoped to be. While (most of) the food was excellent like everyone raves about, I don't think I will be back.

I get it: the 'new kid on the block' trendy restaurant in the heart of Noho. But if I wanted to spend uber bucks $$ for small plates, I would have just gone to Colicchio & Sons. Two out of the 3 dishes we ordered were amazing; but not for the value you pay. The restaurant was vibrant w/ an eclectic bunch of people - almost all of whom looked foreign. 

The Burrata & the beef / sun choke tartar were phenomenal. After taking baby bites to savor the flavors & justify the $15/each plate, we were still hungry... Obviously. We were excited for our ricotta dumplings w/ mushrooms, but were highly unimpressed with this dish. Literally had 3 bites each before the plate was empty, & I could have thought of many other ways to spend $23. Should have ordered the lamb ribs. The dumplings were topped w/ thinly sliced mushrooms that had absolutely NO flavor.

I also wasn't particularly fond of our server, James. You know when you order your meal yet the server feels the need to 'up-sell' & push additional plates on you as 'suggestions'? Yup. I hate that too. He suggested we ordered 4-5 app's & 3-4 main courses! Um, really?! He wasn't too happy when we insisted on our original order. While he came to check on us often, it wasn't done w/ grace or tact & he appeared annoyed with us from the get-go when we didnt order wine. Drop the 'tude dude. We would have ordered a dessert but just wanted to leave at that point. 

Conclusion: checked Estela off my list. On to the next ...

The small small plates menu didn't look particularly exciting, so I didn't rush out to try Estela during the opening months of buzz. Finally though, I gave in to the hype and wanted to see what it was all about and ended up having a delicious, albeit very pricey meal here.

You might miss the little restaurant if you aren't looking carefully, as it's located up a short flight of stairs in what looks like an apartment building entrance, with a facade partially obstructed by construction scaffolding. Once inside though, the space looks much better. There is a long bar with a few tables up front, and a larger area with more tables in the back, though the whole place is pretty small.

Prohibited mostly by the desire not to spend a really silly amount of money on the meal, we actually ordered a reasonable amount and did not get the shocked look we often get from the server as we keep on listing more items:

- Cod and Potato Croquettes ($13 for 4)
This is a must to start with, as these little bites were some of the best of the whole meal. They reminded me of fancy, smaller, good-quality fish sticks, with flaky, buttery fish inside and a lightly fried skin.

- Burrata with Salsa Verde and Charred Bread ($15)
I don't usually like eating a massive blob of cheese, and never actually ordered burrata before, but I figured this would be a good opportunity to try it since it was supposed to be especially good here. I did enjoy it, and it went well with the charred bread beneath it. I still can't get behind eating the oily cheese on its own, but after asking for some additional bread, we finished the rest of it happily.

- Endive, Walnuts, Anchovy and Ubriaco Rosso ($14)
This was a cool-looking dish, with large endive leaves piled into a dome. Below it is all the good stuff, like the walnuts and anchovies and the really rich flavors. The crisp endive and the salty, oily anchovies and walnuts make for a delicious combo. This is a good choice if you want a salad or something with some green in it as it is much tastier than a typical salad.

- Lamb Ribs with Charmoula and Honey ($19 for 4)
This is one of the dishes being hailed as the thing to get here, but this was the one thing I found didn't live up to the hype. You get 4 pretty small ribs, which have quite a bit of fat on them. The quality bites of meat though were quite good, but there just weren't enough of them.

- Ricotta Dumplings with Mushrooms and Pecorino Sardo ($23)
This is the other dish I keep reading about here, and this time I can see why. Another beautiful looking plate, the delicious little dumplings are covered over completely by thin, circular slices of mushrooms. Once you pick through a few of them, you get to the really rich, buttery soft dumplings. This is definitely a good pick for one of the larger plates.

- Beef with Potatoes, Taleggio and Spinach ($34)
The last item on the item, and hence in the section of the largest plates, this was actually the smallest and the most underwhelming, and unfortunately at the highest price. There were two very small pieces of meat, which were very delicious, but way too small and fatty for that price. The taleggio and spinach added a ton of flavor too, and that part of the dish was great, but I think some of the other options might be more satisfying.

- Chocolate Pot de Creme with Coffee and Bourbon ($12)
We just went with one dessert for a change, and it was a great one. This was really rich and chocolatey, with some great crunch from the coffee and crumble layered below the smooth chocolate on top. This is a great way to finish the meal.

Best new restaurant of 2013? I don't think so, but the food certainly is tasty. There are several other new restaurants this year that I would much prefer returning to ahead of this one.

I waited for months trying to get a table- finally got a reservation. Food was excellent, favorite out of the 5 dishes (Burrata, Beef Tartar, Egg Salad, Quail and Ricotta Dumplings) was the Ricotta dumplings. The deserts were okay. Recommend for a party of four to enjoy small plates and good company. Will return with a bigger party.

I've been wanting to try this place for a bit and I definitely was not disappointed in my anticipation.  Met a few girl friends here for dinner and it was a perfect spot for this.  They have a variety of drinks (although we just stuck to wine and simple cocktails) and the small plates were perfect for a social dinner.  We ordered:
-Celery salad - it sounds very simple but it was delicious and refreshing. 
-BURRATA - it was so good that as soon as we tasted a bite, we ordered another one. Forget tomato and basil, salsa verde is how I want to eat all my burrata from now on!  
-Arroz negro with Octopus - good flavor and octopus was done very well
-Ricotta Dumplings - Perfect and the shavings of mushroom on top were unique.  It gave the dish an interesting texture and flavor.  
-Lamb Ribs - really good flavor but our ribs were fattier than I'm used to with lamb
-Cod - it was fine but the fish got lost in it's surrounding ingredients, especially since the fish was in smaller pieces. 
-Parsnip ice cream - Very unusual but we all liked it and it went well with the
-Lemon dessert - I can't remember exactly what was in this but it was very tasty and had the flavor of lemon without really being tart

Overall, I really enjoyed our experience here and will be back.

This place is great! You may miss it walking past. It is upstairs and the entrance looks like  you are walking into someone's house. I love how you can tell how trendy a place is by how minimal the signage is. In this case, non-existent. 

The mushroom and ricotta dumplings was the best thing I tried. I didn't expect that dish to be so delicious!

The two 'gentlemen' (said somewhat lightly because they were loud and obnoxious) ordered what looked like everything on the menu, and I was jealous of their expense account and their capacity for being able to eat so much that they could taste everything. I already know what I want to order the next time we go back, however. 

What we did order--EVERYTHING--was delicious. Inventive and perfect. 

We started with beef tartare with sunchoke. Why hasn't anyone thought to do this before? I've eaten raw beet dishes across the city--tartare and carpaccio--and this is the first place to ever mix the been with sunchokes, which give the beef a nuttiness that is just delicious. My wife almost always leaves the uncooked steer meat for me to enjoy by myself, but this time, we were competing for bites! 

We followed that with the burrata with salsa verde and charred bread. They must be making their own burrata daily and scooping it onto the plate fresh from the inhouse fromagerie, it's that fresh and delicate. Our last savory small plate was the ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo. Um. Get outta here. The little dumplings were like air, topped with paper thin slices of white mushrooms and shavings of pecorino. It's good that I love my wife so I would share, but it was not an easy thing to do. Our server said these were a favorite and I can understand why. 

For dessert we had something that you just can't imagine but once you taste it, you can't imagine never having it again: parsnip ice cream with salty caramel cream. Just trust me on this--really. 

The only slight disappointment was the list of wines by the glass; I"m sure the bottle list is top notch, but of the three glasses we had between us, we didn't really love any of them. Small--very small--complaint. 

Next time, I'm going for a couple dishes I saw our table neighbors' receive: the lamb ribs and the English peas with fresh horseradish. Lots of French diners there the night we were so I think that means something for this French inspired menu.

Went to Estela tonight. The food was outstanding! The place was crowded around 8 pm, so we were lucky to get a seat at the bar. 

We tried Lamb ribs with charmoula and honey, Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo, Endive, walnuts, anchovy, and ubriaco rosso salad, and Strawberry sorbet with candied rhubarb and green tea meringue for dessert. I absolutely loved every bite. The dumplings melted in the mouth, the lamb ribs were cooked just right, the salad was surprisingly good, and the dessert was fantastic.

I loved the vibe and the service was good. Definitely check out this place. You will enjoy the experience! It's worth every penny.

I never thought I would say this but...the best thing here is the endive salad. The mix of textures was so creative and absolutely delicious.

There were really no 'negatives' and perhaps I'm just not the wine connoisseur that other people are but I thought the wines by the glass were quite good and our waitress really knew her stuff about every single last one of them. 

The lamb ribs is what we ended with and they were probably the most disappointing - just super salty and not very interesting. 

Highly recommend saving room for dessert - they again shined by doing all sorts of interesting stuff with textures and generally crushing it.

Highly recommend checking this place out.

Food was alright. Hits and misses. Problem with this joint is that it doesn't come cheap, especially considering the portion size. I would recommend the oysters, which come with salmon roe over them, Arroz negro (squid ink-based rice with octopus) and Ricotta dumplings. The chocolate sorbet over sesame was fairly decent but I found the panna cotta quite unpalatable because of the amount of vinegar added to it. Would have been a lot better without that dash of acid, which doesn't seem to do anything for the panna cotta.

My wife, one of her closest friends, and I dined last week at Estela after hearing wonderful things from our friends and reading some spectacular reviews online.  Our dining experience had several aspects to it, all of it quite different from one another, so I'll attempt to break it down: 

1.) Food: the food as everyone has noted here, is absolutely fantastic.  We had the beef tartare, dumplings with a fantastic sauce (we were literally dipping any bread we could find in the sauce to extend the dish), the burrata (divine), the cod, and the beef with fava beans and asparagus.  All of the dishes were fantastic, and even the cod, which was my least favorite, was far superior to what you find at many restaurants. The prices are on the high side for such small plates, but because the food was so rich, I barely noticed that the portions were pretty small.  FIVE STARS FOR FOOD
2.) Drink: the wine selection here is not what I would have anticipated, and wasn't as robust as you would expect to see.  I think the bartenders know this, because they insisted that the ladies try the wine prior to pouring out full glasses.  I had a couple of negroni's, which I'd rank an 8 out of 10.  Prices are steep though at $14 for most cocktails.  FOUR STARS FOR DRINK
3.) Restaurant Ambiance: Here I think Estela is a victim of their own success.  Many many people were crowding the bar in hopes that they could get a seat at the bar to order dinner, without having a reservation.  The host as a result, was definitely very curt, bordering on rude.  We were sat at a table by the bar, which would have been fine, except people backsides were constantly bumping into us and our food.  Apparently, we didn't get one of the better tables, but this is still what they are offering up to their customers.   RESTAURANT AMBIANCE: THREE STARS

So when you sum it all up, we had a great experience and would go back, but make sure you have a reservation and insist on eating at a table towards the back.

I lived in NYC for over 12 years and am protective when people complain about how "New York" a place is in a negative way. But I have to say, this place is exactly that. The hostess, while beaten down by a horrific job, was completely unreasonable to deal with. Our reservation was changed in error and she could not have cared less or tried to help us at all. The food was great but did not stand out in anyway. There are at least 50 restaurants that do what they do, but the atmosphere at those places are much better with much better service. Not worth the crush of people at the door or the terrible service. Go elsewhere.

Heard great things about this place, and since it was also nominated for the james beard award as hot new restaurant I had to try it. Basically every dish was delicious.

Straight to the food..
Salami - very good, and comes with their bread
Oysters with trout roe - Very good! Tasted so fresh 
Beef tartare - I really liked this, a bit of saltiness and comes with bread again
Blood orange cake with an egg - Interesting sausage paste, pretty good too
Burrata - What is in this? The green sauce was so good and again comes with the same bread... a lot of bread here.
Ricotta dumplings - very small pieces but sure was tasty! Wish I had more!
Panna cotta - This was ok.. not much of a fan.

food was pretty good, but i think i was expecting more.  we got here for our 8 pm reservation but weren't seated until around 830.  we waited at the window sill by the bar and got drinks, and i finished mine before even getting seated.  i was pretty tipsy by the time we sat, b/c i had not eaten anything all day.

we ordered the salted cod croquettes, beef tartare, endive salad, scallops w/ kale and lardo, lamb riblets, ricotta dumplings, and the pork.  my faves of the night were the croquettes, beef tartared, and the pork, which had a nice ramp sauce and was topped w/ potato chips.

it sounds like we ordered a lot but 3 people had no problem finishing, so i think the portion sizes were on the small side.

this is a very sceney place and is a hard reservation to come by.  the place is tiny and cute, so of course it gets crowded, but you can always try your luck at the bar.

Shady rolled into New Yorks' most hyped place since, well, New Yorks' last most hyped place. After buying out the John Varvartos 2014 mewelery collection and drinking a few glasses of sparkling Rose' at nearby DBGB, Shady was ready for a food fest. And a fest it was. The highlights for Shady and his lucky guest were the Cod croquettes and the beef tartare. The Ricotta dumplings were very good, but a little too rich (something Shady never thought he'd say in ANY context) for Shady. The lamb ribs were great, the buratta as advertised and the beef delicious. For all those complaining about portion size, 6 dishes stuffed Shady and Co. Dessert was the parsnip ice cream which was just so-so. Service was terrific and bill for 2 with 6 dishes, dessert and 6 glasses of wine was $250 pre Shady's ALWAYS generous tip. A very good spot, in a cool locale, but suffers only from it's own hype.

I just happen to be in the neighborhood and heard great things about Estela so I  stopped in to see what it was all about. 
My friend and I sat at the bar of this charming little restaurant and had the Rosemary Society (Gin, pear brandy, lemon, grapefruit, rosemary) of which i adored.  Since we had plans for dinner elsewhere we just ordered a few appetizers and they were all so delicious.  
-Pickled Carrots on top of creme fraiche and ground fennel and coriander - refreshing!
- Kampachi with diced apples and yuzu - how can this be bad? very very tasty!
-Mussels with escabeche and toast - wow this was great, never had mussels quite like this before, they came out of the shell, moist and plump and the escabeche was fresh and bright, a great complement to the mussels!

This was a great preview of what they offer so i'll be excited to return for a full on dinner.

Great dinner at the bar here last night. 

Salami - very good -- and what a great idea to serve salami in a dish of EVOO! 
Celery Salad -- excellent (even though I have had dry-farmed celery that's even better)
Arroz Negro -- OUTSTANDING
Lamb short ribs - very good
Ricotta dumplings - excellent
Panna cotta - loved the tangy vinegar & honey combo. 

I was very excited to see two wines from Corsica on the wine list, but I have to say neither really wowed me. I love lighter reds, but the Frais Imperial was too light for my taste. I liked the Ribeira Sacra a bit more, but was really wanting something a little meatier. 

Reviver #47 cocktail -- OUTSTANDING

Great service, interesting crowd. Thanks Estela!

So the food is outstanding.  I mean the Arroz negro is unbelievable - it's like the best miniature paella ever.  And the scallops are amazing.  And generally everything else is amazing.  The ricotta dumplings are a little much especially with the shaved mushrooms that are too heavy and uncooked.  

But the service is ridiculously slow.  We waited a half hour past our res time to be seated and then between courses it was 20 minutes.  But the servers were super nice so I can deal.

Unlikely to return though.  Enough places in the area with better service to go through that again.

Came back to Estela last night for our anniversary and it was every bit as amazing as our first visit.

Cocktails: Richard XII and Rosemary Culture. Both fantastic.

Small plates: Burrata with salsa verde and the lamb rib with chermoula and honey. Loved these dishes so much from our last visit that couldn't pass up ordering them again. Spot on.

Larger plates: Ricotta dumplings and cod.  Also got these dishes last time, but chef is preparing them differently than from our winter visit (more spring flavors now). Both amazing.

Dessert: Strawberry sorbet with rhubarb and green tea meringue. Delish. 

Yeah, we'll be back again.

Before heading Estela last Friday, my friends and I checked out all of the reviews on Yelp to help us order when we got there.   While I completely appreciate all of these detailed reviews, I think I can simplify the description of the Estella experience quite a bit:

1)  unless, you are lucky, it's very probable that you will need to wait a while to be seated and to receive your food.  I'd imagine this is because guests are enjoying their food so much that they don't want to leave, but I also have a theory that the restaurant wants you to be incredibly hungry so that the food just tastes that much better when it is finally placed in front of you

2) the drinks (including wine) are pretty good, but not stellar and probably a touch overpriced

3) You cannot go wrong ordering here!  The food ranges from out of this world spectacular to exceptionally good.   As a group we tasted a lot of the menu, and everyone was raving about every single bite.   Tables may take longer to turn because people cannot stop talking about how good the food tastes.  Honestly, to have food this good you usually need to be in a three star michelin restaurant.  

So despite 1 and 2 above, I will be going back and back and back.

I was a HUGE fan of ISA so I was super hyped when this place opened.  If anything it's even better than ISA.  The small plates are probably the closest in quality to eating in Barcelona that I've found in NYC.  The steak tartare is amazing!  The burrata sounds so simple but I could never make it at home.  The big plates are just superb - love that pork.  Also very nice well priced wine list with a lot of interesting bottles - we had this beautiful red from one of the volcanic Canary Islands - even people who don't love red wine were fighting over the last drops.

Pickled Carrots
Endive
Fluke
Nectarines
Arroz Negro
Lamb Ribs
Ricotta Dumplings
Strawberry Sorbet

Went here for lunch on a friend's recommendation - it was delicious. I would definitely return. We had the burrata, lamb chops, mussels and a couple others and they were all very interesting favours, different from the usual. Good place to catch up with friends.

The lunch plates are small and are much like tapas (eg. Lamb comes with 3 small chops). I would order 2 plates per person and share. Looks like you can so walk in during lunch (less busy) and perhaps may want to make a reservation for dinner.

The service was efficient and friendly, and they gave us plenty of time to enjoy our meal.

really, really good and original/special food clearly made with thought and love.  everything that went into my mouth was delicious.  truly.  i thought the wait staff was super helpful and experienced and knowledgable and loves the restaurant as much as the owners probably do.  the drinks were yummy and the ambiance was funky in a lower east side hipster kind of way.  i don't love sharing and so next time i hope to go back by myself!!!

This restaurant is about a 4.5 star rating. Service was top notch but unfortunately the portion sizes were a different story =(

So let's break down the food, shall we?
- The steak tartare was juicy, perfectly seasoned & chopped finely so the savory flavors could be tasted in every bite.
- The burrata was so creamy & worked in harmony with the tartness of the salsa verde.
- Ricotta dumplings? Soft little creamy balls bursting with flavor in every bite!
- Now the beef is the must try dish! Two pieces of beef seared medium rare to reveal a little bit of pinkness. And every damn bite was soooo good. You can taste the balance of  meat & fat with each mouthful. And the eggplant & leeks? Grilled lightly outside yet melt in your mouth delicious!
- Interesting take on the panna cotta. A tad creamier than most I've had. The vinegar adds a nice touch with the honey.
- Last but not least, the chocolate cake was moist & not too cakey. A tad of a gooey center. Delish! And I must say, a great with the addition of the homemade whipped cream. Yums!

A tad cramped in terms of dining space. Make friends with your neighbors!

A casual place with a great open window near the bar. It came recommended by a chef friend as one of the chefs' places to eat. Outside I saw this stuff teddy bear that was hanging off the traffic light post -  it was cute! Bet the restaurant did not realize this entertaining feature. The food was served tapas style, generally I noticed the generous use of raw fresh herbs and its juice. I haven't had food made with such fresh raw ingredients yet.

The mussel escabeche was fantastic with the tomatoes and fresh herbs, I am talking herbs covering the entire plate that you can't see what was underneath it. The endive made simply with nuts, orange juice and olive oil was so refreshing! The burratta with the raw vegetable juice and herbs were bursting with flavors! The lamb ribs rubbed with a good amount of spice and grilled, the charred outside and moist inside as perfect! The blood cake with a sunny side up egg it was rich and tasty eaten together. The servers were great too - Thanks!

It was quite an unexpected experience. A tiny bit of the hipster element but I would definitely visit again!
Parsnip Ice Cream with Chocolate Caramel. TO DIE FOR! peace.

Got a reservation at 8 pm on a Monday night and boy was it packed! We weren't seated until 8.45, but we were compensated with a free bottle of wine and complimentary appetizer. The food was some of the best I've EVER had. My favorite items were the scallops and ricotta dumplings. Since it's delightful tapas, go in a group and order everything! I highly recommend Estela. My only complaint is the the noise level is high for my taste.
