This is a very fine restaurant, with tapas style (small) plates, and an emphasis on fresh vegetables and herbs, with lots of vegetal extraction and maximum flavors, with all sorts of herbal subtleties.The restaurant is very appealing. It's a bit hard to see, wedged in a narrow space up one flight of stairs. The bar is right off the entrance and it's usually packed so you have to wade through. We have not had any poor dishes here, and the scallops, cod, and ricotta and pork dumplings with potato chips, of all things, were exceptional. Desserts not as compelling, but the pot de creme and some of the sherbets are extremely refreshing. People come here for wine, and the list is very well thought out along the new world whites and reds, with considerable coverage of Jura and Loire. We usually run into wine and restaurant people here, and the list of wine is reasonable to pricey, so is a bit more than casual and not so hipsterish in terms of the people. A slightly older crowd. The service knows their wines and food well. The window in the front is a lovely place to sit. The only downside to all this is that the restaurant is always crowded, till around 9:30 or so, and you have to wait for a bar seat at almost all times after 6pm. They has a mavin du Jura pinot on the dessert list that was luscious, a finger lakes Edelzwicker, a very fresh Puzelat rose, and a lovely Tricot Gamay.

I think Mattos was in the Hamptons this beautiful Saturday night. I had to re read the reviews to confirm I was in the right restaurant. The burrata lacked flavor, the tartar was good, the croquettes brought back childhood nightmares of Gordon's fish sticks, and the scallops were ordinary
and not what I expected . The fried arroz negro was flavorful with great texture, enough to leave you wanting more and the ricotta dumplings melted in your mouth. 
The razor clams and the squid were not on the menu.

This place is pretty great.  I came here a couple times and sat at the bar.  Some of the ingredients they use are at once simple, and utterly transformed to the point where you don't know what they did - but delicious food.  Lamb ribs, ricotta dumplings, burrata, everything is good.      

Nice people work there.  Don't forget your wallet, it's expensive.

I've heard about this place from some foodie friends that I really trust. It was delicious! The mussel dish especially and the burrata were amazing. Very creative food that is truly different than you're standard fancy restaurant. We also had the ricotta dumpling (which were good but I found a bit too salty) and the Lamb ribs (which were very good and tasted a lot like pastrami). I think they really shine in the small dish department more than the larger plates. The dessert, chocolate cake, was phenomenal and our waitress was so sweet and great. I really liked this place and if I can afford it, I'd love to go back.

Spiced almonds: a simple thing that fails more often than at flies. Estrela's are great, and emblematic of the rest of their menu, where the simplest things shine. Salted cod croquettes: often heavy or doughy, here fluffy and fresh, like the platonically ideal offspring of a tater tot and a fish stick. The salsa verde with the burrata is the essence of fresh. (Sorrel? Purslane?) The more complicated things (ricotta dumplings, hangar steak with eggplant) are good, but not really exceptional.

Good wine list and cocktails, with some unusual choices. Tried the finger lakes edelzwicker purely based on novelty, and turned out to be excellent. 

Service is attentive, probably in part because they want to turn your table as quickly as possible, but at least not overtly. (The table next to us apparently lingered 45 minutes longer than expected, given the rather vocal complaints of the next group seated, 45 minutes after their reservation.)

Downside? Crowded, and loud. But, that's the price of being justifiably popular...

I left Estela tonight like a giddy girl, thrilled by dinner and so excited that my family had thoroughly enjoyed a restaurant of my choosing. 

They typically recommend eating family style with 2 plates per person.  As you get further down the menu the plates get larger - there were about 4 courses at the end that were "mains" and even those weren't huge.  At a total of 9 plates + desert we all left full (not stuffed) and completely satisfied! At that rate, it was easier for us to simply choose 4 plates and 2 mains that we DID not want - so we got lucky because we pretty much got to try everything we wanted on the menu and excluded the few dishes we were less interested in trying.

The obvious sign of an amazing restaurant: everyone "ooh and ahhing" after sampling the new dishes that have just arriving and with huge smiles on their faces. 

MY TOP PICKS:
1. beef tartare with sunchoke - the sunchoke chips were a nice touch and really was such a fun texture along with the beef.
2. fried arroz negro w/squid and romesco - WOW, just really unique and so tasty! we all couldn't stop raving about this
3. pork with cucumber, leeks, and borani - sometimes its hard to expect a pork dish to really blow you out of the water, but this did. perfectly tender and flavors to die for.

LEAST FAVORITE, BUT STILL GOOD:
1. lamb ribs - very very tender, but still tasted gamey to me.  my mother disagreed and felt it was perfect and not gamey at all.
2. ricotta dumplings - maybe it's the asian part of me that expects/enjoys something delicious (a treat!) in the center of my dumplings, but although it melted in your mouth it felt like something was missing. personal preference re: dumplings, but this was still done well.. one was enough for me.

Easy to see why Estela was rated the #3 top new restaurant of the year by bon appetite!

The food is really good, eclectic enough and not strange. I 've been there twice and the menu was pretty the same. But that's why I came here, for the Octopus, and beef tartar and the potatoe. This place is adorable.

I cannot say enough good things about the ricotta dumplings and the beef tartare! 

Beef tartare: The crispiness mixed in with the tartare was delightful! My only complaint is that the thick, untoasted bread seemed to clash. 

Ricotta Dumplings: WOW WOW WOW! Probably the most beautifully presented version of this dish I've ever had and surperb tasting! Loved the thin cut mushrooms on top designed to look like shaved truffles. 

HIGHLY RECOMMEND THESE DISHES and I look forward to trying more of the great looking menu!
Outstanding food, wine and service.  Great vibe and atmosphere.  Simply one of the best new restaurants I'v discovered.

If the critics and social media pundits are to be believed, the most nondescript looking dish on the menu, the fried arroz negro with squid and romesco ($23) happens to be one of the buzziest.  It arrives to your table as a completely unadorned circle of black rice, flecked here and there with spots of white squid.  You may wonder if the kitchen has accidentally left off a decorative element - perhaps an artful streak of sauce from a squeeze bottle, a compressed root veg, a sprig of something trendy (sea beans? ramps? purslane? something... anything?) - but I assure you they haven't.  

There's nothing that I can think of that could improve on this austere dish of perfectly seasoned rice and precisely cooked squid.  It gets the subtle notes right - a bit of garlic, the barest whiff of acid for balance, the intermittent crunch of crispy rice.

By most accounts, the experience at Estela is what we've all come to expect from the typical trendy Village/Nolita eatery - moody lighting and dark wood, trendy looking patrons crammed shoulder to shoulder in a shoebox of a dining room, and impossible to get reservations.  But as much as one tries to type cast this restaurant, one can get a glimpse of raw talent in the food and the wine program.

Behind the bar, Thomas Carter, formerly of beverage director at Blue Hill at Stone Barns has put together an excellent cocktail program and an even better list of interesting and non-conventional bottles of wine.  And in the kitchen, Ignacio Mattos (of Isa and Il Buco) is cooking crazy delicious food that arrives with almost no fanfare or flare.

Like the aforementioned arroz negro, salt cod and potato croquettes (4 for $12) is served with only a swipe of aioli and a wedge of lemon on a slightly too small plate.  Such austerity might signal a lack of attention to detail - instead its a sign of Mr. Mattos's confidence.  The croquettes were easily the most perfectly executed I've ever tasted - creamy and tender on the inside and shatteringly crisp on the exterior.  

There was nary a miss on the menu - I don't recall ever tasting burrata ($16) that was fresher or milkier than the burrata at Estela.  Here, it's piled on a piece of toast and soaked in salsa verde and again served in a bowl that's a little too small for its own good.  

Cloud-like ricotta dumplings ($24) are served in an arresting mushroom broth that taste like the best cream of mushroom soup you could ever hope for.  And there was hanger steak cooked to the requested medium rare with pickled beans and creamy new potatoes ($34) that would put any steakhouse to shame.

If we've come to expect flashiness and pomp from our city's best restaurants, its a thing of beauty to find a restaurant that has the cojones to serve modestly plated food in an unremarkable dining room.  Especially when that food tastes as good as it does at Estela.

Good food- BUT OVERPOWERED BY PRETENSION!!
Going into what you think is a low-rent tenement-- swing open a heavy door that at first seemed locked-- you enter a noisy and dispassionate room. You can barely hear the hostess take you to a table where you can't hear your friend's or yourself speak. Then a waitress comes over - smiling but also unable to be heard over the din. She describes a menu that is NOT organized by starters or entrees but by 'richness' of the food-- and only leaving the last four items as an entree size. so sharing is a must. The staff that bring out the food -- do so and don't even explain what they plopped down on the table. After all this -- we  must say that the food is very tasty. But the service, ambience and attitude is not something anyone needs to experience! And lastly the dessert was the best part!

I have come to this place twice now and it was OK both times. The food has good flavor but isn't very exciting. The service is always lacking personality and charm. The decor is cozy, warm and relaxed but all in all I would say it's a fine neighborhood spot but quite pricey for the overall experience. Both times I wasn't super impressed nor was I super inclined to come back. Just ok!

We showed up with no reservation, but the charming hostess was kind enough to make a table work for us (another server also went out of her way to make us feel comfortable during that process -- it was appreciated). We had a beautiful meal. James, our server, was perfect. He comfortably made recommendations when asked for them, projecting poised expertise in a completely unpretentious way. He made us feel right at home. The food was excellent, boasting huge flavors. The desserts were truly exceptional; especially the sorbet. And the burrata may be the best I've had. We will certainly return.

One of the best restaurants I've eaten at in a long time and definitely a highlight of my trip to New York.

There were three of us and we ordered many menu items and split them - everything was fantastic.  EVERYTHING.

It is super expensive though, so definitely should be reserved for a special occasion (we went for my birthday) or if you're looking to impress someone like a perspective significant other.

Either way.  If you're in New York and you love good food, this place should be at the top of your list.

I really want to write a good review for this place but I found it average.
Good ambiance for dates.
Beef tartar was very good. Burrata was good.
The arroz negro was average. Ricotta dumplings was oversold.

After reading about Estela in Food & Wine, I was excited about my reservation and prepared to leave five stars going in. However, upon entry I knew there would be Problems. 

The place was so damn tiny that when they seated me and my boyfriend it was squished between two other couples at very small tables. There were audible groans from our neighbors on either side as they removed excess plates and drinks from the table we were being seated at. 

Our waiter was not very friendly but it may not have been her fault because she didn't seem to have enough space to even stand near our table and tell us about the menu. About 20 minutes later when we saw her again we made sure to order the wine and food right away. 

Not intending to eavesdrop - but due to proximity, I heard that one of the tables next to us was waiting for some of their dishes for over 45 minutes. They happened to have messed up our order as well by giving us additional food. But it was so dark and loud by the time we realized it wasn't our food that we didn't know who to give it back to!

Food-wise this place was annoyingly perfect. Everything was beyond expertly prepared. 
We got the following:
Fluke with kohlrabi and avocado
Burrata with salsa verde and charred bread
Fried arroz negro with squid and romesco (our surprise dish)
Lamb ribs with charmoula and honey
Quail with grapes, parsley, and ajo blanco

It was all seasoned exquisitely and the meat was cooked excellently. I was angrily eating my delicious food as I vowed to never return. 
If you dare, I suggest going with a larger group. STRENGTH IN NUMBERS

Liked very much, didn't love.

On a weird stretch of East Houston, across from a CVS, and up some stairs.

We came on a Sunday night and the vibe was mostly tourists, but it's the HOTTEST place in the city right now.  
We had a nice bartender with some nice wines to choose from and a very decent martini.

It's not a place to linger, or hang out, make sure you have other plans after dinner.
The food comes out FAST and they turn those tables.

We had some delicious bites.
GREAT cod croquettes.......delicious cherry tomatoes w/ figs and dried shrimp (from Louisiana)........and my favorite, an amazing endive salad w/ pecorino and anchovies.
The only disappointment was the squid ink risotto with romesco, which was non existent and squid.

Dinner was done in an hour. 
 We enjoyed it, but wouldn't drive back into the city from NJ for another visit, though if you are in town, do try it, the food was good.

My husband took me here for my last birthday. It was a tour of some of the best restaurants but this was my absolute favorite of the mix (yet interestingly enough, receives the most less-favorable reviews). 

I love the location. Perhaps because for many years, the area was my old stomping ground. So, sentimental attachment might be applicable here. But it's still downtown (number one criteria for a restaurant), near Houston, which is the epicenter of all things below 14th Street. 

The ambiance is sweet, romantic--a perfect NYC backdrop. Tables are close to one another, so depending on your likes and dislikes, you are likely to hear your neighbor's conversation. The flow of wine here is great, with an awesome wine selection. Too bad we had so much bubbly beforehand. We ended up with a few recommendations from our server to taste, but after eating some appetizers, settled on a bottle of Luis A. Rodriguez Vazquez 'A Teixa,' Ribeiro (we were on our way to Spain--by the way, this is a great Spanish white). 

Now for the food. We are big into sharing lots of dishes to taste. Tapas is definitely our thing. 

We started with olives. They were the best olives I've ever had. Several days later, were all over France and Spain and the olives at Estela were the benchmark for olive standard. When my husband left for the restroom, I inhaled each marble-sized ounce of pure heaven. The guy next to me said, "you face resembles that of someone who is eating the best steak of their life." I retorted with, "steak doesn't do justice to these olives." 

I don't even like salted cod. But we ordered it. It converted me for that moment. Not sure it's the first thing I'd order, but if I were a fan of salted cod in general, I think it could be an amazing dish. 

We had mussels. They were some of the best I've had. I'm a sucker for these things, and I left thinking they were pretty amazing. 

We had scallops, lamb, a crunch endive salad and another round of olives. 

I loved every ounce of our dinner at Estela.

Estela has been in the spotlight of late, thanks to an impromptu visit by the epicurious President and First Lady this past month, but I am, perhaps, a little proud of the fact that I chose this venue for brunch prior to that fiasco. The restaurant had not escaped my mental bookmarks, thanks to the presence of Chef Ignacio Mattos, a chef from Il Buco and Isa (the latter of which earned him a James Beard Award nomination), and Thomas Carter, the former beverage director at Blue Hill at Stone Barns. Reservations were easy to make on Rezbook, and we arrived in front of the walk-up entrance to Estela on a Saturday afternoon.

Surprisingly, only one other party was present in the restaurant at the time; I couldn't help but peek at the group several times before whispering to my friend, "Isn't that Danny Bowien? From Mission Chinese and Mission Cantina?" [1]. After the initial excitement passed, we turned our attention to the menus, which offer a concise array of beverages as well as a handful of small plates, meant to be shared. There's no easy way to describe the types of dishes printed, as there's hints of Spanish, Mediterranean, and even Italian influences across the board. Some may find frustrating the fact that only the primary ingredients are listed for each dish, a set up that made choosing a little more difficult. After I'd decided on a glass of rosé, we agreed on a trio of plates for our meal.

First was an interesting take on the traditional "bagel and lox", featuring slices of smoked salmon, shaved horseradish, and capers with a spread of crème fraîche. The capers and horseradish were in just in the right amount, and without overtaking the savoriness of the smoked salmon. The crème fraîche was the perfect contrast in coolness to the crunchy bread, which made for a balanced bite. Just as delicious was the Blood Cake, blood sausage topped with a fried egg and served a top toast. There are some who might shy away from the protein, but it was surprisingly tasty, with only a hint of minerality to it. The onion marmalade made for a smartly sweet addition, and with an oozing egg yolk, we were grateful for the substantial toast beneath to support all the ingredients.

The final bite was the Fried Arroz Negro, or fried squid-ink rice. The rice was well-seasoned and at a chewy-yet-soft texture, complemented well by the squid interspersed throughout. The very center of the plate had surprise of romesco sauce and toasted hazelnuts, a spicy, nutty contrast to the arroz. It did, without surprise, disappear all too quickly, a testament to the deliciousness in the small plate.

There's a certain allure to a meal consisting of shared plates. Perhaps it's the prospect of being able to try a greater variety of dishes and flavors at once, without sacrificing stomach capacity. It may also lie in the fact that sharing food requires a certain level of friendship with your dining companion(s); it forces conversation and occasional abruptness, yet creates an environment that is without borders on possession or time. A meal at Estela can transport you, shedding away the fatigue and bustle of a clamorous city, and force you to focus on the food and people in front of you. And that, in retrospect, is what any good restaurant should aim to do.

--
[1] He helped me confirm this by asking the waiter after they'd left. Yes, chefs and restaurateurs are the only celebrities in my mind.

Only went for brunch but I will be back to check out dinner for sure.

I'm not a huge fan of brunch. I'd rather make eggs and pancakes myself at home. But brunch here was definitely worth eating out, and I'd choose this place over any popular brunch spot any day.

The space is very nice- love the decor and ambiance and it's a nice size. I was always reluctant to go to Estela because the menu is pretty small. So having brunch there was a great introduction to the restaurant. Had the mussels escabeche (very nice with a perfect amount of acidity), the eggs, beans and cured tuna (better than most egg dishes I've had for brunch in this city) and the squid ink rice (a looooot of umami). 

Service was nothing exceptional but we had a good experience and nothing to complain about. After 2 drinks each and these 3 dishes the bill was a little over $100.

Estela has been quite popular lately between the President and the First lady stopping in for dinner along with them being named the #3 best new restaurant by Food & Wine. This was a definite stop for our most recent trip to NYC. I have to say that the food overall was really good but there was a misstep or 2 along the way that made me drop to 4 stars from 5. We also had dinner at Contra the following night and I felt that Contra was better so I feel like it wouldn't do Contra justice to rate Estela the same. To start off with, the space, its nice but tight and extremely dimly lit, this makes trying to take food pics almost impossible without some white balance from another phone, if you are into that sort of thing. Be prepared to get really really close with your neighbors, that's just the way the place is set up. There were 4 of us that went and I feel like this is probably the ideal number, you could do 5 but anymore than 5 or 6 and you will just be getting multiples of dishes on the menu. 
For those not familiar the menu is set up as small plates for everything. This is perfect in my opinion because as long as you have 3 or 4 people you can try a lot of different things on the menu and branch out. We ended up ordering 10-12 things and I have to say that the only thing that I feel did not workout well were the ricotta dumplings. They come in a broth with very thinly shaved mushrooms on top. I just felt like the dumplings didn't have a whole lot of taste to them, maybe it was just me, maybe I burned my palette out on an earlier dish I don't know but that was my opinion. 
The steak tartare was very good but not the best I have had. The salted cod and ham croquettes were awesome, these I would say were fantastic and I wish we had more. The burrata with salsa verde and charred bread was really good, the fried arroz negro with squid and romesco was stunning and quite good as well. We also ordered the quail with grapes, parsley, and ajo blanco and while the quail was pretty awesome I actually found myself liking the greens more. I have to say that my absolute favorite dish that we ordered was the lamb ribs with charmoula and honey, I am a sucker for stuff like this I really like an intense lamb flavor and that's what you get with these. The mussels were also very good and came in a salsa verde broth that was just stunning. Overall Estela is great and definitely worth stopping by and I hope to return in the future when they change up the menu a bit.

I ate at Estela last night after reading about it being voted the Best New Restaurant in Food and Wine.  I was sadly disappointed.  I knew things were headed south after tasting every one of the white wines offered by the glass and finding none of them drinkable.  Strange, as I've never had problems finding a glass of wine I could drink.  Their list is obscure grapes from unknown producers which is fine in theory but they were not good.  On to the food - the olives and salami were drenched in oil as were the lamb short ribs.  The scallops were so salty as to be in edible and I like my food salty.  The steak was served at a perfect temperature but the accompanying potato chips were hard to determine if they were potato or yucca.  All in all would say go elsewhere.

I'm rating this restaurant two stars because we technically did receive food.  That being said, this evening was a total disaster. 

We were in New York for the New York Wine Spectator Wine Experience. We made reservations well in advance for Estela, due to its reputation. Being caught in some traffic on the way, we were 11 minutes late for our reservation for a party of four. Upon arriving, we were told that they had given our table away. The hostess asked us to sit at the bar while they tried to find us a table.  After ten minutes, they told us no additional tables would be available for the evening,  so we decided to eat at the bar.  This isn't the worst part of the evening. 

The service at the bar as lukewarm at best.  It seemed as though the bartender felt as though she was doing us a favor by gracing us with her presence. She returned infrequently to check on us throughout our meal.

Disclaimer: this next statement is not tempered by our lack of a table, and we would have felt this was if we had actually been seated.  The food here is average at best. The previous evening, we had eaten at another we'll known restaurant in this neighborhood which also required reservations weeks in advance. The could not have been more of a night and day difference in every aspect of the evening.  The service was exceptional, the food was world class and they actually seemed to care more about the customer, rather than simply turning a high volume of tables for the evening.

On a side note, due to our proximity to the bar, we were able to overhear the hostess turning away other people who had reservations but were a little late.   Keep this mind when considering Estela.

I read about this place in food and wine magazine and my husband made reservations for my family to eat here on my birthday. We arrived 15 min early because we caught a car from uptown. They wouldn't let us stay inside the building to wait for our reservation even though it was pouring rain outside. Then, even though we CONFIRMED twice they had a high chair, they said they have never had high chairs. The staff was rude, unaccommodating and unapologetic.

Ate dinner for 2 on a Tuesday at 9pm in November.   The space was cozy and cool but very tight.  The bar crowd wasn't turning over and there is no place to wait to be seated.  

Food was generally very tasty and the service was attentive.  However, I think the food was often too salty.  Many of the dishes and especially the meats was sharp with salt.  

The wine was good and the sommelier was interesting and quirky in a good way.  

2 people, 6 plates, 2 drinks and. $60 wine was $250.  Not a value but worth a try.

Cute atmosphere, friendly staff, and DELICIOUS.

I recommend the beef tartare with sunchokes, and the persimmon appetizer.

I will say that the desserts are good but a bit unexciting.  And of the two cocktails I had, one was theoretically delicious but didn't execute well.

I'd definitely go back.

There was a little bit of a wait with a res even for a Wednesday night, but only for about 10 minutes. The line up was burrata, it was creamy and mild as it should be and the toast served beneath was crunchy and seasoned with salsa verde and oil. Next was the scallops, seared and done perfectly, third was uni omelette, interesting smooth uni with a little bit of egginess in there. My favorite was the scallops. The main dishes were the ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino. Little pockets of Rich creamy goodness in mushroom sauce. We also had the beef dish was was hanger steak done a perfect medium rare nicely salted and seasoned.  All in all a delicious meal, highly recommended, well executed!

Totally worth the hype, imo.  Been awhile since I've been to a resto where the food matched the hype and where I completely enjoyed all aspects of my meal.

Burrata, razor clams, ricotta dumplings and monkfish is what we dined on and none of it disappointed.  Burrata was incredibly creamy and made the charred bread the perfect texture along side it. Razor clams were so delightfully garlicky with a bit of kick from the horseradish - super tasty.  The dumplings were light, airy and creamy and I loved the shaved mushrooms with them.  Monkfish was delicious and the perfect sized portion for the two of us.  Dessert was the chocolate cake which had a tiramisu-like consistency...it was out of this world!  Italian and French focused wine list with many affordable options.  We went with a Sicilian red...perfect for what we ate.

Service was friendly and knowledgeable by both the sommelier and waitress and didn't feel rushed at all in order to turn over our table.

Yes, it's fairly small and cramped and loud, but so are the majority of places in the city.  If the food is worth it, it all adds to the vibe for me.  I loved everything about it and can't wait to go back.

This restaurant was on the pricier side and slightly hard to find since the sign is a chalk board one that's quite small and then you have to just spot that before entering a central door and turning to the right. They also will not seat you unless your entire party is there, so be sure to get there on time! The food itself is quite good though -- we were there for brunch and it was fairly lively. All in all, I'd say that this little tucked away gem in SoHo is definitely worth trying out.

These reviews are absolutely on par. Although pricey, the food is amazing here and I'd absolutely go back. It's a great date night spot because it's small dishes, so you can get a bunch and share. For two people, we got 4 dishes and 1 appetizer - I ended up full, but not stuffed.

Let me select what to order for you - get the ricotta & mushroom dumplings (absolutely amazing), mussels on toast, and pork with carrots/leeks. Those are all unbelievable. We also got the beef tartare and croquettes appetizer but thought those were just good, not great.

It gets pretty crowded here so expect to wait for dinner. We had a 30 minute wait for dinner on a Friday night at 7:45pm. Our waitress was wonderful though and super friendly, so overall a great experience.

We went there with a party of four for brunch. The seats were the best seats of the house as we had a cute private corner. The wait staff was attentive and courteous and likable. 
I really wanted to like this place as we got our reservation weeks in advance and were hoping to savor every bit of food and conversation with our friends. The reviews, most of them, were fantastic so the hopes were high. Our favourite meal of the weekend is always brunch! 
We decided to start with coffees and Bloody Marys. I just cannot recommend ordering coffee there, ever, at all. Also I found their version of Bloody Mary a bit much for an empty stomach, but others in our party finished theirs with glee. 

The waitress recommended to order a dish each and then some more to share, which judging by the plates' cost is an expensive option. It is their only option though as the amount on the plate is teeny tiny minuscule and you have to get many to get fed. 

We got the beans/egg dish, 2 orders of lamb ribs, the burrata, the lardo bread and the persimmon with fenchel. I really wish they had some sides that just come complimentary to balance the heaviness of the tiny plates. Lamb ribs were very very greasy and burrata (and a piece of bread underneath) floating in olive oil. The flavours were good, but the amount just angered me past the point of savoring every bite. I am sure though that the ingredients is top-notch! 

We paid $55 each and I left hungry and a bit ill and angered from the whole combination. As I said I was set to like it a lot but it just didn't do it for me. I would say that it is a bit overrated as a fabulous brunch, feels more like sample tasting.

Enjoyed my first and really excellent luncheon experience here.

The tapas-like cuisine served is familiar and homey, but, just a bit quirky to be quite novel and unique.  [This place reminds me of Barrafina in London, if this rings a bell with you...]

Started with some nice everyday sherry.  Wine list is nicely organized, with many affordable gems to choose from.

Service was super friendly, yet, professional enough - a nice mix.

Would I go back?  Yep!

After dining at Estela, I've decided to start rolling with Obama. It appears he's the only one that can get a reservation here. 

I was in the neighborhood at around 10PM on a Thursday night and decided to have a very late meal. The only option was to sit at the bar [it holds about 10 people], where they serve the full menu. The restaurant is super tiny, even by New York standards, and was completely jam packed. 

The bartender seemed less than enthused about serving me. Maybe it was late and she wanted to go home, maybe she just doesn't like her job, I'm not sure, but she was not at all friendly. I digress...

___

Burrata [$16]: Wow. I will preface the description by saying: this is what I imagine a delicious mossy forest floor tastes like. The burrata, so mild, was served on a piece of charred bread, lending a smokey flavor to the dish, and laid on top of salsa verde [this is where the forest comparison comes into play]. It was a little difficult to eat. The piece of bread was big and too hard to easily cut with a knife. Regardless, it was incredible. 

Ricotta Dumplings [$24]: More accurately, I would call it ricotta gnocchi. 

The dumplings were little fluffy pillows of cheese. On top were thinly shaved pieces of mushroom which were there more for textural contrast rather than flavor. I recommend using a spoon to scoop up a piece of mushroom, dumpling, and the sauce underneath [I believe this may have been the pecorino, as it was slightly salty and gave the dish most of its bold umami flavor].

Now that I think about it, who cares what you name this dish when it's so amazeballs. 

Sweet Potato [$12]: The dessert accounts for the 4-star rating. After such a fantastic meal, I was expecting an epic dessert. I'm not really sure what this was. 

The sweet potato came as a type of ice cream/gelato/sorbet thing on top of a cake thingamado. The cake was soaked in honey and vinegar. My taste buds were all kinds of confused. Was this savory or sweet? The dish grew on me as I kept eating it but I wouldn't really say I loved it. I don't like to be confused about my desserts. I'm sure you don't either. 

$71, not including tip, was definitely fair considering the quality of food. Everything was so simple but the flavors were extraordinarily powerful.

Estela is the hip new thing for all the appropriate reasons: small exclusive 'hidden' vibe, delicious innovative menu, small tapas-style portions. Don't be fooled and think anything will be entree-sized even if it is entree priced!   I went with a friend and ordered 4 dishes (croquettes, tartare, dumplings and lamb ribs) and would have left hungry were it not for the flourless chocolate cake which seems to be finished/smothered in creme fraiche and cocoa.  Every dish was very tasty, but small.  That said, it made for a lovely evening out for drinks and 'bites'!

I had a reservation and came and not only was it not honored the maitre'd was incredibly rude and condescending. We never ate at the restaurant and had to leave.
I would never return to restaurant that was so pretentious and snotty

One of the best meals I've had in awhile, and possibly one of the best I've had in NYC. The space is cozy and buzzy, but not overwhelmingly loud. 

We had 8:30 reservations on a Wednesday evening and only had to wait around 10 minutes before being seated. We ordered a bottle of wine to share for the table, as well as:

- Beef Tartare (do not miss this, it's incredible)
- Burrata (no question)
- Mussels (these had such a surprising mix of flavors and were delicious)
- Lamb (well spiced and tasty)
- Croquettes (tasty, nothing standout)

I can't describe what makes Estela stand out so much, except that they seem to be doing everything right (ambiance, service, food, wine, etc.) - it's approachable but upscale and expensive enough to be a nice dinner out without breaking the bank. I highly recommend it and I'm planning on going back soon.

Delicious food.  There is no need to say more about the burrata, beef tartare, etc. Others here already have; and the hype is well deserved. That said, the loudness of the place just about ruins the experience. How loud is it? (I CAN'T HEAR YOU...). F****ng loud. Imagine eating at a JFK runway or in a mosh pit. Maybe it's not that bad; but it's bad enough that the waitress has to bend over you to tell you the specials and hear your order. By all means go; the food is wonderful. But bring ear plugs and a walkie talkie so that you can have a conversation at normal volume with the other people at your table.

All the dishes we had were tasty- the serving portions are tapas style, which is one of my favorite ways to enjoy food (with variety and in small quantities). The most incredible dishes were the beef with potatoes and the lamb ribs.  Our server was quick and brimming with wine suggestions, and the lighting was warm and romantic. However, I will say that this place is TINY. My date and I were seated adjacent to the bar and at one point there were elbows literally within inches from our table. Expansion, please.

KenScale: 8.5/10

Since its opening last year, Estela has maintained its hot streak as one of the most buzzed restaurants in the city, culminating in a visit from President Obama this year. I've had some fabulous dishes at the restaurant last year and been meaning to come back to explore the evolution of chef Ignacio Mattos' kitchen. Lately, I've been hearing a lot of great brunch dishes at the restaurant so even though I'm not a huge fan of brunch in general, decided to visit on a recent Saturday. I was very pleased with the creative take on brunch coming from the restaurant.

On my prior visit for dinner, I didn't get burrata with salsa verde and charred bread. The dish was available for brunch as well, and I decided to go for it this time. The simple burrata dish was one of the best I've had, with elegant flavor and silky smooth burrata making a wonderful dish. I wasn't sure what to make of the combination of pancetta, avocado and egg on Danish pastry when I ordered it, but I could now understand how critics have been raving about this dish. The combination of salty pancetta and sweet Danish pastry somehow worked marvelously alongside avocado and egg. Steak with eggs and potatoes was also very well executed, with juicy meat (which could've used slightly less seasoning) working nicely in flavor with eggs and crispy potatoes. 

The restaurant was certainly on the quieter side during the brunch time (maybe it was during the holiday season?), and I had no problem getting seated right away without reservations. The brunch menu also has a full bar with classic brunch cocktails like Bloody Mary. I'm glad that I found another one of my go-to brunch places in the city.

Came here as a walk-in at 8pm this past Saturday with my boyfriend. We were sat immediately at a table near the front. Very small (maybe 15 tables, tops) and cozy restaurant with a good bar.They had the two of us sitting next to each other, I usually make fun of people who sit like this. It actually was a nice change and made better for sharing all the goodies we ordered.

Started out with two cocktails from the drink list, the Pompelo Sour and the Pinga Rosita. Both were quite yummy.

We then got a bottle of wine, we originally wanted the Nebbiolo but alas they were out. The server recommended the Dolcetto d'Alba instead, it was fab and cheaper than our original choice! I typically prefer fruit-forward like Pinot Noir so this kept me in the same comfort zone. Good overall selection too with French, Spanish, Italian options. 

The goodies:
-Burrata with salsa verde and charred bread: Fantastic
-Mussels escabeche on toast: Different but still good
-Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo: Mmmm-melt in your mouth fluffiness with a complimenting pop of cheese every other bite
-Pork with cabbage and pears: Just, wow. Cabbage is charred and a surprising partner.

Desert we had the blueberry sorbet that was a refreshing end to the meal. We shared everything and it was just the right amount for two over-indulging Italians after a week of holiday gluttony. 


Minor(HA) side note: Adrian Grenier was sitting a few tables away with 4 chicks in true Vinny Chase form. I wanted to hug him and grab his fluffy hair but I restrained myself. Instead I just walked to the bathroom 4 or 5 times so he may or may not think I have digestive problems, totally worth it for eye contact. Swoon.

I simply cannot believe how lucky I am to get to experience such incredible restaurants and the creative chefs behind them...Estela. We got off the plane and ran over to the restaurant for dinner. It is small and cozy...the perfect place to be on our first night in NYC. My vodka martini-straight up-was perfect. I mean perfect - deceptively simple but almost impossible to perfect. The restaurant serves again small plates which is what we are becoming accustomed to - and love because it gives you the opportunity to share and taste a wide variety of courses. First we had the Salted cod and potato croquettes with an incredibly yummy aioli. There were two for each of us-which was perfect-I could have eaten more-the texture was perfect when we took a bite. We then proceeded on down our list - Burrata with salsa verde and charred bread, mussels escabeche on perfectly toasted sourdough toast, the Lamb ribs with charmoula and honey were sheer perfection with it's crispy crust, Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo, the really interesting chocolate cake, and the to die for and totally unique pana cotta. OMG! We were so full...but our taste buds were so happy. Every single bite was devoured and appreciated. One thing to mention that I loved is that the quality and presentation of the food was mindful... authentic... humble in the delivery of perfection. So grateful to the chef and staff, and cannot wait to return!

If its good for President Obama, then it's good for me!

Pros: the food is really, really food. It's a great space, location and ambiance. 

Cons: the prices for what you get is pretty ridiculous

Tips: make a reservation

I am not a fan of giving "less than satisfactory" reviews... Really... I don't like spending time bitching.. Soooo if I DO give a LTS (Less then Satisfactory) review, rest assured there's something about the place I had to report... (Seriously guys, I could save that date)
In a nutshell, the restaurant is a total overblown pile of SALT.  Yes, that's right--- SALT.  Who puts oysters with salmon eggs ("ikura") on-top of a pile of SALT?!!  Estela--- unfortunately does..... 
in addition they:
dont serve soda aside ginger ale and soda water
Do not serve hot sauce (IE no tobasco, just special "Chef Sauce" which I swear is siracha!)
boast uneven booth to chair height making date feel awkward when much shorter in chair.....
....
whatever.... if you dont believe me, I suggest checking out for yourself.  just remember to pack your 20oz bottle of Diet Coke, tabasco, etc....
PS- 2 stars because the staff was at least friendly and only charged us for drinks after professing reason as to why we didn't want the other 2 dishes... I mean, it's hard to get service with a smile these days yeah?!

Came here for brunch and was very impressed. Both dishes sampled were great. The breakfast sandwich, with panchetta, egg, and avocado was delicious - the pastry roll it was served on was extremely buttery and soft.

While everyone seems to be talking about the sandwich, I liked the eggs with beans, and croutons even more. Two fried eggs sat atop a tomato based sauce with croutons, white beans, onions, and harissa - similar to a shakshouka and a fantastic dish.

My only complaint is $14 cocktails which may be fine at dinner, but if you're charging $14 dollar for a bloody mary at a brunch in which most items are in the 14-16 dollar range, it better blow me away, and this one didn't.

Endive salad and monkfish were spot on, very good and creative dishes. Seating is very cramped and uncomfortable, servers try to accommodate. Don't bring large bags or anything bulky and you'll have a good time.

The food is delicious, but pricey if you are judging the portion size.  I appreciate all the attention to detail that he took when creating such amazing flavors.  I was disappointed however how quickly the food came out and felt rushed to devour the food. The timing was definitely off for us.   There needs to be some tweaking of the service.  If you are going to charge $18 dollars for a glass of wine and your customer orders multiple glasses, please give her a new glass.  She should not have to ask.

Absolute gem on Houston Street. We'd been trying in vain to get a table for dinner on Saturday for weeks, so it was a pleasant surprise when we just walked in and were able to snag a cute table for 2. This place has coat check, so you don't have to worry about where to put your giant poofy jacket. 

We started off with the salted cod and potato croquette, then got the fried arroz negro, lamb ribs and beef tartare, then finished off with their amazing chocolate cake and coffee. The croquettes and tartare were the highlight of the night for me. Perfectly flavored and amazing texture. 

The portions here are for savoring not for filling you up, so come prepared. As my friend put it, this is a place to meditate over every bite. Highly recommended for food lovers.

Awesome basic food, small portions, tapas style, for a lot of money.   But not for an insane amount.   Obama ate here if that means anything, and all the gourmet magazines rave about it.   So with all the hype, you expect a lot, and perhaps nobody can live up to this kind of hype, and this place does not.   This is not the best restaurant in town, but it's very, very good.   And considering all the hype, it's surprisingly easy to get a walk-in table and great friendly laid back service.

We were really lookig forward to dining here last night since it was my husband's
birthday.  Believing all of these rave reviews we started with the impoverished
appetizers and chose the carrots.  Well, that is what we got a few carrots
with a small cilantro dip and a cream dip.  Did I mention that the waitress asked
if I were allergic to anything and I promptly informed her 'cilantro.'  Needless to
say this was not a good beginning nor were the carrots anything to write
home about.

Next we ordered the dish that is the talk of this website - fried arroz with squid.
This dish was expensive and not impressive if you have eated at Flors de Mayo
uptown where a very large portion of this black rice and large portions of
squid are offered alive with flavor, delicious and less then half the price.

My husband ordered Pork with Cabbage which was the most expensive thing on the
menu $29.  The poor man was so disappointed saying it was bland as well as 
small in portion.

I ordered the Ricotta dumplings and started choking, gulping water because they
must have poured a pound of salt to this dish.  It was horrible.  I noticed that
my next table neighbor left half of her dumplings when the waitress took away
her dish.

The noise level here was crazy, the food was awful and we were very hungry
but glad to leave this restaurant.  I really believe that the cooks were students
that were learning the recipe as they cooked it.
Very good food. But a little on the expensive side for what they offer. Otherwise a 5 *

This place is loud and cramped. The food was good, but I don't know if it's worth being so uncomfortable over. We were placed next to the bar at a table for two, but had to sit next to each other which was interesting but not ideal. People were putting their drinks on our table, squeezing their butts against our table, and  the loud volume inside made it really hard to have a normal conversation. As for the food, I really enjoyed the squid ink rice,  the beef tartare, delicious endive salad and spicy lamb. The burrata was just ok for me, and I didn't finish the mussels either. We also ordered the steak, and it was not worth the $37, because it basically was 3 bites.

It's good. It's great. Really, it is. Why I can't get to 5 Stars, even I don't know.

It's definitely romantic but not too stuffy -- hip enough to work for friends & small families, too. It's pretty small, located inconspicuously at the top of these small steps and overlooking Houston. Small tables lit by even smaller candles. The music is just loud enough that you can somewhat tune into it (if the company is just that bad).

The wine list is extensive, but have no fear, the staff is very helpful. Not particularly friendly, but surely far from cold. Actually, a loud outgoing waiter would stand out at a place this low-key.

All dishes were at a minimum good, but a few nailed it out of the park. Something about the Mussels Escabeche on Toast didn't do it for me. I recognize that the burnt toast is sort of the Chef's "thing," and I respect that. Perhaps it was what was on the actual toast itself that just didn't do it for me (I couldn't fully grasp the taste of what i was eating). Regardless, I know that's a fairly popular dish. Oh, and the Salted Cod was forgettable. But enough about my whiny privileged taste buds, because the Beef Tartare was crazy good. The Fried Arroz Negro was also super unique and a wise choice. The Monkfish was very good, as well. Oh, and the table next to us had this Burrata looked amazing (live to eat another day, I suppose).

All in all, great restaurant that I highly recommend. No dish will disappoint, and the ambiance is quintessential trendy New York City but without too much snootiness.

I actually signed up to Yelp to write this bad review.

I am not sure why so many people are giving such fantastic review of this place.  The food is overpriced, run of the mill 'foodie' fare.  Let me elaborate on that point: The menu lacks variety(which is not a big deal to me, but the food you have on the menu should be done to perfection), the portions are ala carte, and just not delicious.

While I could easily turn this into a food review.  But I would rather point out the serious flaws of execution within the restaurant.  You spend $6 or $8 for a small bowl of olives that are customary at any 2-bit European restaurant.  The problem is not with the olives, the portion, or even the price....execution....You end up with a nice little bowl of delicious olive oil (and the only thing that is worth the money you just spent) Why on earth they do not give you bread to sop up the oil is beyond reason.  So the best part of the dish gets thrown out.  While I could go into detail on other mis-executions, I will just point out this erroneous example of poor experience.

Several so-so dishes behind me, I like to close with an after dinner drink, at least a coffee if nothing else.  The bright spot on the evening was my wine I had with dinner, where they fell flat on their face was the lack of digestive libations, nor coffee.  At this point I should inform the reader, they have a bar.

While I personally would not eat here again (based on taste, execution, price, and variety) I can imagine a group of 4 ordering the entire menu and finding a dish or two worth eating (then and there, not again).  If you are coming in from out of town, I could not in good conscience say eat here.  If you love wasting money for mediocrity, this might just be the place for you.

Estela has been on my list for a while. In a nutshell, the food here is phenomenal. Small plates with a few larger options at the end of the menu. 

Here is what we ordered:
Pickled carrots 8Olli ham (Virginia) 14
Oysters Beef tartare with sunchokes 16
Burrata with salsa verde and charred bread 16 Lamb ribs with charmoula and honey 21Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo 24

Panna cotta 10Chocolate cake with whipped cream 10

All of our choices were fabulous. The food here is the star. The cocktails were good, (took too long to arrive), the wine was good, the bread was excellent...

Here is what I didn't like about my experience:

We felt rushed. We were told that we had to have everything ordered at the same time. Chef wants it that way... Um, sorry chef.... If you're going to have the table order everything you better have the skills to pace it properly. This chef did not. That is maybe why people like to order as they go. We were told by our waiter to order 7-9 dishes. 7 was fine, even alittle too much. Also, the waiter came by to ask if we were ready to order several times. I'm capable of calling a waiter over to order when ready.
After the check was delivered, again, the waiter came by twice and a lovely random woman came by to look at the folio to see if we had given our method of payment. Clue: when you see a credit card on top of or peaking out from the folio, you know the table is ready to pay. 

This staff needs some training. The food in this restaurant can keep Estela at the top of a foodies list...but the overall experience is important. The "cool kids" will move on to the next place in about a minute. Please spend more time catering to serious customers who require a more complete experience. 

This review started with 4 stars and I've now changed it to 3.
Love the food here--beef tartare, burrata, and ricotta dumplings. Dark, small, New York.

Estela executes simple food with a created twist very well. The charm of the (somewhat small) restaurant is inviting as it feels cozy and rustic. The cocktails follow suit with the food in that they are simple and well thought out to pair with the menu. 
My favorite dishes were the ones that came out first, the beef tartare with sunchokes and the mussels escabeche on toast (I still want more). Both were full of flavor and certainly open up your pallet as you prepare for 3 to 4 more dishes.  Note, the server recommends a pair of guests to order about 6 dishes for a complete meal...we went along with it since the plan was to try whatever was intriguing anyway but don't feel pressured to follow that rule (though you'll probably want to also).
The meal followed with burrata, scallops, arroz con negro, and the ricotta dumplings all of which were perfectly executed and left my palate satisfied with all of the different flavors and textures. In all, this is a wonderfully cozy restaurant turning out fantastic and thoughtful food

One of the best, truly, culinary meals I've had in a long, long time.  Much better than the brunch I had at Isa but just as uniques and weird ingredients driven.  While things are untraditional, the experimentation tastes excellent here.  Bf made a reservation for 930 on a Friday for our anniversary and the place was still so crowded. It's quite loud, small and sceney here so my advise is to plan ahead and not to come with too many people. 

It's all small plates here but they have more entree pricing but I strongly feel that you get great quality and skill for what you pay.  We stated off with two obscure but delicious wines - I forget which red bf had but I had the Italian Fernando which was a very complex, sweet but tart white. It was awesome

We had: 

- the pickled carrots - eh nothing special about this.  Almost raw shaved carrots, vinegar and salt. 

- the burrata which was a delicious texture on a well soaked piece of toast with an am amazing earthy, herby salsa verde. A must try. 

- the arroz which was with squid ink. Normally I'm not a fan,but this left no gritty taste and the rice was cooked with such a different yet satisfying texture it was fun to eat. Crackly, salty.. With little chunks of squid. A must try! 

- the ricotta dumplings which was amazing. It almost felt like they were swimming in a beef consome of some sort so it had a rich, meaty flavor. Also the ricotta and dumplings themselves were on point in regards to form and consistency.  They were topped with yummy shaved mushrooms which was great for presentation and taste.

- we also had the lamb short rib with honey. I didn't taste much only but somehow these ribs were both well bbq 'Ed , smokey and fell off the bone at the same time.  It also didn't taste overwhelmingly gamey which I often feel is the case with lamb. 

-last but not least the desserts. Forget what you've heard about the panna cotta, you can get that anywhere. We shared the sweet potato dessert - itll make everyone go nuts. It seems like a cake soaked with ice cream and chunks of sweet potato but it's just a little salty. It was a good play on sweet and salty. I highly recommend.  Again interesting and tasty. 

$170 for dinner so definitely not cheap. 
Service was prompt, polite- not too formal but waters were always filled. Major talented chef alert!

Had a great meal here. The food is worth a second trip, although the service gives me reason for pause. 

Small, dimly lit and very loud interior. Not the best for an intimate date. 

Ordered 5 dishes (plus one dessert) to share with my husband. we were just about full but maybe a sixth would have been justified. Menu is organized as small dishes to be shared tapas style. Salt cod croquettes were impeccable- light and perfectly crisp breading with beautiful meaty flakes of cod, sublime garlic aioli. Deep, rich arroz negro and squid with complex layers of flavor-- acid, spice and muted bitterness from the romesco. The quail was slightly disappointing- under seasoned and did not feel the cohesiveness with the adjacent pumpkin. Lamb ribs were smoky, spicy, succulent and decidedly delicious and not at all gamey. I could have had oceansful of the pillowy ricotta dumplings floating in earthy mushroom and pecorino. Must try and I would order this again and again. 

We ordered the chocolate cake with whipped cream and it was amazing. Soft, molten chocolate cake (mostly molten, barely cake) topped with a mound of whipped cream (seemingly unsweetened, which I loved) dusted with bitter cocoa. The best part was the bursts of salt sprinkled throughout the dessert. For someone who never craves sweets and actually doesn't even like chocolate much, this dessert was  a bit of a revelation in balance of salt, bitter and sweet and something I would definitely order again. 

One minor gripe (which may have been because I was a bit hangry) was the slow progression of the dishes. There is no complimentary starter bread or olives and the time between ordering the meal and the first and second dish was downright agonizing. We noticed lots of other tables suffering the same fate (eager craning necks at each server who leaves the kitchen). The rest of the dishes moved along quite well but came 2 at a time so the latter part of the meal felt ever slightly rushed. Again, minor gripe. The food is exciting on the palate and beautifully executed for the most part, and I would come back again.

Reservations are definitely necessary, and be prepared to experience NYC restaurant seating at this small but delicious restaurant.  Having planned out in advance that we wanted to come here, I was incredibly surprised with all of the wonderful dishes we tried and ate and couldn't have been more surprised with both the Beef Tartare with Sunchoke and the Squash and Rutabega Truffle tart.  The food here is definitely on the rustic side, but there wasn't one thing we ate that I didn't enjoy (including dessert!).  Along with the beef tartare and squash tart, we also ordered the lamb ribs, ricotta dumplings, and steak. For dessert, we had the tangerine and chocolate sorbet.  The steak was probably my favorite protein item, and there was no question that the tangerine and chocolate sorbet was a home run.  You're definitely in close contact with your neighbors, so be prepared for them to ask questions about what you ordered! I definitely enjoyed our dinner here, and thought that everything we ate was well put together and reminiscent of some of the great places we have here in SF.

Dined here tonight and enjoyed a solid meal. This is a share-plate restaurant where they recommend 7-9 dishes between 2 people. Faves were: burrata (couldn't have been fresher and paired with a basil vinegar purée that was to die for), lamb ribs spiced to perfection and served on a delicate bed of mint and cilantro yumminess, fried arroz with squid was delectable and savory, endive salad with Gorgonzola and vinegar infused croutons. This isn't a refined dining experience but it was fun and cozy in a packed NY resto space. And I was seated next to Jake Gyllenhaal to boot!!!

I am an eater.  It's what I do.  I eat a lot.  I eat at a lot of different places.  I eat with a lot of different people.  I eat a lot of different types of food.  You could say, I love it, perhaps?

If I could give my dinner at Estela 6 stars - nay, 10 stars - I would do it in a heartbeat.  It's one of the more memorable meals I have in a few years.  Sure, the price tag is high and one might think too high given the comfortable and casual atmosphere, but this food is so effing fantastic, it was almost inexpensive when you think about it.

This place is anything but pretentious.  It's cozy and comfortable, and people are just enjoying their meals and having a good time while the food keeps rolling and the cocktail shakers keep shaking (a beautiful sound to accompany any meal).  The wine list is plentiful, and did not disappoint.

The menu is tapas-style, so go with people who like to eat and share a bunch of different things.  As another yelper has said, let me just tell you what to order now so it's taken care of for you:

-Burrata with salsa verde and charred bread - holy effing moly this was THE best burrata I've ever had in my life.  Add that it was sitting atop still crispy yet salsa verde broth soaked bread, and I would go back JUST for this dish.  I drank some of the leftover sauce with the perfectly oversized spoon before they took it away.

-Ricotta Dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo - wow, wow, wow, wow, wow.  Sometimes things called "dumplings" or "gnudi" (which these are not) are disappointing - this is not one of those occasions.  Every single bite of this dish was more heavenly than the next.  I don't even know how to explain it to you, except to say it will exceed all possible expectations.  My friend who doesn't really like mushrooms even loved this dish.  It's beautiful and phenomenal and if I could sleep with a plate of food this would be my eternal bedroom partner.

-Steak with spicy marmalade, potatoes, and taleggio - I felt really lucky that my friend isn't a huge steak fan, but still agreed to get this dish with me, because I got to eat 80% of it, and I totally could have taken down another entire plate of it by myself.  They have a special type of frier that makes their freshly-made potato chips crispy on the outside while soft on the inside.  Don't know what I mean?  You shouldn't, because it's insane, and awesomely delicious.  We took one bite of them and instantly started smelling them, they were that impressive.  My friend said, "Oh my god...I think they smell like...man?"  I think it was a slightly bbq spice.  The steak was so amazingly seasoned and perfectly cooked - you know there was some magic going on in the kitchen, and the best part is that it IS magic - you just don't know why it's 100x better than any other steak you've had.  And the little puddles of taleggio...and the spicy marmalade...ugh I will DREAM about this dish.  IT IS SO EFFING GOOD.

We also had the cod fritters which were a lovely start - perfectly done, and perfectly simple.  For dessert my friend had cheese and I had the "sweet potato with vanilla ice cream and rum" which is a little circle of sponge cake (I think?) soaked in rum with yummy chunks of sweet potato layered over it and delicious vanilla bean ice cream
on top.  It was REALLY refreshingly simple.  A perfect size for one who likes dessert to themselves, or two who are perhaps stuffed to the gills or sharing multiple desserts.

But - let me say - as good as all the food was, what was even BETTER (if there could be such a thing) was the service.  Management - if you're reading this (which I'm sure you're not) - DO NOT EVER LET ZWANN GO!!!!!!!!  Aside from the fact that she has the awesomest name ever, she was one of the best servers I've had in years at any restaurant in any city.  She truly made our meal special.  We were carefully attended to, made to feel comfortable, casual, and at home, and like she was just hanging with us as one of the gals.  She was knowledgable, stayed to chat for a moment when we couldn't help but gush at how good the food was, and here's the best part...

...at the very end of our meal, when all that was left was maybe a 1/4 cup of the mushroom broth and a totally empty steak plate, instead of asking how our meal was and clearing everything away, SHE OFFERED US BREAD TO SOAK UP THE BROTH.  Oh my god, I totally freaked out.  Never, ever, ever have I been randomly offered bread at the END of my meal to soak up the tiniest most delicious bit of broth...it seems like such a simple question - a simple offer - but it absolutely made my night, and rounded out the whole experience as one of the best eating experiences I've had anywhere.  NYC, you win again.  

And, Mr. Ignacio Mattos, I hope you win the James Beard this year.  You sure as hell deserve it.

Had a delicious and charming meal at Estela.  

The space is small, but elegant and romantic.  The waitresses were all very informative and attentive, but not in an overbearing way.  The restaurant was lively, but at the same time we were able to hear our dinner companions.  They suggest ordering about 2 plates per person, so we ordered and shared the following: 

Top three: 
Beef tartare with sunchoke--the beef tartare was diced very small so the bites were very subtle.  dressed differently than many other beef tartare the sunchoke were a great compliment to the dish without being too powerful.  

Endive, walnuts, anchovy and ubriaco rosso--we almost didn't order this dish, but it was definitely in my top three favorite dishes.  The anchovies were subtle and barely noticeable presented through the salad's dressing.  The dressing was acidic and very slightly creamy thanks to the small chunks of parmesan-like ubriaco rosso. Definitely great to soak up with some of Estela's brown bread. 

Fried arroz negro with squid and romesco--I'm a big fan of paella, so the dish is similar to paella thanks to the chewy and crispy texture of the rice. and the addition of squid 

In addition: 
Burrata with salsa verde and charred bread--it's hard to go wrong with burrata, and the charred bread provided a nice smokey flavor to soak up the salsa verde complimented by the subtly creamy, and salty burrata

Ricotta dumplings-lots of good reviews of this, but they aren't dumplings as one might think, more similar to softer, creamier ravioli 

Monkfish with brussel sprouts--the brussel sprouts were raw, which was a nice variation to restaurant's renditions of brussel sprouts, but the fish was extremely salty

Steak with spicy marmalade, potatoes--just a normal steak, very salty especially with the mashed potatoes and potato chips they served on top

Salted cod and potato croquettes with aïoli--pretty fishy croquettes which provided more of a flavor to normal croquettes.  

For dessert:
Molten chocolate cake--the inside of the cake, the molten part was delicious, but surrounded by too much of a meringue like addition

Sweet potato cake--definitely unusual, but the root vegetable taste was very powerful and the sea salt distracted from making this taste like a dessert 

Would recommend, but definitely for a special occasion as the dinner is likely to be quite expensive.

Outstanding food, Attentive service at the bar, and a lovely view of Houston street from the front of the restaurant.

Now I see why Obama ate there when he was in town.

The first thing you need to know about Estela is to make your reservation far in advance. We booked a party of 4 for Friday night about a month in advance, and had to choose between 6 and 10 pm. We went at 6, which is when it opens. We were late and they didn't give us attitude, which I really appreciated. We got recommendations from friends who have been and the bartender, and we had a great experience.

Endives - These were a recommendation from a friend, which we would probably never have ordered otherwise. It's a little confusing when it comes out, because it basically just looked like a bed of endives, but below them is the mix of walnuts, anchovies, and cheese. You basically assemble the endive for yourself, and it is delicious.

Mussels - These come on toast sitting in something like an herbal broth. It comes together really well, and although I thought it was good, it was my least favorite thing that we ordered.

Arroz negro - This was delicious. The rice is perfectly cooked and seasoned and is beautifully presented. 

Ricotta dumplings - These were like a light gnocchi. They were very pillowy and were presented below a layer of very thinly sliced mushrooms. They were delicious.

Burrata - The burrata is great but sits in the same sauce as the mussels, so don't order both.

Swordfish - This was delicious. Perfectly cooked and the marcona almonds are an unexpected but great addition.

Lamb ribs - These were crispy on the outside and deliciously seasoned, and had good chunks of meat on them.

Chocolate cake - This was a chocolate ganache cake, heavy on the whipped cream. Delicious.

I am dying to go again so I can try the rest of the menu!

had a GREAT dinner here the other night, a friend made a reservation for two and we ended up being three which they were able to accommodate. we did have to wait a bit but it was well worth it. 

we ordered 5-6 plates as advised and enjoyed everything. the endive salad had great textures and a little acidity, the burrata with salsa verde was very fresh with an interesting combo of flavors, the fried squid black rice was by far our favorite - a must order! we also had the gnocchi which were super fluffy and light. we enjoyed some desserts which i can't fully recall - i think we had the panna cotta and sweet potato dish, both were good.

the service was amazing, very friendly and welcoming. the ambiance is intimate (it's pretty small)  all around a great time!

I am happy to say that the whole evening was an unexpected treat. The menu was stark and I wasn't sure what to expect. After the first bite I had no idea why I was concerned. 

This is a menu of different. Have I ever had a celery salad? I don't think so. Have I ever had whipped white beans and avocado with my fish?  I don't think so. Have I ever had a sweet potato bread pudding? I don't think so. All of these made dinner at Estela one I will remember for a long time.

I had the perfect anniversary dinner at Estela. Super romantic atmosphere, excellent food and equally as delicious drinks. We ordered about 5 dishes, but the clear star of the night was the swordfish! Perfectly cooked and amazing, amazing flavors. Our first round of cocktails were good, but I am so glad we ordered two more because I keep thinking about them to this day. The mountaineer is probably one of the best cocktails I have had and everyone should try it. I cannot wait to come back here again.

Estela was such a solid meal. My friends and I happened to be in the area during brunch hour, and even though there weren't any tables available, we were able to get a nice area at the bar to wine and dine. 

I started the meal off with a Can Can. This was a delicious concoction of gin and sparkling wine. We ordered the burrata with salsa verde and charred bread. Having gone to Jonathan Waxman's Barbuto, I have high expectations for salsa verde. I thought this one was very good. The bread was already dipped in the salsa so it does get soggy if you don't eat it quickly enough. The burrata was fresh and creamy. 

My girlfriend ordered the fried arroz negro with squid and romesco. This was absolutely delicious and there was a generous allocation of squid. I've normally only had squid ink pasta but squid ink fried rice is now a new favorite.

I ordered the pancetta, egg and avocado on a Danish pastry. The sandwich was kind of on the small side but it was finger-lickin' good. The pancetta was tasty, the egg was cooked over easy and the egg yolk spilled throughout the sandwich. The bread was so soft like a croissant but not oily at all. The avocado was the perfect topping and substituted any need for cheese. 

I was extremely impressed with the food and I can't wait to be back for dinner.

Like a fine wine, Estela improves with age.  

A talented culinary staff, consistently on the James Beard list.  Modern American.  Nothing you haven't seen before, but just better.  Tapas size portion, order accordingly.   

Reservation recommended, or just dine at the bar.
Causal but busy.

Came here for dinner, really enjoyed my meal!  Ordered oysters, lamb and swordfish.  I loved the lamb it was seasoned a little spicy but juicy and flavorful.  The oysters were really good but a little small.  The swordfish was also excellent but the portion was on the smaller side as well.  For dessert we went for cheese and some sort of creamy tiramisu like mousse which was delicious.  I would definitely go back and would love to try more options.
Smooth and uncomplicated but possibly the best Bloody Mary in east downtown. And the bar staff are just laid back and nice.

Excellent restaurant. Forward thinking, inventive cuisine that is the perfect balance of modern and farm-to-table.

I'm a sucker for beef tartare and Estela's has a nice saltiness and crunch to it.

Reservations are really difficult, basically just call and ask for the next 8:30PM table and mark you calendar.
Thomas is the nicest!!!!  We had a great time here!  Everyone was very friendly and the place is super cute!!!! Hope to come back soon!
Excellent, Perfect! May favorite restaurant.  Everything, from food to drinks, wine list and service.  Very happy every time I go there.

Chef Ignacio Mattas... You are a HERO. 
Am gonna keep this short and sweet;  this was my line up:

Yuzu Oysters... We just skipped foreplay and went straight to it...
Burrata w salsa Verde ; Insanely fresh like rolling around (desnudo) in a fresh grassy field,
Beef Tartare; How all rare burgers should taste!
Mussels Escabeche ...I slurped the cilantro broth clean from the bowl...is that a faux pas?
Arroz Negro;  Not just when in Spain, Wake me up for this ANY time...breakfast lunch and dinner...
Steak... BUTTERRRRRRRRRR

...when do we go again?

sidenote...all washed down w a fantastic Burgundy!

5 stars for service and food. The burrata, fried arroz negro rice is incredible, as was the steak. For dessert we ordered the salted panna cotta and it was also amazing. Great spot for dates and for foodies.
So unique and flavorful. Mussels were the best I've ever tasted. Great staff, just lovely!
The staff is lovely, and the wine list works wonderfully with their menu. Definitely try the Burrata and steak tartare!!

I had to check out all the hype about Estela...  And it is warranted!!!  Had great appetizers (cod and potato croquettes, and also the burrata!!!).  As main course, the ricotta dumplings were excellent as well.  And don't share your dessert.  Especially if it's the sweet potato one or the panna cotta. Approved!!!

Yes, there are any number of great NYC restaurants where your dollars will go a bit further. That said, Estela is a lovely spot with much to recommend it:

Oysters with yuzu kosho mignonette ($22): Sweet, spicy, tender, perfect.

Octopus with warm potato salad and smoked paprika ($14): Like a seafood steak. Very meaty. Sizable portion.

Fried arroz negro ($23): Show-stopper. Blend of crispy and soft grains shot through with romesco and delicate squid. Really, really rich. 

Steak with spicy marmalade and potatoes ($34): Great beef that toes the line between rare and medium-rare. But the potato chips on top are silly and have nothing on Kettle Chips or even Lay's tbh.

Swordfish with burnt celery and arugula ($29): Garnishes are actually the star of the show. Fish is fine but I've prepared better at home with swordfish steaks from the farmers market.

I'll add that the portions, to me, are quite respectable, despite reports to the contrary. But my wife and I are runts by American standards, so grain of salt.

Finally, nothing but praise for the lively setting, spot-on service and exciting wine list (especially notable for its modest markup).

There isn't a lot more I can say about the great food at Estela that hasn't been raved about. The service, food and space are great. The food I recommend: Oysters, Swordfish, Fried arroz negro, and Octopus. Everything seasoned and executed perfect. 

I do have one major problem with the steak dish and how it's advertised. 
"Steak with spicy marmalade, potatoes, and blue cheese $34. "

I love rare steak but ours arrived with the center black and blue, and was very chewy to eat. Also there was no blue cheese on the plate and the potato chips where just ok. The spicy marmalade was very good but not enough for me to recommend it to anyone. I was really disappointed. 

Despite the steak plate it was a great experience and I'd definitely come back to try other dishes.

I came a few months after they opened and didn't leave a review, but it would have been 4-4.5 stars. I was disappointed in my most recent experience there. 

Drinks - excellent. Martinis and a couple Amendments. 

Spicy Almonds & Salami - both good..just nothing special in my opinion. Kind of like some great almonds you'd buy at the grocery store, and same with the salami. 

Fluke crudo w/ uni - was most excited for this and it was the most disappointing dish of the night. Fluke smelled very fishy..did not seem fresh. 

Beef tartare - excellent as always

Burrata - very good

Service - OK. Dishes came out at random, no "how's everything?" stop by, not bad service..just didn't add anything in my opinion. 

The place is also just SO cramped. 


Parts of the meal were great but for $180 (including tax and tip) I don't think I will be back any time soon.

This is a kind of modern upscale restaurant. Once waitress saw us with the kids, disappointment could not be hidden.We went for breakfast and I can not complain about the food, everything was delicious. But the portions are pretty small. So if you are planning to get a bulky breakfast this in not a place.

Great cocktails. Also they have dry sherry by the glass, which is not available everywhere. Nice setting on a second floor overlooking Houston street. 

We did not try the food.

Ok, so Estela is even better the second time around. 
Each dish was better than the next. It felt like we fell into some magical world. 

Where the drinks are amazing and never ending. 

Where the scallops melt in your mouth. 

Where burrata is salty and savory and perfect with salsa Verde and crispy bread. It's a perfect bite of creamy cheesy goodness with sauce and a crunch. 

Where the ricotta dumplings needed bread to sop up every bit of the mushroomy goodness. 
Where each dish was perfectly executed. Where each of us couldn't come to a consensus what our top three dishes were. 

Want to know mine? 
Burrata, ricotta dumplings and arroz negro.

Maybe it's the wine, maybe it's the company, maybe it's a major celebration, but this was one the best meals since El Club Allard. 
  A huge fan.
