The food is ok. The servers are helpful. The bussers are a bit rushed. The worst thing about this place is that the tables are packed super tight.

I felt like I was in a sardine can. People passing by would almost knock over things on our table. I could hear the conversation of the table next to us. And if you're unlucky, you'll be sitting next to some loud, obnoxious people like we were.

The food is fine, but overpriced for what it is.
-The scallops were sweet and buttery, but they slice the oysters horizontally into three pieces so there are two pieces that have a nice sear on one side and then the middle piece that was kind of just goopy.
-The cod croquettes were so average and at $13 for four small balls, not worth it. It was fried nicely, but in the end, it's just a fried ball.
-The octopus was super chewy ($15).
-The beef tartare ($17) had crispy sunchokes and some seasoning that I couldn't put my finger on, but it took away from the delicate flavor of the beef.
-The burrata ($17) was bland and not as creamy as it should be.
-The sardine ($21) had too many bones for me, but it was simply grilled. The egg was literally just half a boiled egg.
-The arroz negro ($23) was crispy and a little on the salty side.
-The lamb ribs ($21) were full of, I guess, charmoula. Not my favorite seasoning. The ribs itself were mostly stringy meat and fat.

We split the above dishes among the two of us. We over-ordered, but at least we got to try a good sample of the menu. The food quality and taste does not justify the prices and the tight spacing of the tables. I won't be back.

Delicious and worth the hype. Service was fantastic. The restaurant is small, but we were a large group and were able to get our own big table in the back, so it was pretty comfortable. 

From most to least favorite (more or less):
Steak with spicy marmalade, potatoes, and taleggio 
Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo 
Burrata with salsa verde and charred bread - I wish this came with more bread!
Fried arroz negro with squid and romesco 
Endive, walnuts, anchovy, and ubriaco rosso - the lemon flavor was a surprisingly powerful punch of flavor. Very refreshing for a salad. 
Cod and potato croquettes with aïoli -  These were delicious, but I like anything fried.
Lamb ribs with charmoula and honey - Deliciously smokey, though there wasn't much meat on the ribs and it was pretty fatty. 
Chocolate dessert - Surprisingly dark/bitter chocolate. The texture was great
Octopus with potatoes and pimentón - Too oily/greasy. 
Panna Cotta - Tasty, but i wouldn't ordered it again. It tasted like fancy greek yogurt.

I had a date night here with my husband and left feeling very thirsty. I'll start with the service.  The waiters were very attentive and friendly. 

We shared six dishes and all six were very salty and very close to being inedible.  The chocolate cake that we ordered for desert, seemed to have salt in it as well! The coco dusted on top of the cake was very bitter. It just did not go well together.  

The seating arrangement and space here is extremely tight.  Personally, I do not like restaurants that place tables so close to one another.   

For the price point, I know there are better options in New York.

The restaurant is nicely decorated, though a bit cramped (we were seated by the window area which is probably the most cramped area in the restaurant, but still nice), and the staff was really helpful and friendly.

The reason for the 2 star review was that my wife and I found that the overarching theme of the night was SALT. Everything was exceedingly salty and it seemed to just build up throughout the night. By the time we got our entrees we couldn't finish them because we were so overwhelmed by salt. Because of this, we were glad to have the dessert come out, but found that our melted chocolate cake was more salty than sweet! I appreciate desserts that aren't too sweet because I don't have much of a sweet tooth (though my wife does), but the chocolate cake was probably the most disappointing dish that evening. At least we both had a good laugh out of it.

I did leave thinking that almost everything would have been really tasty if they were less salty, so hopefully the kitchen will address that... and maybe it was just us with a one-time bad experience, after all, Estela was recently rated as one of the top 100 best restaurants in the world.

Def make reservations in advance.  I was a bit annoyed with the restuarant because I had made a reservation and they didn't let me know until about 2 days prior that my reservation was cancelled because they double booked.  Luckily I was able to rebook and find a time for my party.  We had a party of 6 and were seated in the back area.  I loved the back area bc it seemed like a semi private room and blocked out some of the noise.  The food was amazing.  We had the burrata with the salsa verde, beef tartare, mussels, dumplings, steak, pork, lamb, scallops and the arroz negro.  Everything was amazing.  The rice was a bit salty but good.  The steak was really juicy and the spicy marmalade that paired with it was so good.  The burrata was amazing and so fresh. My favorites were the dumplings, steak, burrata. Def a go to.

This meal was definitely one of the best we've ever had. Every dish is savory as all get out. So, definitely come with an appetite, and maybe do some training beforehand on eating more than your fill, because although the plates are small, they will rock your world with both savory flavor and filling potential. We ordered just one plate too many (5 total) and should've stuck to four. 

The lamb ribs were herb crusted to perfection. The ricotta dumplings were maybe the single best bite of anything I've ever had. Burrata was brilliant, scallops were firm but also somehow would explode with flavor and juices. We finished with the steak with spicy marmalade and that was just way too much to try and eat at the end, but we took it home and ate it later. Very very worth it.

Now let's talk about the drinks and wine. The huge wine selection seems daunting until the sommelier shows up and makes everything okay. Our 2005 vintage red paired with each dish somehow brilliantly and uniquely. The special cocktails from the ultra efficient bar tenders were filled with liquids I've never heard of, but were nuanced and had that effect where the flavor stays in your mouth long after you've finished sipping. I highly recommend the smoky mezcal drink whose name I've forgotten. 

Take all that above and pair it with the small, overcrowded, and yet still comfortable atmosphere and service, and you've got a splurge night out that's hard to beat.

Perhaps it's unfair to criticize Estela after only giving it a try for brunch.  But...I'm not willing to spend the dollars required to go back for a dinner, and I feel like potential brunchers deserve a heads up, especially when this was the first place to pop up on Yelp for "breakfast & brunch" while standing at Houston & Bowery.  

I came here with three friends for a Sunday brunch, and was able to walk in and sit right away even though one guy hadn't arrived yet.  Great start, and the toast with lardo and jam "snack" we ordered to tide us over was outstanding.  Coffee was weak and a bit bitter, but otherwise, things are looking promising.

The waitress told us that the menu was designed to share.  At brunch, and with delicious sounding egg/pancetta/avocado sandwiches, French toast, and eggs benedict (it's not called a benedict, and the waitress actually seemed offended when we called it a benedict, but it's eggs/bacon/Hollandaise, so that's what it is), I'm not super interested in small plates for sharing.  She then warned us that the French toast is "very small," so don't order it intended as a meal.  Taking her warning to heart, we order egg sandwiches and benedicts.  

Everything was fine, but extraordinarily small.  So small that one of us joked that if the waitress was worried about the French toast being small, it might have just been a piece of Cinnamon Toast Crunch.  For $16 apiece, an egg sandwich should not be so small that I'm still hungry enough that I agree to order dessert after eating it.  (A word on dessert:  stay away from the panna cotta, unless the phrase "sickly sweet" is appealing to you.)  Personally, I was not a fan of the bun that came with the egg/pancetta/avocado sandwich, which was also quite sweet, but the actual egg was cooked very well, and had some nice hot sauce mixed in.

TLDR:  food was decent, but not really a place for brunch (despite the Yelp "b&b" designation).

We had the Serrano ham, Beef tartare with sunchoke, Burrata with salsa verde and charred bread, and Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo.  The food was extremely tasty and well prepared.  The beef tartare and burrata were just superb -- I highly recommend.  The restaurant has a nice decor and surprisingly is not extremely loud. Wine selection is decent. Service was very pleasant and friendly.

We were here for dinner last night - and it's in the running for the best meal I've had in New York. We came here because it recently ranked at 90th best restaurant in the world (http://www.theworlds50best.com/list/1-50-winners#t51-100), and while I believe that it's clearly extremely difficult to come up with those rankings, I think they made a great choice with Estela.

Menu is mostly small plates to share - the ricotta gnocchi and potato & cod croquettes were standouts, along with the oysters. And the fried arroz negro. So basically, everything we ordered. It was all delicious - and was paired with an excellent riesling, at our waitress's recommendation.

Highly recommend. It's the day after and I'm already looking for an excuse to come back here!
OMG...the steak...the rice...the scallops....the cheese....the whatever....so good.....thank you Jesus so good.

Went here for Sunday brunch with some friends. We almost missed the door for the construction around it. Service was good. My wife had the eggs, beans and harissa. I had the red snapper with horseradish and greens. The harissa complimented the eggs and beans well. Red snapper was cooked well, horseradish was a bit overwhelming but did bring a nice kick to the dish.

Environment : crowded

Food : very delicious!
- Mussels escabeche on toast : sour sauce, delicious mussel with crispy bread, perfect taste
- beef tartare with sunchoke : well marinated, crispy sunchoke mixed with tartare make the taste stand out. Not very appreciated about non-toasted bread 
- burrata : savory, creamy
- fried arroz negro with squid : one of the favorite dish 
- quail, chicken liver, Swiss chard : 

Service : friendly 

Wait : none for seating 15 min for food

Price : pricey 

Overall : every dish is wonderful and satisfied!

make reservations ahead of time especially if you have a large party.

my sisters and i had reservations at 9. we were not seated until 9:30ish which was a little helpful because half of us were running late. it is a tiny place and is a little cramped around the bar area.

the food was delicious. everything we tried was amazing! the fried arroz negro was a little bit salty. but everything else was amazing! the beef tartare with sunchoke was one of my favorite things. it's actually so hard to decide what i like cause it was sooooo good! the steak, scallop, mussels, lamb, burrata... so good! i think they offer a lot more toast that needed but at the same time my sisters and i don't eat that much bread. the bread was mediocre but everything else was so good! no wonder bon appetit chose this place as #2 for one of the newest restaurants.

0 stars. Bad service at bar and bad food over priced. Sent back pork entree. 2 small bad pieces of meat could not cut through tough over cooked. Gave up trying to cut didn't even taste. Awful. Plus all fat tourists from Midwest in terrible tshirts. AVOID

The space a little tight, but deal with it.  The food does not disappoint.  Everything is great, but the real standouts on this menu are the burrata with salsa verde, the lamb ribs, and the fried arroz negro with squid and romesco.

Estela - this place seems to be the new place to go and the new place to love! It's constantly packed, so make sure you get a reservation early. It's American tapas, be ready to share! Here's what we got: 

- Burrata with salsa verde and charred bread - amazing and fresh cheese. My favorite of the night. 
- Fried arroz negro with squid and romesco - It's black rice. And it's fried. But it's so amazing and so delicious. Get it. 
- Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo - This was not as amazing as the other two dishes were. 
- Desserts - also super amazing so be sure to save room here!

It's a great place and on the list of best restaurants in the world! Try it out if you're looking for great dining but at a cheaper price point.

As a bit of context, I came to Estela a short time after it opened and absolutely loved it. I raved endlessly to friends and sent in multiple people. Last month, for my 29th birthday I went back.

We arrived a few minutes early and because our table wasn't ready, grabbed a drink at the bar. There was no room to stand but we squeezed in where possible and proceeded to get bumped into constantly. While this is to be expected in a crowded restaurant, the bigger issue was that while standing at the bar a member of Estela's management team barged into me. Barged is not a word I use often, but when my boyfriend has to grab my arm to keep me from falling, I think it is warranted. This happened twice with no apology.

Shortly after, our table was ready and we were seated at potentially the least ideal table in the entire restaurant. Right next to the loud bar and again, in a spot where we would be bumped into constantly. My boyfriend, who sat on the outside, had his chair bumped into constantly throughout the whole meal. He also kept ducking to avoid the chairs that were being passed over his head. 

Our whole experience was not negative - the food was again delicious, exactly as I remembered. I understand that Estela is a busy restaurant but it would have been nice to have our discomfort acknowledged, as it was apparent on our faces that we were in a bad situation. An apology at the least would have been appreciated.

Estela is a tiny, tiny place even by NYC standards. If you don't like strangers then avoid this place because you will be sharing your dinner conversations with them.
Even though I'm slightly over the small plates concept, the food at Estela was truly excellent. We tried all the standard star dishes: beef tartar with sun chokes, scallops with peas and ricotta dumplings. They were all predictably delicious. The surprise hit of the evening and the most delicious dish we tried was the endive salad. It was so bright & citrusy & slightly bitter & creamy with the cheese & nutty from the walnuts. Really good!
The wine list was simple but good. All wines, even sparkling, are served in the same type of wine glass. I'm not finicky about such things but drinking sparkling wine from a white wine glass was not really fun.

It's been a whirlwind of fancy New American dinners given my in-laws are in town but I suppose that's the perk of having them stay in our living room. That being said, Estela really stood out in the week of nice meals that we've been indulging in.

First, I loved that dining at 6:30 on a Wednesday in a nook in the back translates to a dining experience where you can actually hear everyone at your table speak - pretty ideal when you're dealing with two sets of parents who qualify for senior discounts.

The food was phenomenal, with very few exceptions of things I didn't find that I wanted to eat more of. Here's the lineup:
- salt cod and potato croquettes - fried perfectly and not overwhelmingly salty. Like the best croquette you've had at your favorite tapas restaurant you can't really remember because you drank too much sangria.
- cured fluke with sea urchin - are these all my favorite things? the fluke is almost unrecognizable by sight and when the dish first shows up, you're asking yourself "what idiot ordered a pile of quinoa for dinner?" but then you realize the little grains are actually the fluke and they're concealing a creamy center vat of uni and the whole thing tastes like the sea and all is right with the world.
- fried arroz negro with squid and romanesco - I'd like to eat bowls of this please! excellent soccarat on the bottom so when you scraped it up, you had crunchy bits scattered through every bite.
- burrata with salsa verde and charred bread - I know, it's the dish everyone raves about and I'm pretty sure Barack and Michelle ordered two when they came but honestly? I'm calling out POTUS's foodie cred. This was my least favorite dish of the night. Burrata was good because, well, cheese, but the entire dish didn't taste like anything. 
- lamb ribs with chermoula and honey - this is a lamb lover's lamb; only order if you like knowing exactly what animal you're inhaling and you like to gnaw the bits of meat off bone. The chermoula is spicy and cuts the fat nicely and the honey is just sweet enough to approximate sucking down baby back ribs.
- ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo - 1. have never met a dump I didn't like and these are no exception - light, fluffy, melt in your mouth, yada yada yada 2. the broth on this dish was so good we all surreptitiously drank it with our spoons before realizing no one at the table qualified as polite company. Then we just drank from the bowl, as the broth tastes like liquid artichokes
- pork with burnt cucumbers and leeks - I'm now a convert of cooked cucumbers. 

It can be hard to get into and it's a very small restaurant so if you're going with a large group, definitely make reservations.

Hands down my new favorite restaurant. I sat at the bar for about an hour as i waited for my friend since she was saving the world up in Harlem. Bartenders were super friendly along with people just sitting at the bar.

It's a bit difficult to locate since the entrance is so discrete and narrow. This place has always been on my list but after my sad visit to Narcissa a few days earlier, I was nervous that I would be disappointed from going to another highly acclaimed restaurant but boy was i wrong. This was the PERFECT friday night dinner that i needed after a long week at work. 

We got the
- Cod and potato croquettes which were perfectly fried and it didn't feel too greasy or heavy. Reminded me of cape cod. 
- The raw beef tartar : this had to be the best raw beef tartar i've eaten. There was a unique crunch to the tartar and the dish was just light and refreshing
- the rizzo negro was probably the best dish i had. If anything, i would probably order three of these next time and call it a night. The rice reminded me of like the rice at the bottom of a bimbimbap bowl. crisp. and the seafood? flavor didn't overwhelm.
- the lamb- GAME-Y and tender. just the way that i love my lamb. It was a bit seasoned too much so it was a tad bit salty but. it was delicious.
- the pork- so tender, cooked perfectly, and the cucumbers were marinated perfectly. 

It can get a bit pricey given that it is tapas but it is totally worth it. I will definitely come back here and try the other dishes.

I go for value - although it was delicious, I find the place too expensive.  The dumplings were good (on the salty side) with a string mushroom tasting broth.  What makes it special are the wafer thin circles of some carb covering and laying on top of the dumplings.  But for the price, I can see it under $23.

Everything in the menu was high including the salads.

Ambience? Basic. You open the outer door and immediately are the steps.

Food was new, delicate, interesting, more pungent and not too sweet. Service was great, hostess was informative and nice as well. A little too loud for my ears. We had oysters, ricotta dumplings, endive salad, lamb ribs, beef tartare (yum!), and strawberry sorbet (not my favorite). All the savory items we ordered I'd recommend.
Been several times hoping it will redeem itself. There's something about the service that lacks in a personal touch and makes the whole experience very awkward. Standard nyc trending food fare.
Brunch was a bust. Signature egg sandwich isn't all that it is cracked up to be. Seating is tight and uncomfortable.  Prices are generally quite high.  Dinner is the better play.

It was my second visit to the restaurant. For the first visit, I tried popular dishes like burrata, beef tartare, fried arroz with squid and ricotta dumplings, and it was a definitely five-star experience. The second visit, however, came as a huge disappointment as new dishes were too experimental (we saw what's the intention but didn't enjoy the taste) and a couple of dishes we tried again were worse than the first visit. I wanted to love this restaurant because the first impression was so great, but I don't think I will go again.

I took my fiance here for her birthday - her favorite food is Gnocchi and this is Platt's recommendation to the best in the city. I couldn't agree more. We ordered 2 dishes of it, as everything is almost tapas style but boy, I remember that taste like it was the other day. The other dishes were very good too, but come for the Gnocchi.

Fair-skinned, brown-haired woman working behind the bar on Tuesday night was a huge b**ch and very rude to guests (mocking guests within earshot). Her behavior unfortunately left us feeling a bit ripped off. Other than that, the service, food and drink was amazing (albeit pricey)!

I dined at Estela with a friend last night and I have to say it was a nearly perfect experience! First off, the hostess was extremely friendly. I had a nice cold glass of Lambrusco at the bar while waiting for the table to be ready. Estela has a very impressive wine list - both wines by the glass and by the bottle. For dinner, we decided on a Barbera, which was wonderful. 

All of the food was absolutely delicious - only one small complaint. We started with the croquetas which were perfect - fried perfectly, not greasy, and accompanied by a silky aioli. Next, we went for the kohlrabi and apple salad, which really blew me away. I had always been curious to try kohlrabi and theirs was done perfectly in my opinion - sliced thin with apples, hazelnut, and mint. It was a refreshing starter. We then continued on to the fried arroz negro and the swordfish with celery, pine nuts, and raisins. THE ARROZ NEGRO WAS AWESOME. JUST GET IT. The swordfish was cooked perfectly, BUT it should honestly have been called CELERY with swordfish, pine nuts, and raisins. The dish was completely overpowered by the celery. It would have been a nice accompaniment, but it just took over. Everything on the plate tasted good, but the ratio definitely needs to be altered. Lastly, we ordered the sweet potato dessert. I don't even know what it was to be honest but it was amazing. The dessert menu doesn't look that appealing at first glance and it lacks menu descriptions, but order the sweet potato. It is worth it. It was kind of like a sweet potato cake infused with rum and vanilla and I don't know what else, but it was the perfect ending to the meal. 

In terms of service, the waitress was nice, but not overly friendly or helpful so this might be an area for improvement. However, overall, I had a wonderful time at Estela. It is a bit pricey, but well worth it for an intimate dinner with friends or even a nice date. Treat yourself and go!

Had a nice dinner at Estela last night. The hostess was very nice and remembered my friends name as i walked in and said i was meeting someone. No big deal, but not needing to look at the book and just remembering off hand is the sign of a great hostess!

Quite busy on a Tuesday night at 930, mazel tov. 

I had been craving sausage all day, so we started with the sausage and the cod fritters. Both were delicious. i would recommend both. Had the Celery Negroni to start which was also a winner.

We then got the kohlrabi and apple salad which was very light and refreshing and supprisingly one of the best salads I've had in a long time. Different and comforting at the same time.

Then we got the black rice which as you will probably read in every other review was really great. Get it.

I would pass however on the Swordfish. I just didnt really understand it. The fish was cooked perfectly, however it was just in a pool of celery to the point of it being more of a celery dish. The sauce it was served above was good, but honestly a bit heavier/richer than i expected, but good. I think less celery or maybe a different way of preparing the celery may be a good fix, but as of now it's not a dish I'd recommend.

I dont usually do dessert, but we had a lot of wine left ( which was delicious, great wine list!) so we went for the sweet potato dessert as recommended by our server. I was expecting a super sweet, cinnamon sugar-esc dish, but this was so much better than i could have expected. It was light on the taste buds in such a nice way that I got different waves of flavor as eating it. I would order it again, which says a lot as I'm not a dessert person.

All in all, it was a great meal. But the I don't really think it is a great value. Go if you have money to spend, or if you are serious about the industry and have at least 200 in the bank(aka me.)

PS If you dont like the price, dont let it affect your rating. Thats stupid. You can look at the prices before or when ordering. If its too much money, dont order it.

It's a hidden (literally) gem out there in Soho 
Fantastic food ,we had the arroz negro,lamb ribs ,ricotta ravioli and salsa verde buratta.
Right size ,right flavor ,definitely needs to try the rest of the menu .
Good place to grab drinks before dinner.

This is a lovely spot, right in the heart of the lower east side, bordering soho~

It can get quite crowded inside this cozy little hearth, but it always feels nice and intimate with delicious bites!

Estela makes me wish I were a cow so I could have 4 different compartments in my stomach, one for each dish. 

I got the burrata on charred bread with salsa verde, and shared a side of the cod and potato croquettes. I've never thought about eating burrata with salsa verde. I guess that's why they charge the $16: for thinking it up for you...

Friends got the lamb and the biscuit, both of which were thoroughly enjoyed and quickly consumed. I've been waiting a long time to eat here, but probably not as long as my friend waited for his lamb that came 15 minutes after everyone else's dish arrived, one of which, was the same lamb dish...where's the logic in that?

But I guess I didn't come here to be logical. I came here to eat.
EEEEK. Heard how amazing this place was so went with a friend and we both hated the food! Awful. how disappointing! :(

The food is divine.  Small, scrumptious portions that delight at every bite.  The oysters were the best I've ever had anywhere, plump and so fresh.  The Kohlrabi with apple, hazelnuts and mint is unbelievably savory.  Unfortunately, the noise level is so out of control unpleasant that I doubt I will ever go back.  It's a pity because I could see returning there again and again, and bringing others to enjoy this unusually delicious food.  But my fellow diner and I had to lean over the table and scream at each other in order to have a conversation.  Not ideal for the digestive system.  This is not a place to go for the luxury of fine dining and conversation.

Besides the fact that it was tucked upstairs on the second floor and a couple of people passed it a couple of times, the whole evening was pretty amazing!  The place was too dark for pictures and the best part was they gave us so much food for a party of 8!

I considered giving a five but it wasn't quite that good.  We had the beef tartare, burrata, ricotta dumplings, kohlrabi, and lamb ribs.  The first and last were probably the standouts, especially the ribs.  We tried four different reds by the glass and were happy with them all.  Definitely plan to go back.

Easily the best meal I had during my last visit to NYC. The service was lovely, and despite not having a reservation they managed to squeeze three of us in near to the bar for dinner and drinks. The wine list was terrific, a tight little selection by the glass with some unnusual drops to match different parts of the meal.

I loved the food - classic flavours and ingredients prepared in fresh and innovative ways. Every dish was beautiful to look at and was a textured and balanced to eat. Having three of us meant we could order a wide selection and try a little of everything. I especially loved the burrata, escabeche and a sprightly witlof salad. Perfect for the warm summer evening on which we visited.

Came with three friends (including a NYT written-up chef who made the rez) and proceeded to order what seemed like over half the menu. The server had explained that top section was small plates (like olives), and the whole lower dishes were either medium or large -- although even she was hard pressed to say where one ended and the other began. When our last dish arrived, my wife, not even a huge eater, muttered, "That's it??"   

Perhaps they could benefit from reorganizing the menu, but in the end none of the tiny plates seemed transcendent enough to warrant the extravagant bill. Yes the dumplings were pillowy soft, but surprisingly mild in flavor. The same could be said for the blandish steak tartare, noteworthy apparently only for its distinctive crunch. The burrata was my favorite and a worthy use of sorrell, but in the end, Estela left us hangry and ripped off for what it was -- a little bit of bang for a whole lot of buck.

One of the more memorable meals I have had in a long time.  We loved every dish we ordered including - mussels on toast (I was hesitant to order this, but so glad we tried it), steak tartare, ricotta dumplings. Looking forward to returning very soon!

Great food and environment.  It's a little small but that sets the mood to be more intimate.

Went with a group of 5 and ordered:

1.  Tartare - must get.  Prepared very well and easily shareable.
2.  Burrata - another must get.  The flavors are very unique and another item that can easily be shared with a group.
3.  Lamb ribs - these were OK; not a must get item but I still enjoyed them.
4.  Ricotta dumplings - for a table of 5, we got 2 orders.  These were done very well.  The pasta wasn't overcooked and held together well w/ the filling.
5.  Cod - So yummy.
6.  Steak - EVEN MORE YUMMY.  I could have eaten this all day.  For 1 order, it's about 2 bites per person so ration accordingly.  Or go with some friends who don't like steak as much and you'll be a steak monster for the night.  Wonderful flavor, great texture.  Would come back and order this for sure.
7.  Panna cotta - wasn't anything to brag about.  But a good way to end the night w/ something light.

Overall, I'd definitely come back.  The portions are small and half the menu is tapas style, so suggest going with a groupf of 4-5 to try as many things as possible.

There were some pros: the steak tartar is delicious and our server was a delight. 

But the cons, where to begin. Without being over simplistic the food was just bad and overly priced. I think an average amount you would like spend at Estela is $50 per person on just food with no tax, tip, or beverages. That's fine but you should definitely feel full. 

The steak tartar was tiny, the burrata, again, was tiny and was sitting in some sort of grass broth, the endive salad seemed like a joke it was so small. We ordered two mains that were essentially the size of what traditional small plate was. I felt like I was in an SNL skit about tiny food. 

But even above the size: the burrata was salty with a bizarre, the endive salad was just endives with some strong cheese underneath (why underneath), the pork was just foul and again hidden underneath a couple of pieces of cucumber. 

They definitely hired a great PR person for this place but don't believe the hype.
Worth the visit! Loved the ambiance, service, and adventurous food. Would highly recommend the beef tartare with sunchoke and the ricotta dumplings.

We had an extremely great bottle of red wine here thanks to our amazing sommelier, Josh!!!!

Josh's astrological composition is Taurus Sun, Leo Rising, Sagittarius Moon.  

I trust him with my life!!!!!!!

I didn't like the menu. It was not that appealing. Food was good. Service slow and the venue is packed. We waited 30' despite having a reservation. Bar was tight. I cannot imagine going back. I also cannot imagine why this place has as many stars as it has given all of the other amazing restaurants in NYC huh????

Interesting food, great atmosphere, friendly servers. The food was consistently presented in a minimal, no frills manner (almost everything we ordered was formed in a ring mold). I realize this places importance on the flavors because they must make up for what the presentation is seemingly be lacking. Good thing that everything we ordered had an intricate and surprising flavor profile. I thoroughly enjoyed the egg salad with dried mojama (cured tuna) flakes and deliciously light and crisp rye crackers. The grapefruit, frozen yogurt and Campari dessert was amazing and I was pleasantly surprised by the few small pieces of lovage that were mixed in. We also ordered the pork with charred baby lettuce and while the flavors were delicious the pork was so undercooked I was uncomfortable eating it. My husband and I ordered five plates to share and it was enough food. Would like to return but probably only for a special occasion due to the expense.

Estela is an alternative to every Sunday brunch you get in NYC. When I got tired of French toast, eggs Benedict, waffles, Mediterranean, all you can drink cocktail, I am so grateful there are some more choices.  
Its food is light in character, it's rich in flavor, it's comfortable to eat, just like the decor easy to take in.
There is something humble about the food, the place that doesn't shout exotic or wow. But the taste lingers. Although the price of the food, the staff are very gentle and welcoming. I'll come back as soon as I can.

Absolutely delicious. Loved the rice, the beef tartare, the chocolate dessert, everything. 
For a romantic dinner, it s a little too loud.

On a busy, unattractive stretch of Houston this restaurant is a narrow flight of stairs above street level. It is packed and boisterous. The wine list is expensive and they have nice specialty cocktails. The menu has a plates of different sizes all meant to share. Our waiter suggested 9 plates for the four of us. The normal sided mains ranged in price from mid-20s to mid-30s for the steak. My barometer for how great a meal is, is how much can I remember without looking at the menu. Here's what I remember about Estela. Our middle aged, snarky, condescending waiter did not want to make any suggestions but instead used the old "if it's good enuf to be on the menu.." Line. Good servers are the ambassadors of the restaurant. They can make or break a customers experience. When they are patronizing and curt and too cool to speak with 4 diners that genuinely enjoy going out to dinner, it taints everything about the experience. Some bites, the steak and the burrata in particular were excellent. Others, kohlrabi salad and black rice were solid. The rest I can't remember. What I do recall is we left without ordering dessert and that wasn't a conscious effort but our time was done and we ended up paying $100 a person with each of us having a cocktail and a glass of wine. There's too many great places - old and new - in New York City for servers to act like they're too good to give an opinion or answer a question. If you are annoyed by patrons who want to engage you about the product you serve then you are in the wrong field. Estela had the distinct taste of a place that doesn't recognize its stature in the grand scheme. Show me a restaurant with good food and Nasty service and I'll show you a restaurant with a short lifespan.

I recently had a lovely experience at Estela for brunch! Estela is a great option when you're not in the mood for the eggs/pancake/etc staples for a typical brunch but still want something great on the weekend during the day. I had the frittata which was not what I was expecting but was great nonetheless. If you're vegetarian, your options may be limited but what I had was still delicious. The drinks here are also very strong and very good. 

The atmosphere here is lively and comfortable and the service is attentive and helpful. I highly recommend getting a reservation if you can (they use the Resy app) to avoid waiting as it's a pretty popular option downtown. I look forward to coming here again to try more dishes!

I love Estela.  It's one of my favorite restaurants right now and I go out to eat a LOT.  Great, innovative dishes that sometimes sound weird until you taste them.  Great steak tartare, gnocchi and pretty much everything is great and you won't go wrong.  Can be hard to get a reservation but great to come and sit at the bar.  Also awesome cocktails.

Super-delicious food. Started with beautiful crudo with sea urchin followed by an incredible mackerel dish served with yogurt & beets. Next came exotically spiced lamb ribs which were amazing with a glass of amonitllado sherry. We finished with the rib-eye that was accompanied by a complex paprika-based powder - really unique and memorable! Don't miss the cheese with dessert wines. Yummy stuff.

Estela is a perfect date night spot.  It is dark, cozy, and romantic.  We had a great time, loved the cocktails and the tapas dishes to share.  You MUST have the ricotta dumplings and the arroz negra!  I must say that the brownie dessert was disappointing but not so much that it ruined my experience.  Worth and try for some yummy food, would return for the quality of food for sure!

Good, but absolutely not worth making the LIST!!!I have been to so many better places in the city, I truly do not know how this place made the list. Nothing was memorable, nor service, nor food, tx but No TX!

Went for dinner and was good.  I suppose after all the press/top 100 restaurants etc, I had raised my expectations a little to high, which is maybe unfair.
It felt like a really good bistro, with pretty simple, clean, well executed dishes.  We tried the beef tartare, sea urchin, chicken hearts, lamb ribs and steak.  Alll were good, but nothing mind blowing.   I would recommend, but wouldn't necessarily be rushing back.  Atmosphere was buzzing, but maybe a little too loud.  Would be good for a group.

This is a lovely little restaurant with a great atmosphere but hidden on a horrible main street.  Our emotions went from frustration at not being able to see the door on E. Houston, to concern that any establishment on that drag would not be good, to delight when inside.

The food, with one exception, was excellent to breathtaking.  We had a portion of pickled carrots as an appetizer - very lightly pickled and served with a subtly tasty version of soured cream and some celery salt-like condiment.  It would have been better if our first course had not arrived seconds later, thus we felt slightly pressured to eat up.

That first course was sensational, and simple.  It was a salad of celery, pistachios, blue cheese and mint - a wonderfully subtle and light mixture of fresh flavors.  Next up (unfortunately just as we were starting the salad) was a burrata on charred toast with a salsa verde.  This was good, but perhaps not as good as burrata dishes I've enjoyed elsewhere.  The toast was made soggy by the sauce and the flavors were perhaps too subtle.

The savory highlight of the evening was fried black rice with squid - a creamy rich and subtly flavored delight, looking sensational on the plate and tasting even better.  By this stage the service had slowed down to a sensible pace and we were left to enjoy this wonder, and to savor every last mouthful.

Sadly, the lowlight of the evening, and the reason for four stars rather than five, was the lamb ribs with charmoula.  These were, quite simply, not nice on many levels.  We switched from dishes which were subtly flavored to this bomb of salt and spice, which was all you could taste.  The lamb had apparently been brined with salt and cooked through.  There was no discernible lamb taste remaining, just this overwhelming salty/spicy taste.  Actively unpleasant.

Finally, the restaurant served a panna cotta with vinegar and honey - this was a complete redemption as it was the most wonderful mixture of sweet and sour.  Fantastic.

The wine list was extensive and, as so often in NYC, over-priced.  We operated at the cheap end and had a well-chosen St. Nicolas de Bourgeuil which complemented our food well.

4.5 stars.

I can't remember the last time I had brunch. Has it been a year? Two years? Regardless, I can count the number of brunches I've had on one hand. Translation: my brunch game, is weak. And I don't mean weak for someone living in New York, because brunch is a way of life here. I mean it in the most all-encompassing sense. You know that really uncomfortable emotional dilemma where you know you have a problem, but you haven't yet figured out how to find the willingness to do something? That's me and brunch. Until Estela. I agreed to brunch. I agreed to two meals in one. And my life was forever changed.

Made a reservation for brunch here at 12:30 on a Sunday. The place was moderately busy and continued to fill up during the next hour or so. I came here with a brunch fanatic who very confidently assured me Estela's brunch was one of the most adventurous ones out there. I have literally no way to verify this given my limited experience, but who am to disagree? This food was outstanding. 

As I had hoped, our server suggested sharing, if we were open to it ("If"??? Don't insult me.). After drinking way too much coffee, we ordered:

-Toast w/ lardo and jam (A-/A)
I'm very into eating healthy so the fact that I tried this at all is pretty shocking. The lardo, as you can see in my picture, is basically just a layer of fat. I mean technically it's a type of pork, but for all intents and purposes, it is a big ole slab of fat. And you know what? I'm American, and I think fatty food tastes great (how I feel about myself after eating it is a different story). This was a perfect way to start our meal: salty, sweet and crunchy. Perfect to nibble on as we downed cup after cup of coffee. 

-Endive w/ walnuts, anchovy, and ubriaco rosso (A-/A)
I am going to overlook the fact that the preparation of this dish was incredibly odd. Calling it a "preparation" at all seems like I'm giving it too much credit. The endives were endives. Okay. But all of the good stuff was hiding underneath - was that the point? In any case, the good stuff was more than good. I don't think I've ever tried ubriaco rosso cheese before but it was really yummy and made the dish for me. It's a hard, strong cheese with a nutty flavor, so obviously paired quite well with the walnuts.

-Frittata w/ stinging nettles (A)
Okay, I had to laugh when I saw this on the menu. Stinging nettles?? How ridiculous can you get? Is this like poison ivy? Am I going to get hives on the lining of my stomach? Is the sting supposed to prick my taste buds such that they're more attuned to subtleties of flavor? Our server just replied: "it's good, it's got a nice herbaceous flavor - a little bitter". Completely unfazed by the fact that I was sitting there, incredulous (at that point we obviously needed to order it). This all said, this frittata was light, fluffy and really yummy. It's the smallest of the egg dishes here, so I'd suggest sharing a few things along with this, if it catches your fancy like it did mine. Balanced out our heavier egg dish quite well. It comes with some sort of yogurt sauce as well as some type of onion. All components together made for a very well-rounded dish.

-Eggs w/ beans, croutons, mojama, and harissa (A/A+)
So much more than its simple description. Mojama, as I have just learned, is a kind of salt-cured tuna. So it looks almost like prosciutto or something else you'd get on a charcuterie board. As you can see from the picture, it's quite alluring on top of that perfectly-cooked egg. I thought the croutons would be a bit odd here, but they soaked up a lot of the flavor (the harissa in particular) and added a bit of crunch to an otherwise texturally uniform dish. I could've done without the beans, if I had to eliminate one ingredient. The egg and the mojama though - there's a combination for the ages. 

My only complaints:
a) Our server gave us exactly zero minutes to think about what she wanted. While she didn't seem overtly exasperated at our indecision, she returned every minute on the minute (that's an EMOM, in gym-speak) to ask if we were ready. Maybe try three minutes and then we'll actually have time to think! Otherwise, she was nice enough, and our food came out quickly.
b) Tiny tables, not much space between them. This isn't the case for the whole establishment, but we were cramped. Not optimal. Thankfully, those dining adjacent to us weren't snobby/obnoxious/any variation of these things.
Estela is a great all around place to come in with a well deserving friend and take em out somewhere. All their food is great, even the salads are amazing! will come here again

My boyfriend and I had a great brunch here this morning. The vibe is super hip and we definitely didn't feel cool enough to be eating there but we carried on anyway. The tables are really close together so getting in and out was a bit of an ordeal but that's not really a big deal. 

We ordered the English muffin with whitefish, the eggs with beans and mojama (salt cured thinly sliced tuna) and the French toast. The English muffin with whitefish was DELICIOUS. I took the onion off of mine, but that's just personal preference. I'm usually not a fan of whitefish salad but this was delicious - not too salty or fishy. Not your typical Jewish deli whitefish. My boyfriend loved the eggs with beans. The eggs were cooked well and the dish was an interesting mix of ingredients. The mojama is really salty but it helps cut the spiciness of the rest of the dish. It seems to be a popular dish but it wasn't for me. The French toast though was phenomenal. The top is brûléed so it had this really delicious crunch on top and the creme anglaise is the perfect addition. 

Also their coffee was great. I would definitely recommend!

This place is incredible, I personally love the lamb ribs and beef tar tar. Full on amazing. Estela isn't too fancy or casual, it's one of those places that are In between. If your in the mood for some American, Italian or even tapas food, this is the place to go!

It's been a long time since I've given 5 stars.  And I want to apologize in advance, I do not have any food porn photos.  You see, I was just too busy enjoying the food and company. 

So, the food is...exquisite!  And I'll say this is THE RESTAURANT OF THE YEAR for me.

The servers are...detailed!  My water glass was always full and our table was always clean and wiped down quickly before serving the next dish.

Ok back to the food, they are all shareable.  We loved all the dishes but the ones which stood out were the BEEF TARTARE, BURRATA and the SQUID INK RICE. I really don't want you to limit yourself by just having those dishes because I feel all of chef Ignancio Mattos' dishes deserve equal amount of attention and are well thought out.

The reason why I give this place such high ratings is because chef Ignancio is able to produce common entrees that most restaurants have on their menu and find a way to pair with local ingredients of the season with a little twist of his own majestic flavoring.  Flavors are clean, presentation, execution, and service are spot on.

Fantastic service, and everything we had was sooooooo good. Squid ink rice and ricotta dumplings were divine. I loved the lamb, but it's not for everyone -- very heavily spiced (not just "spicy" but spiced, it's very flavorful) which I loved but I think might overwhelm some. We had the chocolate cake for dessert, which was soooo good and very distinctive, not like any other chocolate cake I've had in texture or flavor. My only warning is that the menu prices can be misleading -- each plate is 22-26 dollars(ish), and it's tapas style, so you want to order 2 or maybe even 3 per person. That gets pricy fast. It was worth it, but don't go thinking your entree will be 24 bucks and be unpleasantly surprised.
Interesting menu but food was just ok.  Nice trendy spot in nolita for brunch and bottomless coffee, but not sure I would rave over the food

I visited Estela with a friend for brunch last weekend. I have to say the location is great just a a block or so away from the train and the restaurant itself is nice, I like the bar and we were seated right away. The food is not too expensive but the drinks seem overpriced. I ordered the eggs with beans which was about 3 stars, I liked the egg and the thinly sliced salmon which I thought was fairly unique but there was too much onion for me to give this dish and place more stars.

I truly hated this restaurant, where we went on a Friday night. Food is way below its reputation, not even one OMG moment. But the worse, by far, was the deafening noise of the place, it looks like they intentionally left the walls and ceiling bare (concrete) to make sure this tiny space would be super-loud. If you can appreciate food while having to shout over the din, that's your place.

The food
-quail- good not special 
-steak : nothing special, the meat was fibrous- not worth it. For the price, the quality of meat should be much higher. 
- monkfish - boiled overpriced average dish - not worth it.
- beef tartare- delicious!

Drinks
Beer- good and can find it elsewhere.
Trinidad cocktail- delicious

Atmosphere- typical soho/ village vibe

Overall we spent a lot for a little food that was mostly ok not great.  Not a good value proposition - we actually feel ripped off.

I think this is my favorite restaurant in my neighborhood.  It's on Houston St and close to Broadway, which is random and not exactly the prettiest block but the place is on the 2nd floor so it's tucked way and feels cozy.  Every dish was innovative and perfect.  You know that the chef paid a lot of attention to every ingredient to create the dishes.  You also can tell that the chef is cool because of the tasteful ambiance and stylish crowd (and they got Aesop handsoap).  Someone I know did their video too. Humble brag.  
https://www.nowness.com/story/anatomy-of-a-dish-estela?utm_source=email&utm_medium=mobile&utm_campaign=share

I visited in October 2015 and enjoyed Beef tartare with sunchoke, as well as the Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo. The beef was silky, the dumplings light and fluffy. The wine by the glass selections were also excellent. But it was packed when I initially arrived, so the noise level is high if you're trying to have a conversation. Try to come at 10 pm when I did and you'll have less noise and more space to breathe and relax.

Nice cosy lil place. I went here on snowmageddon for brunch and it felt great to settle in and get a few dishes to share. The place has a really nice feel to it.

The food is really well prepared and each dish was exquisite. Have a look at the photos and u'll get what i mean....

I was dissapointed by the portion size. Each dish was 15 to 25 bucks on average and they were relatively bite size.....wasnt impressed.

Unless you order two of these small dishes per person, u will walk out of here hungry, guaranteed.

Couldve been four stars but i was tempted to give it two, so went with somewhere in between.

Some of the best bites I've had all year.

The lamb ribs with charmoula and honey were exquisitely tender and flavourful on both visits, and will always be on my list of "must haves" for this restaurant.  The cured fluke with sea urchin was a brilliant bite to start the meal, with the surprisingly generously-sized pieces of mussels in the mussels escabeche on toast a great way to follow.  The beef tartare was also an amazing demonstration of highlighting freshness and textures, which makes choosing which of the three (since the lamb ribs are a given, right?) to enjoy even more difficult.

The kohlrabi with apples, hazelnuts and mint was a surprise hit our first visit there, but replaced with a celery, raisins, pistachios and blue cheese dish which we did not try.  The endive dish was nicely balanced and a walnut-lover's haven, but the kohlrabi will still be one of the few meat-less dishes I will still think back about.

The steak with king trumpets and taleggio was undeniably tasty, but $37 for two pieces of meat that probably summed up to a few ounces?  Yes, we pay a premium for good food and well-sourced products, but the price tag for this particular dish seemed a bit over the top.  

And for dessert?  I'll always love their simple yet decadent panna cotta, and will always look forward to finishing my meal with a bowl.

Cozy little restaurant with excellent food. The mussels were my favorite, one bite filled with flavor. The tartare with sunchokes was great as well. The sunchokes brought a crispiness to this classic dish and made it original for Estela. We had more than half the menu and were pleased with each dish. The portions were smaller, more like tapas to me. We decided against the steak, $37 for 4.5 ounces is where I draw the line. Still, I must reiterate everything we had was of great quality.

A great spot for a date to pick up some bites and wine :)

I am so disappointed in my experience tonight. After Estela opened I was there regularly.  It's been a while since I went in and I'm sure I'll never go back. The food was okay but not worth the price. The bartenders and hosts were cold. Not welcoming, not knowledgeable about the menu and didn't help create a memorable experience. The price point is too high for the service and food quality. Try another place in the neighborhood.

Had dinner here with my wife last weekend. I'd highly recommend Estela if you are not paying or if money has little value to you. We had 5 dishes including the tartare, lamb ribs (3) and burrata, which were all excellent. The pork was just average, but insanely priced at $32 for 4oz of pork shoulder. We passed on the 4.75oz portion of hanger steak for $37 since we could make this at home for $3. Like many new restaurants in NY, the menu is devoid of a single dish that might have a food cost of over ~$5. The wine list is limited and also aggressively priced. Service was attentive and fairly speedy, although the ambiance of a second floor apartment building was underwhelming.
Best breakfast sandwich of my life. Putting avocado, pancetta, and egg on a danish pastry is nothing short of genius.

Though I very much appreciated the inventiveness of these dishes, small details were overlooked that could have definitely improve the overall experience. 

Setting: Small and intimate, booths along the walls and small tables. No complaints, nothing extraordinary! 

Service: Impeccable. Our waitress was so nice and helpful and gave great answers when we asked about dishes or wine. 

Food: 

Marinated Olives: good, but can't really go (too) wrong here 

Beef Tartare: Probably one of the best parts of the meal, a decidedly un-french take on beef tartare with none of the typical capers or mustard. Fresh and light with crunchy bits that were delicious. Served with great crusty bread. 

Mussels on toast: very very weird. Couldn't decide if I liked it or not. But I gave it points for inventiveness. As our waitress explained, mussels are flash cooked, then lightly pickled. Flavors were alright, it was more of a texture thing. under seasoned.

Burrata on toast: Good. Cheese is delicious, always. needed salt. Soaked in some sort of herb sauce/juice

Black Rice: great texture, good flavor, not too fishy. A bit over seasoned. 

Lamb: decent flavor but was crusted too heavily with seasoning, very overpowering. 

Candied squash: very cool dessert with an unfamiliar texture. flavors were good for the most part and it was fun to eat. however there was a pool of Cynara-Infused sauce at the bottom that added a little too much bitterness. 

Overall good, had fun trying lots of dishes but wouldn't come back.

Food is overrated, undersized, and overpriced. The fluke/uni dish was interesting in concept but monotonous in texture and presentation. The priciest items on the menu, including the lamb ribs, monkish and pork, were ridiculously small. I've never paid so much in NY for three tiny lamb ribs, each no longer than my index finger; must frustrating of all, in the small bites of lamb I chewed mostly a dry crust with too much seasoning and a tremendous amount of gristle. The pork dish had the same problem in being tough, though I appreciated its presentation. I think the kitchen handles fish quite nicely, but needs to work on making red meat more palatable. Overall there is too much pretension and cost, and not enough delivery of flavor and satisfaction.

My favorite restaurant in NY. All the babes, all the foods. 

Complaints about the food being weird are weird. If you think the food's weird, go back to The Dutch or Five Leaves and enjoy your shitty avocados and kale, dumb ass. And have a mimosa while you're at it. 

Basically, if Estela was someone I was dating, they'd be the one to help me explore my food sexuality and pushing my limits while putting me in a familiar and comfortable place.

this restaurant has such great potential - inventive food, intimate ambiance. the reviews fluctuate so much i think because of the servers. if you get a great server who is friendly and guides you well with the menu, you can have a great experience. unfort, i got the German waitress who wasn't either attentive or helpful. she may be a wonderful server and could have had an off night. but for these prices, the staff shouldn't have off nights for paying customers.  she checked on us very infrequently, was not helpful with menu choices, and completely off with how much we should order (we ended up ordering too little).  glad others have had a better experience.

I was really excited to do brunch here after reading such great reviews, but was disappointed. Our waitress was pretty rude, which is a red flag. Also, for a place offering brunch, they only serve coffee with milk.. No lattes, cappuccinos, etc. I had the omelette with caviar and creme fraiche, it was pretty bland and when we asked for pepper, we were told they could not offer any, so stuck with the bland omelette. Dessert was good but not memorable, we ordered one of all three offered. The best items were the burrata and ricotta dumplings which saved the meal, poor service, and upped my review to three stars.

The food was absolutely delicious. The wine was amazing. The space is a tad cramped (maybe not designed very well). I know lots of NY places are small, but this was particularly bad. The hostess said our bar seats were available before the people had actually gotten up to leave so we spent a long time standing awkwardly in the middle of the only walkway past the bar waiting for them to leave while being in basically everyone's way. I'd say portions could be a tad better for the prices, but since it was so delicious, it mostly made it worth it.

Estela makes the best breakfast sandwich ever! The bien cuit croissant is amazing. Make sure you ask for the bacon extra crispy (the way it should be). The last time I went, the bacon was undercooked and chewy.

Ordered the burratta, $18 for a small portion with one piece of bread! Then had the fried rice with squid- $23. Again a very small portion with little squid included. Flavours were good but way over priced. Had two glasses of the Chenin blanc and the meal cost us $65 each and that was sharing both dishes. Much better value places in NYC. Nice atmosphere though.

Hidden gem in NYC! The food is out of this world and consistently good- every time I have dinner here it's a wonderful experience. Must try- mussels dish and squid ink rice. The wine list is impressive and they make great cocktails. This is definitely one of my favorite restaurants in Manhattan.

cocktails not worth the price tag
menu items were creative, yet unnattractive

So disappointing. I had wanted to try this place for a while. as I had heard such good things about the chef. 

I was really excited about the uni/fluke, as I love both of those proteins. But the preparation, while pretty, didn't do the ingredients justice. I could taste neither fluke nor uni. It was a waste of ingredients.  

Beef tartar was pretty good, but, you know, what beef tartar isn't?

The endive salad was really very tasty. Totally did not expect that. 

The ricotta dumplings were flavorless and could have benefited form some sort of sauce. 

The lamb ribs were completely over seasoned.

The steak was very good.

I would normally give a place of this quality 3 stars, but given all the hype, the price, and the stature of the chef, I am just giving it two.

Solid brunch spot with good options.

I stopped by as a party of four on a Sunday for brunch, and we split the toast with jam and lardo as a group, and the flavors went together very well. For my entree, I had the egg, pancetta, and avocado sandwich, which was hefty and also had great flavor as well. I also sampled the lamb ribs, which were very tender and tasty. It's a little bit busy and without a ton of space, but worth visiting for brunch if you can get in.

Estela was recommended to us for a date night dinner by a friend in the NY restaurant industry, so we went with high expectations.  Not a fan...

My first impression of the space was that it was very small, loud and very tightly packed and it didn't get better from that point.

We were met at the door by a hostess and since we didn't have a reservation were directed to the bar to wait for a table, which was expected to be at least a half hour.  Waiting isn't typically a problem and since we didn't have a reservation it was expected, except that there is not much space to wait at the bar (the bar is used for diners not for drinkers) so we uncomfortably stood behind the diners at the bar, got a drink and settled in for the wait.   We were seated at the bar after about an hour.  Now to say that the seats at the bar are tightly packed is an understatement.  You can easily share your neighbors food, wine, water and chair/stool.  To my astonishment Estela even seated someone on the corner of the bar, not next to the corner, they actually had the nerve to charge someone for sitting at the pointed corner of the bar !   The bar is tight to begin with, but selling the corner as a dinner seat made the bar feel that much more crowded.  

My date and I were not in any hurry and we let the staff know this when we started to order.
We started with the Egg Salad with Mojama.  It was  good, but it's egg salad.  I was disappointed because you really don't get much of the Mojama because they grate it, instead of thinly slicing it like Serrano ham. the Egg salad was good, but the grated mojama Meh!!!
Next we ordered the Mussels escabeche on toast.  It was good, but a difficult bite because of the construction of the dish.  the mussels were layered on chunky toast.  The flavors were good, but execution was clunky...

Next we ordered Fried arroz negro with squid and romesco and the Pork with burnt cucumbers.  The rice/paella was excellent and if I were to ever go back would be the one thing I would order again, but the Pork with burnt cucumbers and leeks was never delivered so I can't comment on the taste.
 
We were joking about the pork not appearing but it stopped being funny after 45 minutes.  No one really seemed alarmed that a dish was missing and we finally gave up and asked for the check.

 I give Estela an additional star for not charging me for the pork.  I know I never got it, but they were most likely trying to rush something out when we threw in the towel.  When I asked for the check they had of course removed any charge for the no-show pork.

Food for me is theater.  I eat out 3-4 times a week and will frequent places where I am made to feel comfortable.  I will frequent establishments where the food is just OK if I am offered a comfortable dining experience.  In a nutshell I will not be adding Estela to my rotation.

Small cramped space with small plates.  OK food, but not worth waiting for a table or a seat at the bar.

Great ambiance and waitstaff. Small place, but if you get there early enough, you can find a spot at the bar or be lucky enough to score a table. A+ to the ricotta dumplings and lamb ribs. However, skip dessert---while sweet potato with ice cream sounds intriguing, it was not very good.

You could say too crowded, too loud, or too few menu choices for a restaurant where plates are shared. 
But way too good to get anything but 5 stars. Ordinary-seeming  dishes come to life with innovative but subtle variation from what your palate expects. The creativity doesn't call attention to itself with drama,  contrast, or display. It calls attention to itself because it's delicious, superb, original.  Did I say delicious? It deserves repeating. Just make a reservation and go.

Amazing brunch spot in Soho!

Made the reservation through open table for a Sunday brunch. My friend and I went there after a morning work-out so we decided to have something healthier. We ordered oysters with yuzu sauce; egg, pancetta, and avocado sandwich; and, Panna cotta. I also got got to be happy, and my friend got a coffee.

Everything was DELICIOUS! Absolutely enjoyed the yummy oysters, one of the best I had in NYC. The sandwich is rich, creamy and very flavorful. Lastly, the Panna cotta - great contrast of flavors! (As a friend said "it's addictive!").

Definitely worth a visit.

a vertiable feast of tastes. small plates served in rapid sucession, four forks go flying into the middle of the table, slicing, nomming and mmmm'ing. in the midst, little chitchat and recaps, i love this, i didnt care for that, that really changed the way i knew that dish.

started with pickled carrots - my favorite vegetable - but it was mostly just sour and uninspiring. but whatever, cuz a fuckload of courses are coming up. its just that it took a while to really make me go mmmm.

like the cured fluke that came up next, that was really white and bland and forgettable. moving on...the beef tartare started to get me going. nothing like red meat and bread right. haha. 

the burrata is the self proclaimed specialty of this place so we ordered two, and yes, i get it. like this is totally the most inventive burrata iv ever had. i usually find it to be like eggs in spicy tomato sauce - a lot of red. this dish was distinctively green. giving it a completely different flavor and feel. like it was really fresh, almost a little cold. 

and it just kept getting better. a pork dish showed up that was buried in the lettuce. i skipped the rabbit food and greedily took 2 of the 5 pieces of pork. just do it swiftly so theres no awkwardness about it right. haha.

i always find that when you go out to these pricey group dinners is to never be the cheap one. because invariably the bill is split evenly or someone picks it all up, so you best eat whatever you want and try not to feel that dagger to your wallet. keyword, try. 

but i digress, because this black rice had arrived on the table. upon our collective oohs at the flavor, we learned it had squid ink in it, which made it even more enticing. this dish is why this place gets 4 stars. i love it when a restaurant reinvents a dish so simple and basic. like fucking rice. and you're at a table where everyone definitely ate at least 5 servings of it a week growing up, and each and everyone of us was like, holy shit, thats really good. an inventive take on rice. wonderful. 

just as things started getting too interesting, the main course procession ended and so wrapped it up with 3 desserts for the table. the sweet potato one was a turn up, like real talk, each bite into this moist "flan" cake or whatever was a kick of booze to the mouth. and there was a fruit one, sugary, like a red jolly rancher and another one that i honestly dont remember today. oh and i just remembered, we got the cheese plate too that was actually a real treat. i so couldv eaten more haha. 

which is a good transition to wrap up this review. sometimes forgettable but mostly memorable $75-80/pp meal (including tip). i just wish we werent so ravenous, cuz i couldnt take any pictures.

I was reading all the reviews here, amazing this, amazing that, so great, yada yada yada... 

I'm a brunch connoisseur, not a very good yelper but I'm out there checking out what's good and avoiding the not so good.  Estela isn't on top of my list of my top 10 spots to go for brunch.  Trust that I've been to many places. 

Ordered the egg, pancetta and avocado sandwich.  Asked for the pancetta on the side, it came with zero pancetta.  I asked where is it, waitress said "oh thought you didn't want it".  I said yes I want it she says she'll check if I can still get it.  I mean, I'm still paying for it right? 10-12 mins later I checked for my pancetta as I stopped eating another waiter came and said that they don't do that. They don't do what? I asked if they will charge me full price, I was told yes so why can't I get it on the side and not inside my sandwich? Is that too hard to do? Really?  8 mins later pancetta came... Almost burnt :(  I moved on...

The fluke came next, yeah that was unforgettable... Moving on... Again....

The saviour of the day? Or I should say saviour of the brunch? The panna cotta.  Thank goodness that lil situation happened or else it would be no stars for me.
Not your traditional menu selection of brunch food, but definitely a nice and tasty change. The toast with lardo and jam is yummy and the avocado/pancetta/egg sandwich was amazing.

So 3 weeks ago today (4/20), during a recent visit to NYC for dear daughter's spring break, I met a friend for a 7pm meal at Estela.  Let's just say from the start at street entry (the blue door with gold lettering with very little visibility what is inside since it is up a level), the tone is set for a appetizing dining experience.  I did make a reservation a few weeks prior, and glad I did since it was pretty packed the entire time I was there.

While waiting for my friend and the table, I sat at the bar and put myself in the barman's hands-- requesting nothing too sweet but also nothing too bitter.  He served me up the perfect pre-dinner cocktail, which he titled "Old Hickory".  Orange and Peychaud's Bitters, dry and sweet vermouth, ice, and fresh citrus & lemon peel (with some of the essential oils rubbed on the glass) made for some smooth drinking while I awaited my friend!

Once she arrived and we were seated at our table, we decided to go mostly for small plates so we could try more stuff! The Beef Tartare w/ sunchoke, Mussels Escabeche on Toast, and Burrata with Salsa Verde and Charred Bread were truly out of this world.  I think the one that sticks in my mind after all this time is the tartare!  The Endive, Walnuts, Anchovy, and Ubriaco Rosso was a little too bitter/ tasteless for me... likely because it followed all the other dishes.  As the server, I would have suggested this one to come out first but maybe she was thinking palate cleanser.  We couldn't leave without trying the ricotta dumplings (this preparation was with mushrooms and pecorino sardo) and they were delicious!  To wash down all this (mostly) tasty food on a warm spring night, I ordered 2 dry white wines-- a Chamiot (2014 Jacquere from Savoie, FR) and a Chardonnay (2014 A&M Tissot 'Patchwork' label from Jura, FR).

For dessert, we decided to go all out and try 2 of the 4 choices.  Both were splendid-- Panna Cotta with vinegar and honey, and Chocolate Cake w/ Whipped Cream.  Cake was not sweet and the whipped cream was also not sweetened, while the panna cotta's dueling flavors of acidic vinegar and sweet honey were light, refreshing, and on-point!  I indulged in a dessert wine, the A&M Tissot Macvin du Jura Rouge from FR.  Apparently I was on a French wine theme tonight.

Service was just what you'd expect for a place like this (unobtrusive, timely, and friendly) until my friend had to leave earlier than I was ready in order to meet a blind date for post-dinner drinks (she was expecting 2 hours as a reasonable catch-up period with me, but we just had so much to talk about!!).  After that, service got pretty lovely.  I felt bad holding the table and informed our server that I was happy to finish up dessert and wine at the bar so they could turn the table over.  The GM came over, said they were truly appreciative (there was now a line out the door which I didn't notice until I got up and made my way over the bar), and basically told me that drinks were on them at the bar.  I stopped at one glass as I really didn't feel like stumbling all the way back to the UWS via subway on heels to have the whole family see me arrive drunkety drunk.  But it was a lovely gesture!   

Quite enjoyed this foray into Soho!! :)

buck cocktail
i forgot the name. don't matter though... cocktails are not their strong suit. get some wine.

toast with lardo and jam
the jam changes, but what doesn't change is that this bread is WILD GOOD. you got to have powerful teeth though because the bread is real crusty.

burrata with salsa verde and charred bread
very clean tasting burrata. the salsa verde was grassy. not for me, but if you like grass, go ahead.

blood cake with onion marmalade and egg
if you like blood sausage, you'll like blood cake. if you don't, well... lol. i liked it.

eggs with beans, harissa, and mojama
these were some big ass beans! mojama is tuna that tastes like ham. so good, man.

egg, pancetta, and avocado sandwich
*skull emoji* *skull emoji* *skull emoji* estela is killing it.

lamb ribs with charmoula and honey
i had to google "charmoula". it's a north african marinade that probably includes herbs, oil, lemon juice, pickled lemons, garlic, cumin, and salt. word? all of that sounds delicious.

chocolate cake with whipped cream
estela, you are kind of short selling yourself here. this is the lightest chocolate cake i've ever had. it's delicious chocolate air covered in whipped cream. do it!

****

estela is on the cusp of 5 stars. estela is the tv on the radio of restaurants. they are not radiohead. come on now, but they are supremely good. i'm going to listen to "wolf like me" right now.

My friend strongly recommended this place to me, due to their fabulous yuzu oysters; unfortunately someone from our group did not eat raw oysters so we had to give up on that...nevertheless we were able to enjoy a bunch of other signature dishes.

We shared the toast with jam and lardo (the pork). Really impressed by their crunchy toast and that the jam was completely absorbed by the bread. I also enjoyed my white fish muffin - the fish roe was popping up in my mouth! My friend liked her avocado toast a lot as well, with the fact that egg yolk was melting!

Estela was packed the second it opened up at 11:30 for brunch, so a reservation is a must. But once you have enjoyed the great dishes (I will have to test out their dinner version, but so far so good!), every minute of wait would be paid off.

Went for brunch with my boyfriend and we both agreed that for the price what we ate was nothing special. I have heard a lot of people say this place is great so maybe it was just what we ordered or our personal preferences. 

-the BLT sandwich with avocado was good, but I've had better from other places at a much lower cost. The bread is a bit too buttery for a sandwich with mayo and avocado. $16
-the Ricotta dumplings were good! Great texture and good taste ~$22
-the Lamb ribs left a lot to be desired. 4 tiny ribs with not much meat and quite dry. They were very crispy but did not have enough meat on them to go along with the crispy crust, which was a bit too strong in flavor. We left 2 out of the 4 ribs. ~$24

Would not recommend to a friend or return.

Came here on a recent trip to NYC after reading positive reviews and it was all on point.  A cool location, great servers and great food. Started off with small olive plate, then had beef tartare and the burrata. The tartare was delicious but the burrata was excellent. The cheese was smooth and creamy, paired with the herb sauce and the charred bread, it was perfect.  Then we had the squid ink rice and the pork with charred leeks and cucumbers.  The rice is a real stand out, the briny flavour combined with texture from fried bits of something delish and hazelnuts with the calamari.  The pork was also great, the charred veg adding a lot of flavour.  Dessert was a grapefruit gelato but it wasn't just grapefruit gelato.  I'm still not really sure how it was constructed, but it was so refreshing on such a hot night. Highly recommend this place. Service was on point, charming staff stopping to chat and explain everything.

Had a fantastic meal on my own at the bar! The staff was extremely helpful in guiding my meal and attentive through the evening. The tartare is incredible! I'd go again just for this. The buratta was buratta and predictable. Their take was nice but I should have gone a different direction. The lamb ribs were delicious. Quite a fatty cut but incredible. Wish i could have tried more. Loved the atmosphere and the food. Excellent!!

Burrata dumplings, lamb, Black arroz with squids: amazing!!
Panacota and the chocolate cake for dessert are a must

Food is absolutely fantastic here and worth going with several people so you can share plates and try more. The beef tartar, burata and steak were definitely standouts.

Only thing keeping it from 5* is the price and you have to stay on top of reservations - they didn't call when a table was ready but luckily we poked our head in to check on the situation. The food is incredible so it was definitely worth it.

Ermagherd.

Had dinner here last July and it was phenomenal.  (In other news, I write reviews and leave them sitting in draft mode too long!)  The place is definitely busy yet unfussy, and the food is imaginative but approachable.  

My friend YT and I shared several dishes, starting with the endive salad, which I didn't expect to like but was wonderful! The endives are served individually and you basically create a lettuce-wrap style bite with the rest of the ingredients.  Then we had the black rice with squid and romanesco - another dish I didn't expect to like but ended up loving!  We also had the lamb ribs and the pork.  Everything was well done, a little different, but better, than expected.  Can't remember the two cocktails I had but they were boozy and to my liking.

I can't wait for another opportunity to visit Estela and try more of the menu... or maybe I'll be a bad girl and order the same things again!

I'm shocked that I didn't write a review for Estela the first time I dined here a year ago. But here we are, after Estela made it into the World's Top 50 Restaurants of the year. I revisited Estela last night to refresh my memory. 

Hidden yet shockingly good surprises are the name of the game here (including the restaurant itself). Go up the steps from Botanica Bar. Be prepared, it's tiny, packed, bustling, and can feel like everything's gone haywire. Hopefully you'll think that's part of the charm.
