It may be difficult to hear each other, but just cozy up closer and it will all be fine. 

The last official seating for reserved tables is at 10:30pm. My date and I were seated right on time. 

The cured fluke with sea urchin looked pretty plain, the white fluke neatly hiding the wonderful sea urchin below it. Lovely melding of flavors. Our favorites of the night were probably the lamb ribs with charmoula and honey, and the steak on a bed of lovely hashbrown-like potato and amazing chimichurri. 

I really loved how accessible everything looks and feels- simple, with a pleasant twist. Our otherwise sweet server made a lot of mix ups throughout the night, but I'm sure everyone's just had a long night. So we drank and we were merry, and it was just grand.

We came here on a weekend after I saw a couple reviews from local food critics saying this was a mainstay. We sat at the bar so we could get a breeze from the big open window. We ordered the burrata, fluke, squid arroz negro, and swordfish. The fluke was a nice standout dish and uniquely paired with kohlrabi and avocado. The arroz was really salty and had tiny pieces of squid that was hard to pick out from the rice. The "green pesto" that came with the burrata seemed like a simple mint blend and didn't offer much beyond that. We ordered four dishes and if it wasn't for the rice, we would've left hungry. For the amount of money paid I would either expect better flavors or more food. I've definitely had similar types of cuisine that really wow'd with ingredients, flavor, and presentation for a lot less money.

The food is fantastic. Each dish we had at dinner was excellent, rich in flavors and visually appealing. For food, I'd give this place a rating of 4.5 stars. But I am giving it only three stars for the following reason...
The disappointment I experienced with the hostess the following day at brunch time -- My friend who had dinner there with me dropped an item she was carrying in her purse while she was there and didn't realize she didn't have it until she got home. So early in the morning, she called and left a message and also sent an email. I was back in the neighborhood in the afternoon, so I stopped by to see if they had found the item. When I asked the hostess, she said that she had received the voice message and the email and that they had not found the item. And she attempted to dismiss me quickly by saying that if they find it, they will call. However, I was not dismissed that easily. So she finally said "let me get you the manager". When the manager came over, the manager said "oh yes, we have it". Had I not been insistent, we would have had to make at least one more trip to the restaurant! Considering the price of the meal there, that kind of treatment even if the hostess was busy trying to seat guests, is very disappointing.

Estela? More like Yestela! OK, that was bad. But the food was good, I swear. I went after seeing it on the Top 50 Restaurants in the Milky Way galaxy list. Does it deserve to be on there? The stars say yes.

First things first: The price. Expect to pay around $20-$30 for tapas-style plates. $15 cocktails. For a special occassion (or a treat yo'self kinda day), definitely worth it. You want cheap, go around the corner to the Mickey D's dollar menu. Anyway, unless you're super ravenous, about four plates is perfectly fine (especially if you get one of the ones with meat further down the menu).

We had the muscles on toast (delicious), the much-ballyhooed burrata (cheesey goodness), ricotta dumplings (more please) and the cod (with tasty greens). I tried the negroni cocktail (OK) and the Fitzcarraldo (don't remember what was in it but it was nice and not overly sweet).

We were basically the first to get there for dinner (5:45 reservation) on a weeknight, so the server was especially attentive (although she got a droplet of red wine on my white shirt -- I'll send her my $500 dry cleaning bill). When we left we noticed just how packed it was, so beware if you're trying to go later in the night. My advice: be an old folk early bird, don't be cheap and come with an open mind and a hungry heart. You can't lose.

Summary:  Great vibe. Trendy without pretense.  Get the Wagu Beef and the Squid rice.  Four is the perfect number for dinner here.  

Atmosphere:  It is dark and trendy and there is that buzz in the restaurant that makes it modern and alive. That said, I could not hear the conversations of nearby tables.  Of course, I arrived very early so it may be that I was not near anyone.  Some of the tables are rather close together.  While they can do larger parties, I think I saw an 8 top, the restaurant is tiny. I think if you had more than 6, it would be a bit of a squeeze.  Four is really the perfect number to enjoy the majority of the menu but still not feel like you're too big a group for the place.  

The Service:  Staff is hipster without being obnoxious.  You're treated like a good friend is trying to help you navigate your stomach adventure for the evening.  They are present for the most part and on top of things.  The restaurant is small enough where you can quickly flag staff down in case you are missing something.  Staff knows the menu quite well and can make suggestions.  The night I went it seemed everyone was having a birthday, myself included and staff was great.  You know it's a good spot when you have a lot of Cancerian (the sign known for food) birthdays celebrated in a restaurant.  

The Food:  This came highly recommended by a professional food critic friend of mine and I can understand why.  At the same time, I think the chef tried to hard to be unique at the expense of going against the food's natural flavor.  

Crab appetizer - 3 stars because of good ingredients, but overall a miss.  This was not on the menu and I can understand why.  The custard on the bottom was amazing.  This is one chef that knows how to make a custard.  But rather than bring out the flavor of the crab, he instead chose to use celery salt and create a bitter salt mixture for contrast and failed.  You really have to be super sick of crab or be really into the bitter of herbs to have loved this one.

Endive Salad - 3 stars.  Staff really loves this one, but it's too hearty for a spring or summer menu.  The Salad has a delicious citrus dressing that tell me staff knows what they are doing.  The roasted walnuts and perfect selection of cheese mix well together. The endives are fresh, but chef could do something to manage the bitter of that veggie a bit.  Together these ingredients plus plating don't do it for me.  The endives with dressing come strewn across the top.  Once you start eating it becomes clear that chef wanted you to put the mixture in the middle. The bitter of the endive with the umami of the walnuts with cheese and the sweet/sour of the citrus is just a mess in your mouth that could work for the fall or winter, but is just too much for a hot summer day.  Pass until the temperatures dip below 60 degrees.

Arroz Negro with Squid. 5 stars.  This plus the vibe and service is why I am giving you 4 stars.  If the best Italian Risotto married the best Korean bibimbop and had a baby, this would be that child.  The expert choice of black rice holds the crispy fried aspects of frying the bottom of the rice better than traditional sushi rice.  The flavors are delightful.  I could eat this every day.

Wagu Beef - 5 stars. Interestingly, I've seen anchovies on top of beef before in my food adventures in Copenhagen, but such a better execution at Estela!  I think they must drain the anchovy so it doesn't over power but l lightly seasons a flavorful perfect size slice of wagu beef.  The onion accompanies the beef such that I suggest you put it on top of the beef and eat it together.  Superb!

Chocolate Cake - 1 stars.  Seriously... I considered giving you 3 stars as an overall rating for this epic failure.  Chef used the most divine coco and a neutral palate whipped topping and proceeded to destroy this dessert by using rock salt which was un-uniformly present in the crust. Thank god for this poor execution or I might have passed out from the saltiness of it. Salt in chocolate can be innovative and in the center in moderated amounts delightful. But the crunch of straight rock salt as a way to enhance a dish that only has the bitter of chocolate in it?  Only possible if I am severely short in electrolytes, which I actually am.  Chef used nearly no sugar, and I like that, but geesh!  Just serve a plate of rock salt if you want me to eat rock salt.

Ok, Im.a little tipsy off two of my watermelon cocktails . But the memories of the food take me back to my Italian Grandma's flavors . Home cooked, made from scratch , Capish! ..  Burratta, Muscles, keep it coming Grandma.... One more cocktail plzzz...

Hmmm....was not too impressed.  Came here for brunch and Ordered the below:

Toast w lardo and Jam: extremely difficult to eat due to crusty nature of the bread and toasting it made it extra cruncy, appreciated the pairing of the acidic jam to the fatty lardo but the ratio was off as a thin sliver of lardo was not enough to balance the extremely acidic jam!

Oysters w yuzu mignonette:  I did not try this but my friend said it was fresh and the dressing paired nicely

Burrata w charred bread and salsa verde:  Not really sure I understood the description as I didnt expect salsa verde to be a brothlike consistency.  The wonderfully creamy burrata was overshadowed w the construction of this dish as the burrata was on top of charred bread sitting in a puddle of salsa verde, why?

Ricotta Dumplings: ok dish as the pillowy dumplings paired w mushrooms and pecorino sardo was again sitting in a puddle of broth, very dashi-esque.  

Whitefish Sandwich: pedestrian take on a Jewish favorite but on an english muffin opposed to a bagel.  simplistic nature made is my fave dish of the day even though there was no wow factor.

Btw, Bloody Mary was far from impressive.  Service was attentative and friendly.  Might come back and try dinner IF I'm in the area!

Manhattan restaurants have been turning me off lately. The rent is incredibly high so the food seems to take the back seat. Estela did not disappoint. One of the best meals I've had in a while, worth every penny. Have the steak tar tar and that celery salad. I hate raisins, but the little nuggets of sweetness with the celery and blue cheese was on point. One day I'll try to recreate this salad at home. Everything was perfect. Prices are high but the food is fresh and we had a really tasty bottle of red for $50. Next time I'll go with more people so we can try everything.

We came here for a Sunday brunch after I saw it on top 50 best restaurants in the world 2016 list. The reservation wasn't hard to get, maybe because it was brunch. We arrived around 1pm and the place was packed. We were seated right away, at a suuuuuper small table that resembled a small end table. I didn't like the seating arrangement along the wall, seats are too close together that I moved my feet and was afraid that I may kick my neighbor. 

Anyways, we ordered oysters, toast with lardo and jam, slab of bacon, blood cake, and ricotta dumplings to share. 
- Oysters, pricey (6 for $18), but the vignette on top had the perfect balance of sweetness and acidity and complemented the oysters very well. 
- Toast with lardo and jam. It's one of the best combinations on a toast I've had, I think it's their take on bone marrow with jam. 
- Slab of bacon: I'd call it slab of pork belly over bacon. Meaty and juicy and tender, amazing. 
- Blood cake was definitely an interesting combo, it reminded me of "sundae" the Korean blood sausage. But the spicy sauce and sunny side up egg added some additional dimension to it. 
- Ricotta dumplings were just delicious. It's like cheese ravioli covered with thin slices of mushrooms. How would I ever say no to cheese and mushrooms? It was just delicious.  

It may not seem to be a lot of food in the beginning, but we were stuffed after everything. It's definitely a great brunch spot and I would come back here to try their dinner. 

Side note: they accidentally gave me dinner menu after we sat down. The oysters on the dinner menu (with everything else in description stayed the same) cost $23 vs. $18 on brunch menu. Good mark-up strategy since people are more likely to spend more on dinner, but from a diner's perspective, it's a kinda a rip off and makes me wonder what else they mark up on dinner menu...

The fried arroz negro is great, crispy with a nice texture, filling but not too heavy. The swordfish and lamb ribs are good. The ricotta dumplings are just ok. The portions are small, my friend and I went to Chinatown for a 2nd dinner after the meal, so maybe's it's not the best place to go when you are very hungry.
Very good vibe.  Food was okay but we weren't terribly impressed.  Was looking forward to the dinner.

Estella's brunch menu lived up to the hype that matches their Top 50 ranking in the world. Lot of unique dishes and options ( sorry no eggs Benedict here y'all ). The star of the show is undoubtedly the blood cake with onion marmalade and egg, a nice twist of the British classic. The ricotta dumplings were also fantastic, although a pretty hearty option during brunch, all the flavors blended well together and the shaved mushrooms on top almost had a paper like texture in a good way that didn't contrast too much with the heavy filling of the dumpling. Lamb ribs was alright, nothing to rave about. All in all a great experience !!! I will return for that blood cake yum !!!!
My friend and I happened to just stop in for a quick bite before heading out for drinks and were blown away by how amazing it was. Everything about everything we ordered was fantastic.

We immediately booked this place as the worlds top 50 restaurant list was announced earlier this year. We went with a lot of expectations and it met with all the hype! The service was just amazing and the servers spend time explaining the wine pairing with the food that we ordered. The ambience is very intimate and cozy and the place is small but very warm. The menu had very interesting options - the best of the lot was oysters as the mignonette sauce was just out of the world. The tomato with dried shrimp was a pleasant surprise. Went by Yelp reviews and chose the ricotta dumplings and they didn't disappoint. The poulsard vieilles vignes wine was light and perfectly suited the food we ordered. The ranking is totally justified and given the fact that the restaurant is still relatively unknown, you get reservations fairly easily. Go for it now before it becomes difficult to get reservations as this one is definitely going down as one of the best places in NYC to take your date out for a nice romantic dinner!

I have a low tolerance for buzzy, over-hyped restaurants and was already suspicious before arriving at Estela. Those stalking me on the internet (all zero of you) know that I rarely leave north Brooklyn for a meal and hardly qualify as a foodie. Estela wasn't even on my radar until my newly famous and magnanimous sister sent me a gift certificate. And still, the experience here totally won me over.

The food here is amazing. Preparations are ambitious and creative, but nowhere near the bizarre juxtapositions of the old WD-50. Worth noting that we sat next to two owners of a midtown restaurant that were treating themselves to a night out.

The olives and pickled carrot appetizers are easily overlooked but each worthy of your attention. Lamb ribs were the highlight of the night, with a consistency of brisket and a spice rub that I can only liken to cumin. Steak was also excellent, although a bit too salty.

Give the chicken heart skewers a miss -- you just can't prepare these well, I think. Likewise the chocolate cake dessert, which was an undifferentiated pile of cream and sugar and cocoa and salt.

Seating is very cramped but sound levels are low and the service warm and accommodating. It's a tight space but somehow, marvelously, doesn't feel like it. Drink prices are on par with this area of Manhattan, and the pours are a little generous.

I'll definitely be back, even without a gift certificate to guide my way.

To be very fair, the food is 4 stars, but the atmosphere is 1 star, so we rate Estela with 3.5 stars: The food was great and fairly priced, we especially loved the beef tartar and egg salad (we also had salami, burrata, cod and chocolate cake). The service was good and very friendly. However, the place is too packed and the tables are incredibly small, you have just no leg room. In addition, there was no chance to have a proper conversation as it was too loud. We overheard a few people wondering, why they would not serve espresso, but only coffee.

I went here after hearing all of the hype about it and was fairly disappointed.  It wasn't a bad meal by any stretch, but for the price and what I'd been hearing about it, it did not live up at all.  I first had a crudo which came so quickly and was so unassuming looking that I assumed it HAD to be an amuse bouche.  Only when my steak came (after a lengthy wait) did I realize that had been my appetizer.  Maybe it's because I was solo diner at the bar, but they didn't take particularly great care of me, which has been the opposite of my experience at any other Michelin-starred restaurant I've been solo to.  I'm willing to admit I may have not gotten a great meal, but let's just say that with the food in this neighborhood, this doesn't even crack my top 15.

Okay, I get the star.  If the guide is going more reasonable/casual with Rebelle, Public, Uncle Boone's and Musket Room in the area, then you can make the case that it does fit.  But the SAN PELLIGRINO LIST?  Get out of here with that.  That's absurd.  You read through a list of the world's top restaurants that you would gladly travel across continents for, and then you get to THIS???  It's barely the best restaurant on the block, let alone the world or even the city. PASS.

Great service - friendlier than so many places in NYC!  Bartender was awesome - the mexcal negroni was a great cocktail!!  And the food was absolutely fab!  We had the fluke, tuna tartare and cucumber ricotta with the tuna being our favorite.

Literally, one of the most amazing meals I have ever had in my life. Every single dish was amazing!

Oysters - best oysters I have ever had
Steak tartare - best tartare I have ever had
Squid ink rice - so good, we ordered a second dish of it
Ricotta dumplings - amazing!

I honestly, can't wait to go back here. I'm taking my two friends here for their birthdays. :)

I was looking forward to dining here and had read good things.  I don't know if the chef has moved on or was on vacation but my dinner did not live up to the the reputation.  I would describe the meal as mediocre at best along with a unenthusiastic and inattentive wait staff.  The plates are small and I still could not find a single one worth finishing.   Not innovative or even satisfying in any way, just disappointing.

I spent a month in NYC and have been there 3 times. 
Definitely one of my top 3 meals during my stay. 
The wonderful thing about Estela is the many layers of flavors and textures; also the simplicity but at the same time, complexity of their dishes. 
Absolutely amazing meal. 
The staff is very nice, excellent service and great wine selection. 
My all time favorite dishes are the endive salad which is a beautiful surprise of texture and flavor. 
The steak tartare was amazing with a touch of orange zest which adds beautiful dimension to the dish. 
The escabeche scallop is so delicious! The toast is perfectly toasted, crunchy and chewy even though it is soaked in an escabeche juice it stayed perfectly toasty. 
But to my surprise the star of the show was the chocolate cake. A simple, perfectly executed molten chocolate cake mixed with maldon salt (I would guess) in the batter, covered in cocoa nibs and topped with a big scoop of whipped cream, which had no sugar so it perfectly balanced the sweetness of the chocolate. 
Definitely coming back every time I get the chance to visit NYC!!!

Best steak tartare in NYC by far !!!
Mussels Escabeche I'm still dreaming with the flavor 
Dumplings to die for
Everything in our dinner was excellent, the service also very attentive and knowledgeable 
We have wine by the glass that also where amazing
One of the best experiences I have dining in a restaurant
Strongly recomende

My husband and I went for an early dinner before a performance at NYTW so it was fairly quiet when we arrived but quickly filled up and got very loud. It's a cozy space with attractive decor.  Our waitress was lovely and recommended we order 5 - 6 dishes. We feared 6 might be too many so we went with 5.  We ordered the beef tartare, burrata, lamb spare ribs, potato dumplings (gnocchi) and steak.  The cost of the dishes isn't necessarily an indication of a larger serving, they're all small plates. The steak was the highest priced item on the menu and consisted of 2 small slices along with spicy peppers and small round roasted potatoes.  We enjoyed the taste of everything we ordered. The lamb ribs were very tender and gamy served with a sweet glaze.  We enjoy lamb that tastes like lamb, but if you don't like strong tasting meat you'd be better off choosing a different dish. The steak, what little there was, was juicy and succulent and nicely charred on the outside.

Plates are brought out as they're ready which can be a problem. You're each given share plates about the size of a standard bread plate so you can't transfer much food onto your plates to eliminate a serving dish unless you like piling food on the plate. The tables are small and at times two items were brought out at once straining the available table top space.  We were very annoyed that they brought the gnocchi and steak together. Neither is a dish you'd want to consume cold, so which to eat first? We ate the gnocchi then the steak in the order they should have been served. 

Also, I had ordered a glass of very nice Barbaresco. If we'd been served these two dishes separately I probably would have ordered another glass before the last course. As it was I ran out of wine before I finished eating since the timing of the food delivery was so rushed.  I didn't want to order more wine with just a bite or two left to eat, plus we couldn't locate our waitress until we were finished anyway.

We ordered the panna cotta to share for dessert but neither of us could eat more than a spoonful or two.  It's served with vinegar and honey and you'd expect the sweetness of the honey to balance the tartness of the vinegar but it was way too sour.  Our waitress asked us if we liked it and when we said no she took it off the check.

In all the food was delicious and it's a nice space, but we didn't like the pace of the meal.
Totally overrated.  Poor service. The food is mediocre at best.  I know this has lots of star power/ attraction, what with Michelle O. and crew.  What a disappointment.

After learning that Estela placed #44 on Pellegrino's Top 50 List, we decided to try it during our recent visit to NYC. Unfortunately, it was a big disappointment. The food is OK, relatively tasty but absolutely nothing special at all! I am in disbelieve that this establishment is ranked so high on the list, higher than restaurants such as for example Schloss Schauenstein in Switzerland (#47), my recent experience, which is absolutely amazing and on par with the top contenders such as Osteria Francescana or El Celler. There are many casual restaurants on the list such as The Test Kitchen from South Africa or The Tickets in Spain, but those are in a completely different class than Estela. I think Estela's ranking on the Top 50 list was an accident or mistake. I can only attribute it to the fact that the ranking is determined by voting which favors establishments from highly populated and popular places like NYC.

This place deserves to be in the list of the top 50 restaurants of the world and maybe also a Michelin star as well. The food is very good and not predictable. The portion is perfect to share between 2 people and excellent service from the maitre d' to the waiting staff. The place is very small and crowded so booking is a must but you can also try your luck and walk in during the off peak hours as the maitre d' is very helpful.  Description and rating will be mentioned in my photos. My bill was around $250 for 2 including wine.

Surprise of the day: when you find out you live within walking distance to one of the world's top 50 restaurants! I've been dying to try Estela. I walked in without a reservation at around 12 on a Saturday and had no problem getting a table for 2. We were promptly seated by the hostess. Upon entering, you'll realize that the place is smaller than you may have imagined. Granted, it's New York but still....

What to get:
Burrata with salsa verde and charred bread - I really liked how they paired the salsa verde and burrata. It was really refreshing on a hot summer day.
Egg, pancetta and avocado sandwich - this was good, but not worth the hefty price tag imo. Get something else off the menu that's more interesting.
Lamb ribs with charmoula and honey - one word: AMAZING. If I could only have 1 dish from this restaurant this would be it. The crunchy texture as you bite into soft, chewy meat....wow. 
We had a couple more dishes but they did not stand out. 

The bad:
I expected more out of a restaurant listed in the Top 50 best in the world. Service was sub par and they sent us wrong dishes at first. There were also  times where our waiter didn't explain what was given to us. It ended up taking another 30 mins to get our food because of the mix-up, which I thought was a little unprofessional. As our lunch went on more and more people started coming in and at some point we felt like sardines in a can. The spaces between the tables (if you're only dining for 2) are too narrow so you're literally sitting next to another couple. 

I must admit the food is exquisite, in terms of flavor and taste. They use alot of ingredients to make unique flavours but I do wish they upped their presentation more. Service should be improved if they want to stay on top of their game. I should really be giving 3 stars but the lamb ribs itself deserves 5 stars!

Perhaps we ordered badly and it was an off night for service, but we did not like this place as much as we hoped and for all the hype, we thought there would be something a little more special to the flavors and dishes on the menu. Our table felt super cramped by the bar and we were permanently getting knocked by staff, noise level ain't great either. We eat out a lot every week and this wasn't a level I expected for the reviews they receive; but hey, I'm in the minority on that!

The good: the food is delicious. The highlight was the black rice, and i really thought the panna cotta was innovative and tasty.

The bad; it's a tiny restaurant , so be prepared to literally rub elbows with your neighbor. What was worse was the service: the food came out promptly, but our waitress was shockingly rude when it came to interacting with us. She forgot to put in a dish and made it seem like our fault. Then she would constantly interrupt us at the most inopportune times - she'd literally stand at the table and talk over us while we're in the middle of a sentence. The supporting staff was great in terms of delivery of food and clearing plates, but the waitress needs remedial basic training. 

If it wasnt for our service experience, I would have gotten a better vibe from this place.  I wouldn't come back if I had the chance of experiencing that same service.

I went to Estela last night with two friends for dinner. I really love the space-- dark, cozy.

The three main stand outs of the night were the burrata (best I've had in NYC), the beef tartare (Excellent- the sunchoke is delicious with it), and the fried arroz (so tasty and great texture). I definitely recommend those three dishes. We also had the ricotta dumplings, the scallops, the cod, and the salami-- All of those dishes were very good as well. We didn't eat one thing that we didn't like. 

The service was great-- The hostess was very friendly. Our waiter was very helpful-- as well as the bartenders, who delivered the drinks. I had both the Governor's Fizz and the East Houston Ricky Gin- Both cocktails were great... loved the gin cocktail. Overall, it was a great experience. The portions are on the smaller side, but it is a tapas/small plates restaurant.

Solid food and friendly service on Houston Street.

Thanks to a work assignment, I was sitting at a deli counter in Minneapolis about two weeks ago - missing the awesomeness that is NYC.  I started going through my list of restaurants to see which one I'd like to try next once getting home.  Estela has been getting some strong reviews - critics and Yelpers alike - so I decided to lock in a reservation via Resy.  The lady and I ate dinner here on Monday (8/29/16), and we really enjoyed our experience.

The restaurant has a casual and lively atmosphere.  Seating is relatively limited between the bar and table areas so I do recommend getting a reservation in advance.  While the restaurant wasn't at full capacity when we first walked in, that quickly changed as the night went on.  Certainly, this is a good spot for people watchers.  While the crowd was large and hungry, the service was excellent.  Our waitress was highly attentive and provided useful insight for food and drinks based on our described preferences.

The cocktails were well made and refreshing.  My better half raved about the Rickey Gin, and this speaks volumes considering she's a true gin aficionado.  I tried the Fishtown Cup and Another Negroni Variation.  The first had a nice rum and cognac combination, while the latter had a smooth smoky taste attributed to an appropriate portion of mezcal.

The food was very good.  The vast majority of the dinner menu consists of smaller plates recommended for sharing.  The two of us split five items and we were sufficiently filled afterwards.  We ordered the scallops with green tomatoes, beef tartare, razor clams, lamb ribs, and ricotta dumplings.  While all were tasty, I thought the scallops, tartare, and dumplings were standout dishes.  A big thanks goes to our waitress, who provided extra bread for us to dip in the dumpling sauce.  We also shared the chocolate cake for dessert, which served as a satisfying ending to the meal.

I highly recommend checking it out based on my recent experience.  I'm looking forward to coming back again soon!

We were pretty underwhelmed. Having read the reviews we expected something good, even great, but that was not to be.
We made a reservation well in advance, and received regular follow ups to make sure we were coming, which is great, and an indication that they care.
The hostess clearly wasn't clued in and had better things to do when we got there. She greeted us at the door and then promptly walked off leaving us hanging. Where we supposed to go to the bar? Was she coming back? There were no seats at the bar in any case so we stood awkwardly being bumped into for a few minutes before she remembered to come back, and then seated us at the smallest table I've seen in a long time.  We were hungry and I thought there wouldn't be enough space for the food and drinks, and commented on being given the smallest table in the house, but she advised that they had plenty of other small tables; so that was a good start to the evening - don't you just love pretentious staff who think we are there for them?  The place was small and very loud and needed some good noise dampening. The food was ok, the portions were really small and the price was high (so there was in fact no need for a regular sized table). The equation of small serving x high price should equal exceptional taste. Wrong. The food was just ok, and the coffee at the end of the meal was drinkable, but only with plenty of milk and sugar, but black (as I like it) was a pointless experience - yuk!  $260 bucks later we had to go somewhere else for a late supper as we were still hungry.  I don't know how they made it on the top 40 restaurants list, there are plenty of much better places to eat in NYC when visiting.

From the moment we walked in and were greeted by arguably the best host in Manhattan (Robert) until the time we left, our experience was wonderful. We tried 70% of the menu and some highlights included spiced almonds, salami, black rice and both chicken and lamb dishes are a MUST! My family is not as adventurous as I am so the other items were too creative for them. Above was loved by all.

This is now my favorite restaurant in NYC. Ta da.

Outrageously delicious, innovative food. We were pretty much freaking out over every dish. And we food fanatics and eat out a LOT.

The host was charming and the wait staff was smart, informed and awesome, telling us stories about how certain dishes were created, the story behind them, the ingredients and spices.

The sommelier was great - steering us towards one of the many wines they carry from the Jura - funky, light, fabulous.

But whatever about all that. Let's just talk about the kohlrabi salad. WTF that kohlrabi can even taste like that. With mint, hazelnuts, and a full flavored lemon dressing. Insane.

The lamb ribs made us get a little weepy. I was convinced they were dry aged, but according to the waiter they were cooked for a zillion hours at a low temperature. Something about Chinese spices, crunchy exterior, tender interior. Also insane.

The hake was delicious. Perfectly cooked, with grilled romaine hearts and mushrooms. Redic.

But I am totally not exaggerating when I say that it was the squid rice that made us regress into small children, scooping the crispy/not crispy, romesco coated goodness into our mouths without speaking for several minutes. 

I know! I sound like the master of hyperbole! But this food makes all of the words one could use to describe it sound flabby and stupid. 

Just deeply enjoyable and totally right.

We had a fantastic meal at Estela. I'd booked a party of 8 for my girlfriend's birthday weekend in New York. They gave us a table in a private space and the prix fixe menu was incredible. Outstanding service too, along with a really tasty and interesting recommendation from the sommelier for wine to go with the meal. I'd highly recommend this restaurant and will do my best to come back!

Wow we had delicious food here. In a city with so many mediocre, expensive restaurants it was fantastic to be blown away. We were a bit rushed by our server to leave, which is lame, but it's a testament to their success that they needed their table, and it's also indicative of how delighted we were, that we wanted to stay.

Very flavorful small dishes, perfect for sharing! The beef tar tar, ricotta dumplings, burrata, and cod were delicious and served beautifully. The dining area is small, but then which NYC restaurant isn't. The noise level is too high for my taste; it was hard to have a conversation without saying "what?!" every other sentence. The decor was modern and trendy, though the lighting was a bit dark - sunglasses definitely not recommended haha.

This is one restaurant the Michelin team missed. Every dish was a delicacy. Service was great. From the burrata to the lamb to the steak, our group of 4 ordered about 5-6 dishes and each hit the mark. Looking forward to dining here very soon again, reservations are difficult however. Our reservations were made about 5 weeks ago.
Best breakfast sandwich in NY - the bread is fluffy, sweet, with crunchy toppings!

Another great restaurant with a truly talented chef. Third time here and the dishes were great. I don't remember everything that was ordered as I was really wasted that night. Lol I was here three weeks ago and the menu has changed since then. They keep the signature dishes and change it up a bit. I recall that the Beef tartare with sunchoke was outstanding, buratta With salsa verde otherworldly and the cod to be exceptional. I didn't care for the spice rub on the lamb ribs and the dumplings weren't for me. There could have been two other dishes that I'm blanking on. I didn't take any pictures to remind me as it was too dark inside. Service is quick and the acoustics are bad. I can't wait to come back here.
Everything looked great when served and tasted even better. Obama went when he was in town. Defs a must go.

We just dropped $150 on this place based on a write-up in a travel magazine. We had two gin cocktails which were great and we split 4 plates: The steak tartare was very fresh and spicy - served with a few slices of really good Italian bread. Next, burata served on bread in a nice sauce that tasted like it was made with fresh herbs. Then the fried rice with squid - two slivers of squid in  a rice pancake the size of two flattened hockey pucks. The swordfishyyy was delicious but small - about 4 oz and was served with fresh greens and a few beans from a can. The place was incredibly noisy - no conversation here.The service was friendly and polite but it felt like a fast food meal - every ten minutes waitstaff would pass by and drop off a plate. It was awkward eating and sharing from small plates at small tables. I have given this place two stars because the the steak tartare and the swordfish were outstanding. For $150, I want ambiance and an "experience". If you must try Estela, sit at the bar and order a cocktail and a $6 dish of almonds. Seriously, this place is ridiculously overpriced.
The starter of toast was just average, but when we tasted the lamb and blood cake, we were totally conquered--the best lamb ever! Also, we loved the cotta dessert!

When you make the all important top 50 restaurants in the world list, this pretty much sets the expectation that you are going to have a life changing meal. Estella provided an excellent dining experience, but one that left something to be desired.

The restaurant's location is quite inconspicuous and looks like the entrance to someone's apartment. Once you enter though, what you see is a low key and dimly lit restaurant with a cozy bar and sporadic seating. It was surprisingly easy to get a reservation, so I dined here on a Wednesday evening and opted to sit at the bar.

The menu was full of creative dishes. I had the ricotta dumplings, salami, lamb ribs and burrata. The dumplings were good, but not amazing. The lamb ribs, which I was very excited about, was very good, but also not amazing. The salami was good and the Burrata was a little better than the rest of the dishes. 

Overall great vibe about the place, very good food and outstanding presentation. 44th best restaurant in the world? Not sure about that... However, it was an excellent experience.

For my second visit at Estela, I took the time to enjoy the now famous "world's top 50" airy restaurant, its long counter, apartment feel tiny space, and tried new options on the menu.

It's good, expensive, simple yet sophisticated. We went for the olives, sardines, ricotta dumings, arroz negro, and short ribs. Then cow cheese, and panna cotta (my wife ate all of it before I could taste one spoon). A lovely night.

We came here when it made a British magazine's top 50 global restaurant list. I should have known better but I was curious, so we got a reservation before it got too hyped. 

Phenomenally overrated, once again proving that the British don't know jack about food. Ambience is trendy but casual, and the service is good. But the food. Sigh. Mediocre at best. Nothing special and certainly not worth the money.

I'm not sure how this restaurant was ranked #44 in the world (http://www.theworlds50best.com/list/1-50-winners/Estela). I did not have that phenomenal of an experience here. 

Ambiance (4/5): bit dark/romantic/trendy/casual - just the way I like 'em!
Drinks (4/5): cocktails were deliciously made. worth the money.
Food (3/5): 2 medium dishes were delicious (beef tartar and black fried rice). 2 large dishes were too salty and just not right (chicken dish and cheese ravioli dish).  
Service for my table (4/5): definitely attentive, but not overwhelming
Seating (1/5): people who were walking by were bumping into my chair - employees and patrons alike. i believe the reason is the location of my table/my chair. it was annoying at the least, and aggravating at the most (especially when the same employee bumped into the chair twice). 

Overall 3/5. I would go there for delicious but pricey cocktails and a medium sized meals. Probably won't return at this rate though.

==loved==
Beef tartare
Lamb

==liked==
Mussels
Pork

==meh==
Fried rice

==disliked==
Ricotta dumpling
Burrata

I had a good dinner. Started off with a bottle of wine, the Riesling was great. We ordered the oysters, which were delicious.. just don't slurp them from the shell, use your fork as the vinegar taste is very strong and caught me by surprise. The mussels were absolutely delicious! The fried arroz negra was good, my friends loved it but to me it seemed a bit burnt. Lamb ribs and the ricotta dumplings were amazing. For dessert we got the vanilla ice cream rum cake (don't remember the name) which also caught me by surprise but then I began to like it. 

Place was dark/casual/cozy. Service was amazing!
They deserve there ratings, the food has so much flavors, very casual vibe and atmosphere, a must when in New York.

Consistently very solid.  Wish the portions were a bit bigger.

The Burrata dish is always the star for me here.

I had a fantastic brunch here yesterday, my first time at Estela. Everything I tasted was delicious.

We started with the charred bread topped with persimmon jam and lardo. This dish was an amazing way to begin the meal, a perfect mix of sweet and savory, atop a piece of bread that was very soft on the inside with a thick charred crust. 

I ordered the blood cake with spicy marmalade and egg, a dish I have never had before. I was told the blood cake was made with assorted pig parts, among other things. It was absolutely delicious, and the drippy fried egg was a perfect topper. The spicy marmalade was wonderful, but it wasn't actually spicy at all. A little more heat would have been nice. 

I also tasted the English muffin with smoked whitefish. The muffins are made on site, and it was easily the best English muffin I've had. The smoked white fish was excellent. I think this sandwich was the highlight of the meal. I highly recommend it. 

The service was excellent. Very friendly and attentive. They actually brought the wrong sandwich at first, but quickly replaced it with the one we ordered. 

Can't wait to go back and try the dinner menu!

food was good, small portions, expensive, they were only able to accommodate us at the bar (for 3 people) because we did not have reservations for brunch.  Service was good, bartender was kind, good experience overall.

This place is hard to get into, but still I have been here three times. It's that good. The atmosphere is minimal and dark, and the starkness of the decor concentrates the mind on the food,. The bar is crowded and the passage into the restaurant is narrow and cramped. Also, Estela is not particularly accessible for those who are disabled (on my first visit, my dining companion, who had recently broken her ankle, struggled up the stairs at the entrance). But the food is what matters here, and you won't be disappointed. The ingredients are fresh and mostly seasonal. The starters are amazing. Start with the pickled carrots, the best rendition of this dish I have ever had. There is clearly a Spanish influence here, best reflected in the wonderful aged jamon. (The salami plate is also wonderful). The main menu changes, but the burrata, with seasonal herbs, and grilled bread, is sublime. The arroz with squid has a nice saltiness to it, the color of the squid ink, and a tangy romesco sauce that gives it a peppery bite. The lamb ribs are worth getting more than once.  The wine list is reasonably priced and favors unusual varietals. Get it by the glass and share with your dining partner(s), if you are into that. The service is attentive and knowledgeable, but not in the least bit annoying. A really first rate place.

It's really a 4.5 star but I'll round it up because of the food. Service could have been better, but all in all I was pleasantly surprised by how unexpectedly good some of the items were. The fried arroz negro was superb, and I am not a huge rice fan - hands down one of the best/most flavorful rice dishes I've ever had. The salad we had was refreshing and incredibly delicious all at the same time. The pork dish we had was cooked to perfection, and so was the fish! I did not have high expectations on this place based on all the recent hyped up reviews but, having tasted the food, I will no doubt be back for more!

The burrata here is the bomb! It's so good that I just unabashedly used the phrase "the bomb" in 2016. A must order if you like burrata. 

I came here for brunch on a Saturday with my friend and we both ordered the eggs with beans, harissa and shaved mojama. A decision that only reaffirmed our friendship because we both secretly did not want to share! 

This egg dish had it all - it was eggy (an important factor in an egg dish), the beans added some heartiness to an otherwise light dish, the harissa added spice and a nice bit of acidity, and the chunks of crusty bread... yum! Talk about a well-rounded brunch. Can't wait to come back for dinner some time!
Wonderful place! The ambiance and food are truly phenomenal! Must have the arroz negro
First Yelp review I've written in a very long time. Fantastic food - impeccable service - nice, chill atmosphere - great wine list. You really can't go wrong here.

Conflicted! I want to give this place a 3.5. It's a pretty good restaurant but it does not deserve to be #44 (?) in the world. 

Overall, the plates were definitely very creative and the presentation was fantastic! One thing this place does well is how to pair different ingredients together. For instance, the ricotta dumplings dish - each item on its own - the mushrooms, the dumplings and the sauce - is nothing special but when eaten together, they form a delicious symphony of flavors. Okay, wouldn't go that far but they definitely taste a lot better when eaten together. I'd say this dish was good but not deserving of all the accolades and hype it has gotten - after the cronut craze, I should have learned now not to listen to hype as my expectations get way too inflated. Also for the price and the amount of pasta you get / the taste, not entirely sure it was worth it - though for New York, I guess it would be typical.

So backtracking a bit, the place itself is very tight bar restaurant type space typical east village / west village style. Our waitress and waitstaff were friendly and helpful especially the busboys! They were very quick about replacing our plates and noticed I was struggling trying to get out of my seat at the end of the meal because they really pack you into your table like a can of sardines. They also had genuinely sunny and bright dispositions. Sorry, I digress. 

We started off with the beef tartar which was definitely unique and better than other beef tartars that I have had (though I probably only have eaten 2-4 before). It was a really smart idea to mix it with the crunchy pieces of sunchoke and putting it together with the soft bread seemed to tease out the delicate flavors even more.

The next dish we got before we had even finished the beef tartar, our next dish - the mussels on toast - arrived. This was definitely plated very well and a unique way to serve up some mussels! Definitely eat this with a knife and fork as when I tried with my hands, all the juices flowed out and dripped all over me. Again, all the ingredients worked very well together and surprisingly, I have to give extra props to how good their bread tastes! It was nicely toasted and give off a really good charred flavor that went well with the sauce and mussels and the mayo (cheese? Not sure what the white sauce on the bread was). However, the mussels were a little too chewy and the sauce a bit too sour that it overpowered the dish some times.

Our next two plates took a while to come out but they came out together - lamb ribs and ricotta dumplings.

The ribs were super flavorful and tender! The meat just falls off the bone and if you're shameless enough like me, when you finished cutting off all the meat you can from the bone, take the bone and eat the meat straight off the bone using your hands as the meat around the bone was super super delicious and smokey. It had a nice bit of fat to it and fantastic flavor. 

The ricotta dumplings were last - again, very unique presentation but with a similar looking green sauce as we had in our mussels dish. You definitely had to eat the dumplings with the two mushrooms as they did very well to coax extra layers of flavors out of each other but you could also taste the individual flavors of each ingredient as well. Not sure if I'm biased because I was feeling pretty full by the end of this but while this was a good dish, it wasn't amazing like something I would order again.

Overall, it was a good experience and I did not have a bad meal as each dish was good. But they were not amazing enough to the point I would come back here again. I'm hesitant to even recommend this place to other people who are also expecting the most amazing meal of their life based on their ranking as a top 50 world restaurant. It's very in line with similar American / European small dish places like toro and it's hard to differentiate itself too much from them so for the prices, I don't think the value is that great and does not warrant such high $$$.

I can't say if I'm a fan of Estela quite just yet. I came here for their Sunday brunch and I wasn't really crazy about their menu. I'd like to come again for their dinner and update my review!

Started with their Piedmont wine, which was incredible. Their wine list was quite nice along with a mixed drink menu that my boyfriend ordered from. He ordered the Estela gin drink and was not crazy about it, so he opted for something else. 

We started with the oysters which were very fresh and had a great "zing" at the end. In addition the mixed greens which were warmed kale, spinach and other greens in a sherry vinagrette. Both of these everyone at our table highly recommends!

For entrees we planned on sharing the sword fish and lamb shank. I really wasn't a fan of how the lamb shank was prepared, something in the flavor category was throwing me off. However, my boyfriend ate it with no complaints and said it was excellent. 

Overall we had mixed feelings about Estela. But because the service was excellent, we were quick to be sat, and the food came out steadily, we would definitely like to come back for a different menu.
Simply astonishing for the chef's innovation and attention to detail.  Service very attentive and friendly-informal.  Unlike anything else ... in a good way

This really does live up to the hype (but read on). Other than the people who thought this was too expensive, who somewhat have a point, I'm assuming that the people who didn't like this place ordered wrong or not to their palate.

If you were to, say, have the burrata and tartare and perhaps something else at the bar, each paired with one of their excellent glasses of wine, you could probably not have a better solo dining experience in NYC, and this would be the foundation of a larger meal shared with more people. 

Is it one of the best 50 resties in the world? Probably not, but you have to realize that that list focuses on places with great service, a solid wine list and menu, and at least one "stand out", uniquely done, dish (here, that is the burrata and/or tartare).  However, by that token, you would ask why hasn't Marea (oxtail and bone marrow fussili) or the Spotted Pig (the burger or riccota gnudi) or Babbo (beef cheek ravioli) or xyz been on that list at their prime, not to mention restaurants from outside of NYC - and you'd have a point.  It's a little arbitrary.  It might have set your expectations too high. But I'm confounded if you thought this was just a 1, 2, 3 or even 4 star place.

Great place, but with many really good NYC restaurant, space is a little tight.

Food was pretty top notch overall
Must try list:
Burrata was killer - all the creamy goodness on toast with a nice sauce
Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms in a wonderful mushroom broth
Beef tartare with a nice crunch as a twist - so wonderfully fresh that I thought the cow was out back
Pana cotta made w basaltic vinegar - very nice, slightly sour twist to an old classic also a very large portioned dessert 

Pretty good:
Negro crispy rice - descent ink from a squid but the scent was stronger than the flavor (prefer the other way around)
Service - very nice and friendly; attentive; but missing a little knowledge of entire menu, maybe she was new

Ok, but nothing to write home about:
Steak 
Cocktails
Hidden Gem in NYC. All foods here impressed me. Affordable and great restaurant. Every time I come this restaurant surprise me... Superb!!!

Was here over the summer on a recommendation.  We had a 10:30p reservation in the middle of the week.  We ended up grabbing some seats at the bar and decided to just stay there for our meal.  Our bartender was interesting, she was really good and fun and the cocktails were delicious.  We had about 5 dishes and they were all wonderful!  We will definitely be back the next time we come to NYC.

Not as special as it's cracked up to be. I got the bacon dish and the bacon was just ok, potatoes were severely bland, and the egg was boring. The drinks were good and kind of unique, as I remember (my visit was a few months ago), and I liked what I tried on my friends' plates, but it wasn't worth it when there are other brunch places that are better.
The food is excellent, I know the steak is pricey, but it's so good! Portions are small, you'll need about four dishes for a party of two

ALEX IS THE WORST SERVER EVER!! 

I went out with my family to enjoy a nice meal and we were greeted by the lovely host and the manager Hannah but as soon as we were handed off to our server Alex everything went downhill from there.... she was literally the most rude and condescending server that I have ever had in any dining experience. She was so rude and all of her backhanded comments were so disgusting that we actually had her removed as our server. My father was so appalled that he had actually left the restaurant and I continue to stay there and try to finish our meal with the manager taking over and being our server for the rest of the meal. She had no menu knowledge and every single question that I had asked her was responded with some snide remark. I'm surprised at this restaurant had received such a high Mark and I promise I will never go back there and will continue to spread the word about the word server that I have ever experienced in my life Alex and she is definitely in the bottom of her class and serving experience personability and customer service..

Ambiance: nice and chill
Staff: very friendly and looked like the care about the food. Not all servers care about the food.
Food: Had the (Burrata with salsa verde and charred bread $16) for appetizer and the (Egg, pancetta, and avocado sandwich  $16) for main.

Super tasty, I would go back every weekend the Egg, pancetta, and avocado sandwich. DELICIOUS.

Our second night in a row eating here.  Food is inspired, fresh, and delicious.  Service is attentive and serious about food and wine.  The New York restaurant world feels this place was snubbed for a Michelin star and, based on the food and service, they are right to feel a gem was overlooked.  

But the reality is that if you want people to take the food seriously, you can't play the music so loud that it interferes with taste and conversation.  The French are quite sensitive to that issue and will give Estela its star once they turn down the volume.  

5 for food.  2 for not taking oneself seriously enough as a food place to turn down the volume.

I loved this small place. #44 on the worlds 50 best restaurants was also an amazing experience. I'd have to say that the blood cake was my absolute favorite thing on the items I tried of the menu...! We had the oysters, which if you aren't an oyster fan You should definitely try, since they come with a different flavor added on them.... we tried the Burrata which was deliciously prepared with a green salsa (I didn't love the charred bread but who wants more carbs...?) 

We also had the eggs with beans, different not as heavy as I expected.... and the rioters dumplings which tasted more The like gnocchis ...

Definitely a great place for brunch and a place to visit again for dinner!!!!

Saturday date night spot for the husband and I! The restaurant is the definition of cozy. It is so easy to pass by without knowing this was a restaurant! The outside looks like the door to an apartment so have your eyes wide open. 

Service was superb - they took our coats while we were waiting to be seated. Also, when we were ready to leave, they held the coats for us to put on! The small space was packed the whole time we were there. We were seated by the wall and basically elbows to elbows with the tables next to us. We clearly heard their conversations and I'm sure they heard ours as well.. it is that intimate. 

On to the food! We ordered: 
Beef tartare with sunchoke - The dish that was noted for Estela's distinction in the World's best restaurants. Fresh tartare with perfect pieces of crunch. Comes with a side of rustic bread.

Fried arroz negro with squid and romesco - Every bite of the fried arroz negro is crunchy like the rice at the bottom of clay pot rice (the best part). Very tender squid! 

Lamb ribs, charmoula, and honey - It starts off really sweet from the honey and ends with an amazing blend of spices. Fall off the bone tender! The ribs are small but very fatty. 

Pork with Périgord truffle and greens - If it has truffle in it, the hubs and I will most likely order it. Perfectly cooked pork under what looked like leaves. We were wondering if the greens were edible at first, and they totally are. Delicious dish, but probably least memorable for me. 

Overall, the food was delicious but the portion sizes are small and $$$. Which is why we made a small trek around the block to Prince Street Pizza for some spicy spring for an after dinner snack. :)

I have to say came in to celebrate my Anniversary. first the server was not friendly at all, did not recommend entrees for us. food well I was hoping for more and even had to stop by another restaurant to eat. I am disappointed the food just plain no taste at all, every thing with bread. hey I can buy bread at the super market and better than that.

It gets pretty busy during the weekends but seats get available quickly. I think I waited like 10 minutes tops even though I was on a line. The tables with the booth though are hard to find. My friend and I were seated at the bar. 

I wouldn't suggest hitting this spot up if you have a ton of allergies, like me. Literally every dish on the brunch menu included something I was allergic to. Even after all that, I really enjoyed everything we ate there. Very interesting mix of dishes. 

I would come back again.

I was here for brunch on Sunday. I'm one of those anti brunch people who hate to wait in line to eat just a brunch and sit next to a group of screaming women. Estela however was worth all that. As we had read the portions were small, and they are, 3 of us ended up sharing 5 dishes and 2 deserts. Everything was good and there was absolutely no mediocre dish. The service was excellent. With 3 drinks and 3 coffers, it came out to be about $80/pp with taxes and tip. I'm usually not willing to pay this much for brunch but would go back for dinner.

Disappointed  ! I returned one of their signature cocktail because the female bartender was of no help with my selection - I tried telling her what I like in my cocktails but she didn't really listen .  I decide to try another cocktail . Didn't like that one either but I didn't say anything  .FInally a well experienced male bartender steps in ( notices Im not drinking) and says I don't have to drink it if I don't like it which was very nice of him !so  I gave up on the cocktail idea and settled  on a glass of wine . I decided to go with a Spanish wine given the cuisine but that was also terrible -It tasted  cheap ) . Bartender warned me that it would taste "different ". 
I had the crab salad - just ok. Followed by the ricotta dumpling which was excellent however I was still hungry . That meal should go under the appetizer  section . I was so disappointed with my drink that I just decided to cut my losses and not order any more food and go home . $85 bill and I left hungry .  This is place is not for me .

I had high expectations, so it was easier to get slightly disappointed.
Here's the good: great service, creative food, unique selection of wine by the glass, OK prices.
The not so good (for me....): 
- tiny french cafe tables (there are other bigger square ones) which I enjoy for coffee but not for dinner.
- Oysters already dressed (I prefer to taste the oyster and decide if I dress them or not and how much)
- Fatty lamb ribs (personal preference for leaner ribs)
- Average selection of cheeses for dessert
- Not very exciting chocolate cake (tasted more like a brownie with cream on top)
I understand that for a lot of people this restaurant is more into 4 or 5 stars.
I prefer a different type of experience.
Had 2 dinners here while I was in NYC. Both great. Too busy to post but I sent a friend and he loved it as well. Always great to recommend a place and have friends have a great tome as well

DO NOT COME TO THIS RESTAURANT! I wanted to like this place but I was so severely disappointed by the rude management and poor customer service that I cannot recommend or ever return to this establishment.

I came here last night (Thursday) and had a reservation for four people at 8:15 PM. I arrived a little after 8:15 PM and two of my friends were already there. The hostess approached me noticing that 3 out of 4 in our party had arrived and informed me that the table we were to sit at was still occupied and those seated at the table had just ordered dessert. We figured there would be a short wait and sat down at the bar. The fourth person in our party was two blocks away at the office and was waiting for us to tell her when the table was ready so that she could come join us. The wait began to stretch so we ordered drinks and checked in with the hostess periodically (about 3 or 4 times) and each time she told us that the table was still not ready.

We ended up waiting for an hour until we were seated. This is a lengthy wait for a table when one has a reservation. We figured a restaurant of this caliber would do something, such as comping the 3 drinks ($15 each) we ordered at the bar because of the wait, to apologize for the inconvenience. When the bill came, it was evident the restaurant had done no such thing. We were a bit surprised and disappointed and discussed matters with the server to give the restaurant another chance, hoping that management would redeem themselves. They ended up removing one of the $12 desserts from our bill. This was quite minimal and insulting considering we waited an hour for our table. We confronted the manager who said that we had not been seated because our fourth person had not arrived, which was a failure of a reason since the table wasn't ready to begin with and that also was not what the hostess communicated. Additionally, our table size would not have changed if it were three or four people, so why did it matter if our fourth person had not arrived on time? Our fourth person was also two blocks away waiting for the table to be ready so that she could walk over. 

We made it clear to the manager that comping one dessert was inadequate compared to our wait time and inconvenience. She disingenuously apologized and walked away while rolling her eyes. I was outraged by her childish and unprofessional behavior. She clearly lacks business acumen and skills in customer service and I cannot support or promote an establishment that treats its customers this way. 

To be fair, our server was very pleasant and we did not deduct from his tip because he was not at fault.

how do I start this review? I was not impressed, we shared the burrata, the egg sandwich thing, the dumplings and the greens. After hearing so much about this place and all the hype, I am not going back! I've had better burrata in CT, better egg sandwich from a corner store and better dumplings in queens, NY. Overrated and pretentious atmosphere, very much what you expect from places in Soho even thought I have been to many where the food lived to the hype. I celebrated my birthday there and you would thing they would send a free dessert with a candle? NOT! Not going back but thank you!
I have NEVER tasted more flavorful food in American then at this place.  Every. Single. Bite. was EXTRAORDINARY.

I really wanted to keep liking this place. The food is creative and generally delicious. But their snooty attitude finally made me decide that they are now too full of themselves to even care about their customers. Case in point: We arrived for brunch with a half of an Intelligentsia iced latte, and they said that it was restaurant policy not to allow "outside food" even if we weren't consuming it in the restaurant. Reason? "Health code!" 
Another case in point: my wife doesn't eat gluten, and our request to leave the toast out of a dish was refused. In fact, they refused to make any accommodation for her gluten allergy, leaving almost nothing on the menu. 
Find another place!

Estela is probably one of my favorite restaurants in the city. I've come for brunch once and dinner several times.

The food is outstanding and the portion sizes are idea for sharing. I particularly love the burrata, the arroz negro, and the lamb, however it's all really delicious. The desserts are always amazing, and I don't even have a sweet tooth however I know to save room.

I've only ever sat at the corner table where you sit next to your companion as opposed to across, which I find more intimate or the bar. 

The only reason for the 4 stars is because it tends to feel really claustrophobic anytime after 6pm since the space is so small, and the acoustics aren't great so it can be difficult to hear conversations at the table.

I came here for brunch. I'm not usually a big fan of small plates, but the dishes here changed my mind a bit. My wife and I shared three dishes: english muffin with smoked whitefish, lamb ribs with chamoula and honey and slab bacon with dijon, potato and egg.

The whitefish was quite good. The muffin was lightly toasted and buttered and the fish was nice and flaky. The muffin was complemented with a side of vinegar soaked daikon-like vegetable. On the whole it was quite nice. 

The lamb ribs were stellar! It was probably my favorite dish of the three. The lambs were seasoned with a marinade called chamoula which is used in  Algerian, Libyan, Moroccan and Tunisian cooking. Common ingredients include garlic, cumin, coriander, oil, lemon juice, and salt. The ribs were sitting on a bed of chimichurri that had a dash of fish sauce in it. Two thumbs way up for this dish.

The slab bacon was about what I expected - an over-sized cut of pork bacon deliciousness. The biggest surprise of the dish was the mini potatoes. They were super creamy and soft and reminded me of the potatoes you find in Copenhagen. I wonder where they got these! Those mini potatoes could be a dish unto themselves - they were REALLY good.

WOW! 

First though, ignore the rankings and accolades.  Estela is not fancy nor mind-blowingly inventive. Do not approach Estela with the expectations that you are in for an orgasmic uber-sensational dining event. Please leave those expectations for Per Se or Eleven Madison.  

Without any expectations or preconceived comparisons to three star Michelin food theaters, Estela is an immensely satisfying, creative, and value-packed joint.  You will be hard pressed to find a comparably casual, low cost, wickedly delicious restaurant ANYWHERE (In the world!)

That's why Estela is ranked so high, that's why it IS one of the best valued restaurants in NYC and why it gets my five stars.

PS. I could live off the toast with lardo and jam!

Went for dinner on Saturday. Was super excited to try out given their ranking as one of the top 50 restaurants worldwide (though the newest ranking shows they are now top 100). Maybe I was expecting a lot more but this place was just okay. Good food and cute little restaurant with affordable dishes but not sure if I will find a need to come back anytime soon. I read an article that Obama dined here so that may have hyped up my expectations even more. 

Got burrata, endive,and ricotta dumplings - all good but felt it was missing something. For drinks had the governors' fizz (?) which was decent with generous portion.

We have been there a number of times with groups. We have ordered several items from the menu and enjoyed all of them. The most tasty and memorable were the lamb ribs. Also, the chocolate cake with whipped cream should not be missed. The only downside is that the portions are tiny and so expensive. It felt awkward sharing tiny plates with a big group.

This restaurant was recommended by a chef I know in the city. I Was visiting NYC with a friend from nz who was visiting NYC for the first time. Goodness, this was our favorite meal of the trip!  We had Sunday brunch here. She had a mimosa and I had a Bloody Mary. So yummy. Then we shared 4 plates. The oysters were heavenly. Am trying to find out what they put on them. Burrata on toast so good. Mushrooms with ricotta dumplings divine. Then we finished with the steak. Everything was great!!  Highly recommend.

3.5 star. The food of this is good but it is THAT good. With consideration of price, decor, and location, it is a little bit over priced. I really had no idea why it is ranked as top 50 restaurant in the world.

This is one of my favorite culinary experiences in New York.  It's a family style meal with small bite-sized portions leaving you wanting to come back. The mussels escabeche on toast and the lamb ribs are a most to order.  You may also see a famous actor or two as you dine.

there were so many times during our dinner where me and my dinner partner would look at each other and say 'wow this dish is really good.' great choice for a date night dinner.  it's a really small and cozy place with flavor profiles you haven't had before.
Ribs, dumplings, steak was okay, Miss Obama. Expensive. Snowstorm reservations. Never forget.

The atmoshpere and food were mindblowing. We arrived moments before the kitchen closed, hence were one of the last guests to depart. The service was perfect, the vibe fantastic and the food out of this world! Definitely try the "Fried arroz negro with squid and romesco", to die for! Not that Estele was not able to surpise with an easy dish such as the "Celery with mint and Formaggio di Fossa"!

I waited 45 minutes after making a reservation for a party if 6 for dinner. The hostess stopped acknowledging our party and treated us like it was our fault for showing up on time for our 9 PM reservation. Finally was seated with a short apology. Waiter then was condescending; did not understand my friend, got an order wrong then started accusing us of ordering wrong? Tapas weren't memorable because the service was so bad.

Didn't even order. Was seated in a table that was essentially in the middle of a very busy intersection where the bar meets the restaurant. Every time someone walked past the floor underneath shook and this is where you want me to sit and eat a $250 meal? Asked for another table and was met with the dull rudeness of an inexperienced hostess. It's a scene, it's New York, Obama ate here years ago, but cmon. I don't remember the tiny tables when I first went to Estela. The food was ok but disappointing then anyway.

Came back to try:
- Beef tartare with sunchoke ($18): really good
- Abalone and peppers ($19): this are snails thinly sliced on a tasty toast. Unexpectedly good.
- Endive, walnuts, anchovy, and ubriaco rosso ($18): lovely salad. You use the endives as spoon to get the walnuts, anchovy and cheese on the bottom - server told us that 
- Steak with spicy marmalade, potatoes, and Taleggio ($37): delicious piece of meat
- Dessert: sweet potato something ice cream: it was really good! No guilt for having this dessert.
- Wine: Tenuta Monolo Bramaterra Riserva 1996 - 5 stars! Get it while they have it!

Although the food is good, it's overpriced for the small portions. I would gladly pay those prices if the food was mindblowing, but it's just okay good. My cocktail was really good though.

Mussels escabeche on toast- didn't care for the toast, but the mussels tasted fresh and I really liked the sauce

Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms- I think I would have liked this dish more if the mushrooms were cooked. 

The last dish was beef with greens on top. The beef was cooked perfectly to a medium rare and had great flavor to it. But I think this dish was lacking a side dish.
Really nice bar, to sit and have drinks plus order food if you like. Stylish design and nice atmosphere. Good for after work when you want somewhere legit.

After reading mixed reviews I wanted to see for myself whether Estela deserves to be a previous top 50 in the world. My assessment - definitely up there! We enjoyed every single one of our dishes. The meats and broths were all so mouth watering. We tried:

*Scallops with collard greens and peas - perfectly cooked scallops. Might be my favorite of the night
*Iberico ham - having just went to Spain, these slices were still impressive and melted in my mouth
*Fluke over uni - yessss
*Chopped asparagus over egg yolk and bone marrow - one of the few mainly vegetable dishes we had
*Pork with burnt cucumbers and leeks - made me want to try more leek dishes
*Mango sorbet with hijiki seaweed and a sauce that tastes like pimento pepper - interesting mixture but worked

Each dish was so unique and cooked to perfection. Many ingredients are not commonly associated but all worked..we were continuously impressed dish after dish. We also tried a couple cocktails which were also amazing! Mine came in a tall glass with egg white froth neatly filled to the top.

Definitely recommend for small parties (2 or 4). The only negative was how close tables are to each other. Make sure to get a res beforehand!
Food was okay, place is pretty small and definitely overrated if you consider value for the dollar.  There are better options in the area.

I don't get the hype or why this is one the World's Top 100 Restaurants. The food was good (though most of the items we ordered were overly salty) but nothing spectacular. Save your trip, go elsewhere.
Absolutely delicious brunch and exceptional service. Great staff and beautiful ambiance. I can't wait to go back for dinner.  Thank you, Estela!

Was a bit hesitant when my friend suggested we come here, given the mixed reviews on Yelp; however I was pleasantly surprised and satisfied with the dinner!

Venue: located on E Houston, Estela provides a rather intimate setting with its dark interior and tables placed close to each other (so may not the best thing for claustrophobic people).  

Service: servers were very on top of it, frequently checking in and quickly taking plates away to make room for more.  While waiting for our table, they led us to the bar to order drinks.  In a rather weird twist, one of the servers dropped and shattered a glass water bottle right next to us.  They immediately cleaned up and made sure we didn't get wet, but the most considerate part was that they decided to take away, even though it as half-eaten, in case there were any glass shards, and brought out a completely new plate.  

Food:  all dishes are great for sharing; they recommend 2-3 dishes for each person.  Small dishes, but pack a punch flavor-wise
- Cured fluke with sea urchin ($23) - great start to the meal, given fluke is a light fish but with enough sea urchin to give the dish a little richness.  Thankfully the sea urchin wasn't too salty, but could have used more of the urchin in the dish, since you had to dig into the center to get that bite
- Summer squash with pine nuts and miso ($17) - we felt obligated to have veggies at dinner and so we went with the squash.  At first glance, the dish just looks like a bunch of sliced squash, until you hit the pine nuts and miso underneath.  Pine nuts gave a much-needed crunch and the miso is such a unique pairing with squash
- Fried arroz negro with squid and romesco ($24) - definitely one of the highlights of the evening.  Loved the crunchy rice (but not burnt) with the soft squid and the squid ink taste.  The romesco was also slightly spicy to give the dish a bit of a kick
- Grilled foie gras and grape leaf ($35) - a very rich dish, so thankfully the grape leaf provided a bit of freshness to the dish.  Do wish there were less grape leaves because we had to kinda of dig though the stringy grape leaves to find the fois gras
- Iberico jamon with parsnip (forgot the price) - recommended by our server, almost looked and tasted like a steak.  Not overcooked and still very tender.

These dishes, including 2 glasses of wine and 2 cocktails ($15 each), all together cost $100+ per person, or $70 per person for food.  

In the end, was impressed with these super-flavorful tapas and service and so was pretty happy with the experience.  Few edits to some dishes and more space would have made it even better, but I won't be too picky about it.

Our meal did not live up to the hype. 

After hearing amazing things about this place from several friends and co-workers we decided to give it a go. Portions were small, food was incredibly salty and the americano estela cocktail I had was undrinkable and had to be sent back

I ordered the pork dish as my entree, and I legitimately thought they brought me the steak entree by accident because (1) the portion was tiny (2) the texture was that of steak and (3) they didn't ask me how I wanted the pork cooked (common practice) and the mystery block of meat I received was cooked rare 

After an appetizer, two entrees and two drinks, we were $100 poorer and still hungry

Maybe it's just me, but I don't get it....

The food was delicious... however when you go to a restaurant with your girls for an overdue catch up, you want at least standard nice service, especially when the restaurant is not cheap.

We made reservations at their website for 2:15pm, we didnt know that this place closes at 3pm, so the waiter was extremely pushy for us to order, to eat and to get out of there. The whole staff was treating us like we should leave. I understand that if you close at 3 you want to close, but if thats the case then do not make reservations so late available... and I could have done the reservation as late as 2:45, because it was a possibility.
This was not a good experience and we will not be coming back to this restaurant.

3.5 stars for brunch but I'm rounding down because of the awkward service and high prices for the portions. I would probably come back to try their dinner.
