This review is a few months overdue but yelp deleted all my reviews in draft form...First of all the space is tiny so there's no real place to wait except the bar which was fairly crowded. Even though they had empty tables they wouldn't seat me until my friend showed so I awkwardly hovered at the bar with my coat. They did offer to take my coat but I wanted to hold onto it since it was cold in the doorway. We ordered the lamb ribs, egg pancetta and avo sandwich, and a salad I think. My friend doesn't eat cheese otherwise I really wanted to try the burrata or ricotta dumpling. My friend asked for them to put the egg on the side since she was pregnant and couldn't have runny yolk but we were sharing so I still wanted the egg and they were really weird about it. They basically said doing that would require a charge for an extra egg and they also couldnt cut it for us in a way that would put the yolk on half the sandwich. So finally we said never mind and they gave us a knife so we could cut it ourselves. Given my friend explained nicely that she was pregnant and putting an egg on the side is a very simple request, I couldn't believe they had to send someone from the kitchen to condescendingly tell us what an impossible request this was. P.S. The sandwich tasted exactly how it sounds, no more no less. For $16 it's a total rip off. The salad was ok, kinda boring but fine. The lamb ribs were delicious but the three tiny ribs (which decreased in size with each rib) were so little for $21 it was tough. Given my friend's dietary restrictions I would be curious to try more adventurous items on the menu but hopefully with better service next time.

Good food, chill, semi pretentious vibe, small plates, high prices. It was pretty relaxed dining experience at the bar. Cocktails were fine, food was tasty. The mussels, endive salad and arroz rice with squid were all exceptional, tartare wasn't as memorable. I'll return when I have productive day at work.

Highly recommended by my friend but deeply disappointed.
All 3 dishes we ordered were considered big entree portion but they are like tapas. Especially with the $2x+ price tag, we were not happy. 
We came here for brunch and I ordered the slab of bacon. I posted a picture and it looks extremely sad. It looks like our country is under famine. Those little potatoes look cute but hard to eat. The bacon was hard!! That's a big no no! How can you make bacon not tasty?
We had the Ricotta dumplings, the portion is also small (considered it's an "entree"). The skin of the dumplings were really mushy. And I don't really understand the circular mushrooms on top. It's hard to pair it with the dumplings together, physically and in terms of taste.
On a side note, the little glasses for beverage were really cute to look at but not practically. We ordered coffee and it was served with that little glass. We can't even hold the glasses to drink the coffee!
Not coming back.
Really enjoyed having brunch here. The food was good, the wine selection was decent and service was attentive.

I guess.

To be perfectly honest, Estela is one of those special occasion "treat yourself" kind of places.I totally understand that this place comes with the distinction of being one of the top restaurants in the world. *Random: How does one determine if a restaurant is one of the top restaurants in the world?* The food is pretty good and it appears that the folks at Estela took time to create menu with a wide variety of options. However, I do not know if the price of the food really matches the amount of or the experience of the food. I would highly recommend that you grab a bite to eat before dinning here, because you will be hungry afterwards. Do not get me wrong, the food is AMAZING, but you do not get much food. Maybe that is how can get return customers. At least you can request extra bread with your "entrees". I highly recommend the beef tartare (heaven on Earth), the fried arroz negro and the ricotta dumplings. Also, Estela has a very diverse wine list, so can drink what you lack in food.  I should have just drank wine rather than teasing my stomach with the food. 

The atmosphere of the is restaurant is very busy but in a good way. Although the restaurant looks pretty intimate, it can be a little loud. We dined here on a weeknight and the place was packed. It seems like a great place to get fancy cocktails and catch up with an old (or a new) friend. The two times that I have been here my party did not have a wait getting a table with a reservation. The hostess and our waitress were so friendly and nice. I wish that I remembered their names, so I could give them a shout out. I have to say that I did not have a single issue with the service at Estela, which is very rare for a restaurant in NYC.

I do not completely dislike this place, but this is a place where I could justify going only once a year.

My friend and I had brunch here this morning, and it was phenomenal. We split the celery salad (much better than it sounds), whitefish English muffin, eggs & beans, and ricotta dumplings. Everything was incredibly fresh and flavorful, portioned perfectly for sharing. We finished our brunch with the chocolate cake (isn't that how all brunches should end?), and were beyond full and satisfied. Our server was also very nice and helpful. She was genuinely excited about me trying everything for the first time. To top it off, they take reservations, which is all too rare for great brunch spots in NYC.

First off - the food is great. No complaints about the food which is the reason we've been there twice. What sucks is the noise level. Maybe the noisiest restaurant I've ever eaten in. I'm sure  there are those who go for that - a kind of sports bar fine dining ambience where you yell to talk to the person sitting next to you and lean in to hear what they're saying. And I'm sure there are those who love listening to a neo-Wayne's World playlist blasting out of strategically placed speakers while they're eating beautifully prepared food. Not me. Love the food but not into go-go dining. Won't be back.

All hype. Food totally average.
This restaurant is on the San Pellegrino list as one of the top 100 best restaurants in the world....seriously?
I guess it pays to be a sponsor of San Pellegrino? Or in the "club". It is beyond me how a restaurant like this would even be considered on a list like that, in the same sentence as some of those restaurants.
Service was pretentious, and rude. We were made to feel as thought we were lucky to be eating there. Uncomfortable seats, average coffee. 
Yes. We went for brunch. But if you are open for brunch it should be as good as your dinner. No excuses.
Eggs were supposed to be poached, they were hammered. Presentation sloppy. Bread soggy. 
1 star because it was one of the most expensive brunches we have ever been to, even by NYC standards, and the food didn't even deliver. 1 for the service. 
Don't waste your time or money.

If you like paying more than what things are worth, by all means rush to Estela. Although the burrata was tasty as was the steak, the portions are minuscule and, if you are sane, you will feel robbed.

We went here last night for dinner. The food was absolutely amazing. The waiter recommended 4-5 dishes for the two of us. We went for four and a dessert, which was perfect. 
Food rundown:
1. "Burrata, salsa verde, and charred bread": This was probably the best burrata, I've tried in the city. Next time we'll probably get two. Absolutely delicious. The combination of the mild, soft burrata and the crunchy charred bread was perfect.

In between the two dishes they gave us complimentary "Padron peppers with aioli and salmon bottarga". These were delicious - especially the aioli was dreamy. When the nice waiter came with them, I asked if they were spicy, "Only one in ten". Quite an interesting game. Luckily I did not get any spicy ones, and I would probably order these the next time. 

2. "Summer squash with miso and pine nuts" This looked so pretty, but very small, when it came out, and as the big foodie I am, I was sure this would be disappointing. It was not! Underneath the thinly cut squash were the miso and pine nuts, which were absolutely delicious However I would probably try something different next time, as it wasn't super interesting taste-wise.

3. "Fried arroz negro with squid and romesco" This was served as a quite boring-looking black rice dish, but it was so, so good. There was a crunchiness to it, and the squid ink and squid itself was so delicious. Will order again.

4. "Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo" This was probably the most beautiful dish of the night AND so tasty. The thinly cut mushrooms on top were such a perfect balance to the soft ricotta dumplings. I will dream of these in the future. Will order again. 

5. For dessert we had the panna cotta with vinegar and honey. What an experience! Most interesting dessert I've had here in New York. Will order again.

Definitely go here. The ambience is perfect with spot on lighting and well-balanced music and volume. The service was nice and attentive, and the space was cute.

As Public Enemy would have said it... don't believe the hype!! This place was pretty average. The food is good and satisfies, but didn't give me my big (food) O. Had the burrata(very good), lamb ribs (good), dumplings (ok), monk fish (meh) and chocolate cake (best part of the night). It did get pretty crowded on a Friday night. I sat at the bar cause there were no tables. Bumped many elbows, but I'm not mad about that.

Estela is rated in the San Pelli top 100 restaurants in the world but based on my experience, I just don't think it's on that level. It's not terrible but not top 100. 

The food here was decent but the chef has a heavy hand when it comes to salt. 2 of the 3 dishes we got were way too salty. The only highlight was the ricotta dumplings which had very good balance and a much needed break from the other two dishes. The lamb ribs were almost inedible because it was so salty and very fatty, even for my standards. 

Service is pretty good. Perhaps a bit understaffed but the workers were friendly and helpful despite that. there is only one bathroom which results in a constant line up. Not great ambience when someone is standing right behind your table from time to time waiting to use the facilities.

My girlfriend and I came here for her birthday, having heard a lot of great things about it. Have to say, we left a little disappointed.

Don't get me wrong--the food was pretty damn good, and not *terribly* overpriced given the location and quality. The ambience is a little sterile/cold. Not very romantic. The servers and manager on duty were all very lovely and charming people.

My main gripe is that we were seated next to a table full of loud, drunk, French tourists, three bros who were having quite the ball at 9pm on a Monday. The way the restaurant is laid out, the tables are very close together, so we were pretty much right next to them. It was annoying but I more or less blocked it out, at first.

As the meal went on, they got more and more loud, and ceased to be jovial. One of them was clearly upset (or fake upset, I don't know) about something, and kept sharply telling his friend across the table to "shut the f*ck up." Again, I'm not a huge prude, or even somebody that needs every restaurant in Manhattan to be as quiet as a church, but this was really notably unpleasant, aggressive, and noticeable for the kind of establishment Estela is.

I eventually tapped him on the shoulder and asked him if he could please quiet down, because he was being very loud and irritating and disturbing our dinner. He looked at me and then spluttered "no, no I will not." Fair enough, I flagged down a server and complained, asking that something be done about it.

Again, nothing really against the servers or manager. The manager came by very quickly and apologized, and said "when a table opens up" we would be moved, if we wanted. I imagine they spoke to the table full of jerkoffs as well, but I didn't really see. Apparently (according to my gf) the guy I spoke to kept muttering about "if that guy touches me one more time" etc. Whatever. They died down to ignorable levels and dinner continued. The manager came by again and apologized, offering to move us, but at that point they were getting ready to leave and we were more or less over it, so we thanked her, but declined. Eventually they left. I will say that one of them, the guy that was being sworn at, apologized to us, said they were all jet-lagged and his friend was going through some sort of nonsense, etc. He bought us a drink before he left. That was nice of him.

I know none of this was really the fault of anybody working at the restaurant or the chef, but I can't help but have a sour taste in my mouth. We paid quite a bit of money for this bill, for a birthday dinner, and the table next to us was very clearly intoxicated, being profane, and disturbing other customers, and they didn't get kicked out? They comped us a dessert as well, which was also nice.

I don't know. I suppose everything that I wished had happened, happened, and most of it is on that one dipshit tourist (ugly Europeans=the new ugly Americans), but I can't help but be irritated that we had to put up with it. Why wasn't he cut off or told to leave when they started to totally lose it? I suppose I could have been much more vocal with the staff, who once again, were very on top of it, or as much as one could expect. I just wish people would behave themselves in public and not ruin other people's dinners. 

The beef tartare is really good.
Wow! Wow! Each entre was amazing taste, quality food and presentation. Service is excellent. Atmosphere casual dressy Italian feeling. A must if your in Greenwich Area.

Do not come here if you're looking to get a filling meal on a good dime. Prices are out of control and dishes are small. That being said, truly one of the best restaurants in New York City. The service is impeccable. The food is so good. Most dishes have such an exotic twist on them. Really worth every penny honestly.
Food was good. But portions were quite small and pricey...Ambience of the restaurant was good. Size of the restaurant was smaller than expected though.
Everything was beautiful and tasty but portion size for price is very small. The burrata was my favorite. Husband liked the beef tartare. Abalone and fluke was okay, again very small.

I really enjoyed Estela.  The flavors are delicate and the presentation is lovely.  My favorites were the squid ink crunchy rice, the steak tartare, and the ricotta gnocchi with mushrooms.  Cute spot but a bit small.  Cozy atmosphere.  I'd suggest making a reservation.  Nothing mind blowing but a very good meal and reasonably priced.
The food was hit or miss for me.  The squid crunchy rice was one of the best dishes I've ever had, but the other dishes were forgettable for me.

Simply perfection! All I can say is you must go!
Recs:
  Endive salad
  Ricotta dumplings 
  Burrata 
You won't be disappointed.

No the place to go on a budget, let's start with that. Place is expensive. You get what you pay for, didn't have one bite that was not amazing. Throw all caution to the wine and order to your hearts desire, you will not be disappointed (unless you're on a budget and doesn't understand tasting style portions.)

Went here for a birthday, and must honestly say that a two star rating connoting "Meh. I've experienced better." is 100% apt. The food was just okay.  We ordered a variety of dishes, including:

- Arroz Negro squid ink rice (which could have been great but was too salty)
- Burrata (which would have been good, so hard to f* up, but came in a plate of what tasted like juiced parsley, and on top of 1 piece of bread - disappointing to say the least)
ricotta gnocchi with a mushroom broth (the highlight of the evening), and -Lamb ribs (okay).

In addition, as other reviews mentioned, the restaurant is unbelievably cramped and noisy. Service is good. Prices are okay. This is really a restaurant where people go to be seen, in  my opinion. Was disappointed especially as we canceled a reservation at Cosme to eat here instead.  :-( Expected much better.

Estela is a small restaurant tucked away in the lower east that offers great dishes at a hefty price. Believe in the hype and dine here but either eat a pre dinner snack or expect to spend to feel full. We tried a few cocktails and split a bottle of wine. All of which were exceptional. The staff definitely knew their stuff. Come here for a special date night but expect to be in a cramped space. All the dishes we've had here were great but they have a black rice dish that was a standout for us. 

Getting a reservation may prove annoying so be prepared for that but aside from that a great special occasion restaurant.

The service was great, and the lighting was nice, but in general we found it trendy, loud, and overpriced. We went just to try the restaurant and ended up spending $70 for two appetizers and a cocktail. I live in the area; I know Manhattan prices. As another reviewer said, I would be more than happy to pay that or more if the plates were great, but these just weren't. 

The burrata had a good texture, but it was very salty, and it came with an herby sauce that tasted like the herbs had started to wilt. The toast with mussels was just okay, and the portion was tiny. Cocktail was essentially an extra sour G&T without the fizz.
Bad bad service, food was good, but service felt very rushed, for the price point it was really not worth it, this was our second time there, and we will definitely will not be going back
Very good place for dinner. A bit Japanese sent and chic. Mood is romantic. Staff are super kind. You should get the reservation. Bar is the best seat for date night.

A small-ish, quaint, cozy, spot right off Houston. We sat at the bar because, well, just walk in and you'll see why. What a great vibe. The bartender was fantastic too. Attentive, personable, knowledgeable, and well dressed (that matters too haha). For brunch we started with a glass of white wine and NY's own "Yatch Lager". Great selection of wines and beers. Like I always say, you don't need 100 options on your menu, just a few great ones. We started with the burrata with salsa verde and charred bread. Simple perfection. The only problem here is you'll want to order another one and not try anything else on the menu. Trust me. The combo of Creamy burrata, tart salsa verde and the charred bread just warms you and leaves you licking the plate. Next, we had the eggs with beans, harissa and mojama (thin dried salted fish). Loved every bite of this! Everything here was spot on. Service, taste, value and location. Thanks Estela! Can't wait to come back!

Dining at Estela was an experience but I'm not sure if I would recommend it to everyone. The dishes are rather small so it gets pricey pretty easily. We ordered six different dishes/courses to share between the four of us, even though I think they recommend ordering 8-10 for four people. I left the restaurant feeling full, but not all of us did. 

We felt like the staff were rushing us between courses, up to the point that we had to ask our waiters not to collect the plates before everyone at the table was finished.

The restaurant itself is cozy yet elegant, and our own waiter remembered all of our many dietary restrictions incredibly well.

After dining for the 3rd time (once brunch, twice dinner), I officially believe  it does not expectations (contrary to my friends' opinions). Dishes are too average for the price (*). Service is great though.

(*) Crab & seaweed salad was awesome though.

I went here so long ago that I can't recount exactly what I ordered, but what I can recount is that it is still the most memorable dining experience I've had since I moved to NYC 1.5 years ago. 

The dish that stands out the most was one of their deconstructed chocolate dishes--I can still almost taste the flavor and texture today. I will definitely be back.

Dining confounded.  Think that based on your extensive food and dining experience you've got a good idea of what's going to be on the next plate - hah!  Estela will surprise you with every delicious morsel.  

Who puts a restaurant in a 2nd-floor walk up behind a dinky sign?  A culinary bellwether with a unique and impeccable vision, based on this place.

Estela is totally food forward.  In addition to the unusual siting and signage, the decor is understated to a fault.  The gender-neutral restroom is clean and utilitarian, but a far cry from the lavatorial sideshows that become a talking point for many restaurants.  Service is what economists call Pareto optimal - perfectly balanced to the task of guiding customers through an eclectic menu and making sure their experience is unruffled. 

All of this is by way of creating a clean backdrop for food that beggars description.  Cured fluke on sea urchin?  Slab of fish on yellow paste, right?  Nah!  It's delicately marinated fish hashed and formed into a silver-dollar-sized disc floating on a delectable bed of uni.  Fried arroz negro with squid and romesco?  Crunchy pancake of rice with chunks of cephalopod.  Wrong again.  Bits of crackling rice interspersed with sweet/savory melange of tasty rice and flavorful but subtle nuggets of squid.  Makes it very hard not to crowd out your dining partners at the plate.

We had six dishes in all for our party of 3 (not including two exquisite desserts).  I won't describe each of them.  Rather, just go and delight in what is sure to be one of the pinnacle meals of your life.

So incredibly good. The food was literally flawless. The only reason it didnt get 5 stars was due to some portions being too small (esp the orange with shrimp) & not warranting the price (said orange with shrimp shaving was $18 and it more or less was an orange albeit a tasty one!). Solid wine list & sommelier. Excellent gin & tonic. Friendly & professional staff. Very little to complain about.

Had an interesting brunch here over the weekend. "Interesting" because you'll immediately notice the brunch menu is definitely unique. 

SO happy to see that burrata (5/5) is also on the brunch menu, absolutely one of my favorites. Same goes for the ricotta dumplings (5/5) which are the pillowiest lil balls that contrast nicely with thinly shaved raw mushroom. Ordered an endive salad (3.5/5) per recommendation of our waitress, which was heavy handed in the anchovy and too funky for all of us. I also felt the english muffin with whitefish (4/5) was touch too fishy, although still quite delicious. Eggs with beans (3.5/5) sounded better than it ended up being, there are heartier richer versions out there. We ordered an egg pancetta avocado sandwich (4.5/5) for good measure to have something more brunchy, can't really go wrong with this combo. 

I loved my dinner experience more than brunch here, especially since my 2 favorite dishes are on both menus. The tapas-style pacing and service is also preferred for dinner. Overall I think it is a spot better suited to warmer weather with its large range of cold dishes.

Estela is is cool place to bring a date or a place for a fun get together for gossipy women. Order some tapas and wine and chat the night away. 

For regular folks that wants to be full and feel like they got their money's worth... maybe it's not for you. 5 plates of food, no wine, plus tip - $172. Delicious food? Yes. Worth it? No. It was worth $120 max for what we ate. 

Iberico ham - must say it was almost close to the bellota in Spain. Almost. 

Clams - flavor was confusing. Definitely butter. Definitely lemon. Couldn't figure what else was there that made it taste like puke. 

Fried rice negro with squid - ohhhh this was good. Very good. 

Lamb ribs - if you love fat, tender cumin crusted meat, you'll love this. 

Steak with bernaise and turnips. Steak was really delicious. Buttery. Two little slabs were $38 so the quality was really good.

Absolutely delicious food.
Burrata, Truffle pasta were especially good.
Would like to come back whenever we can.
This is now my favorite restaurant in NYC. The food at dinner was amazing, the staff was super knowledgeable and there were so many options for me with several restrictive allergies. I will be back!

After reading that the Obamas came here, I brought my dad here for brunch. Unfortunately, the food was disappointing, especially the endive, which was too sour and raw simultaneously. The 2 stars are for service and ambiance. Save your money and don't come here.

Not sure about the hype of this place. Food was below mediocre and overpriced.  Spiced almonds, pickled carrots, olives for appetizers were so tasteless. Monkfisk was overcooked, steak was mediocre. Foie gras in grape leave was the only edible item but honestly you know you can eat foie gras with anything. Also this restaurant is NOT accommodating at all. When I asked for ice cream they said we have sweet potato dessert with ice cream and they only have  just enough ice cream to serve with the dessert.  Really?  Is this a mom and pop shop where they count every penny. And when I ordered that dessert so i can get the ice cream the sweet potato dessert was disgusting. If people think this place serves good food they have no idea what tasty food is.

Burrata is incredible here. Seriously. One of the best burratas I've had for sure. Gnocchi with shaved mushroom, mussels escabeche, and arroz negro were all great as well. 

Need to return for brunch to try the sandwich.

Only downside is that it's quite a crowded space, but sit by the bar and enjoy the delicious food.

Came here with a group of 4 for a Sunday night dinner.  It's a very small space and we were lucky to have a booth up front so we had a good amount of space and didn't feel cramped.

Our server was generally nice and attentive, though there is a pet peeve I have that came up (more on this later).

The menu is all meant to be shared and so we ordered a bunch of items for the table.

Beef tartare - this was gluten free with the bread on the side, and I thoroughly enjoyed it.

Burrata - this was also gluten free with the charred bread substituted for gluten free bread.  So they have gluten free bread +1.  But, for some reason I still don't understand they refused to serve this dish to us without any bread on it (so the bread had to be gluten free, at least they had that option), and they wouldn't give us the charred bread on the side.  I had this happen to me at the spotted pig before and I'm never going back there because of it, but apparently these chefs don't like the way the dish looks without the bread on it because there's just a blob of cheese.  I don't bloody care that it looks bad, I'm the customer and I'm always right.  And even if you for some crazy reason need bread on it, at least give us the charred bread on the side.  Well we got the burrata with the gluten free bread, and then what looked like burned regular bread was brought out on the side - I assume this was the charred bread so seems like we got it in the end anyway, but the whole thing was ridiculous and annoying.

Cara cara orange with dried shrimp. While good, in no world is this worth $18.

Endive, walnuts, anchovy - this was one of my favorite things we ordered.

Steak with with black sesame Bernaise - very tasty and well cooked, though a small portion

Clams - these were good but nothing special and was pretty small portion.

Monkfish with beets - very soft and well cooked, though a small portion.

For dessert - their chocolate dessert is naturally gluten free and it was very good
Our dining companions ordered the sweet potato dessert and it was way too rum flavored for my liking.

I'll probably be back eventually after I get over my annoyance at the chef - the food was good, though generally small portions.

What a great restaurant, we had such wonderful dinner last night. The atmosphere is elegant but laid back, the service is very thoughtful and excellent, and the food was really unique and extraordinary. 

To drink, we ordered cocktails to start, we had a grapefruit gin cocktail which was very good, but the winner was a cocktail called "The Friend Zone," it's always fun when a great cocktail has a good name to match it. We had a corner seat at the bar, and Ramsey, the bartender, was so great, we just stayed at the bar instead of going to our table, and we would do it again in a heartbeat. 

For dinner we ordered: 

Beef Tartare 
Walnut & Endive Salad 
Raw shrimp with peas 
Ricotta dumplings 
Pork with mushrooms 

Everything was delicious, and recommended by Ramsey, who steered us in the right direction. We will be back soon.

I came here as I saw that the chef was nominated for best chef for the James Beard awards.

When I arrived, I realized that I had actually dined at Estela before!

We were immediately seated and the service was on point throughout the night. I feel like in NYC, that is a rarity (although it shouldn't be). They also were able to adapt and make my favorite cocktail (not on the menu)!

The food I thought was so-so. The dishes were soooo tiny and I felt like it wasn't anything extremely special or that I hadn't tried before. We ordered:
Cured fluke with sea urchin
Mussels escabeche on toast 
Endive, walnuts, anchovy, and ubriaco rosso salad
Fried arroz negro with squid and romesco
Red snapper

and we ordered 2 desserts (although I can't remember which ones at this point)

The best dishes in my opinion were the mussels escabeche on toast and the fried arroz (rice). 

The ricotta dumplings sounded interesting although we didn't opt for that but I would be curious to know what those tasted like.

The restaurant itself is super cozy / romantic and a great vibe. The service was on point. The food wasn't bad but just wasn't a ridiculously positive experience for the price or on par with a James Beard nomination for best chef.

I may have to return for brunch as I'm reading Yelp reviews, it seems like that's the best way to go!

This restaurant needs to get the fuck over themselves. I can't stand snooty people trying to convince me to have dinner at 10 pm. No thanks!! There are thousands of restaurants in this city. I don't need your pity reservation.

Overall, the food was pretty decent; small portions, all meant to be shared. We ordered the English muffin with the whitefish and the lamb ribs - which put our ratings to 4.5 stars. It was our waitress that, unfortunately, led to our rating of 2 stars (which is actually more than generous). She was rude, not helpful and gave us the biggest attitude, for no apparent reason. Everytime we asked for suggestions or for something, it was a quick nod with no facial expression. Not sure about how other people have brunch in the city, but I would think they would want to enjoy brunch in a much friendlier environment.

Overall, a very disappointing experience since I was super excited to try this place, and it wasn't the food or the rest of the staff that impacted the rating, but just the behavior of our waitress.

Maybe my expectations were too high after reading other diners' reviews and the accolades of the two owners.

Our party of 4 was  seated upon arrival and service was great throughout. This was a Sunday brunch outing.

A nice space - cozy, lively, and folks enjoying themselves.

We had the usual cocktails and coffees to start. Pretty standard stuff.

Here's what we had - some shared: burrata salad, oro blanco, lamb ribs, Danish, carrots, beets, and slab bacon. Food generally good but nothing except maybe the slab bacon and burrata as memorable. Many of the dishes were quite small.

We finished with a panna cotta.

Damagers were $280 with tip. We easily could have spent $350 if we added a bottle of wine.

It just wasn't a good let alone a  great experience that would cause me to say "I just got to go back". 

Hopefully you'll have a better experience.

Omg! Omg! Omg! We had four plates and all were exquisite. Had the Ibérico ham, the blood cake sandwich,black rice n those billowy dumplings. The staff were all accommodating, friendly, helpful. Don't want to leave n wanna come back tomorrow. A Perfect dining experience. Try a few of their delicious beers.

We didn't know what to expect heading into Estela but wow we're we happy we went. 
Fantastic ambiance, incredible food and great service.
I highly highly highly recommend the dumplings. I don't think I've ever had anything quite like them.
Our server Michele was always attentive, extremely pleasant and very knowledgeable.
As for the bar.... come with a taste for great cocktails and finish with one of the spectacular wines in their list.
We had the cara cara orange with fried shrimp, ricotta dumplings and muscles on toast (pictured)

I love the plating aesthetic here-- simple, no fuss which allows you to really focus on the quality and flavors of the ingredients itself. This is emphasized especially in the endive and the oro blanco salad dishes. The balance of vegetables and meat on the menu is also laudable as it caters to both vegetarians and meat lovers. Also appreciated are the unique ingredients used in the dishes. Between the 5 of us, we ordered 8 dishes to share, and we left feeling a "good full." Definitely make reservations on Resy as the space is on the small side.
Amazing food, good service.  Was seated a bit late to our table but the staff bought us a round of drinks.  Food was unreal, highly recommend!!

This is definitely an over rated and over priced eatery. The food was decent but nothing special. Don't mind paying premium for outstanding food but paying even 50% of the tab would have pinched. The ambiance ans service too was just above average.

After reading about it, I really wanted to check out this restaurant. We came around 5-ish and negotiated a booking at 9 o'clock the same evening. Perfect. Except when arriving shortly before 9, we were told that our booking was for 9:15. Now, I don't mind waiting 15 minutes for my table to be ready, but I do mind not apologizing for messing up, AND pretending we had not booked for 9 o'clock.
We were told we could take a refreshment while waiting (not on the house, though), and after being pushed around because the place is super busy (monday evening), we were finally asked (told) to go sit at the lovely big open window to wait..
Twenty minutes later, the lady lets us know that the guests sitting at our table are "taking their time", if we wanna wait or wanna sit at the bar instead. I actually enjoy eating at the bar so this was a no-brainer.
We were quickly given glasses of water and got a cocktail, but there was no follow up so had to grab the waiter (bartender) to order the food. We were then told that our selections (most expensive two items on the menu) would properly not be enough food for us (steak and pork) and was recommended to order some more. So, we added a shrimp thing to share.
All three items were delicious. Nicely spiced, great on the palate, super cooked - but barely enough for us. The steak was not a steak, but two big slices of steak (or roast?) topped with a handful of crispy salad leaves and a yummi tapernade to balance it out. Real nice.
The Rhône I had selected for the steak was flawless, but way too young (2016) and super acidic, and didn't go well with the food. 
For dessert we had a delicious chocolate cake covered in smoooooth whipped cream - essentially a chocolate fondant and real tasty. I asked the (other) bartender, who was super cool and very friendly, to make me a custom negroni with gin and vermouth of my choice, which she did to perfection.
Super food, so-so service, awesome bartending.

Our experience was astonishingly lackluster. The Manhattan had way too much sweet vermouth and somehow the bartender ruined Estela's margarita. She took the drinks back after a sip, and we just ordered bourbon neat... which the bartender delivered on the rocks. So we clarified, and the bartender drained the bourbon into new glasses and brought them back to us (?). 

And the burrata isn't good, unlike the reviews say. It's doused with vinegar, unless my mouth was just overwhelmed by the vermouth.

$24 dollars for 4 Lamb Ribs the size of my index finger is highway

robbery. Don't believe the hype, Brunch was absurdly expensive

given the inadequate portions. Never again.

Estela has been on my list for years as it's a nice small plates place near me that despite its excellent reputation is not too difficult to reserve, but I could never quite motivate myself to go. With Ignacio Mattos' recent James Beard nod, I took advantage of my parents' visit (or took advantage of them?) to book a table for brunch.

We were seated for our 12:30 Sunday reservations at two small circular tables for our party of 4-- my parents remarked that it was almost as cramped as Prune. It's a romantic, industrial-inflected space which would make for a sexy dinner spot. Volume levels were decent.

Their brunch menu largely takes the greatest hits from the dinner list and adds a few offbeat breakfast options, like a fried bloodcake sandwich and english muffin with smoked whitefish. Cocktails were similarly avant-garde, and though boozy quite pricey for the pour. We tried four among us-- the Sin Nombre ($17) was the winner, a perfect spicy mezcal drink, but the rest were just a little too overproof to love.

We had planned to order an entree each and a couple share plates, but were told we needed 2-3 dishes a person. We erred on the fewer side at 8, and perhaps should have gotten a couple more as portions are miniscule. Overall, I found presentation pretty but the food to be either underwhelming or precious. Here's the rundown.

Oro blanco ($17): This is an artistic plate of grapefruit slices hiding a small pile of marcona almonds and powerfully salty salt-cured tuna, dotted with some kind of balsamic. The grapefruit slices had a pleasant cleanness to them, but failed to gel with the other components to me, and the portion size is laughably small. Skip it.

Burrata ($16): Good stuff! Salsa verde worked, high quality burrata, nice char on the bread. Not much too it but one of the better dishes.

Lamb ribs ($21): Although on the fatty side, the spices in the crust were quite nice.

Egg and pancetta sandwich ($16): Probably the most normal dish on the menu, but well executed.

Slab bacon ($20): An almost absurdist version of classic bacon and eggs, with a pop-art fried egg over easy and some seriously thick bacon that approached pork belly. Not much to it but again one of the favorites.

Carrot salad ($17): Okay components but again laughably small and simple for the price. Skip it.

Grilled beets ($15): Nah, son, literally three half-beets with a couple well-salted leaves and a normal bearnaise sauce. Skip it. 

Panna cotta with vinegar and honey ($12): The vinegar-honey is a nice touch, but the underlying panna cotta was bland, if technically correct. Skip it.

Overall, damages after tax and tip were over $70 a person, which just didn't feel worth it on both the portion and the execution side. Service was good, but fell short of a high-end experience to me. Pacing was good at 1.5 hours. I'm having a hard time figuring out what exactly bothered me here, but I was so put off by it that visiting Flora Bar and Cafe Altro Paradiso have moved down on my priority list. There just wasn't anything special enough here to justify the price... and I wasn't even paying.
Amazing place you won't be believe how good this place is! It's easily a top 10 restaurant and probably the most reasonably priced.

With all the restaurants in New York we came here on a friend recommendation.  What a mistake. Silly puny portions. Inedible steak (where they refused to cook the steak to even medium rare) and limited menu.  Not worth trying in my opinion.  There are few places worse than this.

I had trouble convincing the wife to come here - she was not excited by the menu.  That changed when our first dishes arrived.  The beef tartare was exceptional - well seasoned, and not like any traditional preparations we've had before.  Our cocktails and wine kept us in a good mood while our other dishes continued to be delivered, each one better than the last (favorites were the snapper and the grilled foie gras).  Even the dessert, of which she was unsure, was fantastic (sweet potato and vanilla ice cream).  I look forward to heading back on my next NYC trip.

I adored my experience here! Service is warm and non-intrusive and the food is inventive and excellent. Highlights were fried arroz negro (tasted like the best crispy bits of a seafood/squid ink paella), Endive with walnuts, anchovy, and ubriaco rosso (the flavors combined perfectly in this dish) and the foie gras with grape leaf. If I had to pass on one dish for next time it would be the ricotta and mushroom dumplings.

One of the servers also gave us champagne on the house after overhearing that it was a special occasion which was a wonderful touch! Would highly recommend Estela for interesting and well executed small plates, and a cute buzzy atmosphere.

Incredible experience here! Estela recently won a James Beard award and it is well deserved. Everything we ordered was exceptional! 

The croissant on the egg sandwich is incredible. We ordered without pancetta. The burrata toast was unlike any other. The trout muffin may look basic but somehow it is mind blowing. Love love love this place.

I was treated to one of the top five meals of my life at Estela.  Our lovely server explained we should order and enjoy our food from the menu top down.  So.. we started with the oysters which I will dream about for the rest of my life.  When I tipped the oyster into my mouth, I was treated to a sea delicacy cradled in two types of homemade vinegar, along with various gentle seasonings.  It was so magical we ordered a second portion. 
We then had the mussels and burrata cheese on homemade bread.  All delicious but my next favorite was the arroz negro.  Cooked so perfectly with just the right bounce back, it made me want to cry. 
Next came the lamb chops with mint and dumplings with thinly shaved mushrooms on top.  All divine. 
The dessert did not disappoint.  The panna cotta was creamy with a bit of salt and the chocolate cake will also bless my dreams. 
Thank you for such an amazing dining experience!!

Holy crap- if this is 5 stars I need to back and change all of my previous 5 stars to 4. This is probably the best meal I've ever had. I came here for dinner, and everything we ordered was wonderful. I am still dreaming of the squid ink rice. The endive salad was also amazing, as was the urchin and the beef tartar. I'm just anxiously awaiting the next special occasion to justify coming back because it is a bit pricey.

Estela I really wanted to love you. I liked you but love it was not. Food was good but I can think of many other restaurants in other towns (SF, LA) that I like a lot more. Also the seating is funky, the wine selection tends towards the interesting but not that pleasant, and the menu is slightly over priced for what it is.
Mind-blowing food with simplicity and attention to details. Perfection achieved with service and beverages too

Estela exceeded expectations by far! Granted, I went after reading some reviews that slightly lowered my bar, but regardless, I know I would have loved the meal just as much. I really appreciated the concept, I think they did an exceptional job at highlighting one, maybe two, ingredients in each dish, with fresh, seasonal flavors that really stood out to create something unique when paired together. Each dish as a whole tasted very novel, I remember exclaiming after each bite that I had never had anything like it before, and wasn't sure how I'd again have the more generic, subtle version.  My only complaint is the acoustics, but thats unsurprising and not at all a deal breaker for such a compact space, just a warning for anyone on a first date, etc. I also loved their wine list! I recommend everything I ordered - the endive, shrimp & peas, lamb ribs, and ricotta dumplings - but I am going to underscore the endives if you're in the mood for something light, crunchy, and so so flavorful. Its probably not given enough credit since it's not a staple, entree like dish, but boy does it deserve it given the awesome texture and taste. I recommend consulting with the waiter about which dishes to order based on your preferences and mood that night, everyone was very helpful. Definitely keep Estela high on your list!

Yes the bacon is amazing! We had the lamb ribs which was very good and buttery but outrageously expensive for such a small portion. Everything else was just underwhelming: Egg breakfast, Oysters Migonette. Will not be returning.

I'd give this place a 3.5 if I could. My girlfriend took me here as this place came highly recommended by a number of nyc chefs we had the pleasure of talking to, so expectations were fairly high. 

This place is tapas style, where you order a number of small plates. For the two people they recommended 4-5 plates. We ordered the special - zuchinni flowers with scallops (meh), cured sea bream w/ sea urchin (meh), endives (ok), beef tartar (great), chocolate cake (amazing). We also got the ricotta dumplings, but after one small bite my stomach soured and I decided not to eat any more and let my girlfriend have the rest. I enjoyed the one bite I had and my girlfriend thought it was really good.  

I will say that everything was expertly crafted and the textures of everything was wonderful to eat. Its mostly the actual flavor that I found lacking.

Amazing food!!! Yes it's a little cramped, it's a little noisy but if you are a foodie, this place is a must. 2 of us shared 6 plates and 2 desserts.  No favorites because every one was interesting and delicious.  And fantastic waiter who was friendly, professional and able to explain exactly  how the fried arroz negro was prepared when I asked.  Not a cheap meal but worth putting on your list! (If the setting was a little nicer this would definitely be 5 stars.)
The restaurant double charged my tip. We put $30 for the tip and they charged us $60 for tip.  This has never happened before in any restaurant.  Also, the food was not worth what we paid for it.

I'm surprised how people can like it. Food is nothing special, personnel is snarky, chairs are uncomfortable. Tight space, very loud. If you sit by the wall, you don't have any personal space. You are trapped between the table and other people on the left and right. You can't even go wash your hands without making people around you all stand up, so you can squeeze in. Food is a joke. Coffee worst ever. Plates are to share but food is difficult to divide between people. Tiny little plates of tasteless food for $20. The whole room is dark, uninviting. Glasses are all dirty and scratched. Don't waste your time people.
A cozy little place with great Tapas. Want to try everything on the menu. The Fried Arroz is a must try. Will return for brunch soon.

I really don't get the hype over Estela. If you don't have a refined palate or simply want to experience weirdly bad food I guess it might be worth checking Estela out, but I was tremendously disappointed. 

Beef tartare with sunchoke- 1/5
This dish seems to be very hyped, but it was probably one of the worst beef/steak tartares I have ever had (and I would consider myself a steak tartare connoisseur having had hundreds if not thousands over the years). The best way to describe it is as an oversalted tuna tartare, but with beef instead of tuna. You don't have any of the richness of a classic steak tartare and it was absolutely drenched in salt. 

Cured fluke with uni- 1.5/5
Ok, so it was santa barbara uni, and the uni itself was good, but overall this dish was a gooey mess. The cured fluke was oversalted (there's a theme here), and overall the dish just had a fairly nasty texture and no balance. Couldn't finish the dish. 

Mussels escabeche on toast- 3.5/5
They brought this to us on the house and it was the best dish of the night. Nothing truly special, but it was refreshing to have at least one dish that was decent. 

Arroz negro with squid and romesco- 1/5
Another salty disaster. This was borderline inedible. I feel it's worth noting that I do not shy away from salty food (most would say I have a preference for more salt in my food), but the food here was ridiculously oversalted, even for me. 

Tilefish with squash blossoms- 3/5
I'm a big fan of tilefish and it was cooked well, albeit again, being a bit too salty. Probably could have been a 4/5 or even 4.5/5 had it not been over-seasoned. 

Cocktails were pretty decent, maybe a 4/5 quality-wise, but the service was slow and selection wasn't that great so even on drinks I'd drop them to a 3/5 overall. 
All in all an awful experience. I can whip up much better food at home, and we had to go grab a bite elsewhere after leaving as we had trouble finishing most of the dishes at Estela. 
Hell, I could go to chipotle and enjoy a meal there more (and at least I won't have to worry about my blood pressure going through the roof due to eating a kilogram of salt). The execution on the food was just atrocious here.

Every dish we had here was on point. Dishes are playfully creative and thoughtfully balanced. Flavor profiles are interesting and showcase quality ingredients, without resorting to heavyhanded flavors or even overly complex plating. Simplicity in presentation reflects discernment and reverence for ingredients and an emphasis on cooking techniques. I grew up and lived in many countries in Asia, and unlike many modern American restaurants I've been to at all price points, I never felt Estela is trying to serve fusion for the sake of it, rather I feel it has taken inspirations and universal flavor profiles from everywhere and only apply them to its own dishes if they elevate the dish or the ingredients in season. And the fact the dishes are not as in your face heavy makes for a very comfortable and relaxing dining experience.

Really enjoyed this restaurant. A very interesting wine list and manageable menu made this a really fun experience. 
The oysters were fresh and the foie gras was delish. Was a tight fit but so are most restaurants in NYC. I would certainly recommend this place. Service was very good and my server was exceptional. Two asterisks...no California wines offered and no cappuccino with dessert although my own coffee carafe made up for it.

Tried Estela a long time ago and had very good memories so decided to try it out for brunch. Both my friend and I had the avocado/egg sandwish that was delicious! The mix of salty and sugary flavors of the bun was amazing. I just wish they served lattes for brunch. Also the place could use a decor update, as it didn't have a very cosy vibe. But I would definitely go back for that sandwish!

We came here after hearing a recommendation from a chef. This is a small place and it was packed and a little cramped. We had a reservation but ended up waiting over 20 minutes for our table. Once we were seated though it was worth the wait. The food is better than the menu let's on. The flavors, textures, and combinations are bold, different, and delicious. They say these are small plates meant for sharing and the waitress recommending ordering 4 for the two of us. We could have gotten away with 3 as the portions are not that small. Our favorite was the endive, which apparently they are known for. I highly recommend this dish. We also had the beef tartare, lamb, and the ricotta dumplings. The lamb was excellent.We enjoyed everything, but would have skipped the ricotta dumplings if we did it again. We were both pleased.
Everything was excellent. The descriptions on the menu understate the impact of the dishes. Everything was so memorable and truly delicious.
They have this poppyseed egg sandwich which will make all of your dreams come true. They also have these mushroom dumplings that will bring a tear to your eye.

Extremely over priced for what they are
Lamb ribs-ribs were not bad but could be flavored a little more. However, as we moved to the veggies underneath, there was disappointedly huge chunks of sand or dirt inside!!!! Service came quickly and replaced this with a pear salad which is very mediocre.
The fried rice-was over cooked yet still the best of the three dishes we had(not including the extra salad)
Red shrimps with shittake- very bad combination since both ingredients are tender and shiitake cannot effectively absorb the seafood flavor while shiitake itself has strong fungi scent that needs neutralization.
Very disappointed!!!!!!

This is my go to spot for a dignified meal out  with excellent foot and drink. The wait staff is exceedingly knowledgeable without being pretentious.  Each visit has fare that makes picking the best of chosen dishes difficult.  Tonight, to mention three of the choices:  the Fried Foie Gras was pretty darn tasty, especially the sauce with bread to soak it up!; The steak and turnips melted in my mouth; and the chocolate cake covered in whip cream was nothing short of light and a  sumptious finish.

Terrible experience today. Two people in my family have Celiac disease and cannot eat any foods with gluten. The chef refused to plate an egg sandwich without the bread.....only offering main entrees as an option. Whatever happened to customer service? Why would the chef not serve the entree without the bread if they didn't have a gluten free option available? We left within 15 minutes of arriving and will not be back. Why eat at this restaurant when there are so many better options so close?

My friend and I made a reservation on one Sat noon and we were right.  It's was jam packed and there were couple people waiting to be seated.  I believe they take walk-in customers but I'd highly recommend to make reservation especially if you wanna come in for brunch. 
The food was pretty good but I gave 4 stars because we were kinda pushed to leave(they were not rude at all but simply there was a long line..)
I wish we could stay bit longer and enjoying the environment.  It's worth trying tho.
Cozy restaurant that really knows what they're doing. Small dishes (not cheap but worth Highly recommend: Fried arroz, jamon iberico, steak tartare.

We've come here twice for my birthday and then my husband's birthday. We found this place because it came up in the search for best gnocchi, and boy were they right! It's so unique and soft and perfect- so much that both times we ordered one for each of us. The burrata is out of this world too- the reason we can't NOT order burrata anytime we see it on any other menu elsewhere. We also ordered the black rice and pork which were tasty too. The only thing I wasn't crazy about was the foie gras and whatever chocolate dessert they gave for the bday. 

Between our first visit years ago and this recent visit, this place is increasing in popularity so definitely make a reservation. It was kinda uncomfortably packed/tight in the bar area but the tables are more spaced out throughout. Dimly lit setting provides a romantic atmosphere. We had a very enjoyable meal and experience here!

Charming spot in the west village. I love to eat at the bar and this place is great for that. The menu is primarily small plates for sharing that are quite fancy and a bit pricey but overall it was a nice, cozy experience on a rainy Sunday afternoon. We arrived at noon and by the time we left about an hour and a half later it was getting busy and more crowded. I love coffee with cream when having brunch but the bartender told me they didn't have cream, only milk (no!) so I asked hom to check with the kitchen for cream and he came back with some minutes later (a trick I use often for these weird new york brunch places that don't believe in having cream available for coffee) the kitchen always has some!

brunch only
I finally came here after Estela has made my yelp bookmark for 2+ years. They have an interesting menu and I was able to enjoy multiple dishes. We started with the salchichon, which was good. Then the oysters (spicy yuzu mignonette) and egg pancetta sandwich, both were alright. The lamb ribs were done so well, and the slab bacon is delicioussss. 
Small space but intimate. Can get crowded and noisy. Make reservation!

Good but overrated. Has benn on my radar for a long time. We got a variety of dishes--around seven--and nothing came close to even wow me. Service was fine, could have been friendlier, especially the girl at the bar. For the price, tastiness of food and ambiance, probably will hit up someplace else in the future in Nolita/Soho.

Amazing !!! The food was out of control. Went with a friend for dinner on a Wednesday night. The restaurant was packed. We sat at a tiny table and it was definitely a cozy fit (aka anytime someone had to go to the bathroom you have to move the entire table into the walkway in order to fit between tables). The only complaint of the restaurant would be how tightly squeezed in we were but the food was so good it still gets a 5/5. 

We got the jicama cocktail and couldn't stop ordering them for the rest of the night- very refreshing. Ordered the oysters, burrata, beef tartare, fried arroz and foie gras. Each dish was incredible, perfectly cooked fried arroz with just the right amount of seafood, creamy burrata in a delicious green oil/sauce, beef tartare which had great texture and the foie gras... let me tell you about the foie gras. It might be the best thing I've ever had. If I could, I would eat that foie gras for the rest of my life. Even writing about it now, I'm drooling a little thinking about how perfect it was. 

And the chocolate cake .... get the chocolate cake no matter how full you think you are. You won't regret it.

I would reorder every single dish and have two dinners here if I could. Maybe I will next time because I will definitely be back. It is the quintessential NYC "trendy" restaurant with a great atmosphere and even better food.

Food: 4
Service: 5
Ambiance: 2.5

Food (from best to worst):

The beef tartare was on point.  The meat was fresh.  The dish was a delightful slight twist on the classic, with a subtle tomato flavor sneaking through.

The burrata was delicious.  The salsa and bread went along perfectly.

The lamb ribs were good, but they could have been a touch more tender.

The ricotta dumplings themselves were well made, but the raw mushrooms struck an odd contrast with the rest of the dish. 

Service:
Fantastic.  Attentive, helpful, and prompt.

Ambiance:
Tables are jammed together and it is very loud.  But that's not too surprising for the City.

Made the mistake of booking here for Valentine's. Forced to share plates and to fill up on bread and uninteresting wine pairings, we honestly wondered if the server had acted in error. It would have been a nice meal for one. We went home hungry and with sore heads.

Damn, mixed feelings. On the one hand the food was crazy good, interesting flavors and use of ingredient, creative presentation. Honestly one of the most interesting stuff I've had in NYC

Only problem was the service! We had to wait for 30 minutes even though we made a booking, also servers were a little short and was running around being super busy, need to improve on the operation. Also ambience wasn't good, was a bit too noisy with crowded people by bar area.

Fabulous and funky little space with so much charm. Food is exceptional. Staff is knowledgeable and passionate about the restaurant. Dinner or weekend brunch are superb. Casual feeling space with excellent preparations on every dish. Do not miss!

This place is amazing! My boyfriend and I came here for a belated Valentine's Day dinner. We made a reservation with them directly and were seated right away. The atmosphere was super cozy and romantic, but a little bit too packed at times (like someone mentioned below about having to move the entire table just to go to the bathroom).

The waiter recommended we order 4-6 dishes to share for the two of us. We ordered 5 and it was the perfect amount of food with room for dessert. We ordered the burrata, tuna, fried arroz negro with squid (my favorite by FAR), pork with truffle, and the steak with turnips. Everything was prepared and presented very thoughtfully. Chocolate cake with whipped cream for dessert was heavenly.

To drink my boyfriend ordered an old fashioned with rye whiskey which was perfectly made and I had wine with dinner that our (very knowledgeable) waiter recommended. 

TL/DR: amazing food, pricey and a little bit crowded
This is the perfect restaurant. There is a reason why every intelligent, living president from the 21st century lets Ignacio cook for them. This man is a genius.

I've been wanting to check out ESTELA for a while and the food did NOT disappoint. 

Our waiter was fabulous--we had looked at the menu and found a few dishes that sounded really good, he agreed and then suggested we order a few others to complement. It was just the right amount of food and a perfect combination. There was NOTHING that I didn't like although I will say some things stood out more than others. Here's what we got (and I noted my favorites):
--Tuna
--Beef Tartar
--Mussels--these were amazing. A flavor of deliciousness in each bite
--Endive salad--which didn't sound that good (or look that pretty) but we were all pleasantly surprised on the taste. Also, I'm not a huge anchovy fan but it totally worked in the dressing (and it didn't taste like anchovies)
--Fried Arroz Negro
--Ricotta dumplings---also delicious and very unusual 

For dessert we got:
--the chocolate cake--which was your "traditional" bittersweet almost flourless chocolate cake
--Sweat potato cake--which sounded really weird but was probably one of the best desserts I've ever had. If we hadn't ordered the chocolate cake, I think we would have had to order another one! 

Overall an amazing meal. The only reason I'm not giving this a five star review is because of the hostess had a bit of an attitude. She asked us not to stand at the back of the bar while we waited for a table (so we could be out of the way), only to then send other people to push past us aggressively to stand at the back of the bar. When she came to take us to our table, she didn't even wait for us to move past people. We also were seated about 20 minutes after our initial reservation (hence us wanting to stand at the back of the bar). Thank

Estela, a treat for a connaiseur! Everything was mind blowing. Every course, every single election of ingredient perfectly chosen & amazing! You need to experience this on your own. Once you arrive, you have just a door with "Estela" on it, you enter and it is a beautiful not so big space in Soho. You need reservations, of course!

Estela, una fiesta para el paladar! Todo es impresionante. Cada plato, cada selección de ingredientes está perfectamente elegido y diseñado!
Tenes que hacer la experiencia vos mismo. Una vez que llegas, sólo vas a ver una puerta con el nombre "Estela", entras y es un hermoso no tan grande espacio en Soho. Se necesitan reservas, por supuesto!
Nice ambiance, great food, but the bench chair is so uncomfortable. The seat is too high for my feet to be on the floor and the table is too low that I had to hunch over the entire time.

I so want to give this restaurant five stars for some of the outstanding dishes we had, but the atmosphere and one of our dishes hold me back. To start with the good - the endive salad and grilled mackerel were outstanding. You cannot go here and not order the grilled mackerel that is served with grapes. The endive salad is also a must order with the endives on a bed of cheese, anchovies and walnuts and coated in a perfect olive oil based dressing. 
However, one dish you can skip is the fried arroz negro with seafood. The dish lacked much flavor and there was no seafood that I was aware of. It was the only dish that made me question the price as it seemed to just be a plate of black fried rice. 
The other negative here was the atmosphere. While the restaurant is nicely decorated, the tables are packed in making for a very, very noisy experience. To hear the person across from you is difficult, and be prepared to shout to compete with the noise. 
Overall, Estela has some truly innovative and outstanding dishes, but the loud atmosphere and some mediocre dishes may make me think twice about coming back.

Estela is one of those high-profile Manhattan restaurants I'd heard good things about despite living in Los Angeles and going to New York maybe once or twice a year. I went for brunch with my friend Katie M. on my last trip, a couple months ago, on my way out of town. We were able to get a reservation for 11:30 on a Saturday about 40 hours in advance (I love a hassle-free brunch). Other than wandering a bit around SoHo, this meal was really the one thing I did before going to the airport that day. It was a great way to savor the last few hours of my visit.

The restaurant was cute and tiny, long but narrow with counter seating and what felt like a handful of small tables. I was glad they had room to hold onto my carryon while we ate. Service was excellent, friendly and helpful. Our waiter Fred did a good job guiding us through the menu, pointing out the house specialties and advising us on portions. He may have underestimated how much we could eat, but that was probably for the best. My gluttony doesn't need to be indulged at every turn.

I started my brunch with the house Bloody Mary, made with vodka, fish sauce, Sara's hot sauce (I don't know who Sara is), and citrus. This was a tasty Bloody, savory with a nice kick. I'd guess that Estela does solid cocktails.

The food was delicious. I'm glad our waiter recommended the endives because I don't know that we would've ordered it on our own, and it was probably the highlight of our brunch. It sounded like a salad, and I like salad, but generally not as much as I like things that aren't salad. This was less of a salad than it was a high-end version of like Chinese lettuce wraps, with fresh endive leaves arranged over a splendid, flavorful mix of walnuts, anchovy, and ubriaco rosso. The endive was fantastic on its own, crisp and beautiful, dressed with a citrusy vinaigrette, and even better carrying a scoop of the walnut, anchovy, and cheese.

I also loved the egg, pancetta, and avocado sandwich. Our waiter noted it was popular on Instagram, and I can see why, what with the perfect soft runny egg and the attractive pastry bun studded with poppy seeds. This was a stellar breakfast sandwich, and I appreciated the fancy pickles that came with it. I always love a fancy pickle. The ricotta dumplings were pretty spectacular, too. They were soft and delicate, served in an aromatic mushroom broth with pecorino sardo and a layer of thin-sliced mushroom on top.

We had room for dessert, so we finished our brunch with chocolate cake and panna cotta. The chocolate cake is apparently the popular choice here, and it was great, spongey and rich and enshrouded in fresh whipped cream. I liked the panna cotta even better, though. This was just wonderful, thick and lush and not too sweet, finished with honey and--the winning touch--a bit of vinegar.

This was a lovely brunch, definitely a memorable way to end my trip. (Also memorable--the unexpectedly long, traffic-plagued ride to the airport, where I at least had a full stomach while I fretted about catching my flight.) I'd recommend Estela if you're looking for a special brunch spot in New York. I'd like to come back--maybe dinner next time, though I'd also be happy to have this exact same meal again.

Estela was a last minute choice for my friends and I,  after missing our reservations at a different restaurant.  Almost walked past the place since it's kind of tucked in with other stores.  We had no idea what we were in for when we walked in the door.  It was past 10pm and we had no reservations.  They were very accommodating and we were seated right away. 

None of us have ever been to a tapas place.  All three of us were staring at the menu, didn't know half of the things listed on there, googling words.  We probably looked a mess. Our amazing waiter, Fred came over and explained how the menu works.  He made a few suggestions that helped us quiet a bit. He was very friendly, sat down and chatted with us about our NY experience. It was our last night in NY and it was a perfect way to end our trip.

We ordered Mussels on toast ( just melts in your mouth), Burrata, salsa verde on charred bread, celery salad ( this was more like a palate cleanser for us), fried arroz negro with squid and romesco, Lamb ribs with charmoula and honey and Ricotta dumplings with  mushrooms and pecorino sardo. Each course was better than the last one.  Food was just amazing!!!!

Don't leave without getting a dessert.  Our server surprised us with couple of desserts and they were on point.  He brought us Sweet potato with Vanilla ice cream and Rum ( our favorite) and Chocolate cake.  They were both delicious but the sweet potato with ice cream won our hearts.  

We had an amazing experience here. I would give it more stars if I could.  Will definitely be back next time we are in town!

Every dish was great. Everything was different than anything I've ever tried and it all went together. 

I docked off a star because the pours were some of the weakest wine pours I've ever seen and the atmosphere was like a dive bar.

The more expensive bottle of the glass of wine you ordered the smaller the pour.

The atmosphere could've been much better. I was touching elbows with the two tables on my sides (not metaphorically but literally I spent my whole meal like this). The girl on my right kept flicking my hair towards me and yes it did touch my face a few times.

unfussy, modern dining meets beautiful and jaw droppingly perfect food. A huge window at the bar overlooks Houston Street - perfect for happy hour that lingers into a late night dinner. The ricotta dumplings and lamb ribs are not to be missed.

Wow! Coming with little expectation we were blown away by the flavors and concept. Each dish was unique and like nothing we've ever had and we eat out a lot. Combinations that seemed odd, fused together seamlessly. What stood out the most was the sauce. The burrata, ricotta dumpling, foie Gras all came sitting in the most sinful sauce. Whoever the saucier is deserves an award. We pretty much licked the bowl clean. It was that good. The only dish I didn't enjoy as much was the lamb as it was a bit too gamey for me. As for the other dishes, I'm still drooling over as I'm typing right now.

I heard good things about this restaurant and I finally decided to visit. The food was actually not bad but the service I received was extremely terrible. The server, Ryan was beyond rude and disrespectful toward my friends and me. He treated us like we do not belong there. We reported it to management but instead of apologizing, they defended him. It's just a shame you pay your money to enjoy a good food and have a good time, but you leave disappointed. I would not recommend this place to anyone.

Estela wasn't mind-blowing, but it was great. Very fish-focused menu, which my friend and I were cool with - we shared the hake, sea bream, mussels, ricotta dumplings, and chocolate cake for dessert. The dumplings and cake were my favorite. The dishes were thoughtful and creative enough; the ingredients were fresh. 

Service was great. I'd try the burrata and beef tartare next time.

Uggghhh this place is SO good! Went here for a birthday with one other person and it was just fabulous all around. The concept is shared small plates, kind of like tapas, and the two of us ordered a total of 6 dishes as per the server's recommendation plus dessert. We started with the raw scallops with cuttlefish and shitake mushroom and the texture of that was so creamy and rich, while the flavor was very fresh, clean and earthy--I thought the shitake flavor overwhelmed that of the seafood a bit, but at the same time it kinda worked too. Next we had the mussels escabeche on toast, and that is just to DIE for--I've really never had any muscles that tasted this good. I can't even really explain it, but you have to try it! The endive salad was also really good, particularly if you're into the caesar-salad-kind-of dressing with anchovies--the walnuts/pecans(?) added a nice nutty flavor and a good crunch. The steak tartare was really good too, but I wouldn't necessarily order it again. It has that nice, classic clean flavor of steak tartare, but this one wasn't particularly special, I'd say. The lamb ribs with chermoula and honey were so delicious also, very well balanced herby flavors with rich, succulent, fall-off-the-bone lamb. And lastly, the fried arroz negro with squid and romesco was really just fantastic as well--the flavors just exploded in your mouth and the toasted rice was an ice texture contrast to the soft, perfectly-cooked squid. We finished the night off with some strawberry sorbet with candied seaweed, which I would definitely skip next time. It wasn't bad per se, but I didn't really care for it. The wine and cocktails were good, but the food really shined here. It's definitely a bit on the pricey side, but oh so worth it! We had a fabulous time and will absolutely be back soon!
Remarkable food.   Service superior, food is interesting, cooked extremely well.   There is something for everyone.   Even the drinks are wonderful.

Food was pretty good. Got the lamb and the squid ink risotto. However, the layout of the restaurant is very cramped. If you're sitting on the bench its almost impossible to get out and use the bathroom

Estela was my friend and my more elevated Sunday brunch choice. I love that they take reservations, making Sunday brunch that much less of a logistical nightmare. The interior is really beautiful, well-designed and hip. The service was incredible as well: I felt really welcome and while I was waiting for my friend, they were polite enough to check in and offer me some water.

The food is all small plates and between the 2 of us, we ordered 3, which was the perfect amount of food. In terms of the food, it was all as tasty as it was creative and aesthetic! My friend and I ordered:

Slab bacon with Dijon, potato, and egg: This dish felt the least creative, as it was just a slab of bacon, though it was plated really beautifully. More importantly, it was delicious, as bacon often is. Would I pay $23 for another slab of bacon though? Debateable.

English muffin w/smoked whitefish and trout roe: This was delicious! They didn't skimp at all with the whitefish filling and the fish complemented the muffin well.

Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo: This was such a pleasure, it tasted like heaven in your mouth. You're not quite sure what to expect at first, since the dumplings aren't obvious, but after the first bite, all you know is that you want more.

My only complaint about Estela is the noise level inside. Thought it was just me and my friend, and the restaurant wasn't that full, I still had such a hard time hearing. If I do come back, it would have to be with a close friend, so that we can enjoy the food without much conversation. 

Next time I'm back, the Burrata and Endive salad are on my list!

Came here for brunch last minute this past weekend.  We ordered the ribs, the bacon and eggs, the oysters and the greens.  The ribs and the bacon were standout; everything else was solid, but unremarkable. 

So why the negative review?  The service was unfriendly and unresponsive.  To be fair, the women at the bar and one of the owners were awesome and warm, but our actual server was anything but.  Maybe he was having a bad day but we had to ask for water a number of times and forgot part of our order.  All of that would be ok, but his overall attitude just oozed of pretension.  He had a talent for making you feel dumb when asking a question (in stark contrast with the others at the restaurant).

PHENOMENAL food and drink. We had several items for dinner, including the burrata, endive, arroz negro and ricotta dumplings. Each was so unique and different from all of the others. The salad of all things was one of my FAVORITE dishes (both at Estela that evening and generally). 

Highly, highly recommend. Wonderful food, wine, and ambiance. Definitely want to come back for brunch.

Came here for dinner three weeks ago. We had a 7:45pm Friday reservation and it was packed. I got there a little early and sat by the bar but since the seats there were a hot commodity, they opted to seat me at our table even though my friend wasn't there yet.

While there were a couple of tables with groups, the restaurant seemed to be predominantly couples on dates. I guess the atmosphere is conducive to dates - very dimly lit, tables are so close to each other, and mostly seating for two.

I can't remember everything we ordered, but some of the items included the mussels, burrata, and arroz negro. While the food was good, it wasn't great. I'm a little surprised by the #80 ranking in the World's 50 Best list for this year.

3.5 stars. Estela's menu has a bunch of really interesting sharing-style small plates, but for the price and quality, it was just so-so. Some dishes were better than others, and I thought it was a little too expensive for the portion size, taste, and ambience.

The mussels on toast was one of my favorites. The endive salad felt a little bit difficult to eat, and the walnut cheese dressing a bit too oily. I enjoyed the grilled foie gras wrapped in a grape leaf, and the pork with samphire was very unique - I don't think I've seen samphire served outside of Ireland!

I enjoyed the wine recommendations from the waitress. My gripes about Estela is that it's incredibly loud, and the tables are really small and tight. I would personally prefer a slightly more intimate experience at this price point.

Made a reservation at Estela about 3 weeks in advance for a Friday evening for 2. There were a few times available and I went with 715pm. We arrived ~10 min early and they sat us immediately. The small bar area and most tables were crowded and they all filled up throughout our dinner.

I had been looking at the menu for weeks and at pics/reviews on yelp so had a pretty good idea of what I wanted to try. The waitress let us know that 4-6 dishes is usually enough for 2 ppl. We went with 6 and it was the perfect amount of food - satisfied but not too full. We ordered the beef tartar, mussels on toast, burrata, endive salad, lamb ribs, and ricotta gnocchi. All of the dishes were amazing so can't pick a favorite. They each had a super unique flare. Truly hadn't had anything close to the flavor in these dishes before. The beef tartar had elderberry in it so it was very different than the usual with a poached quail egg. The burrata came on toast and was served over salsa verde. The endive salad was so fun to eat - kinda felt like lettuce wraps. The lamb ribs literally melted in your mouth... could easily bite through the bone. The ricotta dumplings were SO soft and served with some mushrooms, mushroom broth, and pecorino sardo. Mussels on toast were so cool!

Will for sure be back and highly recommend for a date night or dinner with friends :)

I was meeting a friend here for dinner and I arrived early. The place was small and crowded and I squished into the corner bar area and waited with my other friend, Mr. Alcohol.
