Once seated at our small table, we ordered, I think, five things from the small menu. The dishes are, you guessed it, small plates. Like tapas, but not Spanish. That being said, the food was bomb. My fave was the steak tartare and the black squid rice. Each dish looked like art, except you eat the art. I'll be back for sure.

This is probably one of the best dinner that i ever had. We made reservation on Thursday at 530, went there, got the table and i had no complaints! We ordered drink and it was great, the food was really tasty and they did a really good job for New American style restaurant. Service was good. Can't wait to go back!!!

Truly one of the best meals I've ever had - definitely in New York, maybe even in life. To top it off, our waiter, Fred, was a total gem. He was so engaged with his patrons and genuinely seemed to care about them having a good time. Every item we ordered, including drinks and dessert, was incredible. We tried the beef tartare, the endives and much more. I wish I had taken specific notes on each order because I was obsessed with all of it. I really hope to come back some day. Thank you Fred and the incredible culinary staff!

Visited Estela with another couple for a nice dinner. Food was interesting, tasty however didn't blow my mind considering their pricing. It just lacks flavours a little bit. They do have a good selection of wines and very good service. I will most likely return but not immediately.

Went to Estela with a friend last night and had a fantastic dinner. Five to six small plates was about right for the two of us. We ordered the raw scallops, mussels on toast, burrata, fried black rice, ricotta dumplings, endive salad, and sweet potato cake with vanilla ice cream. Everything was delicious and our favorites were the mussels on toast, burrata, and ricotta dumplings! 

The ambiance was really welcoming and not stuffy at all. Jeans and casual attire are totally appropriate. 

Given how incredible the food is, it's really shocking that you're able to make a reservation. Try to book for an earlier seating than you normally would since it is a longer meal. We were seated at 5:30 and left at 8.

I really enjoyed the food here. Some of the dishes blew my mind: ricotta dumplings, oysters with yuzu kosho mignonette, and buratta. The server was a bit posh when I asked him which cocktail is their speciality while we wait for one more party to arrive. He said our cocktails are paired with the menu... which is fine, but not helpful. I just want a drink..
Love this place! The food is amazing, great wine menu and always kind service. Just go!

Maybe it was over hyped to me so that my 3 visits were decent, but let downs. I just don't get the hype. It was okay. I've tried their prawn, the avocado sandwich, koji-cured salami, and the steak and potatoes. It was all okay, but small portions. I'm a grazer so I'm not into huge portions, but these were even too small for my liking. My friend always gets the ricotta dumplings which again are okay. Maybe it's just me, I'm just underwhelmed.

One can never conquer all the restaurants New York has to offer. I was randomly searching for places to eat on Resy and stumbled on this restaurant. I looked at their menu and they had some of the things I love most - uni and burrata. 

I had a 8pm reservation and the restaurant was packed when I walked in. The tables are super close to each other, which I hate, but when the food started coming out, it was less awkward. 

This place is Mediterranean fusion and tapas style, so we ordered a lot of dishes to share.

Food:

Raw scallop on top of uni and dates - OMG this was so good. My favorite things in life in one bite. The date gave it an interesting texture but the sweetness went well with the scallop and uni

Mussels escabeche on toast - wasn't one of my favorites, but the sauce/broth that they had was so bomb. i couldn't stop drinking it

Burrata, salsa verde, and charred bread - if you're a burrata lover like me, this is a must order. The salsa verde was amazing. So flavorful and the burrata was so creamy

Ricotta dumplings, mushrooms, and pecorino sardo - Almost must have from this restaurant.  I loved the pecorino sardo with this dish. 

Summer squash with pine nuts and miso - this was the most unsuspecting dish of the night. The miso sauce had this distinct taste that my friend and I loved but couldn't tell what it was

Duck - Damn, this main entree blew us away. Perfectly cooked and the skin of the duck was so crisp. The blood sausage sauce was amazing as well. 

Chocolate cake dessert - we were so full, but I had to have my sweets. The chocolate cake was the perfect ending. It wasn't overly sweet but the chocolate hit the spot.

The whole night was perfect. We had some really great wines, and I love the modern atmosphere. The hype is real. Our server never really checked up on us the whole night, but that's okay because we were enjoying our meal so much. Estela is great option for date night or special occasion.

Been passing this place for a couple of years and finally decided to try it one night. I really wanted to love it but it was a huge disappointment. The drinks were bland (I tried a few). The food was ok and it wasn't cheap. I've spent $200 on a dinner for 2 but had great portions and food was amazing. Here i left hungry and desiring flavor. The best thing was the rice. It was great but that's about it. Service was nice overall. The only thing that annoyed me, and I might be weird for this, was that when we had different plates we actually had to request our forks and plates be changed when most restaurants that charge me $30 for rice do that on their own to not mess with the "palate". I of course wouldn't expect this from a diner or no frills spot but if I'm paying that much change the plates. Anyway I've had better food for better prices. Really disappointed. 

The seating against the wall is elevated so it's weird when the other person across from you is floating above you lol. Wouldn't want that for a first date.

This place is outstanding. Love the interior and ambiance almost as much as the ricotta soup dumplings. Beef carpaccio was also incredible; I love how this restaurant is small/sharing plates with a twist. Drinks were delicious too.

Our favorite dishes of the night were the riccata cheese dumpling, red prawn with mushroom and lamb chops.  The dumpling was light and it paired really well with a nicely reduced broth and topped with thinly shaved mushroom.  It was an extremely aromatic dish. 

We were also looking forward to the red prawn dish since the the ingredient was so delicate.  We were not disappointed.  

The lamb dish was also beautifully cooked.  It had a hint of sweetness which drew out the savoriness of the meat.

We find the foie grass dish a bit hard to eat.  But it was innovative.

The black rice had a nice crust.  However, I find it a bit too hard to chew.  It will be better if it the crust is thinner and more seafood were added.

The oyster fish was decent but could use a bit more citrus.

Each dish on the menu looked interesting and tasted good. You can tell the chefs put a lot of thought into each dish.  They also offer a wide selection of wine.  

Without liquor pairing, I would say you are looking to spend 100-120 per person with tax and tip.

We loved the small plates here and had a wonderful waitress. But the other staff was really snooty -- both obnoxious when seating us and pressuring us to leave. Expensive dining should feel more relaxing than this.

Wow! This place personifies Manhattan. Sunday night (granted a holiday weekend) and the place was packed. Cool vibe, music, ambience. Tables are small and the round ones up front are like...really? Get a rectangular one in the back. 

The food is exceptional. Exciting, innovative, each dish is curious. Great wines by the glass. Not your usual. Servers are friendly and helpful. Prices are on higher end but....great food quality. It's a night out and you feel satisfied.  The food presents with a layered theme. I'm not sure it is visually to die for but once you dig down, the top layer covers the rest of the dish, it's a flavor bomb in your mouth. Lick the bowl good.

We had:

foie Gras to finish but mentioning now since last memory - amazing
Lamb chops - delicious. The crust was awesome
Black rice - so good
Scallop and uni - Huge uni fan. The date adds a spectacular perk to the dish. 
Sea bream - lots of wonderful flavors.  The freshness of the greens is a wow of flavor. 
Buratta - pure goodness. 

As I write this I don't have a favorite. All were delicious and already contemplating the return. Do you repeat or try new things. You meet repeat guests. They rave about having tried everything on the menu and still come back, hearing there are some new adds. It's cult like. 

Please keep doing what you are doing. Just be realistic about those round tables up front. Coffee maybe. Not dinner.  And do something about the banquet. It is much higher than normal so your companion on the other side is much lower than you. It's just odd.

So so disappointed. Only not 2 stars because the food was delicious and unique but WOW WHAT A BUMMER. Have been excited to try this place for so long, had reservation Friday 7:45. Inside is cute and lively albeit loud. But if you're going to pay over $200 for dinner for 2 the LEAST you can expect is decent service. Not only was no one friendly it was SO SO SO SO SLOW. I'm talking 20 minutes at one point between a tiny plate of salad and a tiny plate of ricotta dumplings. It was beyond atrocious. Left with a really negative feeling on what should have been a great date night.

Love the food, particularly the burrata and ricotta dumplings.  The foie gras was good too.  The noise, however is deafening so much so that it is unpleasant.  Tables are a foot apart so that you can clearly hear your neighbors shouting at each other.  A restaurant with such high quality food should do something about the environment in with it is served.  It is a disservice to the food.

Went for dinner this time and OMG! So, so delicious. The lanai cocktail is delicious and they offer corkage for $50/bottle (2 bottles max). For a group of 4 we were pleasantly full with 7 dishes and 3 desserts (probably could have done 2 desserts but we were very happy). 

And now the dinner rankings:

1. Burrata (seriously - it's a MUST)
2. Ibérico pork
3. Ibérico ham
4. Fried arroz negro 
5. Lamb ribs
6. Endive salad

Pass on the ricotta dumplings. Definitely the weakest dish - try something else.

For dessert get the chocolate cake. The panna cotta is also amazing, but we all liked the chocolate cake a bit more. We also had the Cheese from Spain - very good but it's hard to compete with the other desserts with our crew.
Wow! Great food! Great drinks! Great service! Great vibe! .Will definitely be back soon. Bravo

Not a typical Michelin 1 star restaurant due to lack of attentive services, uncomfortable seating and cheap ingredients. I wouldn't recommend it. At least I won't go back. 
My wife and I had dinner there. The dining area is small. My wife as sitting on a bench and she couldn't come out with moving the table next to ours. The restaurant is like a pub. Lighting is too dark. We couldn't even see what we were eating.
Service is not sub par. The helper simple dropped the dish on the table. No explanation on ingredients, cooking techniques and what's special about the dish. 
We ordered Iberico ham, beef tartar, rice with black squid ink, ricatto cheese dumpling and iberico pork. The best dish is rice with black squid ink. Beef tartar is simple and it is no expensive beef. Ricatto cheese dumpling is bland, sauce is just like mushroom soup, overwhelms the dumpling. Skin is mushy. Iberico Pork is very raw and half is greasy fat. Perhaps the chef has great cook skills but we couldn't see any sophistication or innovation in the dishes we ordered. Presentation is very minimal.

You must go to Estela! Great service, great food! It is a casual vibe but you get 5 star service! Food is so good, they have an interesting take on classics and at the same time you will eat things you haven't tried before. Don't forget to save room for desert!

Couple of visits here and the Michelin is well deserved IMO

Standouts: black rice, red shrimp, endive, scallop/uni, beef tartare, ricotta ice cream dessert

Excellent but not mindblowing: lamb rib, Iberico pork, burrata, hake, Iberico ham, chocolate cake dessert

Good but would pass to save room for the rest: foie, ricotta dumplings, panna cotta dessert

Fantastic wine list. Cocktails not super special I feel, but solid. 

A little loud and tight - better for parties of 3-4 where the goal is to have a good time. 5 small plates would do well for 2 ppl. You will not be waited on hand and foot a la Per Se but service is efficient, friendly, and considerate without being in the way.

The whole experience was quite a disappointment. The place is so small and packed; therefore, the tables were so close to each that there was no privacy. The noise level was high too. The dishes was average while the service quality was very poor. They made me feel that we needed to finish the meal so quickly that they could give the table to next customer. I do not believe that anyone should experience this while paying $250 for two people.
Came here for one of my monthly anniversaries and what a great pick! Every dish was made with super fresh ingredients with great sauce pairings. Will definitely come here again.

Spectacular food, dismal service... When ordering, we repeatedly asked our waitress that dishes be brought out one at a time, we were here to celebrate a birthday and have a couple of bottles of wine, to make an night of it. She repeatedly and condescendingly assured us, of course, plates are meant to be shared, they will be brought out one at a time, okay, alright, enough, yes, obviously, of course, do you understand, what part don't you understand, is it too complicated for you -- that was her tone and delivery. Cold and dismissive. And then what happened, the food runner brought our second course before we were finished with our first course, and then they never removed the empty plate of the first course so of course they tried to shove our third course on the same tiny table, and while we were trying to eat our second & third courses together they were bringing out our fourth course when I just had to stop them, "no. please remove the empty plate from our first course, please allow us to finish our second and third course before you bring out our fourth course," and then at that point I flagged down a manager not to complain but to engage so that she would be present to prevent further chaos. Thankfully that mostly worked, except it was still quite obvious what the source of the chaos was, the food runner. As someone exited the restaurant, the food runner made mocking gestures behind their back because they weren't walking fast enough for his liking. Two tourists beside us were brought a plate of endives and the food runner asked HAVE YOU BEEN HERE BEFORE DO YOU KNOW HOW TO EAT THIS, they responded in a slight accent "not yet," and he gestures boldly while loudly declaiming "YOU SCOOP IT!" with a completely offensive tone ("like this, you stupid idiots"). And so on and so forth; my guess is that he is exposed to too many stimulants too often, his gestures were at all times highly irritable and sporadic and almost hostile. Back and forth he went, ridiculing & mocking customers, slamming plates down, shoving around drinks. 

And then the opposite became an issue, some other fellow kept trying to remove plates before we finished. Our fourth course, foie gras and grape leaves (an absolute stunner), he tried to yank away our plate before we were even half way through. Our fifth course, pork with anchovies and chicories (an absolute knockout), he tried to yank away before we were even two-thirds finished. Our sixth course, duck with oyster mushrooms and black truffles (an absolute show-stopper), he tried to yank away before we were even three-quarters finished. 

Lots of yanking and shoving, not just at our table, but also at the two tiny tables beside us. That's another issue, three tiny three tables are crammed into a tiny area which is really only big enough for two tiny tables; at least when dishes are at this price point, the people to our left knocked into our table on their way in & on their way out, the people on our right knocked into our table on their way in & on their way out; it's all just too much. I'd love to come back again soon, but not until they yank out & shove aside some bad apples who bring 'em down. 

We both really would have loved to try some of their amazing sounding desserts, but the chaos and tension was just too much. Sadly, on way out the door, we overheard the hostess aggressively say to someone entering, "I didn't ASK you who you are, I _ASKED_ if you had a reservation..."  I wonder how much business they lose due to their humans-as-fodder "customer service," the allure of a Michelin Star can only last so long, and it's no wonder why it took them so long to get one; if only they improved service, I could easily see them getting two... After bolting out the front door, finishing our evening with three scoops of Olive Oil Roasted Plum ice cream next door at Oddfellows made it all better...

The pork katsu sandwich is good but very heavy. The daikon and apple salad on the side is light and refreshing. I eat them in between bites of the juicy katsu. It does complement the taste of the sandwich. Btw you can only get it on Fridays during lunch. 
The panna cotta with vinegar and honey is also good. Hardly tasted the vinegar. I particularly liked the bits of dehydrated bee pollen. Love it! 

The cocktail was just ok. I thought I was only drinking concorde grape juice with a splash of Prosecco and brandy. I couldn't feel any alcohol at that moment.

New York has a very peculiar ability to create surprises in the least expected of places. Nondescript, small and unremarkable are the perceptions one would get from the street while seeking out where Estela is located. It is a place that most likely pass on a daily basis and have absolutely no clue that it is there. It is a place that is not in itinerary lists or guide books for tourists. Well, that's except the Michelin guide of course, which positions Estela at a single star. And a few lists such as World's Best Restaurants. Yet, it's presence in online review platforms is fairly modest and does not scream. 

The chef here, Ignacio Mattos, is from Uruguay and many inspirations for the art prepared here are from his home country with influences from Spain and likely, Italy. At least it so appears based on the profile of the dishes. There are clearly a number of well deserving reasons why this cozy establishment is always packed, despite the small space. 

Every single dish was a delicious creation in its own realm. The Iberico Ham is bursting with meaty flavor and just amazing, some of the best to be had in the world. Burrata with salsa verde is so unusual and delicious, that it's hard to compare with any other burrata. Market Greens, grilled cucumber, lamb ribs, bacon slab and ricotta dumplings are no less impressive. Even the simplest dishes like celery were prepared in a new perspective and opening up combinations that are rarely seen, yet are phenomenal.

And then, chasing down this amazing meal with a local NY beer and the brunch begins to take shape of satisfaction as the morning transitions into an afternoon. It is without a doubt an essential place to observe experiments with rare ingredients and counter any perceptions of what a brunch should be.

Loved every dish. 

Fluke with uni - very good 
Persimmon appetizer - very good 
Oysters - decent
Red shrimp - delicious 
Foie Gras - pretty good
Black rice - must get!
Lamb ribs - very good
Ricotta dumplings - good

So deserving of their star on so many levels. Service, music, ambiance, location, food...all 5 stars! If you want to support smaller establishments and not your standard over-priced overrated, places in NYC, here's the place to come to. One of them. 

It was 2 of us and we got about 5 dishes and several drinks and wine. We got pretty full, it's a lot of food! Their burrata is outrageously good. They do cook a little on the salty side but I love that so didn't mind. Someone else may want to be cautious if that. 

Otherwise, overall, what an amazing place!

I came to Estela per the recommendation of a friend.  First, the 'restaurant' (should really be called a 'tapas place') is located at East Houston Street between Mulberry and Mott.  It is not at an 'exclusive' location.  Prepare to be shocked by the unfair portion to price equation: $17 cocktail, $26 black rice.  The cocktail was not balanced (I'm still recovering from a headache) and the black rice was miniscule.  If you are going for a meal, plan for a $120 budget, drinks excluded.  This is simply disrespectful, especially given the size of everything in the menu.  For those of us working in the arts/culture sector, Estela is simply a waste of money.  Go for it if you are in the 'bling-bling' mood, but otherwise skip and head to any other decently priced and portioned restaurant.  I can recommend Ruby's on Mulberry, a few blocks south, Cafe Gitane or Hakata Tonton in the Village.  Avoid collaborating with the 1%.

The more I come to Estela the more I fall for its persuasions, in particular the salads. They're such a joy to eat, playful, sexy, and actually kind of fun. They're composed so thoughtfully, with some funky blue cheese and toasty walnuts hiding behind perfect little endive boats. I eat them like nachos at the bar.

I hate to through this but I cannot give higher rate.
I'm fine with the cuisine, it's creative BUT!! The service. I've never experienced such unprofessional and rude service, especially after a dinner at Daniel where I was treated like president.

1. The space is really narrow, we hardly have space to  place plates on the table and we literally moved the table away to get out which was super awkward. It's fine if it's a small hype dining place in a market for 20 dollars or so but for this kind of restaurant, I see no possibility to enjoy food in such a bad environment.

2. Our server is scary, she told us (Party of 2 ) that we should order 4 - 6 course and share. We weren't hungry and just want to order 3, she literally PETRIFIED. She was standing there as said nothing and seems so shocked. This is an a la crate menu, not prix fixe, what's wrong with just ordering 3 courses?

3. Again our server. She was talking by rote. When I ask about the portion for each course on the menu (as there's no border of appetizers and mains on that menu) she told me that it's "light to heavy" that's not the answer of my question so I asked again and she looked light "oh you don't understand English?' And answer the same thing. Well, light to heavy doesn't equals small to large.

4. The server told me that the menu is meant to be shared, how ever I like foie gras but my parter don't, so we want to order our own plate and dine at the same time, just like in other restaurant. The server looked so confused and seems like she never seen anyone who don't share. 

5. While we ordered our own plate we still want to share the ricotta dumpling. We hope we can have the dumpling first, and then have our own plates, but the server told us that the order should be EXACTLY the order on the menu. COME ON! It's not a tasting menu, why it has to be the exact order? I'm not doing smoking crazy. Actually, having our own plates together and then share another pasta dish seemed stranger to me, it would be nice to do the pasta first.

I dined here with my husband before we headed to a holiday party, and boy were we wowed. Though we didn't have a reservation, they fit us right in, and our server was wonderful. Knowledgeable, thoughtful, and seemingly excited that it was our first visit. The endive salad lived up to the hype; it is both visually beautiful and the flavors are exciting. The mussels were amazing! And so, so, pretty! The black rice was delicious, but perhaps a bit too salty and rich a dish to follow-up the anchovies. We wrapped it to go and happily ate it at 2am post-holiday party. The ambiance is so warm and inviting, and the soundtrack was a dream. An entirely memorable eating experience.

Amazing tapas style spot! I love the idea of small plates because you get to try basically the whole menu and get a taste of everything. 

I came with two friends and we split 6/7 plates. The standouts were the burrata and beef tartare which were some of the best I've ever had. I also loved the arroz negro which was crispy and salty. We ended with the chocolate cake which was the perfect combo of sweet and rich with a light fluffy cream on top.

Overall, this is an outstanding restaurant that I would highly recommend!
Mussels and lambs are brilliant. Not a big fan of the ricotta dumplings. Not crowded at all on a Sunday night.

Lovely intimate dining experience, incredible staff and delicious food. This place has been on my list to try for quite some time and I'm so glad I finally made it here. Our server was exceptional and had quite a bit of wine knowledge to help us select something that would suit both mine and my husband's opposite tastes. 

The portions are tapas style,so be prepared to share! We unfortunately over ordered, which I wish we would have known as we would have cut one of the dishes for sure- and likely the only one we weren't a huge fan of.

Food had great flavor and creative components- but didn't love the flavor combination on the fish dish or the seasoning of the lamb ribs. 

Our stand out dishes were the duck and the endive. YUM! We'll definitely be back to try more our next time in NYC.

Nothing beats dinner with a nice view, and by view, I'm referring to Jake Gyllenhaal and Tom Sturridge sitting cozily at the table across from me. Jake, who was incredibly hot in person, and I made steamy eye contact when he caught me staring at him. Unfortunately for him, my mouth was preoccupied all night with other meat and creamy substances. Every dish I tried was incredible! I didn't think lamb ribs that tasty existed outside of New Zealand, and boy was I wrong. The burrata was the creamiest I've ever had and the beef tartare was exquisitely textured. Sorry, Jake - better luck next time.

I just didn't get the hype... maybe an off night or I am missing something? Best dish by far was the crunchy black rice and ribs were ok but burrata, endive, foie and ricotta dumplings all left something to be desired. It felt as though each dish was incomplete like for burrata, I would have liked something fresh, endive salad needed something sweet and ricotta dumplings more depth of flavor in the broth. Was really looking forward to this restaurant but based on my experience, not running back

Having just been here once, it's already one of my favorite restaurants ever. We snagged a last minute reservation at a prime time on a Sunday night, which was quite lucky. The vibe was fun and relaxed. The food was amazing.
For our party of two, we had six items, all but one were the menu mainstays. 
The mussel escabeche on toast, it was an ok dish and somewhat hard to eat as it's bigger than bite-sized yet lacked structural integrity.
The beef tartare was the best damn tartare I've ever had. It used bison meat instead of the more fatty beef. Along crisped sunchoke, it makes for wonderful texture and flavor.
The burrata dish was raved about endlessly in all the reviews, but I was not wowed by it. It's the last so-so dish of the night.
The red shrimp was the only dish we had that wasn't a perennial item. I suppose the only reason it's not a classic is because of red shrimps' seasonality. The dish was executed cleanly and packed with intense flavor. Everything about it worked a charm.
The squid ink fried rice was a superb take on a simple dish that's hard to improve. It is surprisingly light considering it's fried carbs. The umami of the squid ink was the star, not an afterthought as it is so often. 
Finally the lamb ribs. Chef Mattos created this dish to challenge himself as he never liked lamb. Well, so was my dinner companion until she tried this. It became her personal favorite while she normally would never have lamb at all. It's a triumph of a dish that can convert the most ardent lamb haters.
Amazing restaurant, highly recommended.

Small and unassuming spot but with a very well executed menu. The entrees all seem like everyday fare from the name, but the ingredients have a twist or something exotic. In addition, the preparation is spot on - right temperature, texture, pleasing to the eye as well as palate.  For example the English muffin and whitefish with roe.  This could be a deli item akin to a tuna fish sandwich, but wow is it a souped up sandwich. I definitely would be curious to come back and to see if they have a spring or summer menu.

The small dish concept is fun and it's nice that you get to try everything on the menu. Service was definitely spectacular and very friendly. Everything I tried was good - enjoyable though not necessarily revolutionary. Best for small groups of people looking to experience food together in a pleasant environment.

A small plates restaurant isn't normally a place that I'd fancy coming to, but a friend back in Sydney had been bugging me to visit for some time. I finally took him up on his suggestion and visited for brunch over the weekend. 
Estela has been around for several years, but only just got a Michelin star awarded for 2020. I made a reservation for 12pm, for a party of two on a Sunday on Resy, which was easy to get even just a couple of days before. 
They seated us at our table when we had both arrived, and we were soon brought menus and water. 
The restaurant is cute on the inside, but was smaller than I thought it would be. The table that they had seated us at was a tiny cafe table, and would have had trouble fitting more than three - four plates on it. 
For the two of us, the waiter recommended that we order 4-5 dishes to share, but we decided to go with three, and were still full afterwards.
We shared the burrata on grilled bread to start. It was served in a sauce of salsa verde, with two leaves of basil on top. It was good, but it is fairly hard to go wrong with burrata. 
Our main dishes were presented next. My friend had the ricotta and mushroom dumplings, which was by far the better looking of the two dishes. She said they were good, but was surprised at the presentation of the mushrooms, raw and sliced on top of the dumplings. She said they were good. 
I ordered the grilled turbot, which consisted of simply grilled fish, with some sliced radish, mayonnaise, and chili paste. It wasn't bad, but felt like something I could have easily made at home. 
We had no complaints about the service, but we waited a longer than normal time for our food, and the restaurant wasn't full. 
I wouldn't mind trying this place again for dinner, but it didn't feel like the food was offering anything unique or special.
As good as it gets! My favorite spot in the city!  Probably one of my fav places ever! I bought the cookbook!

Estela at the Rockefeller Rink: WHAT A RIP-OFF! Three of us went with much anticipation for a great seafood picnic in the famous rink but what a disappointment in terms if the super ridiculous price for what we got. We paid a total of $483 for a tray of seafood, albeit very fresh, consisting of 6 clams, 6 oysters, 1/2 lobster, 6 shrimps, 1 scallop, 1 king crab claw, a bowl of raw tuna. The one star is for freshness and the location. I don't mind paying for good food but for that tray for $483? We should have used that money for a wonderful seafood dinner at Le Bernardin!!!!

I dined yesterday night. The food was very good and the waiter nice and professional. However, we had a terrible experience with the lady host/general manager that ruined it all. We had dinner at 6.30pm and needed to leave the table at 8.30pm, she came to let us know the next party was waiting & told us with bad manners. We said we were leaving in 5 min the time to go to bathroom & get our coats. She kept pushing with lack of grace, so we told her was not our fault that the appetizers came very spaced out. She went defensive & talked down to us saying literally "you need to leave if you want to come back" "it is a privilege to dine here". I said I should have reviewed my generous 20% tip. I am sorry but the privilege is given to me ny my credit card & a regular reservation made using Resy. The host (she) was rude and unprofessional, really intolerable that she is in the hospitable industry & cant address customers with grace. Zero stars if I could and of course we wont be coming back.
NY gem.  If you are trying to "get through" the good NYC restaurants then Estela is a must-visit.  Not great for dietary restrictions.  Decadent food.

Food is tasty but bit over price foe the portions. Dishes is like tapas style and menu is seasonal.  We order everything on the menu with exception of one dessert and one dish that was sold out.   8 main and 2 deserts for four people.   Post dinner still hungry.
New favorite spot in New York! The portions are on the smaller side given the prices but the food quality is incredible. Highly recommend the fried fish burger

Break down- **adheres to the covid protocol **
Location- Second floor warm and cozy feel ambience like walking to someone's apartment. This place is a hidden gem of creative tapas style dishes, out of this world flavors exploding in your mouth. 

**Shot out to the host Sam with the gracious and warm greeting !!

staff- 5/5 very friendly all around , you can tell it's a great team.
Drinks-5/5 we did the bottle - ask for the bottle Menu/ a lot of nice options to choose from - I'm sure the cocktails are good! 
Food - 4.5/5. It was delicious, but I left .5 room to go back and try it again. Lol - joke aside this place is really good- definitely a place for foodies all around. 

Great complexity of pairings and flavors, extremely unique but goes really well.  

I was till hungry for more, tapas for you :) !! 

YUM YUM approves !!!! 

 Check out the pictures below wand drool
Delicious food and so flavorful. Went there for lunch and ordered the lobster omelette, goat cheese, and smoked finish salad. Would probably get all of them again!
Amazing seafood appetizers!! Unexpected combinations of flavors in every savory bite that you just want it to linger awhile longer.

The restaurant is on the 2nd floor, almost felt like a hidden gem on the busy Houston street. It's a cute restaurant with limited seating. The service was great and all the staff are very friendly and attentive.   The food was very thoughtful. Great ingredients with a lot of complex flavors and textures. The only problem for me is that overall the food is just too salty. The first bite tastes great, but once you have 2nd or 3rd bite it was just too much. My favorite (or the least salty) dishes tonight are beef tartare , ricotta dumplings and the chocolate cake. I love the crunchy texture of arroz negro, it's probably the best arroz negro I ever had texture-wise, but it's just a bit salty for me to enjoy more bites

Wow.  You must come here ...

If I could give it 6 starts I would . Can't say enough about this place . It is an absolute must . All Around satisfying.  Thank you estela   For raising the bar.

Can't say enough about this restaurant! The food was absolutely impeccable. The service from the door, from the waitress and the support staff also stellar. If you want superbly executed food, Estela is your place.

Visiting from out of town and the environment and food combined are just impeccable! It's small enough to feel quaint but fancy enough to feel like a special dining experience. Will definitely be recommending to those visiting NYC!

Enjoyed a sprawling meal at Estela on Monday evening. Tried everything on the menu and left with quite a few favorites, but definitely felt there was room to either reduce the options or swap out less rewarding dishes.

Quality: Estela came on my radar because of their famous Beef Tartare, but with Michelin recognition and a lot of fun sounding dishes, decided to visit with friends. With a group of four we were ambitious and ordered the menu. While this allowed a full look at what the restaurant could do, which had some gems I would have never thought to order, it also showed some of the weaknesses I may have avoided. To me the menu breaks down into incredible, solid, and good but skippable dishes. Incredible starts with the Beef Tartare, so tender and perfectly textured with the use of sunchokes. The Raw Scallops, Sweetbreads, and Ricotta Dumplings also fall into this category, each bringing something unique and unexpected. The solid dishes would be the Endive Salad, an item I would have skipped if not with a larger group and glad I got to try, as well as the Fried Arroz Negro, which had a rich depth of flavor. The good, but skippable dishes would be the simple Charcuterie, the Oysters, the Red Gem Lettuce Salad, the Lobster, the Red Snapper, the Iberico Pork, and the Steak. The truth is the mains simply were not on the same level of some of the smaller dishes. Not that there was a single poor dish on the menu, but there is a clear distinction in terms of inventiveness and quality. We also ordered the Panna Cotta and Chocolate Cake for dessert, the Panna Cotta was the clear favorite, but both were nice for a sweet ending.
Quantity: Our group of four ordered every dish on the menu and a few duplicates. It was more food than we needed, but a fun experience.
Value: $24 for the Charcuterie. $25 for the Oysters. $24 for the Raw Scallops. $19 for the Beef Tartare. $20 for the Red Gem Lettuce Salad. $20 for the Endive Salad. $29 for the Lobster. $31 for the Sweetbreads. $27 for Fried Arroz Negro. $36 for the Red Snapper. $27 for the Ricotta Dumplings. $42 for the Iberico Pork. $42 for the Steak. $12 for the Panna Cotta. $12 for the Chocolate Cake.
Ambiance: Estela is located in the Nolita section of Manhattan. Along the busy Houston Street it sits slightly raised from the street level. The space was not quite what I was expecting, it was a small and simple bistro vibe. They have a marble bar near the entrance and then a row of tables on each side of the wall to the back of the narrow space. The decor is extremely simple with just mirrors and low lighting and the acoustics keep it buzzing even when relatively empty. There was also a semi-private wine room towards the back, still part of the restaurant, but more secluded.
Crowd: Reservations are required, and if you are not quick to grab them, expect an early or late dinner.
Service: The service was fantastic even when we threw a few wrenches by jumping back and forth on the menu. The sommelier we interacted with was also lovely and so helpful in finding wines that our party would enjoy. 
Parking: Need to go a few blocks away to find street parking.

Food: excellent, different, and memorable. 
Service: waiter was attentive and took his time to help e find a low ABV wine 
Host: RUDE! The attitude. Told her it was our anniversary after we came in because we were excited to finally eat at a Estela and her response was to look up, smirk and say "umm ok" and look back to her iPad. At least smile? Some people are excited to eat out.

The fried rice was incredible- not something I would ever order as it sounds basic but it was delicious. The scallop was amazing as well. 

Ambiance: perfect

Are you kidding me? I lived in NYC for 5 years and didn't know about this amazing restaurant? Food is so tasty and unique, super friendly service. 
LOVED IT! Its a must try

Not the best looking set of tasting menu but the flavors are OUT OF THE WORLD!! The plating is so clean and minimalistic and mainly focus on the distinctive flavors. I had some doubts at first but oh my, I had an amazing, full, flavorful and very satisfying lunch here a few months ago. My favorite was the crispy duck--I think it's one of the BEST duck I've ever had. Very worth it for a one Michelin starred restaurant and highly recommend.

Confuses me why their Yelp rating isn't nearly 5 stars. Returned recently, and Estela is hands down still one of my favorite restaurants in the city. The quality and innovation of the food is superior. One of the things I love most is their natural wine selection, where they always make the best recommendations. 

My favorites and must try's:
Endive Salad 
Fried Arroz (my ultimate favorite)
Scallops 
Riccota Dumplings 

The Duck was on the salty side but it was still good. 

While on the slightly pricier side and harder end to make a reservation, I'd confidently say it's well worth a trip.

Estela has been my favorite restaurant in NY for nearly a decade. If you like food, you will love Estela. If you like ..... really amazing food presented uniquely (and beautifully) while also tasting out of this world..... you will looooove Estela. Go here. But don't go here if you don't like to eat outside of the box.

The food in excellent, the vibe is excellent and the service is excellent. James was our server and he was so nice and knowledgeable. The ricotta dumplings and the fried arroz negro with squid and romesco are both incredible. You have to show your vaccination card to dine, which I love.

The restaurant has excellent food. No doubt. Presentation is beautiful. Ambience is excellent. 

The most important thing for my dining experience is that I not get sick from the food. Unfortunately the restaurant's carelessness when it comes to dietary restrictions needs to be mentioned. The waiter was alerted early on that I have a gluten intolerance. He identified the dishes I could eat, including one that could be modified. We ordered those. However, the wrong dish was brought, and it was not immediately clear, when I started eating it. I asked, and yes, it contained gluten. They apologized several times and removed the dish from the bill. That was it. There was no other compensation provided.

I would certainly not return. Any restaurant - Michelin star or not  - needs better processes to ensure this doesn't happen. Diners deserve better from any restaurant. There is no excuse.

If you don't have dietary restrictions, I might try it out. You would certainly have a better experience than I did.

I've been coming here for years.  And pretty impressed the quality of food has been consistent throughout.  Endive salad, arroz negro are classics.  We ordered the pork dish which I think is not as successful with the oyster on top.  The duck was pretty good too. This morning place makes me happy
We went for lunch/dinner, we love the place, very cute, great selection of wine. People where very nice and food was very good.

After seeing all the great reviews, I thought the food would be great... but I was so wrong. My party and I got their most popular dishes, but it was so salty. I felt like I was swimming in an ocean from the amount of salt they used in all the dishes we got. We were all so utterly disappointed and upset that we paid around 77 dollars each for such terrible food. I don't understand all the great reviews because we couldn't comprehend how people could swallow the saltiness... We really tried to like it, but the experience wouldn't get any better... I don't think we will ever come again. If you like salty foods, then this is your place.
Incredible food every time. They accept walk-ins too if you are willing to wait. Amazing!

NYC locals. We were really excited for this dinner, sadly it did not live up to the hype. Arrived on time and our table wasn't ready. We were sat at the bar for 2 minutes (why even seat us there) until we proceed to our table shoved in the corner at the POS, right next to the bathrooms. Lovely. 

Our server spoke to us for a grand total of 30 seconds over the entire dinner. 15 of those seconds were us asking for WATER. The food was fine. Not memorable as the other reviews imply. The endive was the best dish but we weren't told how to eat it properly as the real substance of the dish lies below the leaves of the endive. We're not idiots, but some instruction with an interesting dish like that would have been welcomed. The other 5 dishes were just so-so. 

If you're visiting NYC skip this. So much better out there. I recommend Cervo's on the LES, or almost anywhere else.

It's always hard to pick the right rating for a restaurant. I think if it's purely on food, I would've given it 4. 

As others have commented, the restaurant is small and tables are packed close to each other. When we arrived at 5:40, the restaurant was wide open. However, the hostess sat us right next to another table at the corner by the POS terminal. The space was so tight that I had to move the table in order to get in. With Covid, you would think they would try to space people out if possible. 

I asked the hostess if it was possible to get a different table. I was referred to another woman who told me the restaurant was full and there were no alternative tables available. She did come back about 5 mins later offered me to sit at the bar if I wanted. 

However the restaurant was wide open for the next hour including multiple two person tables. You would think it would be easy to move us to a different table until the next reservation arrives. Even when we left 1.5 hour later, there were still 3 tables that had sat empty the entire time. 

Some things are outside of their control, however, I believe this is totally avoidable. They could have planned seating better. At minimum, when asked, show a bit of creativity and flexibility. 

I had also noted on reservation that this is for a birthday, however, there was no mention of it either by the hostess or the waiter. There wasn't even a good bye as we left. This shows you the attitude of this restaurant. 

In terms of food, it was quite good. However, it's not quite on par with some of the other restaurants with 1 Michelin Star. It was a bit on the salty side as others have mentioned. 

The cocktails are not cheap but unfortunately the flavor and balance wasn't quite right.  

Overall, it's a miss for me. It's not a restaurant I would go out of way to experience.

WOW. The food here is wonderful, and our server was absolutely lovely and attentive without being all over us. The scallop squash blossoms were unexpectedly the most incredible thing we've eaten in a long, long time, and the endive salad was also fabulous. It's definitely a splurge, but for a fancy, special night out, it was amazing. Also, loved that they require and check vax cards at the door, which made me feel a lot more safe eating inside (no outdoor space).

The food was good but not great and certainly not worth the ridiculous prices - maybe 15 slices of raw zucchini with some sauce and pine nuts for $20. One review said it was one of the 50 best restaurants in the world which is extremely hard to believe.

A bit disappointed with my most recent Estela experience - was looking forward in coming back but they rotated out a lot of my favourite dishes 

I ordered:
- the charcuterie board - very basic nothing special but good value 
- the sesame chicken - lacking flavour (it was salty enough but the sesame sauce was lacking sesame flavour)
- the ricotta dumplings - way too salty 
- the bacon and tomato sandwich - this was very yummy but half the sandwich had bacon missing 

Probably wouldn't come back again given the ample options in NY. Also resto was packed and the tables are pretty close to each other

I know 2020-2021 has not been easy for restaurants so it pains me greatly to write this but I was planning a milestone 90th birthday dinner that I wanted to be very special that fell flat.

The average of 2 comes from a 4 for food (lots of very salty dishes) and a 1 for service. I booked the chef's table ($175/person) which they market as, "Join us upstairs for an intimate, interactive dinner cooked by estela's culinary director, Sam Lawrence" except my chef's table experience came without a chef. Food was cooked in the main kitchen and brought up to the private dining room, so basically what I had was a private room, not a "intimate interactive dinner." No chef was to be seen anywhere. Beware of the very misleading advertising.

I also made the reservation with my American Express card thinking that it might provide additional exceptional service. Nada. I notified the restaurant at least 2 times, on my reservation and texting with one of the staff people that it was a milestone birthday. The reply from Alison, "Hello! We will absolutely put a candle into the chocolate cake dessert we are serving as part of your pre fixe dinner!"

Dessert comes out without a candle (by the way, the "cake" is moussey cake in a dish with cream on top) so they bring out another panna cotta (there were 2 desserts) with a candle. Have you ever had panna cotta with a candle to celebrate a birthday? How damn pathetic! I even read that, at Vestry, a guest received a signed birthday card from staff! Talk about lack of effort!

Of course, they had no problem telling me that I hadn't met my minimum yet for the room so we felt compelled to order more after dinner drinks and dessert. A guest orders a Macallen 12 which they don't have so they bring him another type of whisky with characteristics that are the absolute opposite of what a Macallen 12 is and they won't charge us for it. I didn't understand the reasoning behind giving him something he didn't want and think that giving it to us complimentary made any difference. We were all perplexed.

Service sucked big time and took away from the whole experience. To add insult to injury, when I contacted the restaurant with my frustrations about the evening, no one bothered to get back to me. 

Nearly $1500 for the whole evening for sh**ty service.  I may not be Obama (their claim to glory) and they may not care who I am but they have this memorable Yelp review to remember me by. Excelling in hospitality is clearly not a priority for them. You work hard for your money, so if you want service, spend your well earned $$$ elsewhere. NY has tons of other options!

This is a must restaurant in NY now. By Ignacio Mattos. The food is fresh and tasty, sophisticated and relatable. A bit acid and based on exceptional quality ingredients. Quite not masking the ingredients' flavors. Here, an oyster tastes a lot like an amazing oyster, and so does a cherry tomato. 
It is quite multicultural, to the extend that it is difficult to classify. 
The wine list is really well done. Very much based on a broad understanding of what is happening in the world in terms of wine. I had a wine from Galicia, resulting in a very recent movement to experiment with wine in a particular area of Galicia that only very expert knowers of the context there know about. 
Only weak point is interior design. Why this space looks like an aging Hells Kitchen old pizza slides place is a mystery to me. The space is not bad, with a big window. A mystery.  That is why I don't give 5 starts to this exceptional place.

I've been here 6-7 times over 8 years. 3 stars because the dishes are flavorful, balanced, consistent, pretty and eclectic. As an example, grilled foie in grape leaves. 

Only 3 stars because 1/2 of the staff were unwelcoming, brash, and hostile at times. 1/2 of the staff were absolutely lovely. 

I worked in hospitality for 10 years in NYC, 5 years with a 3 Michelin star restaurant (Michelin started rating in NYC in 2005, then released the 2006 edition as the first in the US). 

To sum it up, I have never seen such inhospitable behavior from mgmt and veteran staff. Again, some staff were certainly Fantastic. I could put a laundry list of examples together of the examples. Just my feelings here - I don't speak for anyone else. 

Maybe I'm too traditional with hospitality, but I felt it was a shame given the $500 price tag. Needless to say, I won't be going back. There are just too many great restaurants that do BOTH food and HOSPITALITY well. Just My .02.

Whatever they're doing at Estela the world needs them to keep doing it. Wowowow this is the fine dining experience you can't get mad at because the portions are a little more than the standard and with every bite you can tell it's been well thought out and it's absolutely delicious, like touches your soul kind of delicious. They've definitely unlocked some keys here.
You can't go wrong with anything on the menu- be bold and get the thing you're not sure about. The drinks are great as well but very pricey for what it is in my opinion but the service is wonderful and friendly and accommodating. This is the place you take your best friend to, or your lover.

Super bummed about this one. 6 months ago we tried it for the first time and had a wonderful dinner. Then we came back last week and it was painful. 

The food is great (which is even more heart wrenching) because the atmosphere was absolutely deplorable.

How?

The space - They packed in about 2x as many tables as they should have with tables spaced *maybe* 8" apart from each other. I hope you've been hitting your Pilates classes because you'll have to move multiple tables to squeeze by if your legs are wider than 8". I'm fit and I barely squeezed in... forget about leaving the table during dinner.

The noise level - with 2x as many people that should be in here at one time + marble floors + no sound absorption... you can't hear the person across from you. What you CAN hear is the table next to you yelling their conversation over the table. Because that's what it takes.

The timing - for a small plates menu the timing between courses should be fairly quick. However, we were left waiting 20-30 minutes between courses multiple times. We honestly almost left mid dinner but I couldn't get our waiters attention.

I don't usually write negative reviews but this was a truly heartbreaking experience. The food was good - some courses were great - even excellent! The wine list is superb. Kudos to the sommelier and to the chef! 

I won't be coming back because eating in this restaurant felt like a psychological experiment. 

My hope is that they take out a few tables and maybe add some sound dampening equipment. It's a shame to have so much potential drowned out.

I consider Estela to be the epitome of a disappointing restaurant.

While it is espoused for its Michelin qualities, the food simply did not deliver.

They offer virtually no vegetarian options which is astounding for a restaurant in New York City in this day and age. The only option was in fact a ricotta dumpling dish that could be best described as blobs of wet bread (it truly lacked flavor or an appealing texture).

The service was not overly friendly and the tables are totally jam-packed. I would not go back.

Loved it so much and visited again, felt like more of a 3.7 experience this time : ( post pandemic?

First experience was that simplest flavor bomb that left in my mouth. Post pandemic visit, lots of old seafood menu is taken out, which is understandable.

Squid - feel like it's just in a bed of butter soup.

Endive Salad - the leaf wasn't crunchy but stale, not ok that it's not the freshest. The sauce was simply just orange juice. Not exactly sure where the anchovy is used?

Steak tartar - ok but the dried yukon (I think, or yucca) was overpowering and we don't think it compliment well.

Ricotta Dumpling - as it sound, kinda nothing special.

Steak - very good, cooked to perfection.

Clam - good too but not memorable.

Used to be one of my favorite restaurant but not anymore :/

The service was not welcoming at all. Felt pressured while ordering food. Restaurant was incredibly packed, by packed I mean we were basically sharing tables with adjacent tables. And yes, before you ask the gap in between tables was approximately 4 inches. The food was a little bit below the expectations for the price. (Chocolate cake's texture was questionable, scallop with dates' combo was an unfortunate pairing)

Great atmosphere. Amazing dishes and wine list. 
Their sea bream+matsutake+chestnut  dish was to die for.
They have a great BTG list. Definitely order their chocolate cake. Their sepia rice dish was way too salty.

Came across this place while on the hunt for a natural wine bar before a late dinner, and the aesthetic and overall ambiance lured me in. The look and overall vibe inside is wonderful, and exactly what you want when you're sipping on a fine glass, or two.

I hadn't intended to really order "food" food, so my feedback and perspective is more built on my interpretation of this place as a wine bar that serves food rather than a restaurant that serves wine (both wonderful things). The wine list was wonderful, and our server had some wonderful recommendations for everyone and our different tastes. Smoky and funky for me, juicy for my wife, and clean and white for our friend.

Those wonderful elements aside I do have two critiques that yield a 4-star review from my perspective:

1. The service was honestly a little weird. We were able to walk-in, sans reservation, at ~5:30PM so long as we cleared the table by 7:30, which was fine because we planned on dinner later. After being seated our server asked about drinks and got the ball rolling, but after coming back she was seemingly quite taken aback by the news that we were just there for drinks and perhaps an appetizer or two. She clearly went back to the bar and was talking to another server about it, and while this wasn't a big deal it kind of left an odd taste for the rest of our time there, as if just being there for wine and light fare was some subpar utilization of the seats (as if we didn't end up spending ~$160).

2. For food we ordered the charcuterie and dumplings, and while the dumplings were delicious the charcuterie was comical. For $27, or so, we maybe got 4 cracker-size slices of bread, and a similar small count of two different meats. Don't get me wrong, they were good for what they were, but  for the money and general aesthetic I would've expected at least a piece or two of cheese, or some sort of jam. It may have been the most underwhelming presentation of "charcuterie" I've ever encountered, and I just kind of have to chuckle because everything else was lovely.

All that to say this is a lovely place, and the aesthetics and wines are top notch. The food at its price point, from what I experienced, is something I would avoid while you're there for, but this may well just my experience with a specific subset of the menu, and the rest is amazing. Well worth a visit regardless.

I'm surprised that I haven't come here sooner. This place is pretty amazing. You honestly wouldn't think much of it looking from the outside but the food and service are both very much on point. 

The food is both light and flavorful at the same time. My favorites were the beef tartare, the chicory salad, the foie gras, and the squid ink rice. 

The service here is also amazing. Better than some high end restaurants to be honest. Our waitress was confident and knowledgeable. Our food runner was above and beyond with every dish served. I can't speak to how great they all really were. 

Overall the food was a bit pricey for the environment, but I enjoyed it. I think it was a wonderful experience and would definitely come again

If could give this place zero stars, I would. That being said, a 1 star is appropriate for the 1 Michelin they somehow got.  We came here for our anniversary... or thought we were going to. We got there 15 minutes before our reservation and we're told to go to the unrelated bar below for drinks and to come back at our reservation time. We then came back and multiple people were sat before us. 40 minutes after our reservation time we decided to leave. What a terrible experience and a ruining of our special evening. Don't overbook your place. It's an embarrassment for your establishment. Will never recommend.

This place is absolutely amazing! A great experience, good taste, good drinks, yummm. :)
The only thing is that there is no vegetarian option...  Also, it's noisy, don't bring your grandpa or an important work dinner!

We'll definitely be back! We came because we wanted to say hi to a friend while in town. He staffs the bar and makes the best cocktails my wife and I have ever had! So we knew the drinks would be great, but the food was one of a kind and over the top delicious. Every single bite... excellent. Thanks Blake, for making it all happen.

We've been lucky enough to try many high-end restaurants in NYC. Not really sure if Estela is considered one,  but I suppose they pride themselves on their "clientele". Maybe I would be back again in the future to give it another try; however, the service was horrible. The server was so unfriendly and when we told her we didn't like the ricotta (inedible), she didn't apologize or offer to get us anything else...we had to tell her we didn't want it and would order something else instead. We ordered five dishes and none of the food "wowed" us and for the prices, there are so many more restaurants in NY to chose from.

Know it's been said before, but Estela is doing something unique and beautiful. It occupies a space between fine and casual; experimental and comforting; playful and boundary-pushing. 

Finally had a chance to visit Ignacio Mattos' iconic spot last night for a special occasion, and it truly lived up to the hype -- and even surpassed the incredibly high expectations I had for the spot. More than anything else, the meal was remarkably fun. Each course (made for sharing) inspires a genuine playfulness that feels rare, even in a city like New York. 

Dishes like the iconic endive salad embody this -- basically requiring you make mini taco-like boats of the leaves filled with the delicious, texturally mind-blowing granola. Likewise, the scallops with brown butter and potato had similarly fun construction. The scallops aren't prepared as you might expect (crudo?) with a potato mousse atop. Of course, the staples are staples for a reason. The beef tartare, ricotta dumplings and arroz negro all blew me away, too. Finished with the panna cotta, which was the perfect way to end the meal. 

Want to shout out the excellent beverage program too. The cocktails were stunning (try the Vespa), and the wine menu is similarly exciting, featuring a number of fun biodynamic selections from smaller producers. It's very easy to find a great bottle for under $70; the somm picked us one for $56 and it was a delicious Austrian red blend that paired perfectly with the meal. 

This was truly one of those meals you remember for a long time. I cannot wait to come back.

ricotta dumplings were the best thing i've eaten in a long time, loved how they layered the thinly sliced mushrooms on top and the sauce all paired together was magical 
tartare was pretty solid, squid ink rice was nice and crispy, could have skipped the endive dish and the pork

Horrible service. We waiting an hour outside and they kept letting people budge in line. We were the next in line for 40 min, the staff didn't care and kept letting in friends and anyone who budged their way forward. We decided to walk, they didn't deserve our money. Go to the Paella place around the corner.

This was only our second time to dine at Estela, we loved it as much the second time as the first.  Our daughter and son-in-law are regulars so they could help us with the quantity of items and what to order.  The menu is not traditional so the server needs to help you with how much to order if it's your first time.  The menu descriptions can't possibly describe what you will be served, it takes an explanation.  The wine selections pair perfectly with the dishes being served.  I highly recommend giving Estela a try if you can get in.  It's refreshing dining at a Michelin star restaurant that is not stuffy.

If I could put 0 stars I would. Extremely disappointed by the behavior of the management. We waited more than 30 minutes even though we had a reservation. The wait for our table turned into having to order a bottle at over $85 to pass the time. The food and wine list are still particularly good, which resulted in a bill of over $700. This didn't stop the staff from criticizing us for not having a high enough tip and kicking us out of the restaurant. So move on, they don't deserve your money and appreciation. The chef would do better to go offer his cooking in a restaurant worthy of the name.

The restaurant and food were stunning. Good service, although felt a bit impersonal. Don't miss the Endive salad, the ricotta dumplings, or the chocolate cake, which tasted like a cloud. Excellent spot.

I was disappointed with Estela and its ambiance. Unfortunately, it is a tiny place, extremely crammed and noisy, which affects the overall dining experience. The food was good but not exceptional as I had expected. Some of the dishes, such as the endive salad, were extremely salty. Estela, unfortunately, did not meet the expectations of a Michelin star restaurant.

I highly recommend the enclave salad, the mussels & the black rice. 
The only dish our table didn't like was the foie gras 
Everything else was delicious. Great spot for dinner

I've been coming to this place for several years now and it's gone down hill 

Recommend:
Endive walnuts anchovy
Ricotta dumplings 
Fried arroz negro

So so:
Cod with ramps and avocado
Crab with seaweed

Do not get:
Duck
Lobster With mushrooms and green chickpeas
Sublime across two visits, lunch and dinner, about 6 weeks apart. Having eaten and most of the best restaurants in NYC this genuinely my favorite. Pictures are from lunch in June.

I came in for a lunch estela was hosting benefitting planned parenthood. I sat at the bar and was immediately served a drink and the first of four courses on the menu that day. I had reserved the lunch knowing it was going to be four courses, but it was really more like 9! Everything was executed perfectly. I especially loved the endive salad, which I know is a staple on their normal menu. The chocolate cake was perfectly balanced with sweetness and a hint of salt, and it was one of the only chocolate cakes I've eaten where I really got to appreciate the flavor of the chocolate (and trust me, I've tried plenty of chocolate cakes). The drinks were creative and paired amazingly with the courses, and I loved the more sophisticated sub for an espresso martini, which have gotten so popular at bars that it's losing some of its luster. At the end of the meal I asked if I could add gratuity even though I had prepaid for the lunch. The bar staff insisted they were all working that day so they could help raise money. This place seems to be not only a food destination, but a place where its staff want to do good. Would definitely love to come back for dinner next time I'm in the area!

Some standouts but generally overpriced and over-seasoned. The vibe inside is nice (it's a small restaurant and sitting at the bar feels very New York in a good way). 

Beef tartare with sunchokes and elderberries - quite good; you don't taste much elderberry but the sunchokes add a nice crunch.

Foie gras in grape leaves - really nice, would recommend! The grape leaves add freshness/bitterness and the foie is cooked perfectly. 

Arroz negro - way too salty. Flavor is nice if you like squid ink, but there wasn't much squid. Was a bit like Rice Krispies baked with table salt. 

Ricotta dumplings - the raw mushroom was an interesting touch, dumplings were nice but a bit mushy. Would recommend to try at least once though.

Sweet potato with rum ice cream - much too alcohol-forward for me. Not much depth of flavor or texture either, just alcohol flavored mush.
Tiny spot and a little crowded but the food and drinks really hit the spot. Definitely worth the late night res

Walked in on a Saturday at 6pm and got bar seating, which was a bit cramped, but beggars can't be choosers! 

Our waiter/bartender was super sweet and had great recs for both food and drinks. 

We started off with the seasonal crab + celery root and seaweed dish, then went on to the beef tartare (crunchy and creamy!), endive (refreshing, tart, yet savory, and super fun to eat), the foie gras (perfectly tender and rich, wrapped in greens), and ended with the ricotta dumplings, which were the highlight of my night. The food was extremely well thought out and delicately presented; it felt like we went through a whole gastronomic journey with all the textures and taste profiles.

We also got a cheese to share as dessert (it looked like a flower!) and each got a drink - a white wine for myself and a spritz for my friend. All in all, it was a lovely dinner - perfect for date nights or intimate special occasions! It's probably not a great choice if you have a large group, but so delicious that you should stop by.

Tried 3 dishes, 1 dessert, and 1 drink for lunch 2 people ($157 after 20% gratuity) on 7/23/22.

...it was alright I guess?

Made a reservation for lunch, but there were empty tables throughout our entire meal despite it being a Saturday, not sure we really needed to. Our entire meal took maybe 1-1.5 hours, didn't feel rushed or like we were waiting, great pacing.

When we showed up on time for our reservation, there were deliveries still going into the restaurant, we had to wait ~10 minutes for them to finish up before we could even get by (the entrance is tiny, no way you're going in at the same time as anyone else). Kind of weird, but maybe they don't control their delivery schedule and they were running late, I'll allow it.

We were seated at our table for 2, right next to a table of 4. There was another empty table for 2 next to us that wasn't taken for our entire meal. Why not give everyone some space?

Which brings us to the next point. The dining room, and the tables, and the space between the tables, are TINY. You can hear everything the table next to you is saying, and forget about getting up at any point without bothering the people next to you. There are mirrors on the walls which try and make the space look bigger, but they do nothing for the loudness of the room. I actually used the Apple Watch noise level measuring and it tipped into yellow "Loud" at times - I know you make do with what you have, but some cushions/decorations/anything might go a long way towards making it a little more tolerable.

Drinks were great. I ordered the Bloody Mary and it came with a lot of pepper and Thai chili, definitely not a recipe I've had before, big fan.

At this point, the server recommended that we order 4-6 dishes for the two of us. If we had followed this advice, I think we would have had to take food to go - absolutely not what I want to do on a hot NYC day. The portions are decently sized (even for the Michelin star price), go small and order more/eat dessert after.

Two of our ordered dishes were big hits. We ordered two signature Estela classics, the fried arroz negro and the ricotta dumplings, and both were great. The arroz negro had a different texture every bite - my partner and I ate this one really slowly and tried to figure out the ingredients the entire time we were enjoying. The ricotta dumplings are just simple goodness, and it was a great touch for a server to bring us some complimentary bread to soak up the mushroom broth at the end.

One dish missed. The "steelhead trout with sea urchin and seaweed" broke apart oddly (trout is one of the easiest fish to get to be flaky?), the sea urchin was actually used to make the sauce and therefore I could hardly even taste any of the rich, buttery, seafood-y taste that's its signature tasty goodness, and the kelp-y seaweed was drowned in a citrus-y vinaigrette. I couldn't even taste the saltiness of the seaweed, that was a super weird experience.

The "panna cotta with vinegar and honey" dessert was awesome - not too sweet, not too much vanilla, not too acidic, perfect temperature for a HOT summer day in NYC. Great touch by the server to choose this moment to acknowledge our special occasion as well!

I think I'd return with a bigger group to try the entire menu - it's the sort of place where you WANT to try everything. With a bigger group, you're also less likely to get bullied around with the space concerns since you'll literally be taking up more table space, and you'll definitely be able to hear everyone in your group since you can hear everything that's going on in the dining room anyways. I'd LOVE for Estela to fix the dining room to be better for small groups - I really think it'd be as simple as putting in furniture to absorb some of the loudness of a room with brick walls and mirrors. But right now, the environment definitely detracts from the food, and I'd only be back alone at the bar or in a group that'd take much of the space (and unfortunately, that'd probably be at the expense of others).

Wow! This place is amazing! If you really love tapas like I do, then I highly recommend coming here. The employees are very attentive and helpful. Our waiter was very educated on all of the menu items and told us what are the popular dishes that people order. 

This is a very cute place to go on a date night. My boyfriend and I ordered their snapper with uni and seaweed, fried arroz negro with squid and romesco, steak tartare with elderberries, steak yuzu kosho mignonette, and panna cotta. My favorites were the fried arroz negro with squid and romesco and beef tartare. Those are must orders! Everything was delicious.

Kind of a bummer for a $300 meal. The endive salad was spectacular and fried black rice was quite good, but the crab / lobster dishes were not great (crab overdressed; no apparent crab sweetness). The lobster had the opposite issue (basted and charred so the flavor was nice, but served with overly fibrous wood ear mushrooms). The duck (final dish) was the biggest disappointment - lots of connective tissue, which we had to cut around. Honestly I was shocked  they served this piece of protein. In any case, overall I think you could do a lot better for the price point.

While the food may be Michelin quality, the dining experience certainly is not. Read the reviews before coming here. You want to love the place. You say oh it won't matter. But it does. Hard to hear the person across from you. Waiters rush you a bit to get through the courses. Tables were so close together we had to shuffle every time someone nearby wanted to get in or out, almost knocked over friend's glass of wine. 

I get it, small venue, want to fit as many as possible to experience the great food. But reconsider the experience because it really felt more like a crowded bar room than something special.

Absolutely loved everything about Estela. Didn't think something as simple as rice and an endive salad could be this good! Perfect ambiance - dim lit, bustling but still intimate, open bar and perfect service pace too.

tl;dr: super clean food, very creative, clean, loud vibe.

Estela is a stage on which Chef Mattos can execute his singular vision. You can even realize this by flipping through the cookbook. The plates are all white circles - probably all the same half bowl/half plate shape as well. The food is almost always monochromatic; if there is contrast, it is stark.

The flavors map well with the visual. The food is clean, with extreme contrasts in flavors and textures that speak to Mattos' voice. He has something unique to say. The bread and butter course was fucking fantastic.

At the same time, the food felt a bit stale - as if a small fraction of the sex of the original dishes has been taken out. Some of the plates were missing acid and some of the flavors seem to have dulled over the years that the kitchen spent refining them.

Moreover, the place stands alone in the arena of 1 Michelin restaurants. The service is extremely casual and the food is still one rung below other Michelin joints with respect to detail. When we entered, we were directed to a small windowsill up against the bar. The restaurant assured us when we placed the reservation that the kitchen would address listed dietary issues in advance but they seemed flustered when we asked what on the menu would be ok.

Minor issues such as these would be more relevant if Estela had raised prices to be on par with other Michelin joints but they did not. Dinner was approximately $75pp - far less than what we would have paid for a tasting menu anywhere in Manhattan. For the money, Estela is an excellent value proposition.

Overall the dinner was fun, delicious, and with a crowd that seemed full of regulars who really carried the vibe. The dishes are all incredibly unique and really made me want to cook through the entire book in a single sitting. I look forward to coming back or going to one of Mattos' other new joints soon.
Our experience was immaculate but Immanuel was the icing on the cake! So personal and knowledgeable, we appreciated him so much!!
Loved the ambiance, food, drinks, and dessert. we especially liked the beef tartare and foie grad wrapped in leaves.

What a lovely restaurant and excellent experience. Had a beautiful dinner at the bar. The staff was warm, knowledgeable, and super helpful. The vibe of the restaurant is inviting and classy. The menu is seasonal and inspired. The tempo of the meal is fantastic. Wine selection isn't huge, but is solid. Now the star of the show! The confit steelhead trout was unreal! The lobster was mild and a nice middle dish. The dashi broth was very refreshing. The kohlrabi salad with apples was perfect for autumn and the beef tartare with crispy sunchoke was a win. Casual enough for anyone, but super elevated food.
One of my favorite restaurants in the city! A great place for a cocktail and meal with friends, and the food is always exceptional! Definitely give it a try if you have the chance.

The food is divine. Inventive, well spiced, varied. But to spend so much money for a meal and to feel constantly rushed during each course  was really insulting. Why should we be asked two or three times if they can clear our plates but NEVER if we need more water or bread? REALLY? If they can see there is still food on the plates -- why keep hovering us to move on when there was no line outside and we were made they would need our table. They never asked if we wanted another cocktail or glass of wine? We were not going to overstay our welcome. But they're hovering to get us out was infuriating.  We had been here before and to other restaurants in this group -- tonight was not acceptable. 
Gotta admit we were very disappointed!

This was our third trip to Estela, and our second time sitting at the bar for dinner-- for a party of two the bar is the secret to a beautiful experience as it plays to the advantage of a tiny, close dining room. Instead of being crowded into a tight table where your neighbors' conversations are as loud as your own, you're tucked into a pretty, intimate bar where the regulars are sociable and the bartender, Emmanuel (more on him in a second), greets you like a friend. The restaurant is on the second floor, with the bar at the front of the room closest to the  windows and the nighttime lights on Houston. The vibe is elegant-cozy-- a specific and satisfying New York moment perfect for a low-key special occasion (in this case our wedding anniversary).   

If you're lucky you'll be there when Emmanuel is tending bar. Incredibly, he remembered us from our last visit six months ago.
