Both times he was attentive, friendly, knowledgable and generous, providing the perfect suggestion for a kickoff cocktail (the Almost Famous) and tastings of various wines to pair with our courses, which included creamy foie gras, delicate ricotta dumplings, sweet lobster with earthy woodear mushrooms, and juicy duck-- all beautifully presented, delicious and layered with complex flavors. 

When I broke my wine glass, Emmanuel quickly whisked away the pieces of glass, along with the only partially eaten course in front of us and *replaced both at no additional cost*.  Though we declined dessert, Emmanuel presented us with a complimentary "Happy Anniversary" honey panna cotta with Moscato vinegar, airy and smooth. We ate every bite (and were tempted to lick the bowl clean) before stepping into the unseasonably warm November night already planning our next visit.

Best meal I've had in a while (and I was at Cote and i Sodi this month). Everything we had was outstanding:

Beef Tartare
Endive Salad
Ricotta Dumplings
Fried Arroz Negro
Duck
Iberico Pork

Service was great, as one would expect from a Michelin star restaurant. Bartender was cool, I forget his name. Place is a vibe.

Food was definitely on a Michelin star level but the service wasn't quite all that I expected. This is my third 1-star restaurant and I have to put it on the bottom just due to the service. No one was rude and the food didn't take too long, it was just that it wasn't as professional or classy as the other restaurants. We were often out of water, when they poured our water it splashed all over the table, and it was just very laid back inside. That's nothing bad for a normal restaurant but I expect more from a Michelin star restaurant. The restaurant itself is small and cute. It's well decorated and has 2 gender neutral bathrooms. The staff was all kind and helpful. The seating is a little squished but it's ok as long as the people next to you aren't loud. The endive/walnut/anchovy/cheese dish was absurdly good. It's like the weirdest exotic mini taco you've ever had and it hits your mouth with an explosion of delicious freshness, acidity, and savoriness. The lobster was a little underwhelming but still enjoyable. The arroz negro had a strong umami flavor that I really enjoyed but it barely had any squid. The chocolate cake was so rich and sweet and salty and delicious. I LOVED that cake. It was like a purely lava lava cake. Overall, delicious food, SLIGHTLY disappointed by the service but it was still very good.

giving it a five for outstanding of the best of its food and service. tartare abundance of flavor, trout mouthful of surprise, endive stacked atop its anchovies walnuts and mouthful of sharp cheese, chocolate dessert and panna cotta with vinegar honey). all are amazing surprises and creative. duck is fabulous too, but just a notch below the above. one true miss is the ricotta dumplings which were undercooked and gooey, not in an appetizing way. wines excellent, great service. i will check in again to see if dumplings are better executed. despite this technical error - it is a wonderful dining experience....
The endive salad was as memorable as it gets. The arroz negro and dumplings were good but endive salad was out of this world.

Food was really good, My favorite dish was the black rice. It doesn't look like much, but the flavors were fantastic and the chocolate cake was one of the best too!! I really enjoyed the flavor combinations of every dish.

The restaurant is small and the space between tables is very tight. Service was just a little slow.

Food 5/5
Service 4/5
Ambiance 4
Cleanliness 4/5
Value 4

Chocolate cake with whipped cream and panna cotta.... OMG. That's all. 

Dumplings are still my favorite thing on the savory side.

The cara cara shrimp chili dish was interesting. It was tasty. Couldn't tell if it was a dessert or a fruit salad.

TLDR: the fried arroz negro and the ricotta dumplings are two of the best dishes I've had this year. Restaurant is pretty cozy, so I don't recommend you come after shopping or with bags like we did.

Came here on a weekend for lunch with a friend. I actually knew nothing about Estela before coming and I was so pleasantly surprised by how good our lunch was! We ordered the three "signature dishes" as advertised by our waiter: the endive salad, arroz negro, and the ricotta dumplings. We added the duck as well. For dessert we got the panna cotta. 

The fried arroz negro and the ricotta dumplings - I still think about these dishes weeks later. Two of my favorite dishes this year. I would go back just for these. I love the crispy rice texture. The dumplings were so soft and unassumingly flavorful. Great. The salad felt endless. I personally thought there was too much cheese. The duck was also good, but not super memorable. 

The dessert was okay. Vinegar on panna cotta was not my favorite and I gave the rest to my friend after a few bites.

Service was friendly and attentive. Ambiance was casual, but you can dress up if you prefer. Restaurant is quite cozy!

When you're at a one Michelin star restaurant, you expect every dish to be delightful, surprising and fulfilling. Estela was none of these things. 

The endive salad was well-rounded, but felt like a mix of things put together with no real connection. Cheese, nuts, endive, olive oil lack any harmony. 

The truffle they used for the entree was of poor quality, and kind of ruins the dish. 

The black rice was pretty bad, tasting like overcooked bland rice. 

To add insult to injury, In the end the waiter was super rude. He rolled his eyes at us for a super simple request to get the bill and his face was filled with disdain. The space is also super cramped without and room to move your arms. Not sure how this place got its Michelin star, or has managed to keep it. I have serious questions with Michelin for allowing this place to hold a star.

Took my boyfriend here for his birthday dinner and we were blown away. Food was amazing, drinks were strong and great, and the ambiance is very chic and dark. Highlight was the squid ink calamari rice and beef tartare. 

Good people watching too, if you're into that.

My boyfriend and I are regulars here. This place has a well deserved Michelin star. Very cozy date night spot. Service is great, staff all have personalities of their own and are very personable. Great spot for wine as well. 
Iconic dishes:
Duck 
Foie gras 
Steak tartare 
Ricotta dumplings 
Black rice

I was happy to have snagged a reservation here and was looking forward to our early lunch. The space and the vibe are decidedly unfussy, but more informal than I expected. It wasn't bad at all. I just expected a little more attention from our server given the Michelin star rating. That being said, the food is excellent. I would give special kudos for the ricotta dumplings and the fried arroz negro. Also the lobster dish was fantastic. In a city with so many great dining options, Estela is a solid if not spectacular choice.

Always have a great meal here. Love the casual yet modern vibe. Food is always interesting and layered. The service is helpful and friendly without being annoying. Their cocktails are on point. Great spot for a date or to impress a visiting friend.

Ambiance was 10/10! Service was amazing and the food was so good and creative! Their menu is so diverse and the flavor combinations are unlike any I've tried before. Would highly recommend the Arroz Negro
Absolute perfection. This place was very atmospheric,  great lighting, super fun and attentive staff. Everything was delicious and portions were perfect for a small table of guests.

Estela

I spent $300 to walk out of the restaurant hungry. 

Estela is a small intimate restaurant. A great date spot. The service was attentive throughout our entire night and is the star of the experience. Unfortunately, much can't be said about the rest. 

Not much to comment on for the bread and olives, it's what you would expect. The oysters were fresh but tasted like drinking sea water, way too salty. The tartare is perhaps the best dish out of everything we got. The squid ink rice was nice as it at least helped fill the stomach rumbling, the foie gras was appetizing but an awkward experience due to it being soupy. Wrapped up with the steak, which was nice, but felt more like an appetizer than your main entree. 

Overall, I'm surprised by the high reviews this place received. I must be the only one crazy, but it's at 3* at best.

We went for dinner yesterday and was very much disappointed, especially by the service. 

We came to the restaurant earlier than our reservation and was told we can only be seated at the bar. When I asked them to let me know if a table becomes available, they responded that that's very unlikely. However, the host told the party behind us they have the option of the bar or a table but they would need it back by 1.45hrs. I think that the fact that we weren't even given that option was very rude. 

When we finally got seated, our waiter was rushed and when we asked about their recommendation, they only pointed things out without explaining what they were. I had to stop them from rushing away to ask what the dish was.

Lastly, when we moved from the different dishes, I was waiting for our plates and cutleries to be changed. However, that never happened and no one came by for me to ask. After a while, I gave up and continued to eat. To my surprise, when the table beside us was done with a dish, their plates and cutleries were changed. 

For the food itself, we ordered the tartare, the endive, and the ricotta dumplings. The tartare was good but not anything special. The bread was good though! The endive was too sour for my taste. The ricotta dumplings were the best out of the three. However, as it's quite rich, I think it's best to have just a little bit. 

Overall, for a Michelin restaurant, definitely very disappointing.

So delicious!

Service: Incredible. 

Drinks: Got the salted cucumber (non-alcoholic) drink and it was so refreshing. Also got the fake negroni (non-alcoholic) and that was the STAR!

Food:
1. Bread with butter: Bread is very soft and a good accompaniment for the rest of the meal
2. Celery salad: THIS IS A MUST GET! The celery, the herbs, the cheese and the dressing work so well together.
3. Ricotta dumplings: This was insane. The thinly cut mushrooms were so fun and delicious to eat. 
4. Pork: Wonderful! 

Dessert:
1. The chocolate cake is very worth it if you like lava cake. The whipped cream is quite heavy so if that is not your vibe then skip this!

We were so excited to try out Estela, but in the end we found it to be overhyped and underwhelming. We ordered the bread, the celery salad, the ricotta dumplings and the fried rice. All of the dishes were fine (the salad was the standout, while the rice was the too salty to finish). But for what we were paying for the meal, we expected much more. I will say that the service was really great. But we also found, to our surprise, that the ambiance wasn't that great. It's definitely a small restaurant, and we didn't have a lot of space. Overall, an experience that was just mediocre.

My husband and I were so excited to go here for a romantic dinner and were so disappointed. We came here 3 years ago and loved it. This time we had a reservation for an early dinner and were completely rushed by the waiter. He was constantly standing over us and pushing us to order and eat and get our plates cleared. They obviously had an agenda for us to eat and be gone in an hour. It absolutely killed the vibe. For $300+ this should not be the case. Would not recommend this place anymore sadly! Maybe it's better to eat at the bar...

Food met my expectations in terms of complex flavors, given that the restaurant has a Michelin star. I do wish the seating situation was a bit better because there are limited group tables and I wasn't able to add an additional spot to my 4 person reservation. The most notable dishes for me were the ricotta dumplings, the duck, and the lychee sorbet. Cocktails were also on point.

Yes the food is delicious but graciousness counts- a lot! This is not gracious nor lovely dining. The waiter tried to steer us away from what we ordered, we stuck to our guns and were happy. With one lousy olive in my martini I was informed that to have more they would need to charge us. When the sommelier was told about this he defended the position that " they were expensive olives".  That certainly set the mood...This is a restaurant for those who only care about the food- which admittedly is quite good. The staff, the experience, well imo a 5 out of 10. So go if you don't care...

Number 79 on the "top restaurants in the world" list, Estela lives up to its reputation with an exceptional dining experience. From the moment you walk in, the intimate atmosphere draws you in and sets the tone for a memorable meal. The menu is a delightful mix of classic dishes and new creations, with something to suit every palate.

The beef tartare with elderberries and sunchoke was a standout dish, beautifully presented and bursting with flavor. The combination of textures and flavors was perfectly balanced, making for a truly memorable dish. The endive with walnuts, anchovy, and ubriaco rosso was equally impressive, with the sweetness of the walnuts and the saltiness of the anchovy creating a delightful contrast.

The service was excellent with our server providing excellent suggestions throughout the evening. The often recommended fried arroz negro with squid and romesco was a real highlight. The crispy squid was perfectly cooked, and the romesco sauce added a wonderful depth of flavor to the dish. Finally, the crescent duck with ramps and yuca was another standout dish, with the tender duck meat beautifully complemented by the earthy flavors of the ramps and yuca.

Overall, Estela is a must-visit for anyone looking for an exceptional dining experience. The restaurant's Michelin star and other major accolades are well-deserved, and it's easy to see why Estela has become a New York City classic.

The establishment which I think is in an apartment building is small and loud. Not a great first date place since you can't hear anything but the food was spectacular! Dined alone at the bar and had their bestsellers -- the ricotta dumplings, the fried squid ink rice (similar to a paella but better, in my opinion), the scallops with sea urchin and dates, and the lychee sorbet with whipped yogurt for dessert. It sounds like a lot but if you go hungry, it's doable. The price point is fair and they have a great bar. The Michelin star so well deserved. Another trip back is warranted.

Man. This place was amazing. Place has good vibes, the music was 90s mixes and flowing. Ambiance was sexy and sleek. The food was incredible. The wine selection was impressive. We had a sommelier help us pick our ideal wine. Tapas style plating and served one at a time but paced out perfectly.  The ricotta dumplings were some of the best things I have ever put in my mouth before. Seriously outstanding. The beef tartare was exceptional with a thick crusted bread that complimented it perfectly.  Everything was on point. Everything was spot on. Ten out of ten. Will be back. Our server was amazing too!  Very helpful, welcoming and courteous (  short blonde hair, very sweet woman)

We came here for a relaxing Michelan Star level meal and found that service was super rushed and perfunctory, and the waiters insistent that we order more food than we wanted/needed (we did not need as many dishes as we ordered).  Some of the dishes were delicious and some we felt were over-hyped, but the attitude to get us out of our seat (clearly to make room for another patron) really ruined our enjoyment of the evening.

The overall experience started out a little weird - they had electrical issues and said they couldn't serve hot food, so we went to the bar for a drink and to figure out our plans for a new restaurant, but then they came back and said issues had been cleared up. 

Once we got seated, the drink service was very slow - took over 20 minutes for a glass of wine. After that, service picked up and overall it was a nice experience. The food was outstanding - dumplings are a must!

I was surprised to learn this place has a Michelin star. Definitely the bottom of the list relative to other Michelin star places I've been to. The food is good, but it's hard to enjoy it due to several factors: condescending waitstaff, loud pub ambience, cramming together of patrons. You can find good food at many places around nyc. The reason to go to a Michelin restaurant is for the experience, of which service is a key component. Borderline rude, and unprofessional service - they seem unhappy to be there and they do things like roll their eyes when discussing customers seated only a few feet away. The place feels like some bar but without any charm. Only the food is good but hard to actually enjoy the taste due to the stress of the atmosphere and poorly run front of house.

We went way too long between visits, but this was as great as ever. This time, we got bread with butter, olives, scallops, beef tartare, the endive salad, black rice, ricotta dumplings, the duck, and the chocolate cake. Every single dish was excellent, with all of them being strong re-order candidates. The thing is, I'd expect that every single dish is amazing, so I could see an argument for subbing out the dumplings for jamon, or something else for the tuna, etc. Regardless, an incredible restaurant and I'm so glad we finally made it back.

Amazing service, like exceptionally and noticeably good. Great food, short menu but everything is great. We had the cured tuna, gem salad, rice and duck. We both had wine and I liked mine quite a bit. It's a very small, intimate place, so probably best for groups of 2 or 4 max.

Friday night 9pm table. Service was prompt and attentive. We ordered wine by the glass, bread and butter (not complimentary) , side of olives, before our appetizers and mains arrived. Plates are tapas style and meant to be shared . The endive salad was fresh and vibrant, good balance of vinegary dressing and Waldorf salad-esque.  The gnocchi was shaved mushroom was light as air but without missing flavor. The arroz negro was a favorite, like a good paella with crunch of soccarat. The least favorite dish was foie gras wrapped in swiss shard.  Felt the flavors were muted and otherwise texture of the foie was mushy. We were comfortably full and skipped dessert. Check came in just shy of $300 all in. Wine was roughly $120 .

New York is seemingly run down. And this Michelin 1 star rated restaurant was the last place one would think they would find here. 
I reserved this online a month prior to visiting NYC from out of town. 

As we were walking up we heard this middle aged whit guy screaming at the top of his lungs at a 'wife'? It was like something out of the movies. He was berating her while making claims that his drinks with another lady was all just friends...Anyhoo...nice intro to the restaurant.

Once inside were could not hear the drama outside as the restaurant.

We were promptly seated and our waiter immediately introduced himself and let us settle. He came back and explained that this was tapas style and meant to be shared. He suggested about 2 plates per person. The service was impeccable and very prompt. They literally picked up each dish you used previously so you had a clean plate for your next entree. That was a lot of work for the servers.

The meal was outstanding. The scallops were served first and hands down my favorite! The lemon inspired flavoring was amazing. The beef tartare was also delish and had a little zip. The foie gras was melt in your mouth delectable. I'd say the two dishes that I selected ended up disappointing me. The Tilefish was really just white fish and the flavor it picked to wasn't so inspiring. The seaweed was too over bearing and the iberico was just ok. One thing I forgot to take a photo of was the squash! While it looked uninspiring, it was amazing!!! It was fresh raw zucchinis with delicious tangy lemon sauce.

During the course of our 2 hours the place became very lively (5:45-8:45). Clearly a popular place!

This place rocked my socks in a way that I did not even realize possible. The outside and exterior or nothing to write home about it's in sort of a grimy grungy part of New York. Even the interior when walking in the restaurant is pretty small. The atmosphere is not particularly amazing or exciting so I guess my expectations were low. 

We ordered a bunch of small plates, which seem to be the general theme. We were three people and sharing. once the food started to come out, I realized how good this place was. 

The biggest standouts had to be the endive salad, the arroz negra, and the ricotta dumplings. These were flavor and textural explosions. I'm not even kidding, I think about this endive salad every day. 
I don't even like endives. But it had crispy caramelized anchovies, which sounds gross, but it was  this amazing flavor combination. Everything just had the perfect amount of balance. The ricotta dumplings were all so soft and pillowy in this way that I totally did not expect. 

It was also our friends birthday, so they catered to us with Prosecco and a dessert. This was such an amazing experience, and a great surprise, considering I didn't think this would be anything to write home about. And underrated find in New York - it should be on more lists and more people should be talking about it.

Amazing experience. We were referred by an acquaintance who lives locally. The food was unique and creative. The host went the extra mile to accommodate us and even checked in on us during the meal. Our waiter was kind, informative and attentive and the cleanup between courses was crazy quick. My wife and I each had our preferred dishes, and nothing was leftover. The place has energy and is loud but we were still able to talk, unlike at most of our usual home San Francisco spots. We'll be back for sure. Sadly, I don't recall names, but we were there on 6/26.
JH
The food and service were incredible.  Excellent wine suggestions.  Squash and endive courses were immaculate.

Estela is a great upscale restaurant with a more casual vibe. One thing I will note is that their benches are a bit higher than normal chairs so my legs felt a bit weird during the meal. 

The service is incredible and very attentive. I highly recommend ordering the bread - it is extremely fluffy and pairs perfectly with the butter. 

My favorite thing I ate was the black rice - it was like the paella I've eaten in Barcelona! The endive salad was crispy and refreshing. The ricotta dumplings were good, but the texture was bit odd. It was soft all around but the flavor was definitely there.

The food is extraordinary, the staff is great. We've been there several times. But the noise level-ugh. I don't  eT out to hear the people next to me scream at each other. Go before 6 and it's a perfect evening.

The food was good but I was expecting more from reading all the reviews online. The only dish that wow-ed me was the lobster. I came here for brunch and felt like the waiters were rushing us to finish (perhaps to take their break?). At one point I was holding an oyster getting ready to shuck and the server put a dirty plate that he just collected from the table next to us in front of me, signalling me to put the oyster shell on the dirty plate. Was definitely an unpleasant experience to shuck an oyster with a strangers dirty dishes in my face. Not sure how this place has a Michelin star because that type of service wouldn't even be acceptable at a non star restaurant.

This place was good but I'm not sure if I would go back again

The dumplings were in a mushroom sauce and if you not a huge fan of mushrooms, don't get this dish 
The arroz negro is one of their signature dish and I wasn't a fan. 
Endive. Wasn't memorable 
Pork was pretty decent!

I've been searching for a new favorite brunch spot ever since my beloved Maison Premiere stopped doing real brunch (sob). It's harder than you'd think to find a truly unique, creative brunch menu--and no, egg dishes don't even come close to cutting it. 

So when my Yelp bestie since 2011, Kelsey C., was in town for a visit and picked this spot as our last meal together, I figured it had to be quality. I didn't count on it being the best brunch I've had in NYC since, well, Maison Premiere back when they still did leeks and potatoes. 

Oh. My. Flippin'. Ganesh.

I have a new favorite brunch place!!! 

Creative? Check. 
Delicious? Duh.
Not generic and egg-based? Yuppers.

- Oysters with Yuzu Kosho Mignonette: Pungent and tangy, just how I like my mollusks

- Cured Tuna with Black Pil Pil and Ponzu: There are no words to describe the deliciousness of this dish. Seriously. No words. Just cut, spread and eat with bread. Allow your foodgasmic moans to fill the restaurant. This dish. This dish is what all brunch should be.

- Endive with Walnuts, Anchovhy and Ubriaco Rosso: Crunchy, zesty and tangy. The kind of refreshing that you crave on a hot summer afternoon. Uevos could never.

- Lobster with Wood Ears and Grapes: Perfectly cooked and crunchy. Whoever invented this knows their textures.

- Fried Arroz Negro, Squid and Romesco: Crisp where needed, soft where needed, and just the perfect mix of sea brine.

- Wagyu Steak with Beets and Belper Knolle: Perfectly seared beef, perfect soft beets, and perfectly crunchy swiss chard. Wins all around.

Throw in the friendly, attentive service that never let up--even when they got insanely busy an hour after we arrived--and you have a recipe for brunch perfection. The prices are by no means cheap, but the delectable farm-to-table freshness makes it worth every penny.

My last meal in New York, and I managed to squeeze in one more Michelin star. Estela, unlike most of its fine dining counterparts, knows how to do a good lunch. 

Same stuff, smaller menu, so you get a few of the highlights that put this place on the World 50 Best map.
Immediately these buttery Oysters will wow, and the Tuna is a cured-meat masterpiece. Smear on the pil pil, which gives it so much depth.
This Endive looks like just a salad, but load up those boats with walnuts, little anchovy bits and ubriaco rosso cheese, and it is transcendental.
Warm, tender Lobster lays in a sauce that lingers with an herby high. Woodears are a brilliantly unexpected addition, and the texture adds magic to the lobster and grapes. 
Fried Arroz Negro is beautiful, and it's like the best part of paella - all-around crust flavored with squid. 
The Wagyu Steak is their most traditional dish, two perfect cuts of a perfect cut of meat. I don't need the veg, but the beets are lovely. 

Estela. Elegant, bold, yet polished flavors. I would come back to NYC again JUST to have lunch at Estela.

I liked this place, but my boyfriend didn't. 

For some reason, many of their dishes leaned on the sour lemony side? Not bad tasting it's got a lemony zesty tangy bite but def can't have too much. At one point I had to stop eating a dish (Endive Walnut Anchovy) halfway because it was hurting my tongue (lots of vinegar?). Loved the flavor combo tho.

I wish their dishes had more flavor besides sour, like more savory or umami. The arroz, like many paellas tbh, barely tasted like anything. I liked the texture tho it was crispy on the edges contrasted well with the seafood. 

Also very crowded and loud. I like the design but we were very cramped and hard to hear each other so just okay for atmosphere. 

Service was great - the waitress was kind and knowledgeable about all the ingredients of each dish.

The second menu I tried wasn't as amazing as the first one. However, the ambiance of this place is still perfect. The scallops with peaches were the best bite of the whole meal, bar none. The summer squash with pine nuts and miso was also excellent. I didn't like the cured tuna with black pil pil, the foie gras grilled in grape leaf, or the hamachi.

Food is fantastic (the tuna, omg) and it's an inviting setting, but the service was lacking. Stuck-up, pushy waitstaff seemed less interested in hearing what we wanted and more interested in rushing us through our meal to clear the table.

Food 7/10
We came right when it opened for lunch. I think they are probably a bit overhyped. The food is good but it isn't worth all the rave reviews I hear from the people around me. My favorite was probably the squid ink rice and the free bread LOL. The tuna was fresh, but the ricotta dumplings were way too creamy and rich, my lactose intolerance was quaking. I don't think I could justify the price, so it is more of a special occasion kind of spot. 

Atmosphere 8/10
Cute interior, natural lighting and natural wooden furniture. Seats are slightly uncomfortable because it's all wood haha 

Service 9/10
Super friendly service.

Icy cold service.  Told everything's shared and we had to order 7-10 dishes for 4 people and the kitchen would just send it out as they were ready.  So for $700, we got teeny small plates at random times and not even a single smile.  Drinks were outrageously expensive.  Room was pleasantly humble and outrageously loud.  Food good,   But not insane for the price.  Celery salad...good but not for nearly $20 and teeny.  Micro wagu.  Just overall seems like a ripoff for the experience.  Shout out to management... A friendly face goes a long way with this style of service, food and price point.  Attitude only works in the most exquisite of spots and this place is not that.

Superrrrr expensive ong  and the options sre not for the average Joe. I'll give 3 stars for letting us leave without ordering/paying. I would try again if my bank account bounces back from this recession
Amazing food, relaxed atmosphere. You order small plates to share and enjoy the endives with walnuts or the ricotta dumplings that were delicious!

Been wanting to come here for awhile given all the accolades they've gotten. The food absolutely did NOT disappoint & the ambiance, was super cozy and would recommend for date night. However, I was incredibly disappointed by the service we got hence the 1 star knocked off. The waiter we had was a bit belligerent, we barely sat down and was repeatedly rushed to order drinks. We were also being pushed to order more dishes than we wanted and felt vindicated in ordering just enough.

One of my NYC favs. Estela is where you should be if you want to be impressed  They are so good at making minimalist dishes that taste effortlessly refined. The ingredients shine through, and while some remain invisible to the eye, they all come alive in your mouth. At a higher price point but worth it! Only con is that the tables are very close together and it gets kinda loud.

This endive dish is the highlight of my life I had my first endive here and obsessed since. You're presented with a beautiful stack of leaves, that reveals a mixture of walnuts, ubriaco rosso (firm cheese), and sourdough bread. Slight hints of anchovy and orange brings out the fresh bitterness of the endives and the nutty richness of the crumble. It's a lightbulb moment in your mouth 

The fried arroz negro is packed with flavor and while you can't see at first, but there are hazelnuts, crispy rice, and super tender squid mixed in. I love how the textures keep you entertained and the savory umami lingering along! Duck is the more predictable option and while cooked perfectly, lacks surprise.

Don't leave without getting the chocolate cake. It comes out looking like a bowl of just cream. This 3:1 ratio is ideal  The cream is dreamy thick without the oily aftertaste, and the dainty sweetness is a wonderful complement to the rich chocolate foundation. Our table of 2 wiped all this clean so if you need more, add the beef tartare with sunchoke and ricotta dumplings. Both are signatures for a reason (and IF you see the burrata, that needs to be on your table). 

 Endive with walnuts $26*
 Fried arroz negro with squid $31*
 Duck with beets $45
 Chocolate cake with whipped cream $14*

뉴욕에서 정말 세련된 식사를 하고 싶다면 꼭 추천하는 Estela  미니멀한 디쉬에서 엄청난 깊이와 예상치 못한 조합을 맛볼수있다. 엔다이브는 필수 주문! 이쁘게 쌓아올린 야채로 안에있는 호두, 치즈, 빵을 떠먹는다. 소스의 앤초비의 짠맛과 오렌지의 상큼함이 상추의 씁쓸함과 너무나 멋스럽게 어우러짐. 디저트는 생크림을 가득 올린 초콜릿 케이크 강추  3:1 비율로 크림만 먹어도 담백할 정도로 엄청 깔끔하다. 갈때마다 요 두가지는 꼭 시키고 나머지는 그날 끌리는데로 주문하면 무조건 성공이지만.... 육류보다는 해산물 디쉬에서 셰프님 특유의 색갈이 더 잘 느껴진다고 생각됨  단점은 가격대비 양이 적고 테이블이 다다닥 붙여져 시끄러움.

My humble verdict is: Estela deserves their Michelin star!

Love the vibes of this place. It's unassuming and cozy, and the food is phenomenal! Pricey, yes, but the tasty food and great service more than justify it. The dishes are a bit bigger than tapas, and meant to be shared. Don't miss the black rice and the ricotta dumplings!! They also have a short but varied cocktail list - the Tomato Never Dies is smooth and savory, and unlike anything I've ever had before!

I have been there twice and this has been my best meal of 2023. 
The place is packed but, if you can get a spot, it's worth it. Good products beautifully prepared. Sounds like a simple thing but it's difficult to get it right and, at Estela, they definitely do.

their fried arroz negro is a must. so many flavors in it and i enjoyed the hint of lemon zest they put on top of it. the texture is also nice because they add crunchy walnuts in them. also tried their ricotta dumpling and their chocolate cake for dessert. i thought they were just okay imo.

Came here for a birthday dinner with the husband and parents with a reservation so did not have to wait before getting seated. Tried to make reservation about 2 weeks ahead and only the unpopular times were left, so make yours early! The service was good, people were nice. It was a bit crowded environment for me, but we were able to get one of the bigger tables in the back so this was not so much of a problem. The food was amazing! Each dish had such unique mixture of flavors that I have not had anywhere else and the balance was so great! The portions were small, definitely tapas style and meant to be shared. Honestly everything I ate just blew me away, the Michelin star is very well deserved. Did not feel the price was too much for the food, would absolutely come again!

About a 1-1.5: We came to check out Estela for lunch as a group.

The following was ordered to be shared between us all to sample:
+Sourdough miche with butter
+marinated olives
+Charcuterie
+Cured trout with bergamot and dashi
+Grilled lobster with woodears and grapes
+Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo

Unfortunately, we weren't fans of the dishes we had ordered, as what was presented didn't seem to relate to what was stated on the menu.  The food was underseasoned or super bland, and not at all memorable.

Service was more on the pretentious category.

No dice, Estela.

+pretentious service
+poorly represented food

Really just an amazing restaurant that I cannot believe I have never heard about given how close it was to me. The downside is that there are only 2-3 vegetarian options on the menu. The upside is that they were absolutely marvelous. Starting with the persimmon salad, even if you don't think you like this fruit - get it. It's so elegant and the flavors of the pine nuts mesh so well with the fruits & veggies. Really an outstanding dish. And the ricotta dumplings were very good even if the presentation is a bit mixed, with these beautiful cheese "slices" on top but the sauce looking somewhat mid. The kicker was the chocolate cake - GET IT. This is the best dessert I've had in NYC without a doubt, and the creativity of the decadent chocolate covered in a soft cream to where you cannot even see the cake, this was an A+ presentation. The space is kind of interesting as it just feels like the first floor of a SoHo walkup, but interior vibe was nice and the service was very friendly. Would recommend to any of my friends in a heartbeat, and caveat to any vegetarians who may be averse - give it a shot!

Estela was on my list for a while so I was really looking forward to this meal. I don't understand the hype and was pretty disappointed. We ordered all the heavy hitters - steak tartar, endive salad, fried arroz negro, and the ricotta dumplings. Everything was overly salty (endive salad, arroz negro especially) and just didn't seem like it warranted the price or the star? Atmosphere was lively and loud, seating was cramped - definitely a New York City cool crowd vibe.

The fried arroz negro was the saltiest, and there were probably two single tips of squid tentacles hidden in there. 

My least favorite, and unfortunately the last thing that came was the dumplings - it's just...airy dough sitting in mushroom water topped with shaved raw white button mushrooms. I guess it might just be a preference of taste thing? But ending the meal on that note just made me want to leave so bad. Sorry! Can't get on board with this one.

TLDR: A Michelin restaurant thats worth the hype! 

I recently had the pleasure of dining at Estela in NYC, and it was an absolute culinary delight! The squid ink risotto stole the show with its crispy texture and burst of flavors. The persimmon salad was incredibly fresh, and the wagyu steak was nothing short of insanely flavorful and delicious.

To top off the meal, the chocolate lava cake with black sesame dessert was a revelation! It's hands down the best dessert I've had in NYC, offering insane flavors and depth. The combination of black sesame, oozing lava cake chocolate base, and the perfect cream on top created a dessert masterpiece.

Every star in this review is for their food. We took our server's recommendation and shared 4-6 plates, ranked below for balance of flavor and textured mouthfeels. 

Fried arroz negro with squid and romesco - an extremely satisfying bite with multiple forms of crunch coming from the rice and the nuts of the romesco.

Grilled Lobster with woodear mushrooms and grapes - the smokiness of the lobster really permeated each chewy ear. I'm not a fan of lobster at all, but I could eat this preparation any day!

Cured trout with bergamot and dashi - the little beads provided much appreciated bursts of brine.

Marinated olives -  the twist of grapefruit rind was not only a great palate cleanser, but an excellent pregame choice with drinks.

Sourdough miche with butter - the rustic crust is what bread cravings are made of.

Kudos to the bartenders for their Halo Spritz cocktail - it was unbelievably refreshing despite its complexity. 

Now for the ambiance. While our corner table felt "cozy" at first tucked away from the main dining room, it became "the spot" for people to wait for the rest of their party to arrive. We soon ran out of room to be able to get up or lift a drink without elbowing someone accidentally. That was our cue to get the check and go.

Alas, even a Michelin star worthy meal can't stop NYC from doing what it does on a Friday night.

The food was incredible. Everything we got was amazing and flavorful. I really liked the foie gras. I've never seen seared foie gras wrapped in grape leaves. Beef tartar was unique and creative. The oysters tasted super refreshing and the pork had really good seasoning. Desserts were great too. Lychee sorbet was particularly impressive. Our drinks were just okay though. Hard to pick cocktails from the menu that we typically like. The reasons why I gave 4 stars are mostly service and how crowded the restaurant was. Our waiter was pretty cold. And the restaurant was small and all the tables were squeezed into it. My friend couldn't get out of her seat without moving the table.

I will never forget the first time I fell in love with endives. Thank you, Estela. Maybe it was the sommelier's expansive knowledge and the sincere customer service. Or was it the beautiful summer day and good company that possessed me to order what seemed like a silly little lettuce like thing. Estela knows endives.

This post is long. Only read if you want an in-depth analysis of the food, service, and ambiance at Estela. 

Summary: Good ambiance. Don't go for a reservation after 10pm because the staff is checked out and you won't get a Michelin Star experience. Flavor pairings seemed basic compared to other Michelin one star restaurants. 

Ambiance: Great. Dark & candlelit. Just what I want on a night out. 5 stars to this category. 

Service: Apparently good service stops at 10pm because the staff couldn't have cared about us less. We were never checked in on, only visited to order and receive food. To be fair, we got a 10:15pm reservation. It may have been our fault for eating dinner so late. At a regular restaurant I would have dismissed this poor late-night service, but at a Michelin star my expectation is that the service should be excellent throughout the whole evening. 

Food: No Wow! factor. Having been to more than 20 Michelin star restaurants from around the world (yes even Mario is jealous about how many stars I've collected), this is the first one that hasn't served a dish that has wowed me. At every other Michelin star, there is always a dish that makes me think "Wow, I have never tried anything like that before, and I could eat that forever." This one didn't only fail to do that, but disappointed me with their basic flavor pairings.  

We ordered 5 dishes: the olives marinated in oil, the beef tartare, the arroz negro, the ricotta dumplings, and the wagyu steak. Out of these dishes, 3 were okay, and 2 were disappointing. 

Highlight: arroz negro. Reminded me of Spanish paella. Good if you like paella with a crunch. Lowlight: ricotta dumplings. Buy Sargento's mozarella string cheese at the local supermarket and put it in the microwave for 15 seconds for the same effect. 

The wagyu and olives were good. Good not great. What makes these dishes stand out from other wagyu and olive dishes? I am still asking myself that question because nothing about them was unique. 

The beef tartare. Could have infiltrated a grouping of bruschetta and gone unnoticed. The beef was cut very thick, and it was overpowered by the capers and chopped onion. This dish would have deserved the lowlight if the dumplings didn't taste like string cheese. 

The ricotta dumplings. The mushroom slice on top was a cool addition aesthetically, but it did not add to the taste of the dish. This dish reminded me of my 10-year-old self grabbing a handful of string cheeses from the fridge. Estela, if that is what you were going for, you aced it! If not, it may help to decrease the size of the balls of cheese and pair them with stronger flavors. 

Overall, 3/5 stars is appropriate. I wouldn't recommend this restaurant to a friend, but I would accompany my friends to Estela if they wanted to go as a social occassion. However, I would eat beforehand.

Loved this restaurant! Every dish was delicious and surprising. The small plates allow lots of tasting even for two people.  *Spoiler alert* - if you keep reading this review the surprises won't be quite as surprising...

We started with the scallops with brown butter and golden potatoes which was presented as a perfect glossy hemisphere of... something. It turn out the hemisphere was a hyper-smooth potato puree that covered fairly raw scallops finished as a kind of ceviche in light lemon juice. The interplay of rich brown butter and  bright lemon was a unique and yummy.

Next up was the endive with walnuts, anchovy, and ubriaco rosso that continued the "surprise" theme. The again lemony endive completely covered the walnuts and 'chovies so that it initially looked like a plate of endive leaves. The bottom layer was rich and crunchy so that a bite would combine with the endive for a welcome and juicy "pop" in one's mouth.

Our third dish was the star of the evening: fried arroz negro, squid, and romesco. This is essentially the bottom crunchy part of properly cooked paella using black rice. Wow - filling, satisfying, tremendously delicious. If you like paella don't skip this one.

Our entrée was Berkshire pork with market greens and black truffles. A satisfying and filling end to a great meal.

Our server was charming, knowledgeable about both the dishes and the right wine(s) to pair with and efficient. You could not ask for better service.

A little difficult to find, you should make the effort to go to Estela. We're glad we did. Two thumbs up.

Had the most fantastic meal- scallop, arroz negro, steak, and the sweet potato dessert were standouts. Phoebe was amazing and answered every one of our questions, flawless service. My tiny little water glass was constantly full thanks to an incredible service team! Literally made a reservation for later this week to try the rest of the menu while we were sat. Perfect meal, perfect space, perfect team, no notes.

10 out of 10. The food, service, and ambiance were all spot on. Everything pictured below was amazing. We also had, not pictured, the Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino Sardo which were one of my favorites. The Endive salad was my number 1 favorite dish of the day. The Charcuterie and the sourdough bread , though basic sounding, really was delicious as well. The Executive Chef stopped at our table to see how we liked everything and that was such a pleasant personal touch. 

We tried both the Chocolate cake and the Panna Cotta and both were amazing as well. Really great experience and will definitley be back.

always a favorite! endive salad, dumplings and arroz are classics but has the duck this time and it was one of the best best duck dishes i've had. so good will always come back when
here

Estela is probably my favorite "format" restaurant. I feel like their format was more prevalent in the aughts. But I am SO grateful that they have stuck to it. You arrive with your party and they provide you a menu with a listing of items from lightest to heaviest (as in oysters at the top and duck breast or wagyu steak at the bottom).  

If you arrive with two people, they recommend four to six dishes, with a party of four, maybe eight to nine dishes.  Keep in mind, each dish is meant to be shared and is timed perfectly to be delivered one at a time with careful attention paid to when your table appears ready for the next dish. THIS is the feature that makes the meal a great place to meet a friend to catch up over a bottle of wine and a wind range of delicious tastes to both indulge in and discuss (if you're into that).  

I have been going for years, typically with only one other person. However, for my birthday this year, my 10 and 12 year old kids asked that I take them to my "favorite restaurant that I always go to with my friends". I believed they were ready, and they WERE. They were so excited to try this "legendary" place that I always left them home to go to. 

The menu often changes but the two main stays that never seem to change are the beef tartare with crispy sunchokes and the endive leaves, drizzled with olive oil and served with finely chopped candied walnuts, anchovies and "ubriaco rosso" cheese (basically a pecorino romano aged in wine) -- my FAVORITE thing on the menu. 

There is a reason the two dishes mentioned above are mainstays.  They are the best, in my opinion. I have never had a bad dish at Estela.  We always get the oysters of the moment, usually ricotta gnocchi in a mushroom broth perfection. As far as the proteins go, those seem to change the most often. Last night we had the Mackeral with seaweed, favas and avocado the the wagyu with brussle sprouts and tallegio.  

Everything was excellent. I stand by my original assessment that the best way to enjoy this restaurant is with one of your best friends to share a bottle of wine as they deliver one small plate at a time. The format is perfection for that particular scenario, though my kids did rave about the beef tartare, the endive and the wagyu.  

Love You, Estela.

Our brunch on Sunday was one of the most enjoyable meals that I've had in NY. Absolutely everything was first rate: from the staff and service, to the food, to the pacing of our meal, and our cocktails. 

We arrived and were escorted to our table in the back. We were a party of 6 and there's a nice table for this many people. We arrived soon after opening and the restaurant was relatively empty. Within a short time every table was taken but the sound level was comfortable for conversation. We were near the rest room but weren't bothered by the line. Our sever Erik was very helpful. He suggested the prix fixe menu and that's what we chose. There were food sensitivities and the chef worked to accommodate these needs. The prix fixe comes with 3 cold and 3 warm dishes along with dessert. Our cold dishes were the oysters, scallops and endives. The warm dishes were the fried arroz (very much like paella), crescent duck and grilled lobster. Each offering was beautifully presented, distinct in flavor and so very well seasoned. There are reviews from Dan P and Julia F where they describe the dishes, so I won't repeat their wonderful descriptions. Each dish had its very own personality. Our dessert was (flourless) chocolate cake. The chocolate flavor was extraordinary and the whipped cream was so light, it complemented the cake perfectly. 

This is not an inexpensive restaurant. But for extraordinary food and drink, wonderful staff and a fantastic experience, the price was very reasonable.

Estela is all around a very balanced restaurant: good food, good atmosphere, and good staff. I would highly recommend the arroz and the endive salad. We also enjoyed the scallop (looks odd but works)! Kolrabi was good, but not a must. Skip the bread. 

We got a table but honestly I would've enjoyed sitting at the bar. Definitely not a res I'd die to get. Can probably just walk in. I'd like to go back to try their cocktails and dessert.

On my way to try out all 100 restaurants in the NYT lists, I visited Estela for lunch. Unfortunately, it didn't meet the high expectations I had... The service was great and the food was generally well cooked. The scallops were phenomenal. But overall the other dishes were a bit unimpressive and not as creative as I expected.

Came for a special occasion and was not disappointed. We sat at the bar initially as we were early for the reservation. There was some disconnect amongst the hostesses about how/when to transfer to a table.

- Started with the beef tartare. This was an excellent flavor-profile and texture. We debated ordering bread but luckily this came with it, as a tip!
- It seems like every single table orders the endive dish. The aesthetic is super interesting. It's a skosh difficult to eat but there was a good amount of the filling below the endives themselves.
- The crab dish with the celeriac was a highlight of the night. We almost didn't get this but it was just so perfectly executed so highly recommend.
- Fried arroz negro with the squid was the other highlight. The fried-ness of this was perfect. The squid doesn't stand-out but I truly didn't mind.
- The ricotta dumplings were fine. Essentially just a lump of ricotta formed into a dumpling. Probably could skip next time.
- The wagyu steak was well-executed. I appreciated the potato puree it came with and the cooking of the steak was exactly what I wanted.

The biggest downfall of the meal, however, is the space itself. There are just too many tables packed into the space and it is extraordinarily loud, both from the conversations and the music. The service is great but the servers are truly battling amongst themselves for traffic.

A singular experience. Everything is delicious and original. If it's your first time, ask for guidance and get the "classic" items including the endive salad and the crab. 

The drinks and wine list are really interesting and well chosen. 

I've noticed people complaining about the noise or tight space, but those are not unusual for Manhattan and we didn't find them particularly bad anyway. Relax, you will get accustomed to it.

The only negative point is that by this point in the restaurant's successful run,  the staff are somewhat jaded, which is understandable. Smiles are in short supply. We ate at the bar and the bartender, while highly skilled, was brusque, bordering on rude. She also cleared our cocktails before we'd finished them--repeatedly.

The spot: The restaurant is on the smaller side. As a party of two, we were seated in a cozy little nook in the back of the restaurant. Larger groups were seated in the narrow space between us and the bar seating at the front. 

The drinks: The cocktail program here is great and perhaps even rivals the food. I tried the Halo Spritz, an elevated spritz comprising Tximista Blanco, Sirene Canto Amaro, lemon, salted lime, and cava, and the Tomato Never Dies (cute), a martini riff that reminds one of a caprese in beverage form. I think the spritz, with its lively Spanish vermouth, citrus notes, and depth of flavor, was actually my favorite, but the martini was so refreshing and had really strong basil notes. The only thing that would've made this better would've been a mozzarella and tomato skewer garnish. 

The food: If you're a sourdough lover, definitely start your meal with the delicious bread. It's a filling option and only $5 and the butter is heavenly. 

As we were first-timers at Estela, we largely stuck with their classic dishes, including the endive salad, fried arroz negro, and ricotta dumplings. We got one rotating dish, the Crab (celeriac and dulse) which was fantastic in its simplicity. I mostly just tasted sweet, fresh crab and butter, and honestly that was perfect. I only wished that the dish was a bit larger. 

The endive salad was presented as a little foraging adventure, with the vinegar-dressed endives on top of a bed of ubriaco rosso (cheese), walnuts, and anchovies. It was great and not a light salad, but pricey at $28.

Ricotta dumplings were also very good; the best part was the umami-bomb mushroom broth. This was a hearty dish. 

The fried arroz negro, served with squid and romesco*, was a delightful surprise for us. We don't always automatically go for dishes dressed in squid ink, but this was very good. I loved the crispy element to the rice, seafood-flecked bites, and the lively but delicate savory sauce that pulled it all together. 

Finally, we saved a bit of room for dessert and tried the panna cotta. Good but not my favorite version, and I wouldn't probably try a different sweet to end our meal next time.

Popped in for a spur the moment dinner date at 9:30 on Wednesday, only waited for 15 minutes for the table.

Service was amazing, really friendly waiter, knowledgeable, gave great suggestions. Perhaps tried to upsell us more food than we needed but I would never fault someone for that. 

Cocktails were DELISH, I would have loved to try more but I didn't wanna get too messy haha. 

Now onto the FOOD! 

We sprang for the Sourdough with butter. Its always nice to start the meal that way but kind feels like it should be free. Both bread and butter were delicious. 

We started with a Scallop with Green Tomato and basil dish that was so fresh and light, perfect summer appetizer. The scallops are kind of hidden by the tomato slices, I would reverse that so they are on top but I wont start splitting hairs over presentation. 

We also got the Shepherd's Hope, which was a super fresh pea salad type thing with a really bright dressing. highly recommend this OR the Scallop dish but they sort of do the same thing so wouldn't recommend getting them both. 

We capped off appetizers with Oysters. They were amazing but having grown up on the New England coast i think I prefer oysters fresh with  just a hint of lemon. It was fun to indulge for a special occasion but wouldn't order them again at $5 a pop. 

We capped off the meal splitting the Wagyu Steak. WOW, perfectly cooked with the most amazing sesame bearnaise. I found the turnip side a little blah, didn't feel additive. But I honestly didn't care, the steak/bearnaise combo was INCREDIBLE.

I will definitely be back and would recommend this place for a perfect date or special occasion dinner.

What a great delight and surprise. Waitress even went thru menu when I say I had seafood allergies and highlighted what we should order. 

Started with the celery tonic mock-tail. Heavenly. Got a second one later in the meal. 8/10

Beef tartar was a really great beginning to the meal. Bread was a little tough but did its job. 6/10

Endive salad had such a wonderful brightness to it. Huge fan. 7/10

Ricotta Dumplings with mushrooms was a great warm up to the main entree. 6/10

Wagyu Beef with Sesame dressing. Whoa. 9/10

Finishes off the night with the Panna Cotta 9/10 and Chocolate Cake 7/10. Wonderful finish.

Wait staff was wonderful, 9/10

Ambiance, we got there at 5:30pm. One table was already seated. Had a good 30 minutes before it got crowded where the conversations needed repeated due to the loud noise. 6/10

Price point: $130/per person (tip not included)

Definitely would come back.

Honestly can't say enough good things about Estela.  I've yet to have a bad meal or bad dish here.  I dined here 2 days ago and decided to only eat pescatarian friendly dishes.  Usually I go all in on meat dishes.  I ended up being just as happy.  The oyster presentation was good (but those are hard to screw up).  The tuna tartar was extremely tasty.  The black rice with crab has a wonderful flavor.  The ricotta dumplings were light and mouth watering.  What I wasn't expecting was how good the desert was.  I ordered the pana cotta.  It had honey, sea salt, and perhaps vinegar.  The flavors worked exceptionally well with the super creamy pana cotta.  

If you can't tell, I'm officially a fanboy for Estela.  I probably should eat at some other restaurants when I'm in Ny, but it's hard not to come to this little charming spot when I stay in the lower east side.

This was an absolutely first rate dinning experience. Well travelled friends from Australia came to town and invited us. I hadn't heard of it before but the menu looked good and not crazy expensive, however we had to go super early to get a table - usually a good sign. 

The place was empty when we arrived at opening and filled up completely in about 15 minutes. Our server was on top form the entire time. Multiple dietary restrictions emerged, so she went into the kitchen and marked up the menu by hand, tailoring the menu for us in a flash. Never seen anything like it. 

Plan to share everything and get as many dishes as you can. We did 8 items for 4 people including standouts such as scallops, oysters, tartare, dumplings, and wagyu, plus a beautiful chocolate dessert. 

I left feeling like I had learned something new about food in New York, finally in the know, part of those who have been... and you should too. Enjoy!
The food and service were superb! We celebrated our anniversary and everything we had was exquisite. Our favorite was the scallops.

Food was good but the pacing of the meal was weird. The food came out at a sporadic yet glacial pace.

Service was nice. Place was too loud to have a conversation. A real shame.

Amazing restaurant! We had the beef tartare, endive salad, crab, venison, and ricotta dumplings, along with the chocolate cake for dessert. The crab was the star of the meal and you should absolutely order it if it is on the menu when you go! The only dish we weren't super impressed by was the venison, but it did not hinder giving this place 5 stars. This is absolutely worth going to!

10/10 would go again, if only reservations were easier! Makes perfect sense why they aren't though. I didn't even know I liked endives... everything about the visit was great. Service was attentive, ambiance was cute/dimly lit (popular date night it seems), and everything we ate was delicious. My favorites were the scallops, endive salad and the panna cotta. The cured salmon was good and so was the pork, but not as memorable as the other dishes in my opinion.

Not a good place to eat if you have food allergies.  We had a private work event and they didn't inform us that the endive cups they served contained nuts, and it was just listed as "endive cups" without any other ingredients on the menu.  My friend who is very allergic to tree nuts had some and ended up having to go to the emergency room because of the allergic reaction.  I understand the restaurant was informed that someone in our party had a nut allergy.  The restaurant said that they were making a plate without nuts but somehow it got mixed up - just sounds very concerning.  Thankfully my friend seems to be okay now after having an epipen administered at the ER but it's a bad mixup and there could have been serious consequences.

We were able to squeeze in with a last-minute reservation for two.

We had the sourdough miche with butter, the scallops with golden potato and brown butter, endive with walnuts, anchovy, and ubriaco rosso, and finally the ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino sardo.

The highlight was the ricotta dumplings. They were light and creamy and it really let the mushrooms shine. I'm not the biggest mushroom fan, and I would say this really changed my perspective on mushrooms. The mushrooms were light and earthy and when paired in flavor with the ricotta, it was reminiscent of a fine rind on a soft cheese.

I was also really excited to try the endive, but ultimately this dish packed too big of a punch. It has very strong flavors and textures, but I felt that the bitterness of the endive wasn't balanced with enough sweetness. Even the walnuts were a bit bitter.

The sourdough was nothing exceptional, it was more on the sour side, and I think the crust was a bit too bitter as well.

The scallops were perfectly tender - nothing negative to say here. Complemented nicely with the sauce. Quite good and I would happily have it again.

The servers were attentive. The ambiance feels a little rowdy for fine dining or an intimate setting, it can get quite noisy from the other diners.

p.s. not lactose-friendly but with it! - pack your lactaid

Incredible experience.

Food was flawless, from the basics (sourdough & butter) to the mains (tuna, pork, crab).

Service was wonderful, our waiter was very friendly and engaged without being intrusive. He let us sample all kinds of wines in order to find one to our taste.

The space is cozy & convivial, and wasn't particularly loud as others have said. Very easy to carry a conversation.

Only hiccup was that getting seated took a little while due to the previous customers, but our drinks at the bar were comped so really nothing to complain about.

All the dishes we ordered were extraordinary!

- endive salad: 100/10 (I loved the combination of the crispy endive with the salty, vinegary, and crunchy sauce. I can eat this salad everyday)
- ricotta dumplings: 10/10 (loved the texture of the super thin mushroom. The ricotta dumplings were great!)
- crab omelette: 10/10 (the omelette was super silky smooth. The pickled greens on top really helped balance out the richness of the whole dish.)

Service was good, ambiance was very cozy chic. Be wary though that the seats are super small!
Delicious food. Really special. Fun to share the dishes. Lovely waiter. Very noisy, though. We probably won't go back for that reason--just too loud.

1/1 Ambience; 2/2 Food; 0.5/1 Service; .5/1 Value

Tucked away behind a discrete door on an otherwise sprightly Houston St. is the charming and intimate Estela featuring inspired takes on tapas-style western Mediterranean dishes. The ambience traverses rustic bistro with modernity, evocative of a European bistro with chic accents and finishes. It is certainly a small, narrow space, so expect to be privy to the conversations surrounding you. However, it still makes for an excellent date night spot, romantic or otherwise. 

My friend and I ordered a number of dishes to share: crab with celeriac and dulse, grilled tuna belly, fried arroz negro, the ricotta dumplings, and the striped bass with the chocolate cake and celeriac ice cream with figs for dessert. The food was incredible from start to finish with an exquisite array of flavors and textures from the subtle, savory broth and cloud-like dumplings to the umami-rich, slightly crisp arroz negro to the fresh, flaky crab under delicate, buttery celeriac sheets. My favorite was the arroz negro, but the striped bass was a close second as I enjoyed the unique combination of fruits and vegetables paired with the flaky fish. My least favorite was the grilled tuna belly as the fish was difficult to cut through and a little too chewy. The chocolate cake was very dense and almost had a lava cake like consistency, being the dish that finally filled us up. However, I enjoyed the celeriac ice cream more because of the earthy brightness that compliments the figs well, a flavor combination which I was really surprised to find how good it was in ice cream. Otherwise, the food was prepared fresh and it was a delightful experience.

The only setbacks on which I felt the experience could have been better: the service was so-so. When my friend and I ordered our dishes for the main meal (not even dessert yet), our server made an off-hand comment about if we were sure and that we were ordering very heavy today. Neither of us had eaten lunch that morning due to our professional commitments, so in effect this meal was our only real meal of the day. None of the main dishes were particularly filling given the very small portion sizes relative to the steep price, even for the neighborhood either. We were both put off by the comment and initially hesitated to order dessert until we decided that we were still too famished not to order more. Our other server, however, was much kinder and attentive without being intrusive. 

Barring these setbacks, the culinary experience at Estela was excellent, and I would definitely consider returning for special occasions and treat-yourself dining!

Wow this spot was incredible. It's been on my list for years to try and finally made it back to the city & snagged a dinner resy. Started with the endive salad that did NOT disappointed, there were pieces of anchovies, walnuts & cheese under the endive pieces that made each bite with the citrusy dressing so perfectly balanced. I would order again and again! The ricotta dumplings were delicious in the brodo w/ almost aerated slices of cheese on top, each bite was so rich & decadent. The scallops were SO fresh & amazing flavor combo with hazelnuts & dates. The venison was cooked to perfection & the grilled radicchio was the perfect balance. Amazing service with great recommendations for food & wine and explanation of food when it arrived. I absolutely LOVED the ambiance of this spot, it just exudes the NYC vibe of a tiny railroad house/ restaurant with low candlelit lighting, a great bar & few tables. Loved this spot!

I don't have pics of everything I ate because we were too busy enjoying the food and conversation at the table. Service here is always A1. They are attentive w/o being annoying. The restaurant is cozy, it doesn't feel cramped. 

This was my second time here. What I love about the food at Estela is how playful every dish is. Every plate was cleaned, no crumbs. My friend even took the ricotta dumpling broth from bowl to her face, it was so good. 

Things I highly recommend are the beef tartar, the Endive granola, the arroz and ricotta dumpling! 

We also did the cheese board and chocolate cake . 

Tip: I always recommend making a reservation. They be booked and busy.

LOVED our meal here. Every single dish besides the sourdough to start hit the mark.

We ordered:

Sourdough miche with butter 5
Beef tartare with elderberries and sunchoke* 27
Endive with walnuts, anchovy, and ubriaco rosso* 28
Fried arroz negro, squid, and romesco* 35
Ricotta dumplings with mushrooms and pecorino Sardo 35
Venison with huckleberries and radicchio* 51
A pork dish with parsnips 
A sunchoke salad
Chocolate cake

The table of 4 all had different opinions on which dish we loved best, so I'd say that's the mark of a great meal. Chocolate cake was a superb way to end the meal!

Wow had an amazing dinner here! I really don't understand the negative reviews - yes it is small and loud but I could easily hear my date and had no issue with it whatsoever. We walked in without reservations and there happened to be 2 bar seats available which was very exciting. The head bartender was fantastic - he made me his own version of a martini which was more lemony and really nice and refreshing. I was so enthralled by the food that I forgot to take pictures of my dishes! The menu for the night was quite different than what was online so I'll include that in my review. We started with the oysters, very good. We then got the beef tartare and the endive salad - both were incredible and had such a great crunch. We got the crab, it was very unique and good. And we finished with the venison, which I don't believe I've ever had venison before but this dish was incredible! We talked about our dinner all night and I'm still reliving it the next day. Highly recommend this spot!

I've been to Estela so many times over the years and every time I go back I am surprised that it has maintained the high quality of food and drink since I remember it opening a decade or so ago. The space is small and cute on Houston. It has the vibes of a quintessential cute neighborhood New York restaurant. Something you would have wanted to go into on a first date, or with your significant other of 20 years. Estela really hits the occasion for anything intimate and nice - and the space is quite intimate, not large at all.

The service matches the intimacy with honest, kind, and interactive servers. This is what I wish of more servers, however many fancy places have felt much more formal and distant in their service, thankfully Estela does not do this. We spoke to the bartender and requested bespoke drinks, they were all fantastic. We had a great conversation with the waitress and she made some great suggestions on the menu, again all fantastic.

I had many of my favorites, including the ricotta gnudi with mushrooms and black rice (both of which you should get), but really enjoyed the scallops that come served so beautifully and the duck, which was new to the menu and the one thing I hadn't tried yet. It was fantastic!

I'll keep coming back to Estela, it's such a treat. I don't come more than once a year because there's so much dining to do in NYC - but I do think Estela is a standard for NYC small plates and if you haven't been you probably should come.

I came here to celebrate my husband's birthday, and we were both a bit disappointed. We came here for brunch on a Friday afternoon, and it was fairly packed. After looking around, we noticed that everybody had the same thing on their table, which was a dish of smoked trout. It was fine, but nothing too special and too expensive for what it is. We really enjoyed the black sauce that was paired with it but they only gave a small dab of it. The scallops were our favorite. It was delicious and we enjoyed the creaminess and nuttiness of the date. We also ordered a truffle omelette, which was way too salty. The egg was not fluffy and was overpowered by the saltiness of the cheese. Although I did enjoy the wagyu steak dish, I felt the potato chips weren't really necessary and quite random. Some chips were salty and others had no flavor at all. My picture of the steak just looks like a pile of potato chips as it was buried under underneath a mound of them. Overall, just not very worth it for the price. Each dish was pretty much $30 or more, with the most expensive dish being the potato chips (with a side of wagyu) at $54.

Food was unique and so flavorful with unexpected combinations.  The waitress guided us well!  Highly recommended the beautiful Bay Scallops with date and hazelnut! The chocolate cake was also
A standout!

The food and service easily explains the Michelin Star rating.  We shared 7 dishes.  We had the ricotta dumplings, the black ink fried rice, scallops, wagyu beef, oysters,  mackerel and  endive salad.  All are meant to be sharing dishes.  As always, we skip desert.

Incredible experience.  They bring the food out in order of light to heavy...meaning the oysters are first and the wagyu is last.

Our server was spot on.

A bit on the pricey side, but definitely worth the price.

After a recent dinner date at Estela, I felt compelled to write this review after falling victim to a deeply troubling, yet clear-as-day issue with this restaurant. 

My date made the reservation. We were guided to the seating area and ushered to a small two top. I am a male, roughly 4-5 inches taller than my date, so I took the outer chair, allowing her the bench against the wall (Mind you, I'm not staunch about gender norms. It just seemed like the thing to do). To my dismay, when we both sat, I realized that the seat of my chair was dramatically lower than the seat of her bench. Thus, for the remainder of the dinner I was relegated to the posture of a child sitting with his guardian. Fortunately for me, she and I are familiar with each other already, so we could laugh about the absurdity of it. 

And yet, I felt infantilized at times during the meal. I was so thrown by the difference in eye-line that I even started to behave as a child. Fidgeting, loss of concentration, and so on.. I was even tempted to ask for a straw for my drink. 

I thought to myself, as I was sampling the black rice, and various dishes featuring a reductions of this or that, what if this WAS a first date?? Then, the dynamic would be completely thrown off by this establishment given the perversion of their seating. Dare I say, I could imagine a pair meeting for the first time with the potential to fall in love, to get married, to have children, only for that dream to be decimated by the folly of Estela. Because one thing is for certain, it does not matter how self assured you are, if you are forced to sit in a child's seat across from someone, your date will be an inevitable failure. 

For what it's worth: The food is very good.

The food is as amazing as it was on my first visit! There is a reason you keep going back to Estela. The food is creative and delicious, the vibe is so upbeat and the service is perfect. The cocktails and the wine list are terrific as well.
